title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
子曰參乎吾道一以貫之曾子曰唯子出
門人問曰何謂也曾子曰夫子之道忠
恕而已矣
易弘器
同考試官教諭章　批〔此以行言是作得之〕
同考試官教諭鄒　批〔宛然聖門授受口氣〕
同考試官教諭楊　批〔論語義精瑩如此者絕少〕
===
同考試官教諭張　批〔詞理精到〕
考試官學正張　批〔是知心學者〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔純正可式〕
大賢深契乎聖道之傳而因以發其蘊焉蓋聖
道之全體不外乎一貫也大賢深契而發其蘊
焉其亦善學聖人者矣昔者曾子眞積力久學
將有得也夫子乃呼而語之曰道無事於泛求
學莫貴於知要參也知吾之道乎吾非事事而
求之物物而措之也至寂以神天下之感而事
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
子曰：「參乎！吾道一以貫之。」曾子曰：「唯。」子出，門人問曰：「何謂也？」曾子曰：「夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。」
易弘器

translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

The Master said: “Shen! My Way has one thread running through it.” Zengzi replied: “Yes.” When the Master went out, his disciples asked: “What did he mean?” Zengzi said: “The Master’s Way is simply doing one’s utmost for others and extending consideration to them.”

Yi Hongqi

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “This passage speaks in terms of practice; this composition grasps that.”
Associate Examiner Zou, Instructor, comments: “Precisely the tone of teaching transmitted and received within the sage’s school.”
Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “Expositions of the meaning of the Analects as refined and lucid as this are exceedingly rare.”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Both expression and reasoning are refined and exact.”
Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: “Here is someone who understands the learning of the mind.”
Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: “Pure and orthodox; worthy to serve as a model.”

The great worthy deeply apprehended the transmission of the sage’s Way and thereby revealed its underlying meaning. For the entirety of the sage’s Way consists in nothing beyond its single unifying thread. The great worthy deeply apprehended it and revealed its underlying meaning: surely he was one who knew well how to learn from the sage.

In former times, Zengzi had sincerely accumulated learning and exerted himself over a long period, and was about to attain understanding. The Master then called to him and said: “In pursuing the Way, there is no need to search indiscriminately; in learning, nothing is more valuable than knowing the essentials. Shen, do you understand my Way? I do not seek it separately in every affair or apply it separately to every thing. Through utmost stillness, I give a wondrous responsiveness to all that moves us in the world, and affairs …”

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
爲之曲當者同歸而殊途大公以立順應之原
而物理之散殊者百慮而一致成性爲道義之
門一實萬分也大本妙達道之用萬原於一也
吾之道知是而已曾子一聞斯言而卽應之曰
唯蓋當可之施適觸其將得之機而神契之妙
自不假於言語之贅矣于時門人聞言雖同而
悟道則異故於夫子旣出而有何謂之問焉蓋
心法之傳固非淺學所能識而獨得之藴有難
直指而明言故曾子借學者之事而曉之曰夫
===
子之道非有他也卽學者之盡其心而忠焉推
其心而恕焉耳矣是雖勉强以推行若不出乎
下學之功要其體用之合一亦可通乎上達之
妙知忠之達乎恕也推之於物而各足則一實
萬分以昭吾心之大用者卽此而在矣知恕之
本乎忠也反之於已而有餘則萬原於一以立
吾心之全體者又豈有他哉故謂夫子之道不
外於忠恕可也謂由忠恕以求夫子之道亦可
也噫若曾子者可謂善發聖人之藴者矣非其
punctuated: 爲之曲當者，同歸而殊途；大公以立順應之原，而物理之散殊者，百慮而一致。成性爲道義之門，一實萬分也；大本妙達道之用，萬原於一也。吾之道，知是而已。」曾子一聞斯言，而卽應之曰：「唯。」蓋當可之施，適觸其將得之機，而神契之妙，自不假於言語之贅矣。于時門人聞言雖同，而悟道則異，故於夫子旣出，而有「何謂」之問焉。蓋心法之傳，固非淺學所能識，而獨得之藴，有難直指而明言，故曾子借學者之事而曉之曰：「夫子之道，非有他也，卽學者之盡其心而忠焉，推其心而恕焉耳矣。」是雖勉强以推行，若不出乎下學之功，要其體用之合一，亦可通乎上達之妙。知忠之達乎恕也，推之於物而各足，則一實萬分，以昭吾心之大用者，卽此而在矣。知恕之本乎忠也，反之於已而有餘，則萬原於一，以立吾心之全體者，又豈有他哉？故謂夫子之道不外於忠恕，可也；謂由忠恕以求夫子之道，亦可也。噫！若曾子者，可謂善發聖人之藴者矣。非其
translation_en:
…and conduct is fitting in every particular: different paths lead to the same destination. Utter impartiality establishes the source of responding appropriately to circumstances, so that the manifold principles of things, though approached through a hundred deliberations, converge upon one unity. The perfected nature is the gateway to the Way and righteousness: one reality differentiates into myriad particulars. The great foundation wondrously brings into operation the universally prevailing Way: the myriad have their source in the one. As for my Way, knowing this is all there is to it.” As soon as Zengzi heard these words, he immediately replied, “Yes.” The instruction, imparted at just the right moment, touched precisely upon the point at which he was about to attain understanding. The subtlety of his intuitive accord naturally required no superfluous words.

At that time, although the disciples heard the same words, their understanding of the Way differed. Thus, after the Master had gone out, they asked, “What did he mean?” The transmission of the teaching of the mind is certainly beyond the comprehension of those whose learning is shallow; moreover, the profound meaning grasped by Zengzi alone was difficult to point out directly and explain explicitly. Zengzi therefore drew upon the work of learners to enlighten them, saying: “The Master’s Way is nothing other than this: learners fully exert their minds in wholeheartedness, and extend their minds to others in reciprocity.”

Although this involves strenuous effort to put it into practice, and seems not to go beyond the work of learning at the ordinary level, its essential unity of substance and function also gives access to the subtlety of reaching higher understanding. If one understands that wholeheartedness extends into reciprocity, extending it to things so that each receives its due, then the one reality differentiates into myriad particulars: precisely herein lies what manifests the great functioning of our minds. If one understands that reciprocity is rooted in wholeheartedness, returning to oneself [?] and finding more than enough, then the myriad have their source in the one: what else could establish the complete substance of our minds? Thus, it is valid to say that the Master’s Way lies wholly within wholeheartedness and reciprocity; it is also valid to say that one seeks the Master’s Way through wholeheartedness and reciprocity. Ah! Someone such as Zengzi may indeed be said to have excelled at bringing forth the sage’s profound meaning. Had he not …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
學之眞有得焉烏足以語此抑斯道也卽夫子
博約之訓而無隱於二三子者也但學者習矣
不察雖賜之穎悟猶不免於多識之疑以參之
魯亦必待積久而後得惟不違如愚者其殆庶
幾乎蓋上焉者得意而忘言其次因言以得意
是知賜之達不若參之魯參之魯不若回之愚
優優大哉禮儀三百威儀三千
金達
同考試官教諭李　批〔道體事無不在作者類〕
===
〔於優優處泛說殊失本旨子能卽禮會道而文足以發之其善〕
〔作中庸義者錄之〕
考試官學正張　批〔說理精切非有得於道〕
〔者不能作此也〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔詞語充足而思致縝密〕
〔文字之優者是用錄出〕
中庸贊聖道之大必舉禮之全者以見之也夫
道者禮之原也舉禮之全而道無不在焉則其
大也可見矣中庸二十七章發明人道也意以
punctuated:
學之眞有得焉，烏足以語此？抑斯道也，卽夫子博約之訓，而無隱於二三子者也。但學者習矣不察，雖賜之穎悟，猶不免於多識之疑；以參之魯，亦必待積久而後得。惟不違如愚者，其殆庶幾乎！蓋上焉者得意而忘言，其次因言以得意。是知賜之達不若參之魯，參之魯不若回之愚。

優優大哉！禮儀三百，威儀三千。
金達

同考試官教諭李，批〔道體事無不在，作者類〕〔於優優處泛說，殊失本旨。子能卽禮會道，而文足以發之，其善〕〔作中庸義者，錄之。〕
考試官學正張，批〔說理精切，非有得於道〕〔者不能作此也。〕
考試官教授鄭，批〔詞語充足，而思致縝密，〕〔文字之優者，是用錄出。〕

中庸贊聖道之大，必舉禮之全者，以見之也。夫道者，禮之原也。舉禮之全，而道無不在焉，則其大也可見矣。中庸二十七章發明人道也，意以
translation_en:
…his learning had yielded genuine attainment; how else could he have spoken thus? Moreover, this Way is precisely what the Master taught concerning breadth of learning and restraint through ritual, concealing nothing from his disciples. Yet students become accustomed to it without examining it. Even Ci, with his keen understanding, could not escape the mistaken supposition that it consisted in knowing many things; Shen, with his dullness, likewise had to await long accumulation before attaining it. Only the one who never contradicted the Master and seemed foolish came close! Those of the highest order grasp the meaning and forget the words; those next below grasp the meaning through the words. Thus we know that Ci’s perceptiveness was inferior to Shen’s dullness, and Shen’s dullness inferior to Hui’s foolishness.

“How ample and great! The three hundred rules of ceremony and the three thousand rules of deportment.”
Jin Da

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The substance of the Way is present in every affair. Writers generally discuss ‘ample’ in vague terms, quite missing the original purport. You can apprehend the Way through ritual, and your writing adequately brings it out. This is a fine exposition of the Doctrine of the Mean; I select it for inclusion.”

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The explanation of principle is precise and incisive. No one without an apprehension of the Way could have written this.”

Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: “The language is full and ample, and the thought meticulous. This is superior writing, and for that reason it is selected for inclusion.”

In praising the greatness of the sagely Way, the Doctrine of the Mean necessarily adduces ritual in its entirety to make that greatness manifest. The Way is the source of ritual. When ritual is adduced in its entirety, the Way is present throughout it, and its greatness can therefore be seen. Chapter twenty-seven of the Doctrine of the Mean elucidates the human Way, its meaning being that…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖人之道之大豈惟發育峻極而已哉然亦入
於至小而無間也使小有弗入則亦大之未至
矣蓋其易簡之能貫徹於事爲而隨在各足中
正之則分布於酬酢而體物不遺極天下之至
繁有以盡該括之神裕於此而達於彼也舉天
下之至賾有以極充周之妙此有餘而彼無不
足也不亦優優其大矣乎自今觀之敦典於會
通之觀而盡倫之教行焉夫是之謂禮儀於稽
其類不有三百者乎本天常以爲則而陳之藝
===
極以辨天下之異因人情以爲制而章之軌物
以合天下之敬是雖宏綱要領區以別矣而大
經大法所以範圍而不過者道爲之綱維也道
固無體之禮矣果於禮儀而有遺乎顯設於人
文之賁而盡飾之教行焉夫是之謂威儀其數
可陳不有三千者乎登降有度而恭遜之施順
適於動容之間隆殺異宜而品節之詳雍容於
嘉會之合是雖繁文縟節散以殊矣而中規中
矩所以曲成而不遺者道爲之推行也道固無
punctuated: 聖人之道之大，豈惟發育峻極而已哉？然亦入於至小而無間也。使小有弗入，則亦大之未至矣。蓋其易簡之能，貫徹於事爲而隨在各足；中正之則，分布於酬酢而體物不遺。極天下之至繁，有以盡該括之神，裕於此而達於彼也；舉天下之至賾，有以極充周之妙，此有餘而彼無不足也。不亦優優其大矣乎？自今觀之，敦典於會通之觀，而盡倫之教行焉。夫是之謂禮儀，於稽其類，不有三百者乎？本天常以爲則，而陳之藝極，以辨天下之異；因人情以爲制，而章之軌物，以合天下之敬。是雖宏綱要領，區以別矣，而大經大法，所以範圍而不過者，道爲之綱維也。道固無體之禮矣，果於禮儀而有遺乎？顯設於人文之賁，而盡飾之教行焉。夫是之謂威儀，其數可陳，不有三千者乎？登降有度，而恭遜之施，順適於動容之間；隆殺異宜，而品節之詳，雍容於嘉會之合。是雖繁文縟節，散以殊矣，而中規中矩，所以曲成而不遺者，道爲之推行也。道固無
translation_en:
…could the greatness of the sage’s Way consist solely in nourishing and developing all things and reaching the loftiest heights? It also enters into the very smallest things without leaving any gap. If there were anything small that it failed to enter, its greatness would not yet be complete. Its efficacy through ease and simplicity pervades affairs and activities, sufficient wherever it is found; its standard of centrality and correctness extends throughout human dealings, giving substance to things without omitting any. Even amid the utmost multiplicity under Heaven, it fully manifests its wondrous power to encompass everything, abounding here and reaching there. In all that is most intricate under Heaven, it fully realizes the marvel of all-pervading fullness: there is abundance here and no insufficiency there. Is its greatness not boundlessly ample?

Viewed now, it gives substance to the enduring norms through a comprehensive understanding of their interconnections, and thus the teaching that fulfills human relationships is put into practice. These are what are called the rules of ritual propriety. If we examine their categories, are there not three hundred? Taking Heaven’s constant principles as their standard, they set these forth as definitive norms to distinguish the differences among all under Heaven; basing their institutions on human feelings, they make these manifest in rules of conduct to unite the reverence of all under Heaven. Although these broad outlines and essential principles are divided into distinct categories, it is the Way that holds together the great guiding principles and laws by which all is encompassed without overstepping the bounds. The Way is indeed ritual without tangible substance. Could it really leave anything out of the rules of ritual propriety?

It is visibly displayed in the adornments of human culture, and thus the teaching that brings refinement to completion is put into practice. These are what are called the forms of dignified deportment. Their number can be enumerated: are there not three thousand? Ascending and descending have their proper measures, and the expression of respect and deference accords fittingly with every movement and bearing. Greater and lesser degrees of ceremony each have their appropriate application, and the detailed gradations of observance find graceful expression in harmonious ceremonial gatherings. Although these elaborate forms and intricate observances are dispersed into distinct particulars, it is the Way that sets them in operation, fitting the compass and square and bringing each particular to fulfillment without omission. The Way is indeed ritual without …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
形之禮矣果於威儀而有間乎是知禮本乎道
道寓於禮其入乎小者乃所以爲大也體道君
子其功豈可忽哉是故尊德性而存吾心焉所
以極乎其大也道問學而致吾知焉所以盡乎
其細也二者交致其功而聖道之大可馴至矣
或者不察以問學爲可緩是不免擇之不精於
德性也亦蔽矣不然則孔子之問禮問官何哉
吁學者可以自悟矣
君子所性仁義禮智根於心其生色也睟
然見於面盎於背施於四體四體不言
===
而喻
劉憲
同考試官教諭招 批〔根本於心由於氣稟無累此作深得孟子之意而詞意煒然子非根心生色者耶起敬起敬〕
考試官學正張 批〔融會傳註成文必積盛者宜錄〕
考試官教授鄭 批〔曲盡所性之蘊〕
punctuated:
形之禮矣，果於威儀而有間乎？是知禮本乎道，道寓於禮，其入乎小者，乃所以爲大也。體道君子，其功豈可忽哉？是故尊德性而存吾心焉，所以極乎其大也；道問學而致吾知焉，所以盡乎其細也。二者交致其功，而聖道之大可馴至矣。或者不察，以問學爲可緩，是不免擇之不精，於德性也亦蔽矣。不然，則孔子之問禮問官何哉？吁！學者可以自悟矣。
君子所性，仁義禮智根於心，其生色也，睟然見於面，盎於背，施於四體；四體不言而喻。
劉憲
同考試官教諭招批〔根本於心，由於氣稟無累。此作深得孟子之意，而詞意煒然。子非根心生色者耶？起敬！起敬！〕
考試官學正張批〔融會傳註成文，必積盛者，宜錄。〕
考試官教授鄭批〔曲盡所性之蘊。〕
translation_en:
…formless ritual propriety: can it really be separate from ceremonial deportment? Thus we know that ritual propriety is rooted in the Way, and the Way resides in ritual propriety. Its penetration into small matters is precisely how it achieves greatness. How could the gentleman who embodies the Way neglect this work? Thus, honoring our moral nature and preserving our mind bring its greatness to the utmost; pursuing inquiry and learning and extending our knowledge exhaust its finer details. When these two practices bring their efforts to bear together, the greatness of the sages’ Way can gradually be attained. Some fail to understand this and consider inquiry and learning something that may be deferred. They inevitably lack precision in their discernment and are also obscured in their understanding of moral nature. Were it otherwise, why did Confucius inquire about rites and official institutions? Ah! Students may awaken to this for themselves.
“What the gentleman possesses as his nature—benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom—is rooted in his mind. The radiance it produces appears with limpid clarity in his face, fills his back, and extends to his four limbs. Without speaking, his four limbs make it understood.”
Liu Xian.
Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: 〔Being rooted in the mind depends on an unencumbered endowment of vital energy. This composition deeply grasps Mencius’s meaning, and its language and ideas shine brilliantly. Are you not yourself one whose virtues take root in the mind and produce an outward radiance? My respect is stirred! My respect is stirred!〕
Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: 〔He integrates the commentaries into a coherent composition. Surely he is someone with a rich accumulation of learning; this deserves selection.〕
Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: 〔It exhaustively brings out the deeper meaning of what the gentleman possesses as his nature.〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
大賢著君子所性之藴而有積中發外之妙焉
蓋性立天下之有也君子性既積於中矣則其
發外之妙豈容已耶孟子之意以爲君子所性
夫既欲樂不與存而窮達無加損矣顧不有所
藴之可言乎蓋其得於天者有以全於我足於
已者無所待於外仁義禮智根於心也我固有
之也存存者其成性也而純粹之精不誘於攻
取之欲性性者其存神也而清明之稟不梏於
有我之私是其性命於德德勝其氣德之積也
===
亦盛矣由是而生於色也誠則必形和順妙於
英華之發德則能潤光輝溢於篤實之餘以言
乎面非有期於睟也神之所融而聚爲有象自
爾清和潤澤一見之悅而示人可親矣以言乎
背非有期於盎也精之所凝而適得吾體自爾
豐厚盈溢一艮之止而示人可重矣以言乎四
體不必議之後動也從心所欲不踰乎矩不必
言而後信也動容周旋自中乎禮蓋有手之舞
足之蹈而莫知其然者矣夫孰非其根於心者
punctuated: 大賢著君子所性之藴，而有積中發外之妙焉。蓋性立天下之有也，君子性既積於中矣，則其發外之妙豈容已耶？孟子之意以爲君子所性，夫既欲樂不與存，而窮達無加損矣，顧不有所藴之可言乎？蓋其得於天者有以全於我，足於已者無所待於外。仁義禮智根於心也，我固有之也。存存者其成性也，而純粹之精不誘於攻取之欲；性性者其存神也，而清明之稟不梏於有我之私。是其性命於德，德勝其氣，德之積也亦盛矣。由是而生於色也，誠則必形，和順妙於英華之發；德則能潤，光輝溢於篤實之餘。以言乎面，非有期於睟也，神之所融而聚爲有象，自爾清和潤澤，一見之悅，而示人可親矣。以言乎背，非有期於盎也，精之所凝而適得吾體，自爾豐厚盈溢，一艮之止，而示人可重矣。以言乎四體，不必議之後動也，從心所欲不踰乎矩；不必言而後信也，動容周旋自中乎禮。蓋有手之舞、足之蹈，而莫知其然者矣。夫孰非其根於心者
translation_en:
The great worthy reveals the depths of what constitutes the gentleman’s nature, showing the wondrous way in which what accumulates within manifests itself outwardly. For nature establishes all that exists under Heaven [?]. Once the gentleman’s nature has accumulated within, how could its wondrous outward manifestation be restrained? Mengzi’s meaning is that what constitutes the gentleman’s nature does not depend for its existence on what he desires or delights in, nor is it increased or diminished by adversity or success. Surely, then, there are depths within it that can be discussed. What he receives from Heaven can be preserved whole within himself; what is sufficient within himself need await nothing from outside. Benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom are rooted in the heart: these are things he inherently possesses. By preserving them continually, he completes his nature, and its pure essence is not enticed by acquisitive desires. By fully realizing his nature, he preserves its spiritual efficacy, and his clear, luminous endowment is not fettered by selfish attachment to the self. Thus his nature takes its mandate from virtue [?], and virtue prevails over his vital energy. His accumulation of virtue is indeed abundant.

From this it comes to expression in his appearance. Sincerity must manifest itself: harmony and compliance find wondrous expression in its flowering brilliance. Virtue can impart a lustre: radiance overflows from his substantial integrity. As for his face, he does not deliberately seek its serene clarity. His spiritual efficacy suffuses it and gathers into visible form, making it naturally clear, harmonious, lustrous, and moist. Pleasing at first sight, it shows others that he is approachable. As for his back, he does not deliberately seek its fullness. His essence condenses there and finds fitting embodiment, naturally becoming rich, substantial, and overflowing. In the stillness expressed by the hexagram Gen, Keeping Still, he shows others that he is worthy of respect. As for his four limbs, he need not deliberate before acting: he follows his heart’s desires without overstepping the bounds. He need not speak before being trusted: his movements and bearing naturally accord with ritual propriety. Indeed, his hands dance and his feet stamp without his knowing how they do so. And which of these is not brought about by what is rooted in his heart …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
爲之耶是則所性之藴豫於内而利於外道本
至足吾自足焉而已使其達也以之兼善天下
窮也以之獨善其身隨其所遇夫亦安之而已
又何加損之有是何也吾性本無大行窮居也
是故無加損也舜禹有天下而不與孔子用則
行舍則藏凡以是也彼以性爲外而庸心於得
喪者固不勝其私而戚矣孟子存心養性勿助
勿忘雖加齊之卿相而不動心去齊而未嘗不
豫可以占其藴矣
===
易
文言曰元者善之長也亨者嘉之會也利
者義之和也貞者事之幹也君子體仁
足以長人嘉會足以合禮利物足以和
義貞固足以幹事君子行此四德者故
曰乾元亨利貞
張敏德
同考試官教諭聶 批 〔人之四德法天之健斯能合德于天善發揚者其惟子乎〕
punctuated:
爲之耶？是則所性之藴，豫於内而利於外，道本至足，吾自足焉而已。使其達也，以之兼善天下；窮也，以之獨善其身。隨其所遇，夫亦安之而已，又何加損之有？是何也？吾性本無大行窮居也，是故無加損也。舜禹有天下而不與，孔子用則行，舍則藏，凡以是也。彼以性爲外而庸心於得喪者，固不勝其私而戚矣。孟子存心養性，勿助勿忘，雖加齊之卿相而不動心，去齊而未嘗不豫，可以占其藴矣。

易

文言曰：「元者，善之長也；亨者，嘉之會也；利者，義之和也；貞者，事之幹也。君子體仁，足以長人；嘉會，足以合禮；利物，足以和義；貞固，足以幹事。君子行此四德者，故曰：『乾，元亨利貞。』」

張敏德

同考試官教諭聶 批〔人之四德法天之健，斯能合德于天。善發揚者，其惟子乎！〕
translation_en:
…that brings this about? Thus, what is contained in one's inherent nature brings ease within and benefit without. The Way is itself utterly sufficient; I simply find my sufficiency in it. If one attains prominence, one uses it to bring goodness to all under Heaven; if one remains obscure, one uses it to cultivate goodness in oneself alone. Whatever circumstances one encounters, one simply rests content in them. What increase or diminution could there be? Why is this so? Our nature itself knows no distinction between acting on a grand scale and dwelling in obscurity; hence it undergoes neither increase nor diminution. Shun and Yu possessed all under Heaven yet did not involve themselves in it; Confucius acted when employed and withdrew when set aside. All this followed from the same principle. Those who regard their nature as something external and concern themselves with gain and loss cannot overcome their selfishness and are consequently distressed. Mencius preserved his heart and nourished his nature, neither forcing its growth nor neglecting it. Even appointment as a high minister or chief councillor of Qi would not move his heart, and when he left Qi he never ceased to be at ease. From this we may discern what he held within.

Book of Changes

The Commentary on the Words of the Text says: “The originating is the foremost of goodness; the prosperous is the convergence of excellence; the beneficial is the harmony of rightness; the steadfast is the mainstay of affairs. By embodying benevolence, the gentleman is able to lead others; by bringing excellence together, he is able to accord with ritual propriety; by benefiting things, he is able to harmonize with rightness; by remaining steadfast and firm, he is able to manage affairs. The gentleman practices these four virtues. Thus it is said: ‘Qian: originating, prosperous, beneficial, steadfast.’”

Zhang Minde

Comment by Associate Examiner Nie, Instructor: 〔When a person's four virtues take Heaven's vigor as their model, that person can unite in virtue with Heaven. Surely you are one who excels at bringing this meaning fully to light!〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭高　批〔善說乾象之義佳士〕
〔佳士〕
同考試官教諭袁　批〔題長貴簡潔此作得之〕
考試官學正張　批〔詞氣自是渾成〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔精練〕
觀文言申乾象之意而天人合一之妙見矣蓋
君子之有四德猶夫天也而所以行之者健也
乾亦健而已矣天人合一之妙不可見哉文言
申乾象傳之意所以盡其藴也蓋謂乾之道具
===
於易其原出於天神而明之存乎其人是故在
天有元亨利貞在人爲仁義禮智繼之者善成
之者性也仁則心之德愛之理而統天下之善
者在是禮則敬之合德之聚而嘉天下之會者
在是義其動而正用而和公天下之利者乎智
其守之貴行之利一天下之動者乎是則天之
未始不爲人而能體之者君子也君子以仁爲
體無弗愛也大心體物而宜君宜王矣嘉其所
會無弗敬也周旋中禮而有經有緯矣使物各
punctuated:
同考試官教諭高　批〔善說乾象之義，佳士〕〔佳士〕
同考試官教諭袁　批〔題長貴簡潔，此作得之〕
考試官學正張　批〔詞氣自是渾成〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔精練〕
觀《文言》申乾象之意，而天人合一之妙見矣。蓋君子之有四德，猶夫天也，而所以行之者健也。乾亦健而已矣，天人合一之妙不可見哉？《文言》申乾《象傳》之意，所以盡其藴也。蓋謂乾之道具於《易》，其原出於天，神而明之，存乎其人。是故在天有元亨利貞，在人爲仁義禮智，繼之者善，成之者性也。仁則心之德、愛之理，而統天下之善者在是；禮則敬之合、德之聚，而嘉天下之會者在是；義其動而正、用而和、公天下之利者乎？智其守之貴、行之利、一天下之動者乎？是則天之未始不爲人，而能體之者君子也。君子以仁爲體，無弗愛也，大心體物而宜君宜王矣；嘉其所會，無弗敬也，周旋中禮而有經有緯矣；使物各
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: “An able exposition of the meaning of Qian’s Image. A fine scholar.” A separate annotation repeats: “A fine scholar.”
Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: “With a long set passage, concision is especially prized; this composition achieves it.”
Examiner Zhang, School Director, comments: “The language and spirit are naturally integrated.”
Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: “Refined and concise.”
When we observe how the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) elaborates the meaning of Qian’s Image, the subtle unity of Heaven and humanity becomes apparent. The gentleman’s possession of the four virtues is like Heaven’s own, and what enables him to put them into practice is vigor. Qian, too, is simply vigor. Can we not see here the subtle unity of Heaven and humanity? The Wenyan elaborates the meaning of the Commentary on the Images for Qian so as to bring out its full significance. It means that the Way of Qian is fully contained in the Book of Changes, while its source lies in Heaven; making it spiritually efficacious and illuminating it rests with the person. Thus, in Heaven there are origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy; in humanity these become benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom. What continues this is goodness; what brings it to completion is human nature.
Benevolence is the virtue of the heart and the principle of love: in it lies that which encompasses all goodness under Heaven. Ritual propriety is the convergence of reverence and the gathering of virtue: in it lies that which makes excellent all gatherings under Heaven. Is righteousness not that which is correct in its activity and harmonious in its application, making the benefits of all under Heaven equitably available? Is wisdom not that which is precious to uphold and beneficial to practice, unifying all activity under Heaven? Thus Heaven has never been separate from humanity, and it is the gentleman who can embody it.
The gentleman takes benevolence as his substance, leaving nothing unloved. Enlarging his heart to embrace all things, he is fit to be a lord or a king. He makes excellent that which he gathers together, leaving nothing unhonored. All his movements accord with ritual propriety, giving them both warp and weft. He enables each thing to …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
得其利則雖嚴而泰衆動得時措之宜矣知正
而固守之則能擇而守凡事有豫立之基矣是
則人之未始不爲天而其所以行之者至健也
蓋欲之勝者或得以間理氣之餒者不能以配
道君子則直養無害而天德之剛能勝夫人欲
之私故德性常用而四端之善不虧於付畀之
初兼體而不累存神其至矣非天下之至健其
孰能與於此故曰乾元亨利貞以元亨利貞而
必屬之乾者此也蓋天運而不已故物生而不
===
窮非乾則天道亦幾乎息矣是則天人合一之
妙而文王象乾之餘蘊也非文言其孰能發之
抑乾道也天道也人道也皆本於健固也而健
豈易言哉天良能本吾良能顧爲有我所喪爾
有我則私私則二二則息息則與乾道天道不
相似矣君子乾乾自強所以成之於天者亦惟
去其有我之私耳故曰自勝者強
允升大吉上合志也
張正位
punctuated:
得其利，則雖嚴而泰，衆動得時措之宜矣。知正而固守之，則能擇而守，凡事有豫立之基矣。是則人之未始不爲天，而其所以行之者，至健也。蓋欲之勝者，或得以間理；氣之餒者，不能以配道。君子則直養無害，而天德之剛能勝夫人欲之私，故德性常用，而四端之善不虧於付畀之初。兼體而不累，存神其至矣。非天下之至健，其孰能與於此？故曰：「乾，元亨利貞。」以元亨利貞而必屬之乾者，此也。蓋天運而不已，故物生而不窮；非乾，則天道亦幾乎息矣。是則天人合一之妙，而文王象乾之餘蘊也。非《文言》，其孰能發之？抑乾道也，天道也，人道也，皆本於健固也。而健豈易言哉？天良能，本吾良能，顧爲有我所喪爾。有我則私，私則二，二則息，息則與乾道、天道不相似矣。君子乾乾自強，所以成之於天者，亦惟去其有我之私耳。故曰：「自勝者強。」

允升，大吉，上合志也。
張正位
translation_en:
…obtain their proper benefit, then, though stern, he brings tranquility, and all activities are undertaken appropriately and at the proper time. If he knows what is correct and holds firmly to it, he can choose and maintain his course, and every undertaking has a foundation laid in advance. Thus humanity has never been separate from Heaven, and what enables this to be put into practice is utmost vigor. For overpowering desires may intrude upon principle, while enfeebled vital energy cannot accord with the Way. The gentleman, however, nourishes it with uprightness and does it no injury; the firmness of Heaven’s virtue can overcome the selfishness of human desires. Thus his virtuous nature remains constantly active, and the goodness of the four beginnings suffers no diminution from its original endowment. Embracing all things without being encumbered by them, he preserves the spirit to the utmost. Who but one possessed of the utmost vigor under Heaven could attain this? Hence it is said: “Qian: origination, flourishing, benefit, and steadfastness.” This is why these four qualities must be attributed to Qian. Heaven moves without ceasing, and therefore things are generated without end; without Qian, even the Way of Heaven would all but cease. This is the subtlety of the unity of Heaven and humanity, and the further meaning implicit in King Wen’s representation of Qian. Who could have brought it to light but through the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan)?

Moreover, the Way of Qian, the Way of Heaven, and the human Way are all rooted in vigor and firmness. Yet how could vigor be easy to speak of? Heaven’s innate capacity is fundamentally our own innate capacity; it is simply lost through attachment to a self. Attachment to a self brings selfishness; selfishness brings division; division brings cessation. With cessation, one no longer resembles the Way of Qian or the Way of Heaven. The gentleman tirelessly exerts himself and strengthens himself; the means by which he achieves fulfillment in accord with Heaven consists solely in removing the selfishness of attachment to a self. Hence it is said: “He who overcomes himself is strong.”

“Trusted in ascending: great good fortune.” This is because his purpose accords with that of the one above.
Zhang Zhengwei

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭聶　批〔君子脩于家而未獲允升之吉志未孚也安有志既孚而不獲允升之吉者乎子可謂能〕
同考試官教諭高　批〔言其義者矣錄之〕
同考試官教諭袁　批〔善發明君子獲吉之旨講上下交孚處讀之令人〕
灑然
考試官學正張　批〔題義是矣〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔簡明可誦〕
象傳原交獲升之善而著其同德之孚也蓋君
===
子之於天下未嘗孤而立也初六志同於上而
德孚焉則其進而獲善也必矣夫子小象之意
以爲欲升者君子之同心而能升者君子所難
必乃惟初六之辭曰允升大吉則是攸往之利
得於交孚之間而兼善之施溥於協恭之下以
見大人則勿用憂恤而明良胥慶於一時以之
南征則尚往志行而名實得加於上下若是者
而豈徒哉亦以志之上合耳蓋門庭不出由上
無應與之人而拔茅彙征以陽皆在外之志初
punctuated:
同考試官教諭聶，批〔君子脩于家而未獲允升之吉，志未孚也。安有志既孚而不獲允升之吉者乎？子可謂能〕
同考試官教諭高，批〔言其義者矣，錄之。〕
同考試官教諭袁，批〔善發明君子獲吉之旨，講上下交孚處，讀之令人〕灑然。
考試官學正張，批〔題義是矣。〕
考試官教授鄭，批〔簡明可誦。〕
象傳原交獲升之善，而著其同德之孚也。蓋君子之於天下，未嘗孤而立也。初六志同於上而德孚焉，則其進而獲善也必矣。夫子小象之意，以爲欲升者君子之同心，而能升者君子所難必。乃惟初六之辭曰：「允升大吉。」則是攸往之利，得於交孚之間，而兼善之施，溥於協恭之下。以見大人，則勿用憂恤，而明良胥慶於一時；以之南征，則尚往志行，而名實得加於上下。若是者，而豈徒哉？亦以志之上合耳。蓋門庭不出，由上無應與之人；而拔茅彙征，以陽皆在外之志。初

How could someone whose aspirations have already won trust fail to attain the good fortune of ‘ascending with trust’? You may indeed be said to be capable…”〕
Associate Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: 〔“…of expressing its meaning. Accept this essay.”〕 [The comments attributed to Nie and Gao appear to form a single sentence across the two entries.]
Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: 〔“This ably elucidates the meaning of the gentleman’s attaining good fortune. Its discussion of mutual trust between those above and below leaves the reader feeling”〕 refreshed.
Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔“The meaning of the topic is correctly understood.”〕
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔“Concise, clear, and worthy of recitation.”〕
The Commentary on the Images traces the goodness attained through ascending together to its source and reveals the trust arising from shared virtue. For a gentleman never stands alone in the world. When the aspirations of the initial six accord with those above, and their virtue commands mutual trust, its advancement and attainment of good are assured. The Master’s meaning in the Lesser Images is that the wish to ascend is shared by all gentlemen, but the ability to ascend is something they can hardly count upon. Yet the statement for the initial six specifically says: “Ascending with trust: great good fortune.” Thus, the benefit of going forward is attained through mutual trust, and the beneficent influence that brings goodness to others spreads widely through harmonious cooperation and reverence. In going to see the great man, there is no need for anxiety, and an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers rejoice together at the same time. In proceeding southward, advancement is esteemed and aspirations are fulfilled, while reputation and actual achievement accrue to those above and below. Can such results come about without cause? They arise precisely because one’s aspirations accord with those above. For ‘not going out beyond the gate and courtyard’ results from having no one above who responds and offers support; while ‘pulling up couch grass and advancing with its clustered roots’ occurs because the aspirations of the yang lines are all directed outward. title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
六以陰居下爲巽之主當升之時巽於二陽利
用禴者二也上下交孚者也初則賴其孚而因
以上達焉進退得以關其忠升虛邑者三也進
往無疑者也初則隨其進而與之同升焉任職
得以行其術相須之殷也而相契之深利見以
從王之事者乃與類行不戒以孚也奚用憂恤
乎同道相益也而同心相與南征以熙帝之載
者朋至斯孚不謀而協也志有不行乎如是而
其升也固在所必然其獲吉也亦非爲倖致矣
===
否則道之不同不相爲謀抱格天之業者或阻
於機會之難逢而欲升得乎抑論聖主必待賢
臣而弘功業俊士亦俟明主以顯其德上下交
而成泰固其所也而其得進有由也是故貴合
志也虞廷命官必由疇咨僉謀而九官濟濟乃
成風動之休故易於良馬之逐金車之梡每致
意焉則允升合志安得不爲君子之慶
書
敷奏以言明試以功車服以庸

六以陰居下，爲巽之主。當升之時，巽於二陽。「利用禴」者，二也，上下交孚者也。初則賴其孚而因以上達焉，進退得以關其忠。「升虛邑」者，三也，進往無疑者也。初則隨其進而與之同升焉，任職得以行其術。相須之殷也，而相契之深，利見以從王之事者，乃與類行，不戒以孚也，奚用憂恤乎？同道相益也，而同心相與，南征以熙帝之載者，朋至斯孚，不謀而協也，志有不行乎？如是而其升也，固在所必然；其獲吉也，亦非爲倖致矣。否則，道之不同，不相爲謀，抱格天之業者，或阻於機會之難逢，而欲升得乎？抑論聖主必待賢臣而弘功業，俊士亦俟明主以顯其德。上下交而成泰，固其所也，而其得進有由也，是故貴合志也。虞廷命官，必由疇咨僉謀，而九官濟濟，乃成風動之休。故《易》於良馬之逐、金車之梡，每致意焉。則允升合志，安得不爲君子之慶？

translation_en:
…the initial Six, being yin and occupying the lowest position, is the governing line of the trigram Xun, Compliance. At the time of Ascending, it submits to the two yang lines. The line for which “it is beneficial to offer the yue sacrifice” is the second: those above and below trust one another. The initial line relies on that trust to reach upward, and thus, whether advancing or withdrawing, can convey its loyalty. The line that “ascends into an empty city” is the third: it advances without doubt. The initial line follows its advance and ascends together with it, and thus can put its methods into practice in office. So earnestly do they depend upon one another, and so deeply do they accord! Those who find it beneficial to see the great man and thereby undertake the king’s affairs proceed with their own kind, trusting without being admonished. What need have they for anxiety? Sharing the same Way, they benefit one another; sharing the same purpose, they support one another. Those who march south to advance the emperor’s work find trust when their companions arrive and agree without deliberation. Could their purpose fail to be carried out? In these circumstances, their ascent is assured, and their attainment of good fortune is no mere stroke of luck.

Otherwise, those whose Ways differ do not take counsel together. Even someone whose undertakings could reach Heaven might be thwarted by the difficulty of finding an opportunity. Could he then ascend, however much he wished to? Moreover, a sage ruler must await worthy ministers to enlarge his achievements, while outstanding men likewise await an enlightened ruler to manifest their virtue. That those above and below should interact and bring about Peace is indeed fitting; yet their advancement has its grounds. This is why agreement in purpose is prized. When the court of Yu appointed officials, it invariably consulted widely and sought collective counsel. Only with the distinguished holders of the nine offices assembled did it achieve the splendid transformation that spread like the wind. Thus the Book of Changes repeatedly draws attention to fine horses pursuing one another and to the crosspiece of a metal carriage [?]. How, then, could “ascending through trust” and agreement in purpose fail to be a cause for rejoicing among gentlemen?

試功而厚其報法莫有詳焉者矣聖世欲率作
以興事得不於是而加之意哉史臣之意蓋謂
===
帝王有以制上下之經則必有以嚴統御之法
稽之虞舜不可尚已彼以陳志者尚乎言言有
不達吾懼上下之勢隔而稽政者之無其術也
敷言之典其可已耶則必大虛受於聽納之間
使各陳其爲治之說其何以出之身也其何以

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔“Thorough, weighty, and classically elegant. There is not a single superfluous phrase in the entire composition, yet it describes almost exhaustively the intent of official performance evaluation at the court of Shun. Writers of this caliber are exceedingly rare among the examination candidates [?].”〕
Jin Daye (金達也) [?].
Examiner Zhang, Director of Studies, comments: 〔“Classically elegant and worthy of recitation.”〕
Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: 〔“It assuredly surpasses the rest.”〕
In a sage-governed age, the methods for evaluating and rewarding ministers who came to court were set out in detail. Having them present their words, testing their achievements, and generously rewarding them—no procedure could be more thorough. If the sage ruler wished to lead them in undertaking their work and advancing affairs, could he fail to give this his attention? The historian’s meaning was presumably this: when an emperor establishes the enduring order between those above and those below, he must also make strict the methods by which he directs and governs them. Examining the example of Yu Shun, we find that it cannot be surpassed.
For expressing intentions, words are paramount. If words fail to get through, I fear that the positions of superior and subordinate will keep them apart, and those who examine governmental affairs will lack the means to do so. Could the institution of presenting statements then be dispensed with? The ruler must therefore receive them with the utmost openness as he listens, allowing each to state his ideas about governing: how will he put them into practice in his own person? How will he extend them to the people? He must wish them all to come forward, so that none is denied the opportunity to express himself fully.
For verifying substance, achievements are paramount. If achievements are not tested, I fear that the abuses of deception will multiply and that those given to idle talk will embellish their language. Could the institution of testing achievements then be dispensed with? The ruler must therefore examine them comprehensively to ascertain the full truth, rank them higher or lower to assess their abilities, and scrutinize them …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
國以觀政也察之民以觀俗也莫不等而辨之
而無有相爲混淆者矣以激勸者尚乎賞賞以
功懋者大君之所以勵世也有弗然焉吾又懼
激勸之無機而天下日就于惰矣報功之典如
之何而可已耶則必嘉其明作之績而隆其錫
予之恩賜之輅車昭其德之在輿也賜之玄衮
昭其德之在躬也康侯之忠自有以彰於旌異
之際而無功者則亦有以告飭之矣夫是則維
持之制盡藏否之辨明而侯度之所以日謹治
===
道之所以日隆有由然哉抑治世尚行而必敷
言者至公也敬事後食而必試功者至明也不
賞而勸而必以庸者至仁也一事行而三善具
焉唐虞之治其斯以爲至乎是故責實則益隆
虛則損不易之道也成周而下若綜核名實而
吏稱其職稱致治如漢宣者謂非有得於此者
歟
貌曰恭言曰從視曰明聽曰聰思曰睿恭
作肅從作乂明作哲聽作謀睿作聖
punctuated:
國以觀政也，察之民以觀俗也，莫不等而辨之，而無有相爲混淆者矣。以激勸者尚乎賞，賞以功懋者，大君之所以勵世也。有弗然焉，吾又懼激勸之無機，而天下日就于惰矣。報功之典，如之何而可已耶？則必嘉其明作之績，而隆其錫予之恩。賜之輅車，昭其德之在輿也；賜之玄衮，昭其德之在躬也。康侯之忠，自有以彰於旌異之際，而無功者則亦有以告飭之矣。夫是則維持之制盡，藏否之辨明，而侯度之所以日謹、治道之所以日隆，有由然哉！抑治世尚行而必敷言者，至公也；敬事後食而必試功者，至明也；不賞而勸而必以庸者，至仁也。一事行而三善具焉，唐虞之治，其斯以爲至乎！是故責實則益，隆虛則損，不易之道也。成周而下，若綜核名實而吏稱其職，稱致治如漢宣者，謂非有得於此者歟？

貌曰恭，言曰從，視曰明，聽曰聰，思曰睿。恭作肅，從作乂，明作哲，聽作謀，睿作聖。
translation_en:
…in their states to observe their government, and examine them among the people to observe their customs, grading and distinguishing them all so that none are confused with one another. In encouraging effort, rewards are prized. Rewarding those whose achievements are outstanding is how the great ruler spurs the world onward. Should this not be done, I fear that encouragement would lack an effective means and that all under Heaven would daily sink into indolence. How could the institution of rewarding achievement be dispensed with? One must therefore commend their accomplishments in enlightened action and bestow generous favor upon them. Grant them carriages of state to display their virtue in their conveyances; grant them dark ceremonial robes to display their virtue upon their persons. The loyalty of the lord who brings peace is thereby manifested through special honors, while those without achievements likewise receive admonition. Thus the institutions that sustain order are fully implemented, and the distinction between merit and fault [?] is made clear. There is good reason, then, why the standards governing the feudal lords grow daily more exacting and the way of good government daily more exalted!

Moreover, an orderly age prizes action, yet still requires statements to be set forth: this is perfect impartiality. It prizes attending reverently to one's duties before taking one's emoluments, yet still requires achievements to be tested: this is perfect discernment. People exert themselves even without rewards, yet rewards must still be conferred according to merit: this is perfect benevolence. One undertaking is carried out, and all three virtues are present. Was it not through this that the government of Tang and Yu attained perfection? Thus, demanding substance brings benefit, while exalting empty appearances brings harm: this is an unchanging principle. After the Zhou dynasty, rulers such as Emperor Xuan of Han were praised for achieving good government by comprehensively comparing names with realities and ensuring that officials fulfilled their offices. Could one say that they had gained no understanding of this principle?

“Demeanor is to be reverent; speech, compliant; sight, clear; hearing, acute; thought, penetrating. Reverence produces solemnity; compliance produces order; clarity produces wisdom; hearing produces sound planning [?]; penetrating thought produces sageliness.”

之而誠身之道不可以觀乎箕子之告武王意
若曰君子建皇極以作則取諸吾身而自足妙
===
體用以成身本之以敬而有餘自夫人之具五
事也而豈徒哉有物必有則而則所以善乎其
物者也貌取諸恭吾心之莊敬恭之謂也容貌
非此不重矣貌曰恭焉言取諸從吾心之理順
從之謂也辭氣非此不達矣言曰從焉目以司
視也貞觀不眩有以善天下之色是之謂視遠
之明耳以司聽也至虛能應有以善天下之聲
是之謂聽德之聰以至思之所蘊則極深研幾
足以通天下之故足以類萬物之情而恭從明

君子於五事之疇，必著其德而及其用焉。夫五事之德之用，合內外而一之者也。君子演而言之，而誠身之道不可以觀乎？箕子之告武王，意若曰：君子建皇極以作則，取諸吾身而自足；妙體用以成身，本之以敬而有餘。自夫人之具五事也，而豈徒哉？有物必有則，而則所以善乎其物者也。貌取諸恭，吾心之莊敬，恭之謂也；容貌非此不重矣，貌曰恭焉。言取諸從，吾心之理順，從之謂也；辭氣非此不達矣，言曰從焉。目以司視也，貞觀不眩，有以善天下之色，是之謂視遠之明。耳以司聽也，至虛能應，有以善天下之聲，是之謂聽德之聰。以至思之所蘊，則極深研幾，足以通天下之故，足以類萬物之情，而恭從明

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔The exposition of virtue and its application is precise and incisive. It admirably brings out the deeper meaning of Jizi’s teaching and merits inclusion as a model.〕
Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: 〔Writing that elucidates principle, composed with care.〕
Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: 〔Refined and meticulous.〕

In treating the category of the Five Activities, the gentleman must make their virtues clear and extend his discussion to their applications. The virtues and applications of the Five Activities unite the inner and outer into one. When the gentleman elaborates upon them in words, can we not discern the way to make oneself sincere? The intent of Jizi’s admonition to King Wu was as if to say: The gentleman establishes the Supreme Standard as a rule, finding within himself all that is needed; through a subtle mastery of substance and function, he perfects himself, taking reverence as his foundation and possessing more than enough.

Can it be without purpose that human beings are endowed with the Five Activities? Wherever there is a thing, there must be a rule, and that rule is what brings the thing to goodness. Demeanor draws upon reverence: the solemn respect within our hearts is what is meant by reverence. Without this, our bearing lacks gravity; thus, of demeanor it is said, “reverent.” Speech draws upon accordance: the orderly harmony within our hearts is what is meant by accordance. Without this, our words and tone cannot convey their meaning; thus, of speech it is said, “accordant.” The eyes govern seeing. To observe steadfastly without being dazzled, thereby properly apprehending the visible forms of the world, is what is called the clarity of far-reaching vision. The ears govern hearing. To be utterly receptive and capable of responding, thereby properly apprehending the sounds of the world, is what is called the acuity that hears virtue. As for what thought contains, it penetrates the utmost depths and investigates the first subtle stirrings, sufficiently to comprehend the causes of affairs throughout the world and to distinguish by kind the true conditions of all things; and reverence, accordance, clarity…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
聰一以貫之矣夫有是事則有是德純乎其粹
者渾乎其各足固非有待於強勉而後得者也
所謂本然之德者如此然有德必有用而用所
以彰乎其德者也恭之形也則可畏可象自顯
而爲顯著之觀斯以作肅焉從之著也則有倫
有要自發而爲德音之秩斯以作乂焉出其明
焉知來藏往見天下之賾而不亂哲非明之作
耶運其聰焉圖成審會周天下之慮而不遺謀
非聰之作耶以至睿之所發則百慮渾融洞幽
===
明之故而契焉通晝夜之道而知焉而肅乂哲
謀合而一之矣夫有是德則有是用寂然不動
者感而遂通固非有事於脩飾而後成者也所
謂自然之用者如此夫德之與用非有二也敬
以立本而達之用焉則彝倫以叙而皇極有不
建者哉抑是道也達上下者也故五事脩休徵
應焉五事失咎徵應焉天人相與之際不可誣
已王者求端於天非敬曷以哉是故論堯之德
者必曰欽明而舜禹之相授受也亦惟致慎於
punctuated: 聰，一以貫之矣。夫有是事，則有是德，純乎其粹者，渾乎其各足，固非有待於強勉而後得者也。所謂本然之德者如此。然有德必有用，而用所以彰乎其德者也。恭之形也，則可畏可象，自顯而爲顯著之觀，斯以作肅焉。從之著也，則有倫有要，自發而爲德音之秩，斯以作乂焉。出其明焉，知來藏往，見天下之賾而不亂，哲非明之作耶？運其聰焉，圖成審會，周天下之慮而不遺，謀非聰之作耶？以至睿之所發，則百慮渾融，洞幽明之故而契焉，通晝夜之道而知焉，而肅乂哲謀合而一之矣。夫有是德，則有是用，寂然不動者，感而遂通，固非有事於脩飾而後成者也。所謂自然之用者如此。夫德之與用，非有二也。敬以立本而達之用焉，則彝倫以叙，而皇極有不建者哉？抑是道也，達上下者也，故五事脩，休徵應焉；五事失，咎徵應焉。天人相與之際，不可誣已。王者求端於天，非敬曷以哉？是故論堯之德者，必曰欽明，而舜禹之相授受也，亦惟致慎於
translation_en:
…and keenness of hearing: a single principle runs through them all. Wherever there are these activities, there are their corresponding virtues. Pure in their essence, they form an integral whole, each complete in itself; they certainly do not await strenuous effort before being attained. Such are what are called the virtues inherent in our original nature. Yet virtue necessarily has its functioning, and this functioning makes virtue manifest. When reverence takes visible form, it inspires awe and provides a model; it manifests itself as a conspicuous example, thereby producing gravity. When accord finds expression, it has order and essentials; it issues forth as an orderly expression of virtuous speech, thereby producing good order. When clarity of sight is brought forth, one knows what is to come and retains what has passed, perceiving the intricacies of the world without confusion. Is not discernment the effect of clarity of sight? When keenness of hearing is exercised, one plans for completion and carefully examines how things converge, encompassing the concerns of the world without omission. Is not deliberation the effect of keenness of hearing? As for the expression of penetrating thought, the hundred considerations blend into an integral whole. One penetrates the causes of the hidden and the manifest and accords with them; one comprehends the Way of day and night and knows it. Gravity, good order, discernment, and deliberation are thereby united as one.

Wherever there are these virtues, there is their corresponding functioning. What is still and unmoving responds to a stimulus and thereupon penetrates all things; it certainly does not require deliberate embellishment before becoming complete. Such is what is called natural functioning. Virtue and its functioning are not two separate things. If reverent attentiveness establishes the foundation and extends into functioning, the constant human relationships will be put in order. How, then, could the Sovereign’s Ultimate Standard fail to be established? Moreover, this Way extends through what is above and what is below. Thus, when the Five Activities are cultivated, auspicious portents respond; when the Five Activities go astray, adverse portents respond. The mutual interaction of Heaven and humanity cannot be denied. If a king seeks the source in Heaven, by what means other than reverent attentiveness could he do so? 考試官教授鄭批〔舂容不迫，可誦。〕
translation_en:
…the purport of being discerning and single-minded: all speak of reverent attentiveness. When the gentleman examines the teachings of Tang and Yu, he finds in them the entirety of the learning transmitted from mind to mind through a thousand sages.

Book of Odes

“Already drunk with wine, already filled with virtue. May our lord live ten thousand years; may great blessings attend you. Already drunk with wine, your dishes have all been presented. May our lord live ten thousand years; may radiant glory attend you.”

Yi Hongqi

Comment by Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor: “The topic itself is grand and dignified, but writers mostly repeat stale expressions, which is tiresome. Late in the process I came upon this composition: gentle, pure, and elegant, it leaves the reader refreshed. It merits recommendation. It should be” “recorded as a model for the many candidates.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zou, Instructor: “The writing flows and the reasoning is coherent. It does not concentrate exclusively on diction, yet those who do so cannot match it.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: “Its language and tone are harmonious and calm. The atmosphere of peace and prosperity in ‘Already Drunk’ can be vividly imagined.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Quietly elegant and unhurried, it makes the poet’s feelings of blessing and good wishes increasingly apparent. This is how the meaning of the Court Hymns should be expressed.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, School Instructor: “Reading this makes the poet’s gentle, lingering manner still more apparent.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Professor: “Ample and unhurried, it merits recitation.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
詩人兩叙君恩之厚而願其久於獲福也夫景
大昭明而久焉福之全也詩人承君恩之厚而
以是祝之其亦忠愛之不能自已者歟此父兄
所以答行葦也若曰敦典厚親人君之盛德而
感恩圖報臣子之至情今吾君之燕也洗爵之
奠隆於黃耇之養則既醉以酒矣且几筵之設
廣其愛也射樂之舉洽其情也又飽我以德焉
我之寵承於君如此將何以爲祝哉蓋運撫盈
成吾君之福固大矣然不但已也其必於萬斯
===
年介爾以景福焉天休之至延之爲有秩之祜
者俾單厚而未艾元吉之旋引之爲有道之長
者極多益而無窮以百祿則是遒也以萬福則
來同也蓋有與天地相爲久大者矣大斗之酌
加於旅醻之後則既醉以酒矣且醓醢之薦其
品豐也燔炙之陳其物備也又將我以殽焉我
之蒙惠於君如此將何以爲願哉蓋治隆熙洽
吾君之福固顯矣然非自今也其必於萬斯年
介爾以昭明焉重明麗正而所以爲顯比之吉
punctuated: 詩人兩叙君恩之厚，而願其久於獲福也。夫景大、昭明而久焉，福之全也。詩人承君恩之厚，而以是祝之，其亦忠愛之不能自已者歟？此父兄所以答行葦也。若曰：「敦典厚親，人君之盛德；而感恩圖報，臣子之至情。今吾君之燕也，洗爵之奠，隆於黃耇之養，則既醉以酒矣。且几筵之設，廣其愛也；射樂之舉，洽其情也，又飽我以德焉。我之寵承於君如此，將何以爲祝哉？蓋運撫盈成，吾君之福固大矣。然不但已也，其必於萬斯年，介爾以景福焉。天休之至，延之爲有秩之祜者，俾單厚而未艾；元吉之旋，引之爲有道之長者，極多益而無窮。以百祿，則是遒也；以萬福，則來同也。蓋有與天地相爲久大者矣。大斗之酌，加於旅醻之後，則既醉以酒矣。且醓醢之薦，其品豐也；燔炙之陳，其物備也，又將我以殽焉。我之蒙惠於君如此，將何以爲願哉？蓋治隆熙洽，吾君之福固顯矣。然非自今也，其必於萬斯年，介爾以昭明焉。重明麗正，而所以爲顯比之吉
translation_en:
The poet twice recounts the abundance of the ruler’s kindness and wishes that he may long continue to receive blessings. For blessings to be great, radiant, and enduring is their consummation. Having received such abundant kindness from his ruler, the poet offers him this benediction: is this not an expression of irrepressible loyalty and affection? This is how the elders respond to “The Reeds Along the Path” (Xing wei).

It is as though they were saying: “To uphold the established norms and show generous affection toward kin is the ruler’s great virtue; to feel gratitude for kindness and seek to repay it is the deepest feeling of a subject. At our ruler’s banquet today, the washing and setting out of the wine cups enhance the care bestowed upon the hoary elders: thus we are ‘already drunk with wine.’ Moreover, the provision of armrests and mats extends his love, while the archery and music give full expression to his affection: he has also ‘sated us with virtue.’ Having received such favor from our ruler, what blessing shall we offer him? Presiding over an age of fullness and accomplished order, our ruler assuredly enjoys great blessings. Yet they must not stop here: surely, ‘for ten thousand years,’ may we ‘aid you with great blessings.’ May Heaven’s favor, when it arrives, be prolonged into blessings bestowed in due measure, making them abundant and rich, without decline. May the coming of supreme good fortune be extended into the lasting ascendancy of one who possesses the Way, bringing increase upon increase without end. The hundred blessings shall gather here; the myriad blessings shall converge. Thus his blessings shall share the enduring greatness of Heaven and Earth.

“After the rounds of reciprocal toasts, wine is poured from the great ladle: thus we are ‘already drunk with wine.’ Moreover, the offerings of meat sauces are plentiful in variety, and the roasted and broiled meats are complete in their assortment: he also ‘sustains us with delicacies.’ Having received such kindness from our ruler, what wish shall we offer him? His government has attained flourishing harmony, and our ruler’s blessings are assuredly manifest. Yet these are not to date merely from the present [?]: surely, ‘for ten thousand years,’ may we ‘aid you with radiant brightness.’ With doubled brightness adhering to what is correct, that which brings about the good fortune of manifest union …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
者煥耿光於勿替緝熙純嘏而所以昭長發之
祥者普臨照於無疆以土宇則昄章也以人文
則宣朗也殆有與日月同其貞明者矣夫福不
徒大也而且明焉不徒大且明也而又久焉蓋
必如是而後吾人報德之情其少伸乎噫詩人
忠愛之意至矣抑聞孔子之論九經以親親爲
重蓋萬邦協和必始於九族之睦而四方風動
亦自五典之愼徽者基之是其敦本崇化固自
有在矣王者之道至周大備而展親之典尤惓
===
惓焉乃今觀行葦之慈惠既醉之祝頌誠意交
孚而雍穆氣象宛然可想昔人謂二詩見周家
之忠厚太平豈其然乎
商邑翼翼四方之極赫赫厥聲濯濯厥靈
壽考且寧以保我後生
黎澄
同考試官教諭韋　批〔中興之盛摸寫得□□〕
當時詩人之意是知
同考試官教諭鄒　批〔頌美功德夫人能之而詞〕
punctuated:
者，煥耿光於勿替；緝熙純嘏，而所以昭長發之祥者，普臨照於無疆。以土宇則昄章也，以人文則宣朗也，殆有與日月同其貞明者矣。夫福不徒大也，而且明焉；不徒大且明也，而又久焉。蓋必如是，而後吾人報德之情，其少伸乎！噫！詩人忠愛之意至矣。抑聞孔子之論九經，以親親爲重。蓋萬邦協和，必始於九族之睦；而四方風動，亦自五典之愼徽者基之。是其敦本崇化，固自有在矣。王者之道至周大備，而展親之典尤惓惓焉。乃今觀《行葦》之慈惠、《既醉》之祝頌，誠意交孚，而雍穆氣象宛然可想。昔人謂二詩見周家之忠厚太平，豈其然乎？
商邑翼翼，四方之極。赫赫厥聲，濯濯厥靈。壽考且寧，以保我後生。
黎澄
同考試官教諭韋，批〔中興之盛，摸寫得□□〕當時詩人之意，是知。
同考試官教諭鄒，批〔頌美功德，夫人能之，而詞〕
translation_en:
…makes that brilliant light shine without ceasing. Continuing in brightness and great blessing, that which manifests the auspicious promise of enduring prosperity casts its illumination everywhere without limit. In territorial extent, it is vast and splendid; in cultural achievement, radiant and clear. Indeed, it seems to share the constant brightness of the sun and moon. Such blessing is not merely great, but also bright; not merely great and bright, but also enduring. Surely only then can our wish to repay our ruler’s virtue find some small fulfillment! Ah, the poet’s loyalty and love are consummate indeed. Yet I have heard that, in discussing the nine guiding principles of government, Confucius placed particular weight upon affection for one’s kin. Harmony among the myriad states must begin with concord among the nine degrees of kinship; and the transforming influence that moves the four quarters likewise rests upon the careful cultivation of the five human relationships. There is thus a firm foundation for strengthening the roots and exalting moral transformation. The Way of kings reached its full development under the Zhou, whose institutions for showing affection to kin received especially devoted attention. Now, contemplating the benevolence of “The Reeds Grow Thick” (Xing wei) and the blessings and praise of “Already Drunk” (Ji zui), we see sincerity inspiring mutual trust, and can vividly imagine their atmosphere of harmony and reverence. Earlier writers said that these two poems reveal the Zhou house’s loyal generosity and great peace. Might this indeed be so?
The city of Shang is grand and orderly, the pole toward which the four quarters turn. Resplendent is its renown; illustrious is its spiritual power. May there be longevity and peace, to safeguard us who are born hereafter.
Li Cheng.
Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor, comments: 〔“The flourishing of the restoration is depicted with □□.”〕 The poet’s intention at that time is understood [?].
Associate Examiner Zou, Instructor, comments: 〔“Anyone can extol achievements and virtue, but the wording…”〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
能達意場中如此作者絕少
同考試官教諭揚　批〔頌義貴渾厚作者類多浮〕
冗子獨迥異宜錄以式
同考試官教諭張　批〔詞理精粹而燁然之光不〕
可遏善說詩者
考試官學正張　批〔詞不費而理自足〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔辭意渾詞與衆自別〕
詩人頌賢王中興之盛而因以裕諸後焉夫國
勢振而聲威隆商王之中興亦盛矣則其垂裕
===
於後也宜哉此商人祀高宗之樂也其意若曰
功之懋者其勢必昌積之厚者其澤必遠我高
宗之中興也斯其至矣乎但見商邑之蒞也刑
賞肅而紀法明有以飭王章於不紊敬畏崇而
萑綱一有以振百度於維貞宅中之地蓋翼然
其改觀矣由是惟皇建極而中外式焉約天下
而定之趨大觀在上而遐邇則焉合天下而協
其軌四方之渙不翕然其會極乎是以播之而
爲聲也風行而聲聞且赫赫乎德之廣運蓋洋溢
punctuated:
能達意，場中如此作者絕少。
同考試官教諭揚，批〔頌義貴渾厚，作者類多浮〕冗，子獨迥異，宜錄以式。
同考試官教諭張，批〔詞理精粹，而燁然之光不〕可遏，善說詩者。
考試官學正張，批〔詞不費而理自足〕。
考試官教授鄭，批〔辭意渾詞，與衆自別〕。
詩人頌賢王中興之盛，而因以裕諸後焉。夫國勢振而聲威隆，商王之中興亦盛矣，則其垂裕於後也宜哉！此商人祀高宗之樂也。其意若曰：功之懋者，其勢必昌；積之厚者，其澤必遠。我高宗之中興也，斯其至矣乎！但見商邑之蒞也，刑賞肅而紀法明，有以飭王章於不紊；敬畏崇而萑綱一，有以振百度於維貞。宅中之地，蓋翼然其改觀矣。由是惟皇建極而中外式焉，約天下而定之趨；大觀在上而遐邇則焉，合天下而協其軌。四方之渙，不翕然其會極乎？是以播之而爲聲也，風行而聲聞且赫赫乎！德之廣運，蓋洋溢
translation_en:
…can convey the meaning; writers like this are exceedingly rare among the examination candidates.

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “In expounding a hymn, substantial depth is prized. Most writers are superficial and prolix; you alone are markedly different. This should be recorded as a model.”

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The language and reasoning are refined and pure, and their brilliant radiance cannot be suppressed. Here is someone skilled at explaining the Poetry.”

Examiner Zhang, School Director, comments: “The wording is economical, yet the reasoning is complete in itself.”

Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: “The wording and meaning are rounded and substantial [?], naturally distinguishing this from the rest.”

The poet praises the flourishing restoration under a worthy king and thereby provides for later generations. When the strength of the state was revived and its prestige grew, the restoration under the Shang king was indeed magnificent. How fitting, then, that he should leave a rich legacy to posterity! This is the music performed by the people of Shang in sacrificing to Gaozong. Its meaning is as follows: where achievements are great, power must flourish; where accumulated merit is substantial, its benefits must reach far. Surely our Gaozong’s restoration attained the utmost in this!

Consider his governance of the capital of Shang: punishments and rewards were administered with rigor, and rules and laws were clear, so that royal institutions were kept orderly and free of confusion. Reverence and awe were exalted, and the governing framework was unified [?], so that all institutions were reinvigorated and maintained in rectitude. The centrally situated capital thus assumed a new appearance of stately order. Accordingly, the sovereign established the supreme standard, and those within and beyond the realm took it as their model, drawing all under Heaven together and fixing their common direction. A grand example stood above, and those far and near followed it, uniting all under Heaven and bringing their courses into accord. Did not the scattered peoples of the four quarters converge harmoniously upon that supreme standard?

Thus, when this influence spread and became renown, it traveled like the wind, and his reputation was resplendent indeed! The far-reaching operation of his virtue overflowed…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
乎中國而施及蠻貊矣何赫赫乎著之而爲靈
也德威而人心惟畏神功之丕振蓋自光天之
下以及于海隅矣何濯濯乎然此豈一時之盛
已哉天壽平格旣膺夫難老之休福履孔綏且
介以和平之慶夫惟其壽也則道久化成而所
以垂裕後昆者自申錫於無疆凡其御都邑以
屬人心也萬世其永賴矣惟其壽而寧也則身
安德滋而所以佑啓後人者咸正大而無缺凡
其繼聲威以震天下也萬年如一日矣不有以
保我後生乎是則由其中興之盛也而業光於
===
前由其垂裕之遠也而澤及於後此高宗所以
爲賢而崇以百世不遷之廟不亦宜哉抑高宗
之功固大矣然豈無所自哉天命降鑒下民有
嚴敬天之心也不僭不濫不敢怠遑事天之政
也是故平荆楚以服諸侯莫非天命有在而中
興之本誠在是矣雖然聖敬日躋上帝是祗而
九圍之式昭受帝命成湯之所以造商也若高
宗者其亦率乃祖攸行而無忝者歟
punctuated: 乎中國而施及蠻貊矣，何赫赫乎！著之而爲靈也，德威而人心惟畏，神功之丕振，蓋自光天之下以及于海隅矣，何濯濯乎！然此豈一時之盛已哉？天壽平格，旣膺夫難老之休；福履孔綏，且介以和平之慶。夫惟其壽也，則道久化成，而所以垂裕後昆者，自申錫於無疆。凡其御都邑以屬人心也，萬世其永賴矣。惟其壽而寧也，則身安德滋，而所以佑啓後人者，咸正大而無缺。凡其繼聲威以震天下也，萬年如一日矣。不有以保我後生乎？是則由其中興之盛也，而業光於前；由其垂裕之遠也，而澤及於後。此高宗所以爲賢，而崇以百世不遷之廟，不亦宜哉？抑高宗之功固大矣，然豈無所自哉？天命降鑒，下民有嚴，敬天之心也；不僭不濫，不敢怠遑，事天之政也。是故平荆楚以服諸侯，莫非天命有在，而中興之本誠在是矣。雖然，聖敬日躋，上帝是祗，而九圍之式；昭受帝命，成湯之所以造商也。若高宗者，其亦率乃祖攸行而無忝者歟？
translation_en:
…throughout the Central States and extended to the Man and Mo peoples. How resplendent! Manifested as numinous power, his virtue inspired awe, and people’s hearts were filled with reverence. The great unfolding of his wondrous achievements reached everywhere beneath the radiant heavens, even to the corners of the seas. How illustrious! Yet could this have been the flourishing of merely a single age? Heaven bestowed longevity, and harmony prevailed: he had already received the blessing of enduring old age. His blessings were abundantly secure, further enhanced by the felicity of peace and harmony. Because he enjoyed longevity, his Way endured and his transforming influence became established; the ample legacy he bequeathed to his descendants was thus bestowed repeatedly without limit. His governance of the capital and other cities, binding people’s hearts to him, would remain a source of support for ten thousand generations. Because his longevity was accompanied by tranquillity, his person was at ease and his virtue grew; all that he did to protect and guide his successors was upright, great, and without defect. His continuing renown and authority, which awed all under Heaven, would endure for ten thousand years as for a single day. Did this not provide protection for us, the generations born afterward?

Thus, through the flourishing of his restoration, his achievements shed glory upon those before him; through the far-reaching legacy he bequeathed, his beneficence extended to those after him. This is why Gaozong was deemed worthy. Was it not fitting that he should be honored with an ancestral temple whose tablet would remain unmoved for a hundred generations? Yet, great as Gaozong’s achievements certainly were, could they have been without a source? Heaven’s mandate descended with its scrutiny, and the people below held him in awe: this expressed his heart’s reverence for Heaven. Neither erring in rewards nor being excessive in punishments, and never daring to lapse into idleness or ease: this was his government in service to Heaven. Thus, his pacification of Jing and Chu to bring the regional lords into submission was in every respect an expression of Heaven’s mandate resting upon him. Here indeed lay the foundation of his restoration.

Nevertheless, it was through daily advancing in sagely reverence, honoring the Lord on High, and becoming a model for the nine regions that Cheng Tang illustriously received the Lord’s mandate and founded Shang. Was not Gaozong likewise one who followed the conduct of his ancestor without bringing him dishonor?

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄

===

春秋屢紀諸侯之邦交而深寓乎公天下之心
焉夫天下爲公無所事於盟矣聖人深致意於
諸侯之盟會豈得已哉昔者大道之行也諸侯
以信相與未有所謂盟也逮德下衰于是司盟
始設於秩官而爲諸侯之常事矣聖人思有以
維之也是故于瓦屋之參盟謹焉于齊衛之胥
命善焉于蕭魚之會美焉蓋前此皆特盟也三
punctuated:
春秋

秋七月庚午，宋公、齊侯、衛侯盟于瓦屋。〔隱公八年〕

考試官學正張批：〔發明惡盟貴信義殆盡〕
考試官教授鄭批：〔老成精當宜冠本房〕

春秋屢紀諸侯之邦交，而深寓乎公天下之心焉。夫天下爲公，無所事於盟矣。聖人深致意於諸侯之盟會，豈得已哉？昔者大道之行也，諸侯以信相與，未有所謂盟也。逮德下衰，于是司盟始設於秩官，而爲諸侯之常事矣。聖人思有以維之也，是故于瓦屋之參盟謹焉，于齊衛之胥命善焉，于蕭魚之會美焉。蓋前此皆特盟也，三
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

“In autumn, in the seventh month, on the gengwu day, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Qi, and the Marquis of Wei covenanted at Wawu.” 〔Eighth year of Duke Yin〕
“In summer, the Marquis of Qi and the Marquis of Wei mutually pledged their word at Pu.” 〔Third year of Duke Huan〕
“The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Xiaozhu in attacking Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu.” 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xiang〕

Liu Xian

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: 〔“His exposition makes the sage’s concern for a world shared by all seem visible before one’s eyes.”〕 Accept this essay.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, School Instructor: 〔“He elucidates almost exhaustively the aversion to covenants and the esteem for trustworthiness and righteousness.”〕
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Professor: 〔“Mature, precise, and apt; it deserves first place in this examining section.”〕

The Spring and Autumn Annals repeatedly records diplomatic dealings among the feudal lords, profoundly embodying a concern for a world shared by all. When the world is shared by all, there is no need for covenants. Could the sage’s close attention to the lords’ covenants and assemblies have been anything but a necessity? Formerly, when the Great Way prevailed, the lords dealt with one another in good faith; there was as yet no such thing as a covenant. When virtue subsequently declined, the office of Supervisor of Covenants was first established among the regular officials, and covenant-making became a routine affair among the lords. The sage sought a means of holding them together. Thus he treated the three-party covenant at Wawu with caution, approved the mutual pledging of words between Qi and Wei, and praised the assembly at Xiaoyu. Before this, all covenants had been between two parties; three…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
國爲盟自瓦屋始是烏可以不謹也約劑煩而
疑日以厚忠信泯而亂日以滋末流傾危之弊
罔將無所不至矣噫有虞氏有未施之信焉夏
后氏有未施之敬焉其諸春秋謹參盟之意歟
古者不盟結言而退也齊衛相命寔爲近之是
烏可以不善也去載書而不尚乎詛詈牲歃
而從事於眞誠太上淳龎之風蓋庶幾其有望
矣噫以信易食聖人所以荅子貢焉以信易生
君子所以甚桓王焉其諸春秋善胥命之意歟
===
至若盟不足恃鄭不可信也悼公乃能推誠以
懷之是烏可以不美也觀其納斥禁侵而兵車
之力不遑禮因歸國而彼此之心不虞鄭自玆
不肯南向而朝者二十四年焉楚由是不敢北
向而窺者歷有三世焉至誠感人之驗不亦章
章明甚矣乎經故書蕭魚之會以美之也此義
行則大道可復民心可歸今之天下即古之天
下矣此聖人之本志也柰之何古道之不可復
也故參盟未已也有諸侯齊盟者矣齊盟未已
punctuated:
國爲盟，自瓦屋始，是烏可以不謹也？約劑煩而疑日以厚，忠信泯而亂日以滋，末流傾危之弊，罔將無所不至矣。噫！有虞氏有未施之信焉，夏后氏有未施之敬焉，其諸《春秋》謹參盟之意歟？古者不盟，結言而退也。齊衛相命，寔爲近之，是烏可以不善也？去載書而不尚乎詛詈牲歃，而從事於眞誠，太上淳龎之風，蓋庶幾其有望矣。噫！以信易食，聖人所以荅子貢焉；以信易生，君子所以甚桓王焉。其諸《春秋》善胥命之意歟？
至若盟不足恃，鄭不可信也，悼公乃能推誠以懷之，是烏可以不美也？觀其納斥禁侵，而兵車之力不遑，禮因歸國，而彼此之心不虞。鄭自玆不肯南向而朝者二十四年焉，楚由是不敢北向而窺者歷有三世焉。至誠感人之驗，不亦章章明甚矣乎？經故書蕭魚之會以美之也。此義行，則大道可復，民心可歸，今之天下即古之天下矣。此聖人之本志也。柰之何古道之不可復也！故參盟未已也，有諸侯齊盟者矣；齊盟未已
translation_en:
…a covenant among three states began at Wawu: how could this fail to call for caution? As covenant documents multiplied, suspicion grew daily; as loyalty and trustworthiness faded, disorder increased daily. In their eventual course, the resulting instability and peril would seemingly stop at nothing [?]. Alas! The house of Yu possessed trustworthiness before putting it into practice, and the rulers of Xia possessed reverence before putting it into practice. Might this be the meaning behind the Spring and Autumn Annals’ caution concerning the three-state covenant? In antiquity, men did not swear covenants: they gave their word and withdrew. The exchange of pledges between Qi and Wei indeed approached this practice. How could it fail to merit approval? Dispensing with written covenants and setting no store by curses, sacrificial animals, and the tasting of blood [?], they devoted themselves to genuine sincerity. There was thus some hope of recovering the simple, generous ways of highest antiquity. Alas! To forgo food for trustworthiness was the teaching the Sage gave Zigong; to forgo life for trustworthiness was the principle by which the exemplary man severely censured King Huan. Might this be the meaning behind the Spring and Autumn Annals’ approval of the exchange of pledges?
As for a situation in which covenants could not be relied upon and Zheng could not be trusted, Duke Dao nevertheless extended his sincerity to win Zheng over. How could this fail to merit praise? Consider how he withdrew the scouts [?] and forbade incursions, so that the force of war chariots had no occasion for use [?]; he treated the prisoners courteously and returned them to their state [?], so that neither side harbored apprehensions about the other. From that time Zheng refused to face south and pay court for twenty-four years, while Chu consequently dared not turn north and seek an opening for three successive reigns. Is this not conspicuously clear proof that utmost sincerity moves others? The Classic therefore records the meeting at Xiaoyu to praise it. If this principle were put into practice, the Great Way could be restored and the people’s hearts won back: the world of today would become the world of antiquity. This was the Sage’s original intention. Yet why could the ancient Way not be restored? Thus, before three-state covenants had ceased, there were collective covenants among the regional lords; before collective covenants had ceased…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
也又有霸者摟諸侯而主盟者矣其流至於口
血未乾而渝盟交質子而不信者矣然則聖人
之志何由而遂乎故其言曰大道之行也與三
代之英丘未之逮也而有志焉此歸與之嘆發
於在陳四代禮樂不得已而一授之回也然則
春秋之作獨非此意乎蓋至是而後見夫子之
心
甲午晦晉侯及楚子鄭伯戰于鄢陵楚子
鄭師敗績公會尹子晉侯齊國佐邾人
===
伐鄭〔俱成公十有六年〕夏公會尹子單
子晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯曹伯邾人伐鄭
冬公會單子晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊人
邾人伐鄭〔俱成公十有七年〕夏公會齊
侯于夾谷公至自夾谷齊人來歸鄆讙
龜陰田〔俱定公十年〕叔孫州仇帥師墮
郈季孫斯仲孫何忌帥師墮費〔俱定公〕
十有二年
李𢮿
punctuated:
也，又有霸者摟諸侯而主盟者矣。其流至於口血未乾而渝盟，交質子而不信者矣。然則聖人之志何由而遂乎？故其言曰：「大道之行也，與三代之英，丘未之逮也，而有志焉。」此歸與之嘆發於在陳，四代禮樂不得已而一授之回也。然則春秋之作，獨非此意乎？蓋至是而後見夫子之心。
甲午，晦，晉侯及楚子、鄭伯戰于鄢陵，楚子、鄭師敗績。公會尹子、晉侯、齊國佐、邾人伐鄭。〔俱成公十有六年〕夏，公會尹子、單子、晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、邾人伐鄭。冬，公會單子、晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊人、邾人伐鄭。〔俱成公十有七年〕夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。〔俱定公十年〕叔孫州仇帥師墮郈。季孫斯、仲孫何忌帥師墮費。〔俱定公〕十有二年。
李𢮿
translation_en:
…and then there were hegemons who drew the feudal lords into their grasp and presided over covenants. This tendency went so far that covenants were broken before the blood of the oath had dried on their lips, and even the exchange of sons as hostages failed to secure good faith. How, then, could the sage’s aspiration be fulfilled? Thus he said: “The practice of the Great Way and the outstanding men of the Three Dynasties—I, Qiu, did not live to encounter them, yet I aspire to them.” Hence his sigh, “Let us return!” arose while he was in Chen; having no alternative, he entrusted the rites and music of the Four Dynasties in their entirety to Hui. Was the composition of the Spring and Autumn Annals not likewise motivated by this intention? Only at this point do we perceive the Master’s heart.
On the jiawu day, the last day of the lunar month, the Marquis of Jin fought the Viscount of Chu and the Earl of Zheng at Yanling. The Viscount of Chu and the army of Zheng suffered a crushing defeat. The Duke joined the Viscount of Yin, the Marquis of Jin, Guo Zuo of Qi, and men of Zhu in attacking Zheng. 〔Both entries are from the sixteenth year of Duke Cheng.〕 In summer, the Duke joined the Viscount of Yin, the Viscount of Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, and men of Zhu in attacking Zheng. In winter, the Duke joined the Viscount of Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, and men of Qi and Zhu in attacking Zheng. 〔Both entries are from the seventeenth year of Duke Cheng.〕 In summer, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The Duke returned from Jiagu. Men of Qi came to restore the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. 〔All these entries are from the tenth year of Duke Ding.〕 Shusun Zhouchou led troops to demolish the fortifications of Hou. Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led troops to demolish the fortifications of Fei. 〔Both entries are from Duke Ding’s reign〕, the twelfth year.
Li 𢮿 [given name uncertain].

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭招　批〔分別霸功王化處甚有分曉不凡之士也〕
考試官學正張　批〔春秋義是如此〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔高古迥異他作〕
春秋紀晉魯之事見服人者不以幸而以理也
蓋天下莫大於理而幸勝者不足言矣觀於厲
公孔子之事不亦可見也哉在昔晉厲襲累霸
之餘以逞其鴛鄭之志鄢陵一戰楚君傷而師
敗焉宜霸業爲益振矣然未幾而楚氛愈熾晉
===
勢益微區區目前之勝曾無補於後日之失者
何哉君子曰此幸非恃勝之說也蓋方楚共強
而鄭成貳正敵國外患時也使厲公能釋鄭求
其內寧舒楚以爲外懼則鄭之歸也有日矣乃
令用卻至六間之謀徼呂錡一矢之捷所恃以
成其功者幸焉而已國以幸勝是故其心驕焉
其政怠焉師有三伐之勤而不能回南向之轅
朝有三卿之去而竟行乎欒氏之譖力疲於奔
命釁起於不虞茲非自貽之戚歟春秋書之以
punctuated:
同考試官教諭招批〔分別霸功王化處甚有分曉，不凡之士也。〕
考試官學正張批〔春秋義是如此。〕
考試官教授鄭批〔高古迥異他作。〕
《春秋》紀晉魯之事，見服人者不以幸而以理也。蓋天下莫大於理，而幸勝者不足言矣。觀於厲公孔子之事，不亦可見也哉？在昔晉厲襲累霸之餘，以逞其鴛鄭之志。鄢陵一戰，楚君傷而師敗焉，宜霸業爲益振矣。然未幾而楚氛愈熾，晉勢益微。區區目前之勝，曾無補於後日之失者，何哉？君子曰：「此幸非恃勝之說也。」蓋方楚共強而鄭成貳，正敵國外患時也。使厲公能釋鄭，求其內寧，舒楚以爲外懼，則鄭之歸也有日矣。乃令用卻至六間之謀，徼呂錡一矢之捷，所恃以成其功者，幸焉而已。國以幸勝，是故其心驕焉，其政怠焉。師有三伐之勤，而不能回南向之轅；朝有三卿之去，而竟行乎欒氏之譖。力疲於奔命，釁起於不虞，茲非自貽之戚歟？《春秋》書之以
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: 〔The distinction between hegemonic achievement and transformation through kingly rule is drawn with great clarity. This is no ordinary scholar.〕
Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: 〔This is indeed the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals.〕
Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: 〔Elevated and antique in style, markedly different from other compositions.〕
The Spring and Autumn Annals records the affairs of Jin and Lu to show that bringing others into submission depends on principle, not luck. Nothing under Heaven is greater than principle; victory gained by luck scarcely merits discussion. Is this not evident from the affairs of Duke Li and Confucius?
In former times, Duke Li of Jin inherited the legacy of successive hegemons and sought to gratify his ambition to subdue Zheng [?]. In a single battle at Yanling, the ruler of Chu was wounded and his army defeated. It seemed that Jin’s hegemony should thereby have grown stronger. Yet before long Chu’s threatening power grew ever greater, while Jin’s position steadily weakened. Why did this paltry, immediate victory do nothing to offset the losses that followed? The gentleman says: “This was luck, no grounds for relying on victory [?].”
At that time Duke Gong of Chu was powerful, while Duke Cheng of Zheng wavered in his allegiance: this was precisely a time of rival states and external threats. Had Duke Li been able to leave Zheng alone and seek peace within his own state, easing pressure on Chu so that it remained an external deterrent, the day would have come when Zheng returned to allegiance. Instead, he employed Xi Zhi’s [?] plan exploiting six weaknesses and sought victory through a single arrow from Lü Qi. What he relied on to achieve success was luck alone. Because his state won through luck, his mind became arrogant and his government negligent. His army endured the toil of three campaigns, yet could not turn back Zheng’s chariot shafts from their southward course. At court, three high ministers were removed, yet the slanders of the Luan clan ultimately prevailed. His strength was exhausted in responding to emergencies, and disaster arose unexpectedly. Was this not sorrow he had brought upon himself? The Spring and Autumn Annals records this in order to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
爲幸勝者戒也至若魯定秉積弱之後以當強
齊之衝夾谷一會萊兵加而偪好焉在魯勢斯
亦危矣然未幾而侵疆盡歸名都繼墮區區式
微之魯非復前日之比者何哉君子曰此以理
服人之徵也蓋方齊景横而三家悖正外陵内
叛時也使孔子而威刼於裔夷謀沮於私黨則
魯之削也滋甚矣乃今明兩君合好之禮申百
雉都城之禁所恃以相其君者理焉而已爲國
以理是故言出而順事爲而成行乎諸侯則謝
===
過不暇而何敢逞其強行乎大夫則改步惟謹
而何敢仍其僭威重於三軍化成於俄頃兹非
自強之驗歟春秋書之以爲循理者勸也故觀
於晉事可見霸功之淺觀於魯事可見聖化之
大王霸之相遠固如是也范文子嘗曰惟聖人
能内外無患斯言蓋有見哉厲惟不用以及於
此也悼公起而三駕焉蕭魚之會其重光矣魯
定昏而桓子庸焉女樂之受孔子之行不脱冕
矣用之弗終爾也不然魯其東周乎豈止齊人
punctuated: 爲幸勝者戒也。至若魯定秉積弱之後，以當強齊之衝，夾谷一會，萊兵加而偪好焉，在魯勢斯亦危矣。然未幾而侵疆盡歸，名都繼墮，區區式微之魯，非復前日之比者，何哉？君子曰：「此以理服人之徵也。」蓋方齊景横而三家悖，正外陵内叛時也。使孔子而威刼於裔夷，謀沮於私黨，則魯之削也滋甚矣。乃今明兩君合好之禮，申百雉都城之禁，所恃以相其君者，理焉而已。爲國以理，是故言出而順，事爲而成。行乎諸侯，則謝過不暇，而何敢逞其強？行乎大夫，則改步惟謹，而何敢仍其僭？威重於三軍，化成於俄頃，兹非自強之驗歟？春秋書之，以爲循理者勸也。故觀於晉事，可見霸功之淺；觀於魯事，可見聖化之大。王霸之相遠，固如是也。范文子嘗曰：「惟聖人能内外無患。」斯言蓋有見哉！厲惟不用，以及於此也。悼公起而三駕焉，蕭魚之會，其重光矣。魯定昏而桓子庸焉，女樂之受，孔子之行，不脱冕矣，用之弗終爾也。不然，魯其東周乎？豈止齊人
translation_en: …to serve as a warning to those who gain victory by good fortune. As for Duke Ding of Lu, he inherited a state long weakened and faced the onslaught of powerful Qi. At the meeting at Jiagu, troops from Lai advanced and used coercion in the proceedings of friendship [?]; Lu’s position was indeed perilous. Yet before long, all its encroached-upon territory was returned, and the walls of its major fortified towns were subsequently demolished. Why was this small, declining state of Lu no longer what it had been? The gentleman says: “This is evidence of winning others’ submission through principle.” At that time, Duke Jing of Qi was overbearing and the three great families were defiant: it was precisely a time of aggression from without and rebellion within. Had Confucius been intimidated by the outlying barbarians, and had his plans been thwarted by private factions, Lu would have suffered still greater losses. Instead, he clarified the rites governing friendship between the two rulers and reaffirmed the prohibition against city walls exceeding one hundred zhi in extent. What he relied upon in assisting his ruler was principle alone. When a state is governed through principle, words are accepted when spoken, and undertakings succeed when put into practice. Applied among the feudal lords, it leaves them scarcely time enough to apologize for their faults: how would they dare flaunt their strength? Applied among the grandees, it makes them scrupulously reform their conduct: how would they dare persist in their usurpations? Such authority outweighs the Three Armies, and its transforming influence takes effect in an instant. Is this not proof of strengthening oneself? The Spring and Autumn Annals records these events to encourage those who follow principle. Thus, in the affairs of Jin we can see the shallowness of hegemonic achievement; in the affairs of Lu we can see the greatness of sagely transformation. Such indeed is the distance between true kingship and hegemony. Fan Wenzi once said: “Only a sage can be free of troubles both within and without.” How perceptive these words were! Duke Li failed to put this into practice, and so came to such a pass. Duke Dao arose and mounted three campaigns; at the meeting at Xiaoyu, Jin’s glory shone anew. But Duke Ding of Lu was benighted, and Huanzi was mediocre. When the female musicians were accepted, Confucius departed without even removing his ceremonial cap. It was simply that they failed to employ him to the end. Otherwise, might Lu not have become an Eastern Zhou? Would it merely have been that the people of Qi…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
傾心三家革面已也是知王道有神用而無近
功
禮記
詩言其志也歌咏其聲也舞動其容也三
者本於心然後樂器從之
李褰
同考試官教諭詹　批〔樂以彰德說者多未〕
明此作精切得旨錄以示式
考試官學正張　批〔得論樂旨〕
===
考試官教授鄭　批〔簡當可誦〕
記者論樂必原夫德之發而及樂之成也夫德
蘊於心樂乃德之華也則樂由德之發而後成
也不其然乎樂記之旨如此且樂之作不能離
乎器而樂之本則有在於德也樂以彰德何如
蓋人生而靜性本寂然未有所謂詩也及性感
爲情必形諸言而詩以著凡以宣暢其湮鬱者
一天機之不可遏也詩未有成聲固泯然未有
所謂歌也及志動爲詩乃永言之而歌以彰凡
punctuated:
傾心、三家革面已也？是知王道有神用，而無近功。

《禮記》
「詩言其志也，歌咏其聲也，舞動其容也。三者本於心，然後樂器從之。」
李褰

記者論樂，必原夫德之發而及樂之成也。夫德蘊於心，樂乃德之華也，則樂由德之發而後成也，不其然乎？《樂記》之旨如此。且樂之作不能離乎器，而樂之本則有在於德也。樂以彰德，何如？蓋人生而靜，性本寂然，未有所謂詩也。及性感爲情，必形諸言，而詩以著。凡以宣暢其湮鬱者，一天機之不可遏也。詩未有成聲，固泯然未有所謂歌也。及志動爲詩，乃永言之，而歌以彰。凡
translation_en:
… turning their hearts toward him and the Three Families changing their outward conduct? From this we know that the Kingly Way has a wondrous efficacy, rather than merely short-term achievements.

Record of Rites (Liji)
“Poetry expresses one's intent; singing gives melodic expression to one's voice; dancing sets one's bodily bearing in motion. These three are rooted in the heart; only afterward do musical instruments follow.”
By Li Qian 李褰.

Associate Examiner Zhan, Instructor, comments: “Music makes virtue manifest; most interpreters have failed to understand this. This composition is precise and penetrating and captures the meaning. It is included to serve as a model.”
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Captures the essential meaning of the discussion of music.”
Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: “Concise and apt; worthy of recitation.”

In discussing music, the author of the Record necessarily traces it to the expression of virtue before proceeding to music's completion. Virtue is stored within the heart, and music is virtue's flowering. Thus music takes shape only after virtue finds expression—is this not so? Such is the meaning of the Record of Music (Yueji). Moreover, the performance of music cannot dispense with instruments, yet music's foundation lies in virtue. How does music make virtue manifest?

Human beings are tranquil at birth; their nature is originally still, and there is as yet nothing called poetry. When that nature is stirred and becomes feeling, it must take form in words, and poetry thereby emerges. All that releases and gives free expression to what has been pent up is simply the irrepressible working of Heaven's impulse. Before poetry takes shape as musical sound, there is still no distinct manifestation of what is called singing. When intent is stirred and becomes poetry, its words are prolonged, and singing thereby emerges. All that …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
以舒揚其意趣者一天眞之不容已也由是樂
意油然施之四體手以舞之不知其所以舞足
以蹈之不知其所以蹈亦欣喜之情所由以敷
達矣夫德發於外雖有三者之殊推厥所原則
由一心而出蓋性具於心德本於性惟此心因
物而有感則此志遂形而爲詩而歌也舞也皆
從此作矣和順之英華性情之流衍也夫然後
越之金石絲竹以諧其聲則倡和清濁迭相爲
經有平中而無淫濫也所以流通精神而奮至
===
德之光者此矣音律抑何盛耶從以干戚羽旄
以治其飾則俯仰疾舒要其節奏有正齊而無
陵犯也所以動盪血脉而導至和之藴者此矣
物采抑何華耶是則德本於心以成乎樂此樂
以彰德而爲德之華也樂其可以僞爲乎哉大
抵樂有本文非二物也惟情深文明本末具舉
而後可以言樂此舜之韶所以盡善盡美孔子
聞之忘味也然五帝殊時不相沿樂何哉蓋樂
以彰德亦以象功聖人與時偕行而已故惟聖
punctuated: 以舒揚其意趣者，一天眞之不容已也。由是樂意油然，施之四體，手以舞之，不知其所以舞；足以蹈之，不知其所以蹈，亦欣喜之情所由以敷達矣。夫德發於外，雖有三者之殊，推厥所原，則由一心而出。蓋性具於心，德本於性，惟此心因物而有感，則此志遂形而爲詩，而歌也、舞也，皆從此作矣。和順之英華，性情之流衍也。夫然後越之金石絲竹，以諧其聲，則倡和清濁，迭相爲經，有平中而無淫濫也。所以流通精神而奮至德之光者，此矣。音律抑何盛耶！從以干戚羽旄，以治其飾，則俯仰疾舒，要其節奏，有正齊而無陵犯也。所以動盪血脉而導至和之藴者，此矣。物采抑何華耶！是則德本於心，以成乎樂；此樂以彰德，而爲德之華也。樂其可以僞爲乎哉？大抵樂有本文，非二物也。惟情深文明，本末具舉，而後可以言樂。此舜之韶所以盡善盡美，孔子聞之忘味也。然五帝殊時，不相沿樂，何哉？蓋樂以彰德，亦以象功，聖人與時偕行而已。故惟聖
translation_en:
…that gives free expression to its meaning and feeling is entirely the irrepressible working of innate genuineness. Thus the impulse toward music wells up spontaneously and extends to the four limbs: the hands dance without knowing why they dance; the feet stamp without knowing why they stamp. Through these movements, too, feelings of joy find full expression. Although virtue manifests itself outwardly in these three distinct forms, tracing them to their source shows that they all issue from a single heart. Human nature resides in the heart, and virtue is rooted in human nature. When the heart is stirred by things, its intent takes form as poetry, and singing and dancing alike arise from this. These are the splendid flowering of harmony and compliance, the outpouring of human nature and feeling.

Only then is this expressed through metal and stone, strings and bamboo, to harmonize its sounds. Leading and responding voices, clear and deep tones, alternate to form an ordered pattern, balanced and measured, without excess or license. This is what allows the vital spirit to circulate and brings forth the radiance of consummate virtue. How magnificent are its tones and pitches! Shields and axes, feathers and yak-tail standards follow, giving order to its adornment. Bending and straightening, swift and leisurely movements all conform to the rhythm, properly aligned and without encroaching upon one another. This is what stirs the blood and vessels and draws forth the inner richness of consummate harmony. How splendid are its material ornaments!

Thus virtue, rooted in the heart, finds fulfillment in music; music manifests virtue and becomes its flowering. How could music be produced through pretense? In general, music has both a foundation and an outward pattern, but these are not two separate things. Only when feeling is deep and its outward pattern radiant, with root and branches alike fully realized, can one speak of music. This is why Shun’s Shao music was perfectly good and perfectly beautiful, and why Confucius, upon hearing it, forgot the taste of food. Yet the Five Emperors lived in different ages and did not inherit one another’s music. Why was this? Music manifests virtue, but it also represents achievement: sages simply move in step with their times. Therefore, only sages…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
者之能作也彼不聞性與天道者不足與論樂
矣
福者備也備者百順之名也無所不順者
之謂備言內盡於己而外順於道也忠
臣以事其君孝子以事其親其本一也
上則順於鬼神外則順於君長內則以
孝於親如此之謂備
羅良
同考試官教諭詹　批〔體信達順之旨發明透徹而詞亦精當非有志忠孝者乎錄之〕
考試官學正張　批〔講忠孝之理甚切可錄〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔理精而明詞約而盡〕
===
記者推福之義在於備必著其所以備也夫盡
己而順道則德無不備矣賢者之祭其受福固
如此哉祭統之意若謂賢者盡祭之義固存乎
福而所謂福者何哉蓋福之爲言備之謂也備
豈強致哉亦曰百順而已矣然所謂百順者亦
惟以吾心之理妙時措之宜而施無不順焉斯
punctuated:
者之能作也，彼不聞性與天道者，不足與論樂矣。
福者，備也；備者，百順之名也。無所不順者之謂備，言內盡於己而外順於道也。忠臣以事其君，孝子以事其親，其本一也。上則順於鬼神，外則順於君長，內則以孝於親，如此之謂備。
羅良
同考試官教諭詹　批〔體信達順之旨，發明透徹，而詞亦精當，非有志忠孝者乎？錄之。〕
考試官學正張　批〔講忠孝之理甚切，可錄。〕
