記者推福之義在於備，必著其所以備也。夫盡己而順道，則德無不備矣。賢者之祭，其受福固如此哉！祭統之意若謂：賢者盡祭之義，固存乎福，而所謂福者何哉？蓋福之爲言，備之謂也。備豈強致哉？亦曰百順而已矣。然所謂百順者，亦惟以吾心之理，妙時措之宜，而施無不順焉，斯
translation_en:
…can create it. Those who have not heard the teachings concerning human nature and the Way of Heaven are unqualified to discuss music.

“Blessing means completeness. Completeness is the name for conformity in all things. To conform in every respect is what is called completeness: this means fully realizing what lies within oneself and outwardly conforming to the Way. A loyal minister thereby serves his ruler, and a filial son thereby serves his parents; their foundation is one. Above, one conforms to the spirits; outside the household, one conforms to rulers and superiors; within it, one acts filially toward one’s parents. This is what is called completeness.”

Luo Liang

Associate Examiner Zhan, Instructor, comments: 〔The purport of embodying sincerity and achieving conformity is explained thoroughly, and the wording is also precise and apt. Is this not someone devoted to loyalty and filial piety? Accept it.〕

Examiner Zhang, School Director, comments: 〔The principles of loyalty and filial piety are discussed with great pertinence. It merits acceptance.〕

Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: 〔The reasoning is refined and clear; the wording concise yet comprehensive.〕

The author of the Record traces the meaning of blessing to completeness and necessarily makes clear how that completeness is attained. If one fully realizes what lies within oneself and conforms to the Way, one’s virtue will be complete in every respect. Surely this is how the worthy receive blessings through their sacrifices! The meaning of “The System of Sacrifices” (Jitong) seems to be this: when the worthy fully realize the meaning of sacrifice, blessing assuredly lies therein. But what is meant by blessing? The word “blessing” means completeness. Can completeness be forcibly attained? It is simply conformity in all things. Yet this conformity in all things consists solely in using the principles within one’s own heart to attain a subtle mastery of what is fitting in each timely action, so that every application accords with them. title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
謂之備矣何以言之蓋道見於事而行之在
我使已有弗盡則違於道而難以言順矣必反
身以存誠眞實之懿率之以躬行湛一不虧無
一毫之僞妄也如是則虛中以體物推已之心
循之以泛應性眞流布無一事之矯拂也內盡
於已而外順於道如此可謂無不順矣又何以
見之彼忠以事君臣之職也孝以事親子之分
也有不本於自盡乎必鞠躬盡瘁勵匪懈之節
承懽養志厚罔極之恩則臣子之道盡矣殆見
===
行義素孚精誠默契質諸鬼神合德而不疑矣
以事君言之志同道合而倚任之有賴恪恭所
事外焉孚於君而無所違也以事親言之服勤
盡孝而繼述之有託共爲子職內焉悅其親而
無所悖也夫然則體信而達順道修而德全信
乎純篤不欺而可以爲備矣備非所以爲福乎
抑此內盡外順卽忠恕之理也忠臣孝子求諸
我而已立身天地在我者一有歉焉其不忝所
生哉張子曰聚百順以事君親又曰無入而非
punctuated: 謂之備矣。何以言之？蓋道見於事，而行之在我。使已有弗盡，則違於道而難以言順矣。必反身以存誠，眞實之懿率之以躬行，湛一不虧，無一毫之僞妄也。如是則虛中以體物，推已之心循之以泛應，性眞流布，無一事之矯拂也。內盡於已而外順於道，如此可謂無不順矣。又何以見之？彼忠以事君，臣之職也；孝以事親，子之分也。有不本於自盡乎？必鞠躬盡瘁，勵匪懈之節；承懽養志，厚罔極之恩，則臣子之道盡矣。殆見行義素孚，精誠默契，質諸鬼神，合德而不疑矣。以事君言之，志同道合而倚任之有賴，恪恭所事，外焉孚於君而無所違也。以事親言之，服勤盡孝而繼述之有託，共爲子職，內焉悅其親而無所悖也。夫然則體信而達順，道修而德全，信乎純篤不欺而可以爲備矣。備非所以爲福乎？抑此內盡外順，卽忠恕之理也。忠臣孝子，求諸我而已。立身天地，在我者一有歉焉，其不忝所生哉？張子曰：「聚百順以事君親。」又曰：「無入而非
translation_en:
…this is called completeness. How may this be explained? The Way manifests itself in affairs, but putting it into practice rests with oneself. If one fails to exert oneself fully, one departs from the Way and can hardly be said to accord with it. One must turn inward to preserve sincerity and put the excellence of genuineness into personal practice, maintaining an undiminished purity and singleness, without the slightest trace of falsehood or delusion. Thus one empties the heart to comprehend things and extends one's own heart in responding to all circumstances. The genuineness of one's nature flows forth, without anything forced or contrary in any affair. To exert oneself fully within and accord with the Way without: this may be called according in every respect.

How else can this be seen? Serving the ruler loyally is the duty of a minister; serving one's parents filially is the obligation of a son. Could either fail to be rooted in exerting oneself fully? One must devote oneself utterly to service and cultivate unwavering diligence; one must attend to one's parents' pleasure and nurture their aspirations, deepening one's response to their boundless kindness. Then the way of minister and son is fully realized. One will then see righteous conduct consistently inspiring trust and perfect sincerity achieving an unspoken accord: tested before ghosts and spirits, one's virtue accords with theirs beyond doubt. In serving the ruler, shared aspirations and agreement in the Way make one dependable when entrusted with responsibility. Reverently attending to one's service, one outwardly wins the ruler's trust and acts without contravention. In serving one's parents, diligent labor and full filial devotion make one worthy of being entrusted with carrying on their purposes and undertakings. Fulfilling the duties of a son, one inwardly pleases one's parents and acts without opposition.

Thus, embodying trustworthiness and attaining accord, one cultivates the Way and makes one's virtue complete. Truly, being wholly sincere and free of deception may be called completeness. Is completeness not what constitutes blessing? Moreover, this full exertion within and accord without is precisely the principle of doing one's utmost and extending consideration to others. Loyal ministers and filial sons seek it only in themselves. Standing between Heaven and Earth, if there is any deficiency in what rests with oneself, would one not disgrace those who gave one birth? Master Zhang said: “Gather together every form of accord to serve your ruler and parents.” He also said: “There is no situation one enters that is not…

translation_en:
…complete accord. The gentleman delights in attaining this Way: this is precisely the meaning. Thus the Book of Changes, in commending filial offerings, likewise takes gathering as their foundation. If one can gather together every form of accord, filial offerings can achieve their purpose. The principle of gathering is subtle indeed; only the worthy can realize it.

Zhang Minde

It is recorded here to serve as a model for the many scholars.” [The transcription appears to displace parts of this comment.]

Comment by Associate Examiner Gao, Instructor: “[Transformation is discussed fundamentally in terms of virtue and achievement. Throughout the piece, language and meaning blend seamlessly, requiring no further correction or trimming. An excellent composition.]”

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
爲外王之業而其功有所不容禦何則有其德
者非德之盛也有其業者非業之大也滯於其
迹囿於其偏固不能達之於大而進於化是不
足以語聖聖也者非不以德先天下也而天下
不知有聖人之德非不以道治天下也而天下
不知有聖人之道是豈聖人之有所爲而爲也
哉要亦德深而幾不露業盛而功不顯渾內外
於無迹者耳此則純粹之精也神化之妙也聖
備之極也天下之人殆將涵泳鼓舞於聖人之
===
化而莫之知者矣豈惟人不知之雖聖人亦不
得而自知之也使存之於內者幾有所容測而
德不足以語盛發之於外者功有所容禦而業
不足以語大聖人顧得而自名之曰此吾之德
也此吾之業也天下之人亦得指而名之曰如
是而爲聖人之德也如是而爲聖人之業也則
其所謂德者未始不流於隘而其所謂業者殆
亦不免泥於迹耳奚足以言大奚足以言化奚
足以言聖也哉今夫天之生人也太極以凝其
punctuated: 爲外王之業，而其功有所不容禦。何則？有其德者，非德之盛也；有其業者，非業之大也。滯於其迹，囿於其偏，固不能達之於大而進於化，是不足以語聖。聖也者，非不以德先天下也，而天下不知有聖人之德；非不以道治天下也，而天下不知有聖人之道。是豈聖人之有所爲而爲也哉？要亦德深而幾不露，業盛而功不顯，渾內外於無迹者耳。此則純粹之精也，神化之妙也，聖備之極也。天下之人殆將涵泳鼓舞於聖人之化而莫之知者矣。豈惟人不知之？雖聖人亦不得而自知之也。使存之於內者，幾有所容測，而德不足以語盛；發之於外者，功有所容禦，而業不足以語大。聖人顧得而自名之曰：「此吾之德也，此吾之業也。」天下之人亦得指而名之曰：「如是而爲聖人之德也，如是而爲聖人之業也。」則其所謂德者，未始不流於隘，而其所謂業者，殆亦不免泥於迹耳。奚足以言大？奚足以言化？奚足以言聖也哉？今夫天之生人也，太極以凝其
translation_en:
…it becomes the achievement of outward kingliness, and its efficacy cannot be resisted. Why is this? Merely possessing virtue is not virtue at its fullest; merely possessing achievements is not achievement at its greatest. To remain attached to outward traces and confined to a partial aspect certainly prevents one from attaining greatness and advancing to transformation. This is insufficient to warrant speaking of sagehood.

The sage does indeed lead the world through virtue, yet the world is unaware of the sage’s virtue. He does indeed govern the world through the Way, yet the world is unaware of the sage’s Way. Could this mean that the sage acts with a deliberate purpose in view? It is simply that his virtue is profound while its incipient workings remain unrevealed, and his achievements flourish while their efficacy remains unseen: inward and outward are blended into a unity without traces. This is the essence of purity, the subtlety of spiritual transformation, and the ultimate perfection of sagehood. The people of the world are, one might say, immersed in and inspired by the sage’s transforming influence without knowing it. Nor is it only others who do not know it: even the sage himself cannot be conscious of it.

Suppose that the incipient workings of what he preserves within could be fathomed, so that his virtue could not be called abundant; and that the efficacy of what he expresses outwardly could be resisted, so that his achievements could not be called great. The sage could then identify them himself, saying, “This is my virtue; this is my achievement.” The people of the world could likewise point them out and name them, saying, “Such is the sage’s virtue; such is the sage’s achievement.” Then his supposed virtue would invariably lapse into narrowness, and his supposed achievement would hardly escape being mired in outward traces. How would this warrant speaking of greatness? How would it warrant speaking of transformation? How would it warrant speaking of sagehood?

Now, when Heaven brings human beings into being, the Supreme Ultimate gives coherence to their …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
性其性同也二氣以範其形其形同也則何有
於愚何有於賢何有於聖也而孟軻氏以大而
化之歸諸聖豈天之所以降才者爾殊而聖人
有絶德於天下也乎殊不知聖人之所以至於
化者非有以異於人也不爲知誘不爲物化氣
之昏明不足以蔽之遇之吉凶不足以戕之性
所同也而所以盡其性者聖人之所爲帥也夫
人不得而同也形所同也而所以踐其形者聖
人之所爲塞也夫人不得而同也是故始之以
===
善焉善之實而信也信之積而美也美之發而
光輝也德輝之合而大也而要之以化焉此入
聖之漸也噫學而至於化幾之神也功之極也
德之純也道之至也聖人之能事畢矣是故以
觀乎聖人之内也而見其順性命也和道德也
具衆理也會萬善也通知晝夜也窮物理也盡
人情也存之於内者莫非聖人之德也以觀乎
聖人之外也而見其脩六禮也明七敎也齊八
政也勸九歌也表裏人物也彌綸天地也出入
punctuated:
性，其性同也；二氣以範其形，其形同也。則何有於愚，何有於賢，何有於聖也？而孟軻氏以大而化之歸諸聖，豈天之所以降才者爾殊，而聖人有絶德於天下也乎？殊不知聖人之所以至於化者，非有以異於人也。不爲知誘，不爲物化，氣之昏明不足以蔽之，遇之吉凶不足以戕之。性所同也，而所以盡其性者，聖人之所爲帥也，夫人不得而同也；形所同也，而所以踐其形者，聖人之所爲塞也，夫人不得而同也。是故始之以善焉，善之實而信也，信之積而美也，美之發而光輝也，德輝之合而大也，而要之以化焉，此入聖之漸也。
噫！學而至於化，幾之神也，功之極也，德之純也，道之至也，聖人之能事畢矣。是故以觀乎聖人之内也，而見其順性命也，和道德也，具衆理也，會萬善也，通知晝夜也，窮物理也，盡人情也，存之於内者莫非聖人之德也。以觀乎聖人之外也，而見其脩六禮也，明七敎也，齊八政也，勸九歌也，表裏人物也，彌綸天地也，出入
translation_en:
…nature; their nature is the same. The two vital forces shape their physical form; their physical form is the same. How, then, can there be distinctions between the foolish, the worthy, and the sage? Yet Meng Ke assigns to the sage the condition of being great and becoming transformed. Can it be that Heaven bestows capacities so differently, and that the sage possesses virtue unrivaled throughout the world? This utterly fails to recognize that the sage’s attainment of transformation does not arise from anything that distinguishes him from other people. He is neither enticed by knowledge nor changed by external things. The darkness or clarity of his vital force cannot obscure him, and good or ill fortune cannot injure him. Human nature is shared by all, yet in fully realizing that nature the sage acts as a leader [?], and ordinary people cannot match him. Physical form is shared by all, yet in fulfilling that form the sage brings it to fullness [?], and ordinary people cannot match him. Thus one begins with goodness. When goodness is made real, there is sincerity; when sincerity accumulates, there is beauty; when beauty manifests itself, there is radiance; when virtue and radiance unite, there is greatness. Finally, all culminates in transformation. These are the successive stages of entering sagehood.
Ah! When learning reaches transformation, this is the spiritual subtlety of incipient movements, the culmination of effort, the purity of virtue, and the utmost attainment of the Way. All that a sage can accomplish is complete. Thus, when we consider the sage’s inward being, we see that he accords with his nature and Heaven’s mandate, harmonizes the Way and virtue, possesses all principles, brings together every goodness, comprehends day and night, fathoms the principles of things, and fully understands human feelings. Everything preserved within is the sage’s virtue. When we consider the sage’s outward activity, we see that he cultivates the six rites, elucidates the seven teachings, orders the eight affairs of government, encourages the nine songs, gives both outward expression and inward substance to people and things, encompasses and orders Heaven and Earth, and moves in and out of …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
造化也進退古今也發之於外者莫非聖人之
業也人見夫聖人之德脩於內也而遂以爲聖
人之德倚於內而可以內求者也而不知聖人
之內而無內而所以脩乎內者忘乎內者也人
見聖人之業發於外也而遂以爲聖人之業倚
於外而可以外求者也而不知聖人之外而無
外而所以發乎外者忘乎外者也天德之立者
因天命自然之理而全之耳是故所知者天德
之良知也所能者天德之良能也而天下之仰
===
其德者夫固囿於其德而莫之知者也夫是之
謂發微而不可見夫是之謂清通而不可象夫
是之謂其幾也有所不容測王道之敷者因天
下自然之勢而道之耳是故順萬事而吾無所
容其情也普萬物而吾無所容其心也而天下
之仰其業者夫固安於其業而莫之知者也夫
是之謂順帝則於不知夫是之謂忘帝力於何
有夫是之謂其功也有所不容禦盛德大業至
矣哉今夫天其靜也專其動也直而萬物由之
punctuated: 造化也，進退古今也，發之於外者莫非聖人之業也。人見夫聖人之德脩於內也，而遂以爲聖人之德倚於內而可以內求者也，而不知聖人之內而無內，而所以脩乎內者，忘乎內者也。人見聖人之業發於外也，而遂以爲聖人之業倚於外而可以外求者也，而不知聖人之外而無外，而所以發乎外者，忘乎外者也。天德之立者，因天命自然之理而全之耳。是故所知者，天德之良知也；所能者，天德之良能也。而天下之仰其德者，夫固囿於其德而莫之知者也。夫是之謂發微而不可見，夫是之謂清通而不可象，夫是之謂其幾也有所不容測。王道之敷者，因天下自然之勢而道之耳。是故順萬事而吾無所容其情也，普萬物而吾無所容其心也。而天下之仰其業者，夫固安於其業而莫之知者也。夫是之謂順帝則於不知，夫是之謂忘帝力於何有，夫是之謂其功也有所不容禦。盛德大業，至矣哉！今夫天，其靜也專，其動也直，而萬物由之
translation_en:
…creation and transformation, advancing and withdrawing through past and present: everything manifested outwardly is the sage’s achievement. People see that the sage’s virtue is cultivated within and consequently suppose that it resides within and can be sought there. They do not understand that, for the sage, the inward has no inward boundary, and that what enables inward cultivation is forgetting the inward. People see that the sage’s achievement manifests itself outwardly and consequently suppose that it resides outside and can be sought there. They do not understand that, for the sage, the outward has no outward boundary, and that what enables outward manifestation is forgetting the outward.

Establishing heavenly virtue consists simply in following and fully realizing the spontaneous principle of Heaven’s mandate. Thus what the sage knows is the innate knowing of heavenly virtue, and what he can do is its innate capacity. Those throughout the world who look up to his virtue are indeed encompassed by it without understanding it. This is what is meant by manifesting the subtle yet remaining invisible; this is what is meant by being clear and all-pervading yet admitting no representation; this is what is meant by the incipient workings having something that cannot be fathomed. Extending the kingly Way consists simply in following the spontaneous tendencies of the world and guiding them. Thus I accord with the myriad affairs without inserting my own feelings, and extend universally to the myriad things without inserting my own mind. Those throughout the world who look up to the sage’s achievement indeed rest secure in it without understanding it. This is what is meant by following the Sovereign’s standards unawares; this is what is meant by forgetting the sovereign’s power and asking what it has to do with oneself; this is what is meant by his efficacy having something that cannot be resisted. How consummate are this abundant virtue and great achievement!

Now Heaven, in its stillness, is concentrated; in its movement, it is direct; and through it the myriad things…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
以資始焉天之所以成化也今夫地其靜也翕
其動也闢而萬物由之以資生焉地之所以成
化也然其主宰之神推行之妙則固莫得而測
其幾而其功亦有不容禦者矣學而至於能化
則所存者與天地同其體所發者與天地同其
用是知聖人者合德於天地而上下同流者也
是故巍巍乎成功煥乎文章四方從欲風動堯舜
以之帝也而安安允克重華協帝而罔愆者性
而化焉者也聖敬大烈彰信丕冒湯武以之王
===
也而制事制心敬勝義勝者反之而化焉者也
達而在上明光迓衡以成文武之德者周公也
融其思兼之迹而化焉者也窮而在下從心所
欲不踰矩聖之時者孔子也生知安行不思不
勉無事於化而自無不化者也若顏子之見道
於卓爾而未達一間是其大而幾於化焉者也
若伯夷之清也伊尹之任也柳下惠之和也皆
聖人也舉其所至而言之者也然清矣而非化
於清也任矣而非化於任也和矣而非化於和
punctuated:
以資始焉，天之所以成化也。今夫地，其靜也翕，其動也闢，而萬物由之以資生焉，地之所以成化也。然其主宰之神、推行之妙，則固莫得而測其幾，而其功亦有不容禦者矣。學而至於能化，則所存者與天地同其體，所發者與天地同其用。是知聖人者，合德於天地而上下同流者也。
是故巍巍乎成功，煥乎文章，四方從欲風動，堯舜以之帝也。而安安允克，重華協帝而罔愆者，性而化焉者也。聖敬大烈，彰信丕冒，湯武以之王也。而制事制心，敬勝義勝者，反之而化焉者也。
達而在上，明光迓衡，以成文武之德者，周公也。融其思兼之迹而化焉者也。窮而在下，從心所欲不踰矩，聖之時者，孔子也。生知安行，不思不勉，無事於化而自無不化者也。若顏子之見道於卓爾而未達一間，是其大而幾於化焉者也。若伯夷之清也，伊尹之任也，柳下惠之和也，皆聖人也，舉其所至而言之者也。然清矣，而非化於清也；任矣，而非化於任也；和矣，而非化於和
translation_en:
…and thereby derive their beginnings: this is how Heaven accomplishes transformation. Now Earth, when still, gathers inward; when moving, opens outward. The myriad things thereby derive their life: this is how Earth accomplishes transformation. Yet the spiritual efficacy of their governance and the subtlety of their operation are such that no one can fathom their incipient workings, while their achievements likewise cannot be checked. When learning reaches the capacity for transformation, what one preserves within shares the substance of Heaven and Earth, and what one expresses outwardly shares their functioning. Thus we know that the sage unites his virtue with Heaven and Earth and moves in the same current above and below.
Hence, towering achievements, resplendent cultural forms, and the people of the four quarters following their wishes as though stirred by the wind: through these Yao and Shun ruled as emperors. Their natural ease and assured capacity, and Shun’s successive brilliance, which accorded with Emperor Yao without error, were instances of transformation through inborn nature. Sagely reverence and great accomplishments, manifest trustworthiness and far-reaching protection: through these Tang and Wu ruled as kings. Their regulation of affairs and of the mind, with reverence prevailing over negligence and rightness prevailing over desire, were instances of transformation through returning to their original nature.
Successful and occupying high office, making virtue radiant and welcoming peace, thereby completing the virtue of Kings Wen and Wu—this was the Duke of Zhou. He attained transformation by dissolving the traces of his deliberation and comprehensive attainment [?]. In straitened circumstances and occupying a lowly position, following his heart’s desires without overstepping the bounds, and being the sage who acted in accord with the times—this was Kongzi. Knowing from birth and acting with natural ease, without deliberation or exertion, he had no need to work at transformation, yet spontaneously there was nothing in him that was not transformed. As for Yanzi, who perceived the Way standing loftily before him but remained one interval short of reaching it, he was great and close to transformation. As for Boyi’s purity, Yi Yin’s acceptance of responsibility, and Liu Xiahui’s harmony, they were all sages: these descriptions identify the attainments each had reached. Yet Boyi was pure without attaining transformation in purity; Yi Yin accepted responsibility without attaining transformation in responsibility; Liu Xiahui was harmonious without attaining transformation in harmony…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
也非所謂大而能化也非所謂内外兩忘也非
所謂神化性命通一無二也夫所謂大而化之
者大而能化也化則自不見其大之之迹矣故
達巷黨人之稱夫子曰大哉孔子博學而無所
成名夫子亦嘗賛堯之德曰大哉堯之爲君蕩
蕩乎民無能名焉蓋其無可見之迹是亦無可
名之實耳故曰大而化之之謂聖非孟子造道
之深其孰能與於此然孟子善言聖矣而卒未
至於聖者何也其言曰自生民以來未有盛於
===
孔子也又曰乃所願則學孔子也其希聖之心
非不至也而未化者蓋優入聖域之爲難也故
曰孔子無迹顔子微有迹孟子其迹著有迹則
未易以語化矣雖然君子之學以聖神功化爲
要歸固不當以近小者自限也然不能以一蹴
而至焉積累之漸自善信美大而至於化則其
功不可誣也若曰化可爲也而躐等而進焉則
亦不足以語聖修之功而固亦何所得也哉故
曰化不可助長順焉可也孟子曰勿忘勿助其
punctuated: 也，非所謂大而能化也，非所謂内外兩忘也，非所謂神化性命通一無二也。夫所謂大而化之者，大而能化也。化則自不見其大之之迹矣。故達巷黨人之稱夫子曰：「大哉孔子！博學而無所成名。」夫子亦嘗賛堯之德曰：「大哉堯之爲君！蕩蕩乎，民無能名焉。」蓋其無可見之迹，是亦無可名之實耳。故曰：「大而化之之謂聖。」非孟子造道之深，其孰能與於此？然孟子善言聖矣，而卒未至於聖者，何也？其言曰：「自生民以來，未有盛於孔子也。」又曰：「乃所願，則學孔子也。」其希聖之心非不至也，而未化者，蓋優入聖域之爲難也。故曰：「孔子無迹，顔子微有迹，孟子其迹著。」有迹則未易以語化矣。雖然，君子之學以聖神功化爲要歸，固不當以近小者自限也。然不能以一蹴而至焉。積累之漸，自善信美大而至於化，則其功不可誣也。若曰化可爲也，而躐等而進焉，則亦不足以語聖修之功，而固亦何所得也哉？故曰：「化不可助長，順焉可也。」孟子曰：「勿忘勿助。」其
translation_en:
…nor is this what is meant by being great and capable of transformation; nor is it what is meant by forgetting both the inner and the outer; nor is it what is meant by spiritual transformation, human nature, and destiny forming a single unity without division. What is called “being great and transforming” means being great and capable of transformation. Once transformed, one naturally displays no trace of the process of becoming great. Thus a man of Daxiang said in praise of the Master: “Great indeed is Confucius! His learning is broad, yet he has achieved fame in no particular field.” The Master also once praised the virtue of Yao: “Great indeed was Yao as a ruler! So vast was he that the people could find no name for him.” Since there were no visible traces, there was likewise no definite substance that could be named. Hence the saying: “One who is great and transforms is called a sage.” Had Mencius not penetrated the Way so deeply, who could have attained such understanding?

Yet although Mencius spoke well of sagehood, why did he ultimately fail to attain it? He said: “Since humankind first came into being, there has never been anyone greater than Confucius.” He also said: “As for what I wish, it is to learn from Confucius.” His aspiration to sagehood was certainly wholehearted. That he had not yet undergone transformation was presumably because entering the realm of sagehood with ease is so difficult. Hence the saying: “Confucius left no traces; Master Yan left slight traces; Mencius’s traces were conspicuous.” Where traces remain, one cannot readily speak of transformation.

Nevertheless, the learning of the gentleman takes sagehood, spiritual attainment, achievement, and transformation as its ultimate goal. He certainly ought not to limit himself to what is immediate and petty. Yet he cannot arrive there in a single leap. If, through gradual accumulation, he proceeds from goodness, to sincerity, to beauty, to greatness, and finally to transformation, the efficacy of his effort cannot be denied. But if he says that transformation can be deliberately accomplished and advances by skipping stages, this is insufficient to qualify as the work of cultivating sagehood. What, indeed, could he gain from it? Hence the saying: “Transformation cannot be forced to grow; one may only follow its course.” Mencius said: “Neither forget nor force growth.” Might this be…

text:
繼志述事孝切因心欣逢
華帙之渙頒幸沐

體
punctuated:
繼志述事，孝切因心。欣逢華帙之渙頒，幸沐洪恩之覃被。萬物得所，率土騰懽。竊惟聖人通天下以爲一身，王道擴善端而保四海。粤稽醫術，實本仁心，政理所先，民生攸寄。昔炎帝審藥以知性，逮軒皇命官以辨方。微詞隱於後代之繁蕪，大義漓於諸篇之支委。執持兩可，議論多門。蓋擇焉未精，遂博而鮮要。欲會衆言之克一，有待天縱之多能。
恭惟睿宗獻皇帝，德隆廣運，學懋緝熙。含春備四氣之和，中正運一元之化。洽好生之德，視民如傷。體
translation_en:
… In carrying forward his predecessor’s intentions and completing his undertakings, your filial devotion springs deeply from the heart. We rejoice to receive the widespread distribution of these splendid volumes and are fortunate to enjoy the far-reaching bounty of your great grace. All things find their proper place, and all the land rejoices. We humbly reflect that the sage regards all under Heaven as one body, and that the kingly Way extends the beginnings of goodness to bring security to the Four Seas. Examining the art of medicine, we find that it is indeed rooted in a benevolent heart: it is a foremost concern of governance, upon which the people’s lives depend. In antiquity, Yandi examined medicinal substances to understand their properties; later, the Yellow Emperor appointed officials to distinguish remedies. Subtle teachings became obscured by the prolixity of later ages, and great principles were diluted amid the ramifications of the various writings. Practitioners maintained ambiguous positions, and arguments proliferated in many schools. Because selection lacked precision, breadth of learning yielded little that was essential. To bring these many teachings into unity awaited one endowed by Heaven with manifold abilities.
We reverently consider Emperor Ruizong Xian: his virtue was exalted, encompassing all and reaching afar; his learning was assiduous and ever more luminous. Embodying spring’s vitality, he possessed the harmony of the energies of all four seasons; centered and upright, he set in motion the transforming power of the primal unity. His life-loving virtue extended everywhere, and he cared for the people as though they were injured. He embodied …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
大造之仁對時育物當
內殿時幾之暇
躬檢方書令醫臣選擇之精
親揮
宸翰首述憂時之旨次條對證之方舉要刪繁
分門析類跋以
龍藻冠以
鴻文肫肫爲民深懸孔思洋洋經世媲美文
謨誠將開萬世之太平而躋八荒於仁壽
===
者也書成自昔傳廣於今茲蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
仁明武以參天
誠神幾而入聖
敬一發聖賢之蘊學本傳心
精禋達
郊
廟之儀治如指掌
恩濡九有屢
punctuated:
大造之仁，對時育物。當內殿時幾之暇，躬檢方書，令醫臣選擇之精；親揮宸翰，首述憂時之旨，次條對證之方，舉要刪繁，分門析類，跋以龍藻，冠以鴻文。肫肫爲民，深懸孔思；洋洋經世，媲美文謨。誠將開萬世之太平，而躋八荒於仁壽者也。
書成自昔，傳廣於今茲。蓋伏遇皇帝陛下，仁明武以參天，誠神幾而入聖。敬一發聖賢之蘊，學本傳心；精禋達郊廟之儀，治如指掌。恩濡九有，屢
translation_en:
…the benevolence of the great creative power, nurturing all things in accordance with the seasons. In the intervals between attending to affairs in the inner palace, he personally examined books of medical prescriptions and ordered his medical officials to select the finest among them. Taking up the imperial brush himself, he first set forth his concern for the times, then arranged prescriptions according to the conditions they treated, extracting essentials and removing excess, dividing them into categories and distinguishing their types. He supplied an imperial postscript and prefaced the work with a magnificent composition. With heartfelt devotion to the people, he cherished profound concern for them; in his comprehensive care for the realm, he rivaled the splendid counsels of antiquity. Truly, he intended to inaugurate peace for ten thousand generations and bring the people of all eight regions to benevolence and longevity.
The book was completed in former days; its circulation has been broadened in our own time. For we have reverently encountered Your Majesty the Emperor, whose benevolence, enlightenment, and martial virtue rank with Heaven, and whose sincerity and subtle spiritual discernment attain sagehood. Through reverence and singleness of purpose, you disclose the profound teachings of sages and worthies; your learning is rooted in the transmission of the mind. Through pure sacrifice, you fully realize the rites at the suburban altars and ancestral temples; governing is as clear to you as viewing your own palm. Your favor bathes the nine regions, and repeatedly…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
詔纘祖
德被八紘數行讞獄
登崇賢後
朝端長君子之風
昭賁人文海內合太和之治追念
先皇舊典未廣流傳爰
嘉臣下建言遂令刋布
天章燦耀雲漢昭回
作者聖而
述者明重華允協
美於前而
盛於後奕世彌光遐邇具瞻蓋家傳而人誦
臣鄰快覩眞而命而耳提將使蔀屋窮簷
無不納之壽域則雖羣生庶類亦皆置之
陽和
蕩蕩難名欣欣相告臣等樗櫟下材猥荅竝
列才非濟世學愧知方開卷有懷頓覺沉
疴之去體執經具在恍如寒谷之回春喜
punctuated:
詔纘祖，德被八紘，數行讞獄。登崇賢後，朝端長君子之風；昭賁人文，海內合太和之治。追念先皇舊典未廣流傳，爰嘉臣下建言，遂令刋布。天章燦耀，雲漢昭回。作者聖而述者明，重華允協；美於前而盛於後，奕世彌光。遐邇具瞻，蓋家傳而人誦。臣鄰快覩，眞而命而耳提，將使蔀屋窮簷無不納之壽域，則雖羣生庶類亦皆置之陽和。蕩蕩難名，欣欣相告。
臣等樗櫟下材，猥荅竝列，才非濟世，學愧知方。開卷有懷，頓覺沉疴之去體；執經具在，恍如寒谷之回春。喜
translation_en:
…edicts to carry forward the ancestral legacy. Your virtue extends to the eight reaches of the world, and you have repeatedly ordered reviews of criminal cases. You elevate and honor the descendants of worthies, fostering the ways of gentlemen at court; you glorify cultural accomplishment, bringing all within the seas into a reign of supreme harmony. Recalling that the former emperor’s established texts had not circulated widely, you graciously approved your servants’ proposal and ordered their publication. The imperial writings shine resplendently, like the luminous sweep of the Milky Way. The author was a sage, and the transmitter is enlightened: their successive splendors are truly in accord. Excellent under the predecessor and flourishing under his successor, they shine ever more brightly from generation to generation. Near and far, all look upon them; every household transmits them and every person recites them. Your attendant ministers rejoice to behold them, as though receiving personal instruction and admonition at the ear [?]. You will bring even those dwelling in dark hovels and impoverished homes into the realm of longevity; indeed, all living beings of every kind will likewise be embraced by this vernal warmth. So vast is this bounty that it defies naming; joyfully, people tell one another of it.
We, your servants, are inferior timber, like useless ailanthus and oak, yet unworthily stand together in the ranks [?]. Our abilities cannot succor the age, and our learning falls shamefully short of understanding the proper way. Opening the volume, we are moved, suddenly feeling as though a chronic illness had left our bodies. Holding the classic, with everything present before us, we feel as though spring had returned to a frozen valley. Our joy…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
溢豫鳴榮逾晉錫伏願
欽時五福益彰
皇極之光
敷錫庶民咸囿
聖神之澤
天地位而萬物育
陰陽調而風雨時老者安少者懷敬效
堯封之祝
日之升月之恒載歌
===
天保之章〔臣〕等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
策五道
第一問
punctuated:
溢豫鳴，榮逾晉錫。伏願欽時五福，益彰皇極之光；敷錫庶民，咸囿聖神之澤。天地位而萬物育，陰陽調而風雨時。老者安，少者懷，敬效堯封之祝；日之升，月之恒，載歌《天保》之章。〔臣〕等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叄場
策五道
第一問
translation_en:
…our joy overflows in exultant expression, and our glory surpasses the honors bestowed in the hexagram Jin (Advance). We humbly wish that, reverently attending to these five blessings, Your Majesty may further manifest the radiance of the August Ultimate, and that, bestowing blessings upon the common people, you may encompass all within your sagely and divine beneficence. May Heaven and Earth assume their proper places and the myriad things flourish; may yin and yang be harmonious, and wind and rain arrive in season. May the aged enjoy peace and the young receive loving care: we reverently emulate the border warden’s blessings upon Yao. Like the rising sun and the enduring moon: we sing the ode “Heaven Protects” (Tianbao). We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sagely Majesty with the utmost fervor and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks and make them known to Your Majesty.
Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
易弘器
同考試官教諭韋　批〔此作能發揚我〕
皇上敬一之心法同符
皇祖可以覩子之忠誠矣
同考試官教諭鄒　批〔我〕
皇上敬一之箴五箴之註布之天下家傳人誦子能鋪張不遺蓋仰覩
聖學而有得者
同考試官教諭楊　批〔數陳詳悉可謂善鳴〕
國家之盛者矣
同考試官教諭張　批〔我〕
===
太祖註洪範與
皇上敬一箴五箴註皆聖賢傳心之要先後一揆此策揚厲明盡其涵泳
聖化而能言其盛者歟
考試官學正張　批〔忠愛之誠溢于言表〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔賛揚而且精核可式〕
大哉帝王之心學乎自其著述者言之則
爲垂世立教之典自其英華者言之則爲
經天緯地之文自其精藴者言之則爲性
punctuated:
易弘器

同考試官教諭韋，批〔此作能發揚我〕皇上敬一之心法，同符皇祖，可以覩子之忠誠矣。

同考試官教諭鄒，批〔我〕皇上敬一之箴、五箴之註，布之天下，家傳人誦。子能鋪張不遺，蓋仰覩聖學而有得者。

同考試官教諭楊，批〔數陳詳悉，可謂善鳴〕國家之盛者矣。

同考試官教諭張，批〔我〕太祖註《洪範》，與皇上《敬一箴》、《五箴註》，皆聖賢傳心之要，先後一揆。此策揚厲明盡，其涵泳聖化而能言其盛者歟？

考試官學正張，批〔忠愛之誠，溢于言表。〕

考試官教授鄭，批〔賛揚而且精核，可式。〕

大哉，帝王之心學乎！自其著述者言之，則爲垂世立教之典；自其英華者言之，則爲經天緯地之文；自其精藴者言之，則爲性
translation_en:
Yi Hongqi

Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor, comments: “This composition brings out our Emperor’s method of cultivating the mind through reverence for the One, showing its accord with that of the imperial ancestor. From it one can discern your loyal sincerity.”

Associate Examiner Zou, Instructor, comments: “Our Emperor’s Admonition on Reverence for the One and his Commentary on the Five Admonitions have been disseminated throughout the realm, transmitted in every household and recited by everyone. You have expounded them fully, omitting nothing. Surely you have looked up to the learning of the sage emperor and gained insight from it.”

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “The points are set forth in full detail; this may be called an able proclamation of the dynasty’s flourishing greatness.”

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Our Taizu’s commentary on the Great Plan, together with our Emperor’s Admonition on Reverence for the One and Commentary on the Five Admonitions, all contain the essentials of the transmission of the mind by sages and worthies. Earlier and later works follow the same standard. This policy essay celebrates and elucidates them clearly and exhaustively. Is its author not someone who has steeped himself in the sage emperor’s transforming influence and can articulate its greatness?”

Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: “The sincerity of his loyalty and devotion overflows beyond his words.”

Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: “Laudatory yet also precise and rigorous: it can serve as a model.”

Great indeed is the learning of the mind practiced by emperors and kings! Considered as writings, their works are canonical texts that establish instruction for generations to come; considered in their literary brilliance, they are compositions that order heaven and earth; considered in their profound import, they concern human nature…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
命道德之懿自其源流者言之則爲繼統
傳心之要自其綏猷立極者言之則爲太
平致治之本堯典虞書禹謨湯誥郁郁乎
同光竝美焉是知治本於道道本於學學
本於敬敬本於心心主乎一而惟皇之極
建焉緝熈之學純焉時雍之治成焉此我
太祖高皇帝之所以創業我
皇上之所以中興
聖學
===
聖治主敬建極有以比隆於前聖而陋漢唐宋
於不足言矣猗歟盛哉請敬敷揚以對自
古帝王以一身而爲天地民物之主其本
皆存乎一心以一心而宰萬事萬化之樞
其本則存乎一敬敬也者所以懋聖學而
建皇極者也唐虞三代詩書所紀固彰彰
可徵焉是故于堯見欽明之學於變之化
焉于舜見温恭之學風動之治焉于禹見
祇台之學平成之績焉于湯見敬躋之學
punctuated:
命道德之懿，自其源流者言之，則爲繼統傳心之要；自其綏猷立極者言之，則爲太平致治之本。堯典、虞書、禹謨、湯誥，郁郁乎同光竝美焉。是知治本於道，道本於學，學本於敬，敬本於心。心主乎一，而惟皇之極建焉，緝熈之學純焉，時雍之治成焉。此我太祖高皇帝之所以創業，我皇上之所以中興。聖學聖治，主敬建極，有以比隆於前聖，而陋漢唐宋於不足言矣。猗歟盛哉！請敬敷揚以對。
自古帝王以一身而爲天地民物之主，其本皆存乎一心；以一心而宰萬事萬化之樞，其本則存乎一敬。敬也者，所以懋聖學而建皇極者也。唐虞三代，詩書所紀，固彰彰可徵焉。是故于堯見欽明之學、於變之化焉；于舜見温恭之學、風動之治焉；于禹見祇台之學、平成之績焉；于湯見敬躋之學
translation_en:
…the excellence of human nature, Heaven’s mandate, the Way, and virtue; considered in terms of its origins and transmission, it is the essential means of continuing the succession and transmitting the learning of the mind; considered in terms of establishing enduring principles and setting the supreme standard, it is the foundation for bringing about peace and good government. The Canon of Yao, the Documents of Shun, the Counsels of Yu, and the Announcement of Tang shine together in splendid brilliance and beauty. Thus we know that government is rooted in the Way, the Way in learning, learning in reverence, and reverence in the mind. When the mind is centered on unity, the sovereign’s supreme standard is established, the learning of ever-brightening virtue becomes pure, and harmonious government is achieved. This is how our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the dynasty and how our reigning emperor has brought about its resurgence. Through sagely learning and sagely government, taking reverence as their guiding principle and establishing the supreme standard, they have equaled the greatness of the ancient sages, making the Han, Tang, and Song appear so inferior as to be unworthy of mention. Ah, how glorious! Permit me respectfully to expound upon this in reply.
Since antiquity, emperors and kings have, in their own persons, been masters of all people and things between Heaven and Earth; the foundation of this lies entirely in the mind alone. With this single mind they preside over the pivot of all affairs and transformations; the foundation of this lies in reverence alone. Reverence is the means by which sagely learning is advanced and the sovereign’s supreme standard established. The records of the Poetry and Documents concerning the ages of Yao and Shun and the Three Dynasties furnish clear evidence of this. Thus, in Yao we see learning marked by reverence and discernment, and its transforming influence; in Shun, learning marked by gentleness and deference, and government whose influence moves like the wind; in Yu, learning expressed in his declaration of personal reverence, and the achievement of bringing the land into order; in Tang, learning through which he daily advanced in reverence…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
允殖之休焉于文武見敬止敬義之學怙
冒求清之烈焉帝道而帝王道而王天下
所以會歸於皇極而心法之傳有自來矣
自是而漢而唐而宋英君誼辟代有其人
要之敬德未純心學不講漢高則不事詩
書竟安馬上此漢治之所以雜霸唐雖弘
文開館而躬行不逮此唐治之所以雜夷
宋雖根本可觀然亦未能追三代之盛以
遊乎堯舜之天也蓋皆因陋就簡小小補
===
塞此何以稱焉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝再造乾坤功德之盛振古無比其
所以上追往聖而垂
聖子
神孫億萬世之訓者一本於心學乃於洪武二
年特
命儒臣書洪範揭之
兩廡以備觀覽且
親為之註先之以五行五事八政五紀所以推
punctuated:
允殖之休焉；于文武見敬止敬義之學，怙冒求清之烈焉。帝道而帝，王道而王，天下所以會歸於皇極，而心法之傳有自來矣。自是而漢而唐而宋，英君誼辟，代有其人。要之，敬德未純，心學不講。漢高則不事詩書，竟安馬上，此漢治之所以雜霸；唐雖弘文開館，而躬行不逮，此唐治之所以雜夷；宋雖根本可觀，然亦未能追三代之盛，以遊乎堯舜之天也。蓋皆因陋就簡，小小補塞，此何以稱焉？
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，再造乾坤，功德之盛，振古無比。其所以上追往聖，而垂聖子神孫億萬世之訓者，一本於心學。乃於洪武二年，特命儒臣書《洪範》，揭之兩廡，以備觀覽，且親為之註。先之以五行、五事、八政、五紀，所以推
translation_en:
…and the blessings of a people truly flourishing. In Kings Wen and Wu we see learning devoted to abiding in reverence and maintaining reverence and righteousness, and the achievements of sheltering the people and seeking a purified realm. Those who followed the Way of the sage emperors became sage emperors; those who followed the kingly Way became true kings. Thus all under Heaven converged upon the August Ultimate, and the transmission of the teaching of the mind had its origins in antiquity. Thereafter, through the Han, Tang, and Song, each age had its outstanding rulers and righteous sovereigns. In essence, however, their reverence for virtue was not pure, and the learning of the mind was not cultivated. Gaozu of Han neglected the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, remaining content to rule from horseback: this is why Han government was adulterated with the methods of hegemons. Although the Tang established the Institute for the Advancement of Literature, its rulers’ personal conduct fell short: this is why Tang government was adulterated with barbarian practices. Although the foundations of Song rule were worthy of regard, it too could not match the flourishing of the Three Dynasties and dwell beneath the heaven of Yao and Shun. All merely made do with crude and makeshift arrangements, patching small gaps. How could these warrant praise?
We reverently reflect upon our Emperor Taizu Gao, who recreated Heaven and Earth. The grandeur of his achievements and virtue was unmatched throughout antiquity. His emulation of the sages of old and the instructions he bequeathed to his sagely sons and divine descendants for countless generations were rooted entirely in the learning of the mind. In the second year of Hongwu, he therefore specially commanded his Confucian officials to transcribe the “Great Plan” (Hongfan) and display it in the two side galleries for consultation and inspection; he also personally composed a commentary on it. He began with the Five Agents, the Five Personal Activities, the Eight Affairs of Government, and the Five Regulators of Time, thereby expounding…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
皇極之體也繼之以三德稽疑庶徵福極
所以昭皇極之用也
功隆著述炳矣日星義貫天人燦然指掌一
哉
皇心乎眞有以洞傳心之祕而闢萬世之太平
者乎又嘗
語贊善劉三吾曰洪範一篇帝王爲治之要
道也所以立皇極叙彝倫保萬民叙四時成
百穀本於天道驗於人事箕子爲武王陳之
而謙讓未能朕每爲之惕然大哉
皇言乎究感通之理以上探乎爲治之原念箕
子之陳而深嘆乎武王之讓眞有以契疇
範之精而思前聖之未逮者乎是蓋
聖人之德本於天成故其入心學之優也有餘
功
聖人之學著之話言故其發前聖之蘊也皆明
訓豈徒知之亦允蹈之故本五行而敬
天授時焉敬五事而正已檢身焉厚八政而豐
punctuated:
皇極之體也；繼之以三德、稽疑、庶徵、福極，所以昭皇極之用也。功隆著述，炳矣日星；義貫天人，燦然指掌。一哉，皇心乎！眞有以洞傳心之祕而闢萬世之太平者乎！
又嘗語贊善劉三吾曰：「洪範一篇，帝王爲治之要道也。所以立皇極，叙彝倫，保萬民，叙四時，成百穀，本於天道，驗於人事。箕子爲武王陳之，而謙讓未能，朕每爲之惕然。」大哉，皇言乎！究感通之理，以上探乎爲治之原；念箕子之陳，而深嘆乎武王之讓。眞有以契疇範之精而思前聖之未逮者乎！
是蓋聖人之德，本於天成，故其入心學之優也有餘功；聖人之學，著之話言，故其發前聖之蘊也皆明訓。豈徒知之？亦允蹈之。故本五行而敬天授時焉，敬五事而正已檢身焉，厚八政而豐
translation_en:
…the substance of the August Standard. He followed these with the Three Virtues, the Resolution of Doubts, the Various Signs, and Blessings and Calamities, thereby illuminating the operation of the August Standard. His achievement in writing shone like the sun and stars; its meaning encompassed Heaven and humanity, as clear as something displayed in the palm of one's hand. How unified was the imperial mind! Did he not truly penetrate the secret of transmitting the mind and open the way to peace for ten thousand generations!
He also once told Liu Sanwu, Admonisher to the Heir Apparent: “The chapter ‘Great Plan’ contains the essential Way by which emperors and kings govern. Establishing the August Standard, ordering the constant human relationships, protecting the myriad people, ordering the four seasons, and bringing the hundred grains to maturity are rooted in the Way of Heaven and verified in human affairs. Jizi explained it to King Wu, yet there was a modest profession of inability [?]. Whenever I consider this, I am filled with apprehension.” How great were these imperial words! He investigated the principles of responsive communion, tracing them upward to the source of good government; reflecting on Jizi's exposition, he profoundly admired King Wu's humility. Did he not truly grasp the essence of the categories of the Great Plan and ponder what even earlier sages had not attained!
This was surely because the sage's virtue was endowed by Heaven: thus his exceptional attainment in the learning of the mind left him ample capacity for further achievement. The sage's learning was expressed in his utterances: thus all his disclosures of the earlier sages' profound meanings were lucid instructions. Did he merely understand them? He also faithfully put them into practice. Thus, taking the Five Phases as his basis, he revered Heaven and promulgated the seasonal calendar; attending reverently to the Five Affairs, he rectified himself and disciplined his conduct; giving due weight to the Eight Affairs of Government, he enriched…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
財利民焉協五紀而脩德致祥焉以乂三
德則剛柔正直竝用也以明稽疑則龜筮
庶謀協同也以驗庶徵則五氣時若也以
徵福極則諸福咸臻也泰和之治蕩蕩乎
無能名矣
列聖相承率由是道欽惟
成祖文皇帝著
聖學心法以弘燕翼之規
宣宗章皇帝著五倫書以明彝倫之道善繼善
述先後一揆治隆俗美常如一日有由然
===
也恭惟我
皇上聰明
天縱懋隆
聖學敬
天勤民法
祖建極中和位育之效固已光四表而格上下
矣
聖心敬一之學惟時惟幾不自滿假乃於
punctuated:
財利民焉，協五紀而脩德致祥焉。以乂三德，則剛柔正直竝用也；以明稽疑，則龜筮庶謀協同也；以驗庶徵，則五氣時若也；以徵福極，則諸福咸臻也。泰和之治，蕩蕩乎無能名矣！
列聖相承，率由是道。欽惟成祖文皇帝著《聖學心法》，以弘燕翼之規；宣宗章皇帝著《五倫書》，以明彝倫之道。善繼善述，先後一揆，治隆俗美，常如一日，有由然也。
恭惟我皇上，聰明天縱，懋隆聖學，敬天勤民，法祖建極。中和位育之效，固已光四表而格上下矣。聖心敬一之學，惟時惟幾，不自滿假，乃於……
translation_en:
…to increase wealth and benefit the people; by harmonizing the Five Regulators of Time, he cultivates virtue and brings auspicious signs. In governing through the Three Virtues, firmness, gentleness, and uprightness are employed together. In clarifying the Examination of Doubts, tortoise-shell and milfoil divination accord with the counsels of the many. In testing the Various Verifications, the five atmospheric influences follow their proper seasons. In examining Blessings and Extremities, all blessings arrive together. So boundless is this rule of supreme harmony that no words can describe it!
The successive sage emperors have all followed this Way. We reverently recall that Emperor Wen, Chengzu, composed Essentials of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa) to extend his plans for securing the well-being of his descendants; Emperor Zhang, Xuanzong, composed the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) to illuminate the Way of the enduring human relationships. They skillfully carried on and fulfilled their predecessors’ purposes, following the same standard from one reign to the next. There was thus a reason why flourishing government and fine customs remained constant, as though throughout a single day.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor, endowed by Heaven with intelligence and discernment, has greatly advanced sagely learning, revered Heaven and diligently cared for the people, emulated his ancestors and established the supreme standard. The effects of equilibrium and harmony—Heaven and Earth taking their proper places and all things receiving nourishment—have already shone to the four quarters and reached above and below. In his sagely heart’s pursuit of learning through reverent concentration on the One, he attends to the proper moment and the slightest beginnings, never resting in complacent self-satisfaction. Thus, during…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
萬幾之暇親灑
宸翰製爲
敬一之箴又取宋儒范浚心箴程頥視聽言動
四箴皆爲之註頒之天下家傳人誦其所
以紹唐虞心法之淵源開後學進脩之門
路眞與
聖祖之註洪範者同一道矣蓋嘗伏覩
敬一之箴則
敬神仁民也謹獨脩德也心箴則
===
正一心以參三才也視箴則用舍明也聽箴
則
聽德之要也言箴則合於天理而因諸人情
也動箴則事皆合道也語明意盡得以仰
窺
皇上之心卽
聖祖之心
皇上之學卽
聖祖之學故
punctuated: 萬幾之暇，親灑宸翰，製爲《敬一之箴》，又取宋儒范浚《心箴》、程頥視聽言動四箴，皆爲之註，頒之天下，家傳人誦。其所以紹唐虞心法之淵源，開後學進脩之門路，眞與聖祖之註《洪範》者同一道矣。蓋嘗伏覩《敬一之箴》，則敬神仁民也，謹獨脩德也；《心箴》，則正一心以參三才也；《視箴》，則用舍明也；《聽箴》，則聽德之要也；《言箴》，則合於天理而因諸人情也；《動箴》，則事皆合道也。語明意盡，得以仰窺皇上之心卽聖祖之心，皇上之學卽聖祖之學，故
translation_en:
…in the intervals between the myriad affairs of state, Your Majesty personally wielded the imperial brush to compose the Admonition on Reverent Single-mindedness. You also took the Admonition on the Mind by the Song Confucian scholar Fan Jun and Cheng Yi’s four admonitions on looking, listening, speaking, and acting, and provided commentaries on them all. You promulgated them throughout the realm, to be handed down in every household and recited by everyone. In carrying forward the profound tradition of the teaching of the mind from Tang and Yu—that is, Yao and Shun—and opening a path of moral advancement and cultivation for later students, this truly follows the same Way as the sagely ancestor’s commentary on the Great Plan.
I have reverently read the Admonition on Reverent Single-mindedness: it teaches reverence for the spirits, benevolence toward the people, vigilance when alone, and the cultivation of virtue. The Admonition on the Mind teaches rectifying the mind so as to participate with Heaven and Earth in the Three Powers. The Admonition on Looking teaches clarity in what to adopt and what to reject. The Admonition on Listening teaches the essentials of hearkening to virtue. The Admonition on Speaking teaches conformity to heavenly principle while accommodating human feelings. The Admonition on Acting teaches bringing every undertaking into accord with the Way. Their language is lucid and their meaning fully expressed, enabling us reverently to glimpse that Your Majesty’s mind is the very mind of the sagely ancestor, and Your Majesty’s learning is the very learning of the sagely ancestor. Thus…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
敬一之箴猶之洪範之建極也五箴之註猶之
五事之敬用也
神謨
聖訓相爲表裏眞有以見
聖學之純粹焉而不雜
聖心之敬一焉而不息此所以合帝王之全纘
列聖之美而成
今日之治也然猶未也繪無逸之圖所以立
皇極也著
===
明倫之典所以叙彞倫也
恤刑之使屢遣寛租之
詔屢下所以保萬民也
喜雨有吟
祈雪卽應所以成四時也嘉禾瑞麥
郊苑呈祥所以成百穀也凡若此者皆由
皇上本敬一之心以建維
皇之極其内聖之盛德至矣是以叙疇順事之
功化潛孚神運而外王之大業直與天地
punctuated: 敬一之箴，猶之洪範之建極也；五箴之註，猶之五事之敬用也。神謨聖訓，相爲表裏，眞有以見聖學之純粹焉而不雜，聖心之敬一焉而不息。此所以合帝王之全，纘列聖之美，而成今日之治也。然猶未也：繪無逸之圖，所以立皇極也；著明倫之典，所以叙彞倫也；恤刑之使屢遣，寛租之詔屢下，所以保萬民也；喜雨有吟，祈雪卽應，所以成四時也；嘉禾瑞麥，郊苑呈祥，所以成百穀也。凡若此者，皆由皇上本敬一之心，以建維皇之極。其内聖之盛德至矣，是以叙疇順事之功，化潛孚，神運，而外王之大業直與天地
translation_en:
The Admonition on Reverent Single-mindedness is like the establishment of the supreme standard in the Great Plan; the annotations to the Five Admonitions are like the reverent application of the five personal activities described there. Divine counsels and sagely instructions complement one another as outer expression and inner substance. They truly reveal the unalloyed purity of His Majesty’s sagely learning and the unceasing reverent single-mindedness of his sagely heart. Through these he combines the full excellences of emperors and kings, carries forward the virtues of the successive sage rulers, and brings about the good government of today.
Yet this is not all. Having the Illustration of Against Idleness painted serves to establish the supreme imperial standard; composing the Great Code Clarifying Human Relations serves to put the enduring human relationships in order. Repeatedly dispatching envoys to review punishments with compassion and issuing edicts to remit land taxes serve to protect the myriad people. His verses rejoicing in rain and the immediate response to his prayers for snow serve to bring the four seasons to fulfillment. Auspicious grain and wheat displaying favorable portents in the suburban imperial parks serve to bring the hundred grains to maturity.
All such things arise from His Majesty’s grounding himself in a heart of reverent single-mindedness to establish the sovereign’s supreme standard. His abundant virtue as an inner sage has reached perfection. Thus, in his achievement of ordering the categories of the Great Plan and bringing affairs into accord, his transforming influence penetrates imperceptibly and operates with divine efficacy; and his great undertaking as an outward king directly joins Heaven and Earth …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
而同流也合而觀之
聖祖之註洪範而未及乎敬一五箴也誠若有
待於
今日我
皇上之建極叙疇也其於洪範之理則又兼舉
而一以貫之矣書曰有典有則又曰監于
成憲敢以是爲
聖天子頌焉
第二問
張敏德
===
同考試官教諭聶　批〔朱陸均有益於世敎者也始之異者見之異終之同者道之同也子能發之其亦知其心事者乎〕
同考試官教諭高　批〔此作蓋尚論古人而有得者錄之以釋羣言之惑〕
同考試官教諭袁　批〔朱陸門人各求相勝而論説不同此策果道其故而復折衷于聖人眞知言哉〕
考試官學正張　批〔此策得朱陸異同之旨〕
punctuated:
而同流也。合而觀之，聖祖之註《洪範》，而未及乎《敬一五箴》也，誠若有待於今日。我皇上之建極叙疇也，其於《洪範》之理，則又兼舉而一以貫之矣。《書》曰：「有典有則。」又曰：「監于成憲。」敢以是爲聖天子頌焉。

第二問
張敏德

同考試官教諭聶　批：〔朱陸均有益於世敎者也。始之異者，見之異；終之同者，道之同也。子能發之，其亦知其心事者乎？〕
同考試官教諭高　批：〔此作蓋尚論古人而有得者，錄之以釋羣言之惑。〕
同考試官教諭袁　批：〔朱陸門人各求相勝，而論説不同。此策果道其故，而復折衷于聖人，眞知言哉！〕
考試官學正張　批：〔此策得朱陸異同之旨。〕
translation_en:
…and flow together with Heaven and Earth. Considered together, the Sagely Founder’s commentary on the Great Plan did not extend to the Five Admonitions on Reverent Unity, as though it truly awaited the present day. In establishing the supreme standard and ordering the categories, our Emperor has comprehensively embraced the principles of the Great Plan and threaded them together with a single principle. The Book of Documents says, “There are statutes and rules,” and also, “Look to established regulations.” I venture to offer these words in praise of the sagely Son of Heaven.

Second Question
Zhang Minde

Associate Examiner Nie, Instructor, comments: 〔Zhu and Lu both benefited the moral teaching of the age. Their initial differences were differences of understanding; their ultimate agreement lay in the unity of the Way. You have been able to elucidate this: might you also be one who understands their deepest intentions?〕

Associate Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: 〔This composition shows insight gained through examining the ancients. It is selected to dispel the confusion arising from the many competing opinions.〕

Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: 〔The disciples of Zhu and Lu each sought to prevail over the other, and their arguments differed. This policy essay indeed explains the reasons for this and then adjudicates between them by reference to the sages. Truly, its author understands these teachings!〕

Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: 〔This policy essay grasps the essential grounds of agreement and difference between Zhu and Lu.〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授鄭 批〔論學精到〕
吾道之大明於天下也如日月星辰之臨
照於下土而其大行也若江淮河漢之朝
宗於海是故其光不晦其流不息全體之
而聖者其於道也斯安焉安則圓神不滯
旁行不流蓋渾渾乎與道爲一而非道之
所能拘執矣是故其常其變其經其權其
禪繼其征伐其制作其刪述隨其所之何
敢以同異置論也脩是道而爲賢者其於
===
道也斯勉焉勉則以道爲的以聖爲宗以
聖人之言之布在方冊者爲依據而效習
焉於是家異其說人殊其言雖所論辯間
有不同要皆闡明性命之原究極理道之
本凡以羽翼典訓發揚聖蘊也開來繼往
功莫尚焉固可黨同伐異私加是非毀譽
哉嗚呼論人者當折諸聖而原其心焉可
也執事發策以朱陸異同爲問豈非憂道
學之失其眞也乎請究言之道學之名前
punctuated:
考試官教授鄭批〔論學精到。〕

吾道之大明於天下也，如日月星辰之臨照於下土；而其大行也，若江淮河漢之朝宗於海。是故其光不晦，其流不息。全體之而聖者，其於道也斯安焉。安則圓神不滯，旁行不流，蓋渾渾乎與道爲一，而非道之所能拘執矣。是故其常其變，其經其權，其禪繼其征伐，其制作其刪述，隨其所之，何敢以同異置論也？脩是道而爲賢者，其於道也斯勉焉。勉則以道爲的，以聖爲宗，以聖人之言之布在方冊者爲依據而效習焉。於是家異其說，人殊其言，雖所論辯間有不同，要皆闡明性命之原，究極理道之本，凡以羽翼典訓，發揚聖蘊也。開來繼往，功莫尚焉。固可黨同伐異，私加是非毀譽哉？嗚呼！論人者當折諸聖而原其心焉可也。執事發策，以朱陸異同爲問，豈非憂道學之失其眞也乎？請究言之。道學之名，前
translation_en:
Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: 〔The discussion of learning is penetrating and precise.〕

The great illumination of our Way throughout the world is like the sun, moon, and stars shining upon the earth below; its wide propagation is like the Jiang, Huai, He, and Han rivers flowing toward the sea as toward their sovereign. Thus its light never dims, and its current never ceases. Those who embody it fully and become sages are at ease in the Way. Being at ease, they are spiritually responsive in every direction without obstruction, extending their activity everywhere without drifting astray. Wholly integrated, they are one with the Way, rather than constrained by it. Thus, whether in constancy or change, in adherence to enduring principles or discretionary judgment, in abdication and succession or punitive campaigns, in establishing institutions or editing and transmitting the classics—wherever their course leads, how could one presume to judge them in terms of sameness and difference?

Those who cultivate this Way and become worthies apply themselves diligently to it. In their diligence, they take the Way as their target and the sages as their models; they rely on the sages’ words preserved in books, emulating and studying them. Consequently, schools differ in their teachings and individuals in their statements. Although their arguments sometimes differ, all are essentially elucidating the source of human nature and destiny and probing to the very foundation of principle and the Way. All seek to support the canonical teachings and bring forth the sages’ profound meaning. In carrying forward the past and opening the way for the future, their achievement is unsurpassed. Can one really side with those who agree and attack those who differ, arbitrarily pronouncing them right or wrong, disparaging or praising them?

Alas! Those who judge others should measure them against the sages and examine their underlying intentions. You gentlemen have posed a policy question concerning the similarities and differences between Zhu Xi and Lu Jiuyuan. Is this not out of concern that the Learning of the Way might lose its true character? Allow me to discuss this fully. As for the term ‘Learning of the Way,’ in earlier times…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
古無此羲皇開天太樸混蒙所謂上天之
載無聲無臭孰從而名之又孰從而言之
耶卦畫而天地之精兹焉洩矣堯舜繼之
衍而爲精一執中之訓傳心之要法無以
易此者已而禹湯文武君焉周公相焉故
其道行至孔子而師焉故其道明是故博
文約禮所以教顔子也明善誠身所以啓
曾子也其於虞廷精一之旨一而已矣子
思得其統而中庸作焉至其統括之妙乃
===
在於尊德性道問學之片詞舉脩德凝道
之大端以開示後學之進脩者昭昭也子
思傳之孟軻其盡心知性之言與夫知言
養氣之學蓋與誠明之訓實相表裏軻死
而不得其傳也漢有董子言正心而遺主
敬唐有韓愈言誠意而遺格致二子當世
名儒也所見所論所遺如此區區楊雄馬
融孔頴達諸子尚何望哉至於有宋濂溪
周子崛起而承之不由師傳默契道體其
punctuated:
古無此。羲皇開天，太樸混蒙，所謂「上天之載，無聲無臭」，孰從而名之，又孰從而言之耶？卦畫而天地之精兹焉洩矣。堯舜繼之，衍而爲精一執中之訓，傳心之要法無以易此者。已而禹湯文武君焉，周公相焉，故其道行；至孔子而師焉，故其道明。是故博文約禮，所以教顔子也；明善誠身，所以啓曾子也。其於虞廷精一之旨，一而已矣。子思得其統，而中庸作焉。至其統括之妙，乃在於「尊德性，道問學」之片詞。舉脩德凝道之大端，以開示後學之進脩者，昭昭也。子思傳之孟軻，其盡心知性之言，與夫知言養氣之學，蓋與誠明之訓實相表裏。軻死而不得其傳也。

漢有董子，言正心而遺主敬；唐有韓愈，言誠意而遺格致。二子當世名儒也，所見所論所遺如此，區區楊雄、馬融、孔頴達諸子，尚何望哉？至於有宋，濂溪周子崛起而承之，不由師傳，默契道體，其
translation_en:
…in antiquity there was no such designation. When Sovereign Fuxi opened up the world, primordial simplicity remained undifferentiated and obscure. As the saying goes, “The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell.” Who could then give them a name, and who could speak of them? Once the trigrams were drawn, the essential workings of Heaven and Earth were thereby revealed. Yao and Shun succeeded him, developing this into the teaching of refinement, single-mindedness, and holding fast to the mean. Nothing could replace this essential method of transmitting the mind. Thereafter Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu ruled as sovereigns, and the Duke of Zhou served as minister; thus their Way was put into practice. When Confucius came to serve as teacher, their Way was clarified. Thus broad learning in cultural matters and restraint through ritual were how he taught Master Yan; understanding goodness and making oneself sincere were how he instructed Master Zeng. These were entirely at one with the purport of refinement and single-mindedness taught at Shun’s court. Zisi received this lineage, and the Doctrine of the Mean was composed. The marvel of its comprehensive scope lies in the brief phrase “honor the virtuous nature and pursue inquiry and learning.” It plainly sets forth the principal means of cultivating virtue and firmly establishing the Way, showing later students how to advance in their cultivation. Zisi transmitted it to Meng Ke. His statements about fully realizing the mind and knowing one’s nature, together with his teachings on understanding words and nourishing vital energy, were indeed complementary to the teaching of sincerity and illumination. When Meng Ke died, no one received his transmission.

In the Han there was Master Dong, who spoke of rectifying the mind but omitted making reverence fundamental; in the Tang there was Han Yu, who spoke of making the intentions sincere but omitted investigating things and extending knowledge. These two were renowned Confucian scholars of their times. If such were their insights, their discussions, and their omissions, what could one still expect of such lesser figures as Yang Xiong, Ma Rong, and Kong Yingda? When the Song arrived, Master Zhou of Lianxi rose up and carried on this tradition. Without receiving it through a teacher, he tacitly apprehended the substance of the Way. His…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
所論著若太極圖若通書皆前聖之微言
千載之絕學而斯文賴以復振其後河南
程氏兄弟與夫橫渠張子者出相與講明
其學推周子以接乎子思孟氏之傳又推
子思孟氏以達乎孔子堯舜之統使聖人
之道燦然於世雖其門人各自為說而支
滴汗漫之病難乎免焉則固習其說而私
之者弊之也於程張何病哉嗣是而有朱
子繼作本周程之學以參諸游楊尹呂之
===
見有以會衆說之繁而折其衷又得呂祖
謙張敬夫輩往來上下考究精詳有以集
諸子之長而成其大蓋六經之註述大定
而後缺者補散者合畧者詳鳴者息此所
以上有功於列聖以纘其緒於千百載之
前下有大造於學者以指其迷於千百載
之後精乎無以議為也獨臨川陸氏九淵
兄弟意見稍有不同而二家之門人者流
又各是其師說是以朱陸異同之辨至今
punctuated: 所論著，若《太極圖》，若《通書》，皆前聖之微言、千載之絕學，而斯文賴以復振。其後，河南程氏兄弟與夫橫渠張子者出，相與講明其學，推周子以接乎子思、孟氏之傳，又推子思、孟氏以達乎孔子、堯舜之統，使聖人之道燦然於世。雖其門人各自為說，而支滴汗漫之病難乎免焉，則固習其說而私之者弊之也，於程、張何病哉？嗣是而有朱子繼作，本周、程之學，以參諸游、楊、尹、呂之見，有以會衆說之繁而折其衷；又得呂祖謙、張敬夫輩往來上下，考究精詳，有以集諸子之長而成其大。蓋六經之註述大定，而後缺者補，散者合，畧者詳，鳴者息。此所以上有功於列聖，以纘其緒於千百載之前；下有大造於學者，以指其迷於千百載之後。精乎，無以議為也！獨臨川陸氏九淵兄弟，意見稍有不同，而二家之門人者流，又各是其師說，是以朱、陸異同之辨至今
translation_en:
…His writings, such as the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tu) and the Comprehensive Writings (Tongshu), all conveyed the subtle teachings of the earlier sages and a learning whose transmission had been broken for a thousand years. Through them, this cultural tradition was revived. Thereafter, the Cheng brothers of Henan and Master Zhang of Hengqu emerged and together expounded his learning. They traced Master Zhou’s connection to the transmission of Zisi and Mengzi, and traced Zisi and Mengzi back to the succession of Confucius, Yao, and Shun, making the Way of the sages shine brilliantly in the world. Although their disciples each developed their own interpretations and could hardly avoid the faults of fragmentation and unchecked diffuseness [?], it was those who rigidly adhered to these interpretations and treated them as their private possession who corrupted the teaching. What fault could there be in Cheng and Zhang themselves?

Following them, Master Zhu arose to carry on their work. Taking the learning of Zhou and Cheng as his foundation, he examined it against the views of You, Yang, Yin, and Lü, bringing together their numerous interpretations and arriving at a balanced judgment. He also benefited from exchanges with Lü Zuqian, Zhang Jingfu, and others, exploring matters in every direction and investigating them with precision and thoroughness. Thus he gathered the strengths of the various masters and brought their learning to full fruition. Once the commentaries on the Six Classics were largely settled, omissions were supplied, scattered material brought together, abbreviated treatments elaborated, and contentious voices stilled. Thus he rendered service to the sages above him, continuing the thread they had handed down hundreds and thousands of years before; and he greatly benefited learners below him, pointing out their errors for hundreds and thousands of years thereafter. How refined his achievement was—beyond criticism!

Only Lu Jiuyuan and his brothers of Linchuan differed somewhat in their views. The followers of the two schools each upheld their own master’s teachings, and thus the debate over the agreements and differences between Zhu and Lu, down to the present day…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
未已也爲朱氏之說者主道問學焉蓋以
陸氏専於尊德性而畧於道問學其弊也
將流於禪學之空虛矣爲陸氏之學者主
尊德性焉蓋以朱氏先於道問學而次於
尊德性其弊也將流於世儒記誦訓詁之
習矣門戶旣分互相爭辯以求勝然就而
論之朱子之於格致亦取二程之說曰涵
養須用敬進學在致知夫苟存心而不致
知焉將使學者不至於廢學乎此朱陸異
===
同之大較也故常爲之說曰朱子之才近
曾子故其學也確子靜之才近顏子故其
悟也敏有曾子之魯必有三省之勤而後
一貫之道可聞有顏子之聰而不由博約
之訓拳拳而服膺焉吾知其不能見道於
卓爾矣此則象山初年之學似有所未盡
也雖然此言其始也未究其終也鵝湖之
論辯詳矣白鹿之會講再矣二公之見固
有始異終同者今觀象山之講君子喻於
punctuated:
未已也。爲朱氏之說者主道問學焉，蓋以陸氏専於尊德性而畧於道問學，其弊也將流於禪學之空虛矣。爲陸氏之學者主尊德性焉，蓋以朱氏先於道問學而次於尊德性，其弊也將流於世儒記誦訓詁之習矣。門戶旣分，互相爭辯以求勝。然就而論之，朱子之於格致，亦取二程之說曰：「涵養須用敬，進學在致知。」夫苟存心而不致知焉，將使學者不至於廢學乎？此朱陸異同之大較也。
故常爲之說曰：「朱子之才近曾子，故其學也確；子靜之才近顏子，故其悟也敏。有曾子之魯，必有三省之勤，而後一貫之道可聞；有顏子之聰，而不由博約之訓，拳拳而服膺焉，吾知其不能見道於卓爾矣。」此則象山初年之學似有所未盡也。雖然，此言其始也，未究其終也。鵝湖之論辯詳矣，白鹿之會講再矣，二公之見固有始異終同者。今觀象山之講「君子喻於
translation_en:
…has not yet ceased. Those who uphold Zhu’s teachings emphasize pursuing inquiry and learning. They consider that Lu concentrates on honoring the moral nature while neglecting inquiry and learning, a failing that will lead to the emptiness of Chan Buddhist learning. Those who follow Lu’s learning emphasize honoring the moral nature. They consider that Zhu puts inquiry and learning first and honoring the moral nature second, a failing that will lead to the ordinary Confucian scholars’ habits of memorization, recitation, and textual glossing. Once separate schools had formed, they disputed with one another, each seeking to prevail. Yet, considering the matter closely, Master Zhu, in his treatment of investigating things and extending knowledge, also adopted the teaching of the two Cheng brothers: “Nurturing oneself requires reverent attentiveness; advancing in learning lies in extending knowledge.” If one merely preserves the mind without extending knowledge, would this not lead students to abandon learning? Such is the broad outline of the similarities and differences between Zhu and Lu.
Thus I have often explained it as follows: “Master Zhu’s natural abilities resembled those of Master Zeng, and so his learning was solid; Zijing’s natural abilities resembled those of Master Yan, and so his insight was quick. Someone with Master Zeng’s slowness must also possess his diligence in examining himself on three counts before he can hear of the Way unified by a single thread. Someone with Master Yan’s intelligence who does not follow the teaching of broadening learning and restraining oneself through ritual, earnestly taking it to heart, will, I am certain, be unable to perceive the Way standing loftily before him.” In this respect, Xiangshan’s learning in his early years seems to have been incomplete. Nevertheless, this speaks of his beginnings without fully examining his later development. The debates at Ehu were thorough, and at Bailu they met again to lecture. There were indeed points on which the two masters’ views differed at first but ultimately converged. Now, examining Xiangshan’s lecture on “The gentleman understands …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
義也朱子以爲切中學者深痼之病及其
與項平父書也亦云子靜專尊德性熹平
生道問學之功多又云子靜好處自不可
掩此則象山晚年進德自知早年之失而
加意窮理故朱子有棄短集長之說而朱
子亦自悔其論說太廣註釋太多則於象
山尊德性之說蓋又兼而有之也是故朱
之道問學者非朱之異也所道者吾聖人
之問學也然謂之道問學之功多者非謂
===
棄德性而不尊也如是而謂之世儒之訓
詁吾不信也陸氏之尊德性也非陸之異
也所尊者吾聖人之德性也然謂之尊德
性之功多者非謂其棄問學而不道也如
是而謂之禪學之空虛吾不信也則夫謂
其學之入於禪者豈非恐其徒之流弊至
此歟昔者子夏篤信聖人而親受其業再
傳而爲田子方莊周豈子夏之道然哉傳
之者失其眞耳猶之學夷惠之清和者先
punctuated:
義也，朱子以爲切中學者深痼之病。及其與項平父書也，亦云：「子靜專尊德性，熹平生道問學之功多。」又云：「子靜好處，自不可掩。」此則象山晚年進德，自知早年之失，而加意窮理，故朱子有棄短集長之說。而朱子亦自悔其論說太廣，註釋太多，則於象山尊德性之說，蓋又兼而有之也。
是故朱之道問學者，非朱之異也，所道者吾聖人之問學也。然謂之道問學之功多者，非謂棄德性而不尊也。如是而謂之世儒之訓詁，吾不信也。陸氏之尊德性也，非陸之異也，所尊者吾聖人之德性也。然謂之尊德性之功多者，非謂其棄問學而不道也。如是而謂之禪學之空虛，吾不信也。則夫謂其學之入於禪者，豈非恐其徒之流弊至此歟？昔者子夏篤信聖人，而親受其業，再傳而爲田子方、莊周，豈子夏之道然哉？傳之者失其眞耳。猶之學夷惠之清和者，先
translation_en:
…righteousness, Zhu Xi considered it to strike directly at a deeply entrenched failing among students. In his letter to Xiang Pingfu, he also said: “Zijing concentrates on honoring the moral nature; I, Xi, have throughout my life devoted more effort to pursuing inquiry and study.” He further said: “Zijing’s strengths certainly cannot be obscured.” This shows that Xiangshan, as he advanced in virtue in his later years, recognized his earlier errors and applied himself more earnestly to investigating principle. Thus Zhu Xi spoke of discarding shortcomings and bringing together strengths. Zhu Xi himself also regretted that his discussions were too extensive and his annotations too numerous; thus he also incorporated Xiangshan’s teaching of honoring the moral nature.
Therefore, Zhu’s pursuit of inquiry and study was no distinctive invention of his: what he pursued was the inquiry and study of our sages. To say that he devoted more effort to inquiry and study does not mean that he abandoned the moral nature and failed to honor it. To characterize this as the mere textual exegesis of conventional Confucians—I cannot accept that. Likewise, Lu’s honoring of the moral nature was no distinctive invention of his: what he honored was the moral nature taught by our sages. To say that he devoted more effort to honoring the moral nature does not mean that he abandoned inquiry and study and failed to pursue them. To characterize this as the emptiness of Chan learning—I cannot accept that. Was the claim that his learning slipped into Chan not prompted by fear that the errors of his followers might eventually lead to this? In former times, Zixia firmly trusted the sage and personally received his teachings; yet after two transmissions these became the learning of Tian Zifang and Zhuang Zhou. Could this have been the character of Zixia’s Way? Those who transmitted it merely lost its true substance. It is like those who study the purity of Boyi and the harmony of Liuxia Hui, who first acquire…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
得其隘與不恭而申韓刑名之害蓋原於
道德之意君子之學其初何可不愼也後
之言學者吾惑焉曰主靜曰存心則羣聚
而尊之曰此象山之學也吾師之弟子也
一聞言程朱之學者則羣指而譏之曰此
世儒之見也王通氏曰成我者夫子也通
於夫子受罔極之恩後學之於朱子猶王
通之於夫子也童而習之白首而乃爲操
戈之計忍乎哉嗚呼陸氏之學由存心以
===
達於致知今則幷其知而不致矣朱氏之
學由致知以達於存心今則謂其不復致
力於心矣不究其心之同而惟究其迹之
異執一偏之見而欲以定天下後世之公
是也其可乎要之千聖一心萬古一道有
象山之高明而後可以言顏子之愚有晦
庵之純粹而後可以言曾子之魯由其論
之異以求其心之同由其心之同以求其
道之一要皆以求至乎聖人之道也是故
punctuated:
得其隘與不恭，而申韓刑名之害，蓋原於道德之意。君子之學，其初何可不愼也？

後之言學者，吾惑焉。曰主靜，曰存心，則羣聚而尊之，曰：「此象山之學也，吾師之弟子也。」一聞言程朱之學者，則羣指而譏之，曰：「此世儒之見也。」王通氏曰：「成我者夫子也。」通於夫子受罔極之恩。後學之於朱子，猶王通之於夫子也。童而習之，白首而乃爲操戈之計，忍乎哉？嗚呼！陸氏之學，由存心以達於致知，今則幷其知而不致矣。朱氏之學，由致知以達於存心，今則謂其不復致力於心矣。不究其心之同，而惟究其迹之異，執一偏之見，而欲以定天下後世之公是也，其可乎？

要之，千聖一心，萬古一道。有象山之高明，而後可以言顏子之愚；有晦庵之純粹，而後可以言曾子之魯。由其論之異，以求其心之同；由其心之同，以求其道之一。要皆以求至乎聖人之道也。是故
translation_en:
…first acquire their narrowness and irreverence; and the harmful doctrines of punishments and names taught by Shen Buhai and Han Fei originated, indeed, in the ideas of the Way and its virtue. How could a gentleman fail to exercise care at the outset of his learning?

I am perplexed by those of later times who speak of learning. When someone speaks of making stillness primary or preserving the mind, they gather together and honor him, saying, “This is the learning of Xiangshan; he is a disciple of our teacher.” Yet as soon as they hear someone speak of the learning of the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi, they all point at him and mock him, saying, “These are the views of commonplace scholars.” Wang Tong said, “It is the Master who has brought me to fulfillment.” Tong received boundless kindness from the Master. Later students stand in relation to Master Zhu just as Wang Tong stood in relation to the Master. Having studied his teachings in childhood, can they bear, once white-haired, to devise plans to turn their weapons against him? Alas! Master Lu’s learning proceeds from preserving the mind to extending knowledge; now, however, they even neglect to extend their knowledge. Master Zhu’s learning proceeds from extending knowledge to preserving the mind; now, however, they claim that he devoted no further effort to the mind. Rather than investigate what their minds shared, they investigate only the differences in their outward practices. Can they cling to a one-sided view and presume thereby to determine what all the world and future generations should acknowledge as right?

In essence, the thousand sages share one mind, and through all ages there is one Way. Only after attaining Xiangshan’s loftiness and illumination can one speak of Master Yan’s apparent foolishness; only after attaining Hui’an’s purity can one speak of Master Zeng’s apparent dullness. Through the differences in their arguments, seek what their minds share; through what their minds share, seek the unity of their Way. The essential aim in all this is to attain the Way of the sages. Thus…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
深山窮谷遐陬僻壤其顯晦陰晴之不同
也而其得照於日月星辰之明同也澗溪
沼沚潢汙行潦之於江淮河漢之流不同
也而其趨下以歸於海則同也夫是之謂
大同中庸曰道之不行也我知之矣知者
過之愚者不及也道之不明也我知之矣
賢者過之不肖者不及也嗚呼中庸其至
矣乎請以是而爲明問復
第三問
金達
同考試官教諭李　批　〔選舉考課〕
國家官人要法也法本盡善顧奉行者何如耳使銜鑑精明則舉錯
自當子能言及于此且他作俱可觀不當爲得人
賀耶
考試官學正張　批　〔通篇斟酌三代及漢〕
唐宋得失知指諸掌末復以用法在人尤爲有見子
〔必究心〕
當世之務者歟之
punctuated:
深山窮谷、遐陬僻壤，其顯晦陰晴之不同也，而其得照於日月星辰之明同也。澗溪沼沚、潢汙行潦之於江淮河漢之流不同也，而其趨下以歸於海則同也。夫是之謂大同。《中庸》曰：「道之不行也，我知之矣：知者過之，愚者不及也。道之不明也，我知之矣：賢者過之，不肖者不及也。」嗚呼！中庸其至矣乎！請以是而爲明問復。
第三問
金達
同考試官教諭李批〔選舉考課〕：國家官人要法也。法本盡善，顧奉行者何如耳。使銜鑑精明，則舉錯自當。子能言及于此，且他作俱可觀，不當爲得人賀耶？
考試官學正張批〔通篇斟酌三代及漢〕：唐宋得失，知指諸掌。末復以用法在人，尤爲有見。子〔必究心〕當世之務者歟？之
translation_en:
…Deep mountains and remote valleys, distant corners and secluded lands differ in their exposure and concealment, shade and sunshine; yet all alike receive the light of the sun, moon, and stars. Ravines, streams, ponds, islets, stagnant pools, and rainwater differ from the flowing waters of the Jiang, Huai, He, and Han rivers; yet all alike tend downward and return to the sea. This is what is called the great unity. The Doctrine of the Mean says: “Why the Way is not practiced, I know: the wise go beyond it, and the foolish fall short of it. Why the Way is not understood, I know: the worthy go beyond it, and the unworthy fall short of it.” Alas! How consummate is the mean! I offer this in reply to your discerning question.
Third Policy Question
Jin Da
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔Selection and appointment, and evaluation of performance〕 are essential methods by which the state appoints officials. The methods themselves are entirely sound; everything depends on those who implement them. If their discernment is clear [?], appointments and dismissals will naturally be appropriate. You have addressed this point, and your other compositions are all worthy of attention. Should we not celebrate having found a worthy man?
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: 〔Throughout the essay, you weigh the Three Dynasties and the Han〕 and the successes and failures of the Tang and Song, knowing them as clearly as the palm of your hand [?]. At the end, you return to the point that applying methods depends on people—a particularly perceptive observation. You 〔must have devoted your attention to〕 the affairs of the present age, must you not? [The transcription ends with an isolated 之, of uncertain meaning.]

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授鄭　批〔連日披閱場屋類皆擬拾陳言敷演成篇殊爲可厭晚得此作酌古準今亦千餘言供〕
〔鑒鑒有實用于其抱經濟之學者耶敬服敬服〕
聖王所以宰制萬物論擢俊彥安乂海宇
洋洋乎德意宣布刑罰省而威行如流無
他故焉由其道故也古之言選舉考課者
任道後之言選舉考課者任法此古今之
異而治否之繇也是故吾選於衆而舉錯
焉則舉錯以天下而不以我雖舉錯一二
===
人焉而所以行乎億千萬人者此何可限
量歟故曰任道吾泥其法而進退焉而黜
陟焉擇之未必其精而考之未必皆容如
是而欲得賢不肖之眞以昌其化於天下
吾知其必不能矣故曰任法明乎此者可
與言政理矣請因明問而悉言之夫自咨
汝岳牧九德咸事選舉之制其殆昉於是
乎敷言試功黜陟幽明歷代沿之遂成考
課之法爰考其時百僚師師百工惟時唐
punctuated:
考試官教授鄭批〔連日披閱場屋，類皆擬拾陳言，敷演成篇，殊爲可厭。晚得此作，酌古準今，亦千餘言供〕〔鑒鑒有實用，于其抱經濟之學者耶？敬服！敬服！〕
聖王所以宰制萬物，論擢俊彥，安乂海宇，洋洋乎德意宣布，刑罰省而威行如流，無他故焉，由其道故也。古之言選舉考課者任道，後之言選舉考課者任法，此古今之異，而治否之繇也。是故吾選於衆而舉錯焉，則舉錯以天下而不以我。雖舉錯一二人焉，而所以行乎億千萬人者，此何可限量歟？故曰任道。吾泥其法而進退焉，而黜陟焉，擇之未必其精，而考之未必皆容。如是而欲得賢不肖之眞，以昌其化於天下，吾知其必不能矣。故曰任法。明乎此者，可與言政理矣。請因明問而悉言之。
夫自咨汝岳牧，九德咸事，選舉之制，其殆昉於是乎？敷言試功，黜陟幽明，歷代沿之，遂成考課之法。爰考其時，百僚師師，百工惟時，唐
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Professor: 〔Over successive days of reading examination scripts, I have found that nearly all imitate and pick up stale expressions, expanding them into essays. This is exceedingly tiresome. Late in the process I obtained this piece, which weighs antiquity against the present; its thousand-odd words are offered〕〔for scrutiny and have practical value [?]. Might its author possess learning suited to ordering the state and bringing relief to the people [?]? My respects! My respects!〕
The sage kings governed all things, assessed and promoted outstanding men [?], and brought peace and order throughout the realm. Their beneficent intentions spread far and wide; punishments were few, yet their authority flowed like water. There was no other reason for this: it was because they followed the Way. Those in antiquity who discussed selecting and recommending men and assessing their performance relied on the Way; those in later ages who discussed these matters relied on regulations. This is the difference between antiquity and later times, and the reason for good government or its absence. Thus, when I select from among the multitude and appoint or set men aside, I do so for the sake of all under Heaven, rather than for myself. Although only one or two men may be appointed or set aside, the effects extend to countless millions. How could their reach be measured? This is what is meant by relying on the Way. If I cling to regulations when advancing and dismissing men, demoting and promoting them, those selected will not necessarily be the finest, and the assessments will not necessarily all be fitting [?]. To proceed thus and yet hope to ascertain men's true worth or unworthiness, thereby extending the ruler's transforming influence throughout the realm—I know this must be impossible. This is what is meant by relying on regulations. With someone who understands this, one may discuss the principles of government. Allow me to respond to your discerning question by explaining fully.
Beginning with “Ah, you chiefs of the mountains and regional governors,” and “those possessing the nine virtues all serving in office,” did the system of selection and recommendation perhaps originate here? “Have them set forth their words and test their achievements”; “dismiss the obscure and advance the illustrious”: successive dynasties followed these practices, and they eventually became the rules for assessing officials' performance. Examining that age, we find that “the hundred officials took one another as models,” and “all the officers fulfilled their duties in due season.” Tang …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
虞之盛典謨所稱何以加焉逮於成周其
法大備考之周官司馬以德詔爵以功詔
祿以能詔事以久奠食以詔王治而又有
聽官府之六計曰廉善曰廉能曰廉敬曰
廉正曰廉法曰廉辨以弊羣吏之治至于
歲終則有歲會聽其政事而廢置之至于
三歲則又大計羣吏之治而爲之誅賞焉
蓋視唐虞之法爲益密矣漢初有選部尚
書自郡縣以上始赴調選掾曹以下得自
辟除其法似簡而未免私濫之弊至成帝
始立常侍等官以主公卿郡國之選光武
又改爲吏部尚書以總三曹之事其選法
漸以備矣而考課之法則郡守得課令長
刺史得課守相由御史丞相以上之天子
其甘泉明堂之受計論百官而明黜陟者
雖未盡合乎古制然亦不失乎成周之遺
意也唐之選法分爲文武文選吏部主之
武選兵部主之而又置考功以掌百官功
punctuated:
虞之盛，典謨所稱，何以加焉？逮於成周，其法大備。考之《周官》，司馬以德詔爵，以功詔祿，以能詔事，以久奠食，以詔王治。而又有聽官府之六計，曰廉善，曰廉能，曰廉敬，曰廉正，曰廉法，曰廉辨，以弊羣吏之治。至于歲終，則有歲會，聽其政事而廢置之；至于三歲，則又大計羣吏之治，而爲之誅賞焉。蓋視唐虞之法爲益密矣。

漢初有選部尚書，自郡縣以上始赴調選，掾曹以下得自辟除。其法似簡，而未免私濫之弊。至成帝，始立常侍等官，以主公卿郡國之選。光武又改爲吏部尚書，以總三曹之事，其選法漸以備矣。而考課之法，則郡守得課令長，刺史得課守相，由御史丞相以上之天子。其甘泉明堂之受計，論百官而明黜陟者，雖未盡合乎古制，然亦不失乎成周之遺意也。

唐之選法，分爲文武。文選，吏部主之；武選，兵部主之。而又置考功，以掌百官功
translation_en:
…the flourishing age of Yu, celebrated in the Canons and Counsels—how could it be surpassed? By the time of the Zhou dynasty, these procedures had become fully developed. Examining the Offices of Zhou, we find that the Minister of War advised on ranks according to virtue, stipends according to achievement, and duties according to ability; he established emoluments according to length of service, thereby advising the king on government. There were also six criteria for assessing the government offices: integrity with goodness, integrity with competence, integrity with diligence, integrity with uprightness, integrity with adherence to law, and integrity with discernment. These were used to judge the administration of all officials. At the end of each year, annual accounts were submitted, and officials’ administration was reviewed to determine their dismissal or retention. Every three years, there was also a comprehensive assessment of all officials’ administration, followed by punishments and rewards. These procedures were thus even more detailed than those of Tang and Yu.

In the early Han, there was a Minister of Personnel Selection. Appointments at the commandery and county levels and above went through selection and assignment, while subordinate clerks and those below them could be appointed directly by their superiors. These procedures appeared simple, but did not escape the abuses of favoritism and indiscriminate appointment. Only under Emperor Cheng were such offices as Regular Attendant established to oversee the selection of the highest court officials and officials of the commanderies and kingdoms. Guangwu subsequently changed the office to Minister of Personnel, placing it in overall charge of the affairs of the three bureaus. The procedures for selecting officials thus gradually became complete. As for performance evaluation, commandery governors could assess county magistrates and chiefs, and regional inspectors could assess commandery governors and kingdom chancellors; the results were submitted through the censors and the Counselor-in-Chief to the Son of Heaven. The reception of accounts at the Hall of Light at Ganquan, the assessment of all officials, and the clear determination of demotions and promotions did not wholly conform to ancient institutions, yet still preserved the intent handed down from the Zhou.

Under the Tang, selection procedures were divided into civil and military branches. The Ministry of Personnel directed civil selection, and the Ministry of War directed military selection. A Bureau of Evaluations was also established to take charge of all officials’ merits…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
過善惡之考大率舉四善二十七最以爲
例而善狀之外又有侍近選司考較之最
下逮宿衛屯牧莫不有稽是主之以善兼
之以最而差爲九等似可究功過之實矣
然專於任人罔知任法而謂能究其實者
否也宋之選法兼總左右文臣屬左選武
臣屬右選至於興國元祐紹興之考亦不
越四善三等以爲則也蓋四善則參諸唐
法而稽差之要則先於治事功課撫養之
===
最至於給紙磨勘等法是通取善最參考
治行而第爲三等似可覈名實之眞矣然
專於任法畧於任人而謂能覈其眞者否
也大抵漢法尚爲近古唐宋之法雖詳而
弊愈滋其去成周之制遠矣我
國家用人參考前代之制而損益之以科目
取士以資格論官制盡善矣或謂其若狹
與拘者蓋徒見成周選舉之制於今若或
有閡而不知科目資格之設可以囿中材
punctuated:
過、善惡之考，大率舉四善二十七最以爲例，而善狀之外，又有侍近、選司考較之最，下逮宿衛、屯牧，莫不有稽。是主之以善，兼之以最，而差爲九等，似可究功過之實矣。然專於任人，罔知任法，而謂能究其實者，否也。
宋之選法，兼總左右，文臣屬左選，武臣屬右選。至於興國、元祐、紹興之考，亦不越四善三等以爲則也。蓋四善則參諸唐法，而稽差之要，則先於治事、功課、撫養之最，至於給紙、磨勘等法，是通取善最，參考治行，而第爲三等，似可覈名實之眞矣。然專於任法，畧於任人，而謂能覈其眞者，否也。
大抵漢法尚爲近古，唐宋之法雖詳，而弊愈滋，其去成周之制遠矣。我國家用人，參考前代之制而損益之，以科目取士，以資格論官，制盡善矣。或謂其若狹與拘者，蓋徒見成周選舉之制於今若或有閡，而不知科目資格之設，可以囿中材
translation_en:
…faults and good or bad conduct. In general, the four virtues and twenty-seven criteria of excellence served as the standards. Besides records of virtuous conduct, there were also criteria of excellence for evaluating palace attendants and officials responsible for selection; these extended down to palace guards and those managing agricultural colonies and pastures, leaving none without a basis for assessment. Virtue was thus the principal consideration, supplemented by excellence, and officials were ranked in nine grades. This would seem sufficient to ascertain their actual merits and faults. Yet to rely exclusively on people, without understanding reliance on rules, and claim that one can ascertain the facts—is this possible? No.
The Song system of selection encompassed both the left and right branches: civil officials belonged to the left selection branch, and military officials to the right. The evaluations of the Xingguo, Yuanyou, and Shaoxing eras likewise took no more than the four virtues and three grades as their standards. The four virtues drew upon Tang regulations, while the essentials of assessment and ranking gave priority to excellence in administering affairs, accomplishments in office, and nurturing the people. Together with such procedures as issuing assessment sheets and scrutinizing service records, this system considered virtues and excellence comprehensively, examined administrative conduct, and assigned officials to three grades. This would seem sufficient to verify whether reputation matched reality. Yet to rely exclusively on rules, while neglecting the people entrusted with their application, and claim that one can verify the truth—is this possible? No.
On the whole, Han regulations remained close to antiquity. Although those of the Tang and Song were detailed, abuses multiplied, and they departed far from the institutions of the Zhou. In employing men, our dynasty has consulted the institutions of preceding ages, making additions and reductions. It selects scholars through examination categories and assesses officials by their qualifications and seniority: the system is altogether sound. Some say that it seems narrow and restrictive. They merely perceive that the Zhou system of selection and recommendation might encounter obstacles today, without understanding that examination categories and requirements of qualification and seniority were established to keep men of middling ability within bounds…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
而豪傑不羈之士固不爲所限也爲今之
慮不患科目資格之不得人而特患選法
之不精耳三年一考六年再考九年通考
法甚詳矣而或謂其似繁與畧者蓋徒見
成周考課之制於今若或不同而不知年
資格例之論所以待常流而聞望異能之
士固不安於是也爲今之慮不在人法之
偏任而在考法之不審耳故科目非狹也
資格非拘也而吾必曰司選法者之狹與
===
拘也任法非繁也任人非畧也而吾必曰
司考法者之繁與畧也蓋選法而公且明
矣則鑽刺之途塞覬圖中原名郡以自封
殖者何人也倖進之門閉用智用動以徼
不次之擢者何人也如是而人才彙征仕
路清泰由科目而得者循資格而用者大
德小德大賢小賢咸效其用而選法莫良
於此矣其於狹若拘也曷病焉至於考課
之法則循其資望而又嚴核其行實以參
punctuated: 而豪傑不羈之士固不爲所限也。爲今之慮，不患科目資格之不得人，而特患選法之不精耳。三年一考，六年再考，九年通考，法甚詳矣。而或謂其似繁與畧者，蓋徒見成周考課之制於今若或不同，而不知年資格例之論所以待常流，而聞望異能之士固不安於是也。爲今之慮，不在人法之偏任，而在考法之不審耳。故科目非狹也，資格非拘也，而吾必曰司選法者之狹與拘也；任法非繁也，任人非畧也，而吾必曰司考法者之繁與畧也。蓋選法而公且明矣，則鑽刺之途塞，覬圖中原名郡以自封殖者何人也？倖進之門閉，用智用動以徼不次之擢者何人也？如是而人才彙征，仕路清泰，由科目而得者、循資格而用者，大德小德，大賢小賢，咸效其用，而選法莫良於此矣。其於狹若拘也，曷病焉？至於考課之法，則循其資望，而又嚴核其行實，以參
translation_en:
…yet outstanding, independent men are certainly not constrained by them. The concern today is not that examination categories and qualifications fail to yield suitable men, but simply that the methods of selection are insufficiently refined. An assessment after three years, a second after six, and a comprehensive assessment after nine: these regulations are very detailed. Yet some call them seemingly cumbersome and cursory. They see only that the Zhou system of performance assessment appears in some respects different from that of today, without understanding that rules concerning seniority and qualifications are intended for ordinary men; men of reputation and exceptional ability certainly do not rest content within these limits. The concern today lies not in relying disproportionately on either men or regulations, but in insufficient care in the methods of assessment.
