司考法者之繁與畧也蓋選法而公且明
矣則鑽刺之途塞覬圖中原名郡以自封
殖者何人也倖進之門閉用智用動以徼
不次之擢者何人也如是而人才彙征仕
路清泰由科目而得者循資格而用者大
德小德大賢小賢咸效其用而選法莫良
於此矣其於狹若拘也曷病焉至於考課
之法則循其資望而又嚴核其行實以參
punctuated: 而豪傑不羈之士固不爲所限也。爲今之慮，不患科目資格之不得人，而特患選法之不精耳。三年一考，六年再考，九年通考，法甚詳矣。而或謂其似繁與畧者，蓋徒見成周考課之制於今若或不同，而不知年資格例之論所以待常流，而聞望異能之士固不安於是也。爲今之慮，不在人法之偏任，而在考法之不密耳。故科目非狹也，資格非拘也，而吾必曰司選法者之狹與拘也；任法非繁也，任人非畧也，而吾必曰司考法者之繁與畧也。蓋選法而公且明矣，則鑽刺之途塞，覬圖中原名郡以自封殖者何人也？倖進之門閉，用智用動以徼不次之擢者何人也？如是而人才彙征，仕路清泰，由科目而得者、循資格而用者，大德小德，大賢小賢，咸效其用，而選法莫良於此矣。其於狹若拘也，曷病焉？至於考課之法，則循其資望，而又嚴核其行實，以參
translation_en:
…Yet men of outstanding talent and untrammeled spirit are certainly not constrained by these provisions. The concern today is not that examination categories and eligibility requirements fail to secure suitable men, but simply that the methods of selection lack precision. An evaluation after three years, a second after six years, and a comprehensive evaluation after nine years: these regulations are very detailed. Some nevertheless describe them as cumbersome or cursory. Such people see only that the present system of performance evaluation differs in certain respects from that of the Zhou dynasty; they do not understand that judgments based on seniority, qualifications, and established rules are intended for ordinary men, while men of reputation and exceptional ability certainly do not remain content within these bounds. The concern today lies not in placing undue reliance on either men or regulations, but in insufficient rigor in the methods of evaluation.

Thus, examination categories are not narrow, nor are eligibility requirements restrictive. I would insist that it is those administering selection who are narrow and restrictive. Reliance on regulations is not cumbersome, nor is reliance on men cursory. I would insist that it is those administering evaluation who are cumbersome and cursory. If selection is impartial and discerning, the avenues for scheming to obtain office will be blocked. Who then could covet posts in celebrated commanderies of the Central Plain to enrich and entrench himself? If the gates to advancement through favor are closed, who could employ cunning and maneuvering [?] to seek promotion outside the regular order? In this way, talented men would advance together, and the paths of official service would be clear and orderly. Those recruited through examinations and those appointed according to their qualifications—men of greater or lesser virtue, of greater or lesser worth—would all put their abilities to use. No method of selection could be better than this. What grounds would there be to complain of narrowness or restriction?

As for methods of performance evaluation, one should take account of officials’ seniority and standing, while also rigorously examining their actual conduct and achievements, in order to weigh these against…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
酌乎輿論則雖洛陽少年驟致通顯亦不
以爲嫌爲吏者至長子孫亦不以爲久催
科政拙若陽城者吾得以程其能而僞增
戶口如王成者吾得以察其詐其能者進
而不能者斯下下矣考課之法若此誰議
其繁與畧也大抵天生賢才自足以供一
代之用何至借才於異代哉科目取人豈
在唐虞三代下也漢舉孝廉而徐淑以冒
年進則所謂茂材卓行濫叨章服者豈盡
無之唐宋以科目而陸贄韓愈裴度李絳
諸人與夫韓范富歐司馬光朱熹輩皆碩
輔名儒焉是不可以類觀乎其或有不然
者又安可罪法之不善爾也無乃司激勸
者之舛其道歟孔子曰舉直錯諸枉能使
枉者直然則化導之機亦在舉錯之得其
當爾又何必復鄉舉里選之制盡三載六
計之法然後爲備哉此一得之見也惟執
事進而教之
punctuated: 酌乎輿論，則雖洛陽少年驟致通顯，亦不以爲嫌；爲吏者至長子孫，亦不以爲久。催科政拙若陽城者，吾得以程其能；而僞增戶口如王成者，吾得以察其詐。其能者進，而不能者斯下下矣。考課之法若此，誰議其繁與畧也？大抵天生賢才，自足以供一代之用，何至借才於異代哉？科目取人，豈在唐虞三代下也？漢舉孝廉，而徐淑以冒年進，則所謂茂材卓行、濫叨章服者，豈盡無之？唐宋以科目，而陸贄、韓愈、裴度、李絳諸人，與夫韓、范、富、歐、司馬光、朱熹輩，皆碩輔名儒焉，是不可以類觀乎？其或有不然者，又安可罪法之不善爾也？無乃司激勸者之舛其道歟？孔子曰：「舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。」然則化導之機，亦在舉錯之得其當爾，又何必復鄉舉里選之制，盡三載六計之法，然後爲備哉？此一得之見也，惟執事進而教之。
translation_en:
…weigh public opinion, then even if a young man from Luoyang rapidly attains high and prominent office, this need not arouse misgivings; nor need an official’s service be considered too long merely because it continues until his children and grandchildren have grown. In the case of someone like Yang Cheng, inept at administering tax collection, we can assess his abilities; in the case of someone like Wang Cheng, who falsely inflated household and population figures, we can detect his fraud. The capable will advance, while the incapable will be demoted [?]. If performance evaluations operate in this way, who could criticize their complexity or brevity?

Heaven produces worthy talent sufficient for the needs of each age: why should we have to borrow talent from another age? How could recruitment through examinations be inferior to that under Tang and Yu or the Three Dynasties? The Han recommended the filial and incorrupt, yet Xu Shu gained advancement by falsifying his age. Can it be that among those designated as possessing outstanding talent and exemplary conduct, none undeservedly received official robes and insignia? The Tang and Song used examinations, and men such as Lu Zhi, Han Yu, Pei Du, and Li Jiang, together with Han, Fan, Fu, Ou, Sima Guang, and Zhu Xi, were all eminent ministers or renowned Confucian scholars. Can we not judge the system by such examples? If some proved otherwise, how could we blame the system as defective? Might it not instead be that those responsible for encouraging and motivating men have gone astray in their methods?

Confucius said: “Raise up the upright and place them above the crooked, and you can make the crooked upright.” Thus, the key to moral transformation and guidance also lies in making the proper choices about whom to advance and whom to set aside. Why must we restore the system of recommendation by districts and selection by villages, and fully implement triennial evaluations and the six criteria of assessment, before considering our arrangements complete? This is but one modest insight of mine. I ask that you receive it and instruct me.

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
第四問
同考試官教諭招　批
劉憲
〔通幽明之故達古今之變斯可謂之儒況天人一理星度反天象之顯著者詎曰不知可乎〕
〔子非徒知之於前人之占候得失俱能論說如指諸掌末復論議而不盡其詞足以占子之所養矣〕
考試官學正張　批
〔天象可以理推者也子不歸之數而歸之理其言之有見者乎〕
考試官教授鄭　批
〔象緯之學鮮生若答者絕少子能究之而善言其故亦可謂擅場之作矣使美人健美〕
===
羨
攷象緯哲機祥察於無形者莫尚乎智成
幽贊之能協皇極之用者莫大乎聖人蓋
曆象日月星辰在璇璣玉衡此天道也故
惟智者爲能明敬授人時以齊七政此王
政也故惟聖人爲能體是以明於經斯明
於天道矣明於天道斯明於王政矣執事
策諸生若曰儒者無不知也天道政紀宜
punctuated:
第四問

同考試官教諭招批。劉憲。
〔通幽明之故，達古今之變，斯可謂之儒。況天人一理，星度反天象之顯著者，詎曰不知可乎？〕
〔子非徒知之，於前人之占候得失，俱能論說，如指諸掌。末復論議而不盡其詞，足以占子之所養矣。〕

考試官學正張批。
〔天象可以理推者也。子不歸之數而歸之理，其言之有見者乎？〕

考試官教授鄭批。
〔象緯之學，鮮生若答者絕少。子能究之而善言其故，亦可謂擅場之作矣。使美人健美〕

羨。

攷象緯，哲機祥，察於無形者，莫尚乎智；成幽贊之能，協皇極之用者，莫大乎聖人。蓋曆象日月星辰，在璇璣玉衡，此天道也，故惟智者爲能明；敬授人時，以齊七政，此王政也，故惟聖人爲能體。是以明於經，斯明於天道矣；明於天道，斯明於王政矣。執事策諸生，若曰：「儒者無不知也，天道政紀宜
translation_en:
Fourth Policy Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, on Liu Xian’s answer:
〔One who comprehends the workings of the unseen and the manifest and understands changes past and present may indeed be called a Confucian scholar. Moreover, Heaven and humanity share a single principle, and the positions of the stars are conspicuous manifestations of celestial phenomena [?]. How could it be acceptable to profess ignorance of them?〕
〔You do more than merely understand this subject: you can discuss both the successes and the failures of earlier observers’ prognostications as clearly as pointing to something in your palm. At the end you offer further discussion without exhausting what you have to say; this is sufficient to reveal the depth of your cultivation.〕

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor:
〔Celestial phenomena can be inferred through principle. You attribute them to principle rather than numerical calculations: surely your words show insight?〕

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Professor:
〔In the study of celestial configurations, students who answer as you do are exceedingly rare [?]. You can investigate the subject thoroughly and explain its underlying reasons well: this may indeed be called an outstanding composition. The closing phrase is garbled: “make the beautiful person robust and beautiful” [?].〕

Admiration [?].

For examining celestial configurations, discerning incipient signs [?], and perceiving what has no visible form, nothing surpasses wisdom; for accomplishing the work of assisting the hidden processes of transformation and bringing into accord the operation of the August Norm, none is greater than the sage. Computing and observing the sun, moon, and stars by means of the armillary instrument and jade sighting tube concerns the Way of Heaven; thus only the wise can understand it. Reverently communicating the seasons to the people and thereby bringing the Seven Regulators—the sun, moon, and five planets—into harmony concerns kingly government; thus only the sage can embody it. Therefore, understanding the Classics leads to understanding the Way of Heaven; understanding the Way of Heaven leads to understanding kingly government. In setting this policy question for us students, you say, in effect: “There is nothing a Confucian scholar does not know. The Way of Heaven and the ordering of government ought …”

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
儒者能言之夫愚則何能言哉雖然經史
所陳學士大夫所稱蓋側聞之試以質焉
可乎自黃帝創受河圖始明休咎爰建星
官顧其文不經見已後王代興紹天闡繹
體元則大莫不崇植斯理神明其用若驪
翰寅丑之所尚黃星素祇之所徵其術異
由其揆一也當時篤古博物代有其人閎
者馳其辯約者微其詞達者折其衷咸有
論著莫可殫述是後掌故最秘士所與資
===
授而切劘之者不過遷史兩漢晉隋以來
志記所載與書詩禮經疏義之文外此則
編袠既鮮無所承傳靡得而稽焉愚反復
明問惟以堯典月令爲旨而占驗弗及意
在玆乎是故萬物之精上爲列星各宿錯
峙咸有攸屬在野象物在朝象官在人象
神禾之能易已今觀堯典以中星定仲月
者蓋人君嚮明而治南面而視仰而觀之
中星定而以次諸星可眡也以順節宣以
punctuated:
儒者能言之。夫愚則何能言哉？雖然，經史所陳、學士大夫所稱，蓋側聞之，試以質焉，可乎？

自黃帝創受河圖，始明休咎，爰建星官，顧其文不經見。已後王代興，紹天闡繹，體元則大，莫不崇植斯理，神明其用。若驪翰寅丑之所尚、黃星素祇之所徵，其術異，由其揆一也。當時篤古博物，代有其人，閎者馳其辯，約者微其詞，達者折其衷，咸有論著，莫可殫述。是後掌故最秘，士所與資授而切劘之者，不過遷史、兩漢、晉、隋以來志記所載，與《書》《詩》《禮》經疏義之文。外此則編袠既鮮，無所承傳，靡得而稽焉。

愚反復明問，惟以《堯典》《月令》爲旨，而占驗弗及，意在玆乎？是故萬物之精，上爲列星，各宿錯峙，咸有攸屬。在野象物，在朝象官，在人象神，禾之能易已。今觀《堯典》，以中星定仲月者，蓋人君嚮明而治，南面而視，仰而觀之，中星定而以次諸星可眡也，以順節宣，以
translation_en:
…Confucian scholars should be able to discuss these matters. But how could an ignorant person such as I speak of them? Nevertheless, I have heard something of what the classics and histories set forth and what learned scholars and officials discuss. May I venture to submit it for your judgment?

When Huangdi first received the River Chart, he began to distinguish auspicious and inauspicious signs and thereupon established the celestial offices—the constellations. Yet the relevant writings are not found in the classics. Later kings arose in succession, following Heaven and elucidating its patterns, embodying the primal principle and taking its greatness as their model. All upheld these principles and brought their wondrous efficacy into operation. Such matters as preferences for black or white and for the yin or chou month, or the portents of the yellow star and the white earth spirit [?], differed in method because their underlying standard was one. In those times, every age had men devoted to antiquity and versed in many things. Those of expansive learning developed their arguments at length; those inclined to brevity made their language subtle; those of comprehensive understanding adjudicated between them. All produced writings, too numerous to recount exhaustively. Thereafter, this inherited lore became deeply secret. The materials scholars could draw upon for instruction and mutual refinement amounted to no more than the records in Sima Qian’s history and in the treatises and histories of the two Han dynasties, Jin, Sui, and subsequent periods, together with the texts and commentaries of the Documents, Odes, and Rites. Beyond these, surviving volumes were few, with no continuing transmission and nothing available for verification.

I have repeatedly considered your illuminating question. It takes the Canon of Yao and the Monthly Ordinances as its guiding texts, without addressing divination and the verification of portents. Is this where its intention lies? Thus the essences of the myriad things become the arrayed stars above. The stellar lodges stand interspersed, each with its corresponding domain: in the countryside they symbolize things; at court they symbolize offices; in human beings they symbolize spirits. [The following phrase, 禾之能易已, is unclear [?].] Now, examining the Canon of Yao, its use of culminating stars to establish the middle month of each season rests on this: the ruler turns toward the light to govern and faces south to observe. Looking upward, once the culminating star is identified, the other stars can be viewed in sequence. This serves to regulate seasonal activities in their proper order, and to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
布時令故中星爲要焉天官書以北極爲
稱首者蓋天運至健三光迭曜而極星不
移總而論之樞紐建而周天之星俱拱也
以含元氣以察分至故北極爲大焉至於
堯典仲春舉星鳥而月令主弧仲夏舉星
火而月令主亢仲秋舉星虛而月令主牽
牛仲冬舉星昴而月令主東壁書之中星
常後月令中星常前鄭康成釋禮則曰月
令舉其初朔尚書舉其月中未喻其旨矣
===
孔穎達之疏禮則曰月令但舉其大畧蓋
以不合於曆數何言之踈矣斯殆不知夫
歲差所由始哉春秋運斗樞所次七星一
天樞二璇三璣四權五衡六開陽七搖光
一至四爲魁五至七爲杓魁杓合故曰斗
焉居陰布陽故稱北焉石氏乃曰一主天
二主地三主火四主水五主土六主木七
主金也又曰一秦二楚三梁四吳五燕六
趙七齊也其占法殊焉天官書則曰杓携
punctuated:
布時令，故中星爲要焉。《天官書》以北極爲稱首者，蓋天運至健，三光迭曜，而極星不移。總而論之，樞紐建而周天之星俱拱也。以含元氣，以察分至，故北極爲大焉。至於《堯典》仲春舉星鳥，而《月令》主弧；仲夏舉星火，而《月令》主亢；仲秋舉星虛，而《月令》主牽牛；仲冬舉星昴，而《月令》主東壁。《書》之中星常後，《月令》中星常前。鄭康成釋《禮》則曰：「《月令》舉其初朔，《尚書》舉其月中。」未喻其旨矣。孔穎達之疏《禮》則曰：「《月令》但舉其大畧。」蓋以不合於曆數，何言之踈矣！斯殆不知夫歲差所由始哉！
《春秋運斗樞》所次七星：一天樞，二璇，三璣，四權，五衡，六開陽，七搖光。一至四爲魁，五至七爲杓，魁杓合，故曰斗焉。居陰布陽，故稱北焉。石氏乃曰：「一主天，二主地，三主火，四主水，五主土，六主木，七主金也。」又曰：「一秦，二楚，三梁，四吳，五燕，六趙，七齊也。」其占法殊焉。《天官書》則曰：「杓携
translation_en:
…to promulgate the seasonal ordinances; hence the importance of the culminating stars. The Treatise on Celestial Offices gives the northern pole pride of place because the movement of Heaven is supremely vigorous and the three luminaries shine in succession, while the pole star remains unmoving. In general terms, once the pivot is established, all the stars throughout the heavens gather around it in homage. It contains the primordial qi and provides a means of observing the equinoxes and solstices; hence the northern pole’s preeminence.
As for the Canon of Yao, it names the Bird star for mid-spring, whereas the Monthly Ordinances specifies the Bow; for mid-summer it names Fire, whereas the Monthly Ordinances specifies Kang; for mid-autumn it names Xu, whereas the Monthly Ordinances specifies Qianniu; and for mid-winter it names Mao, whereas the Monthly Ordinances specifies Dongbi. The culminating stars in the Book of Documents are consistently behind, while those in the Monthly Ordinances are consistently ahead. Zheng Kangcheng, in explaining the Book of Rites, says: “The Monthly Ordinances gives the stars at the new moon beginning the month, while the Book of Documents gives those at mid-month.” He has failed to grasp the meaning. Kong Yingda, in his subcommentary on the Book of Rites, says: “The Monthly Ordinances gives only a broad outline.” Presumably he says this because it does not accord with calendrical calculations—how imprecise his explanation is! Surely this betrays ignorance of the origin of the precession of the equinoxes!
The Spring and Autumn: The Moving Pivot of the Dipper (Chunqiu yun dou shu) lists the seven stars in order: first Tianshu, second Xuan, third Ji, fourth Quan, fifth Heng, sixth Kaiyang, and seventh Yaoguang. The first through fourth form the bowl; the fifth through seventh form the handle. The bowl and handle together give it the name “Dipper.” It occupies the yin region and distributes yang, hence its designation as “Northern.” Master Shi, however, says: “The first governs Heaven, the second Earth, the third fire, the fourth water, the fifth soil, the sixth wood, and the seventh metal.” He also says: “The first corresponds to Qin, the second to Chu, the third to Liang, the fourth to Wu, the fifth to Yan, the sixth to Zhao, and the seventh to Qi.” His method of divination is different. The Treatise on Celestial Offices, by contrast, says: “The handle draws along…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
龍角衡中南斗魁枕參首斗爲帝車運于
中央臨制四海分陰陽建四時均五行移
節度定諸紀皆係於斗也其取義異焉斯
殆有見於七政所由叙哉夫所謂歲差者
蓋後世史官攷諸中星與太初曆不協大
要日躔之次常失不及未敢有制也迨晉
虞喜始創差法宋何承天倍之隋劉焯折
衷之唐一行復推以大衍皆以所推之年
爲日退一度至校以堯典月令之差又不
===
符合或謂呂不韋巳用差法故不宗堯典
載考自堯甲子歷秦莊襄漢太初越宋紹
興甲子積年三千四百二十一其日差也
計度以四十三積分以七千八百八十八
然或百歲計或七八十歲計又莫一焉噫
差法是也其不能必一者非差之咎也昔
者聖人作曆考之以象曰日月星辰驗之
以氣曰陰陽寒暑積之以數曰抄忽毫釐
夫以至微之數而推至變之氣動息升降
punctuated:
龍角，衡中南斗，魁枕參首。斗爲帝車，運于中央，臨制四海。分陰陽，建四時，均五行，移節度，定諸紀，皆係於斗也。」其取義異焉，斯殆有見於七政所由叙哉！
夫所謂歲差者，蓋後世史官攷諸中星，與太初曆不協，大要日躔之次常失不及，未敢有制也。迨晉虞喜始創差法，宋何承天倍之，隋劉焯折衷之，唐一行復推以大衍，皆以所推之年爲日退一度。至校以《堯典》《月令》之差，又不符合。或謂呂不韋巳用差法，故不宗《堯典》。載考自堯甲子，歷秦莊襄、漢太初，越宋紹興甲子，積年三千四百二十一。其日差也，計度以四十三，積分以七千八百八十八。然或百歲計，或七八十歲計，又莫一焉。噫！差法是也，其不能必一者，非差之咎也。
昔者聖人作曆，考之以象，曰日月星辰；驗之以氣，曰陰陽寒暑；積之以數，曰抄忽毫釐。夫以至微之數，而推至變之氣，動息升降
translation_en:
…the horns of the Dragon; the Crossbar aligns with the Southern Dipper, and the Bowl rests upon the head of Shen. The Dipper is the celestial emperor’s carriage: it revolves at the center, overseeing and governing the Four Seas. The division of yin and yang, the establishment of the four seasons, the balancing of the Five Phases, the shifting of seasonal measures, and the fixing of calendrical cycles all depend upon the Dipper.” Its interpretation is different. Might this reflect an understanding of how the seven celestial governors—the sun, moon, and five planets—are brought into order?
As for what is called precession, later court astronomers examined the stars culminating at the meridian and found that they did not agree with the Grand Inception Calendar. In general, the positions through which the sun passed consistently fell short, but they did not venture to establish a rule. Only with Yu Xi of the Jin was a method for calculating precession first devised. He Chengtian of the Song doubled it; Liu Zhuo of the Sui adopted an intermediate value; and Yixing of the Tang calculated it anew using the Great Expansion Calendar. Each took the number of years he had calculated as the period in which the sun retrograded by one degree. Yet when these were checked against the discrepancy between the Canon of Yao and the Monthly Ordinances, they again failed to agree. Some say that Lü Buwei had already used a method of calculating precession and therefore did not follow the Canon of Yao. Further investigation gives a total of 3,421 years from Yao’s jiazi year, through the reign of King Zhuangxiang of Qin and the Grand Inception era of the Han, down to the jiazi year of the Shaoxing era of the Song. The accumulated solar displacement is reckoned at forty-three degrees, with a fractional total of 7,888 units [?]. Yet some reckon one degree per hundred years, others per seventy or eighty years: here too there is no agreement. Alas! The method of accounting for precession is correct. That its values cannot invariably be uniform is no fault of precession itself.
In antiquity, when the sages made calendars, they investigated celestial phenomena—the sun, moon, stars, and asterisms; verified them against qi—yin and yang, cold and heat; and accumulated numerical quantities down to the minute fractions called chao, hu, hao, and li. Now, using quantities of the utmost minuteness to calculate qi in its utmost variability, with its movement and rest, rising and falling…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
不諆也盈縮遲速不律也非變通以達其
滯神明以妙其用毫忽之爽躔次之謬幾
南北易位冬春互建矣故杜預曰治曆者
當順天以求合非爲合以驗天程朱亦論
陰陽盈縮不齊不能無差凡此皆獨觀其
原者也愚故曰明於經者明於天道者也
非大智孰能與於此七政者肇於虞書至
漢劉歆張衡雅善星理厥術尤精歆曰太
極運三辰五星于上元氣轉三統五行于
===
下三辰合於三統五行合於五星三辰五
星而相經緯也衡曰文曜麗乎天其動者
七爲日月五星故曰七政皆緯又曰日陽
精宗也月陰精宗也五星五行宗也日行
黃道月與五星皆出入黃道也是故聖人
有作齊七政以立元測圭箭以候氣明九
道以步月交遲速以推星攷黃道之斜正
辨天勢之升降而交蝕詳焉噫明乎此其
於正政也視諸掌乎夫先王之以授人時
punctuated:
不諆也，盈縮遲速不律也。非變通以達其滯，神明以妙其用，毫忽之爽，躔次之謬，幾南北易位、冬春互建矣。故杜預曰：「治曆者當順天以求合，非爲合以驗天。」程朱亦論陰陽盈縮不齊，不能無差。凡此皆獨觀其原者也。愚故曰：明於經者，明於天道者也。非大智，孰能與於此？
七政者，肇於虞書。至漢，劉歆、張衡雅善星理，厥術尤精。歆曰：「太極運三辰五星于上，元氣轉三統五行于下。三辰合於三統，五行合於五星，三辰五星而相經緯也。」衡曰：「文曜麗乎天，其動者七，爲日月五星，故曰七政，皆緯。」又曰：「日，陽精宗也；月，陰精宗也；五星，五行宗也。日行黃道，月與五星皆出入黃道也。」
是故聖人有作，齊七政以立元，測圭箭以候氣，明九道以步月，交遲速以推星，攷黃道之斜正，辨天勢之升降，而交蝕詳焉。噫！明乎此，其於正政也，視諸掌乎？夫先王之以授人時
translation_en:
…cannot be predicted [?], and their waxing and waning, slowness and speed follow no fixed rule. Unless one adapts to change to overcome impediments and applies spiritual insight to make their operation subtle, discrepancies of the slightest magnitude and errors in celestial positions could almost cause north and south to exchange places and winter and spring to exchange their appointed seasons. Thus Du Yu said: “Those who construct calendars should follow Heaven to seek agreement, rather than contrive agreement to test Heaven.” Cheng and Zhu likewise discussed how the waxing and waning of yin and yang are uneven and cannot be free of discrepancies. These men all possessed exceptional insight into the underlying source. Thus I venture to say: those who understand the Classics understand the Way of Heaven. Who but someone of great wisdom could participate in this?
The term “Seven Regulators” originated in the Documents of Yu. By the Han dynasty, Liu Xin and Zhang Heng were well versed in the principles governing the stars, and their techniques were especially refined. Xin said: “The Supreme Ultimate moves the Three Luminaries and Five Planets above; primordial qi turns the Three Systems and Five Phases below. The Three Luminaries correspond to the Three Systems, and the Five Phases correspond to the Five Planets. The Three Luminaries and Five Planets thus serve as warp and weft to one another.” Heng said: “The patterned luminaries adorn Heaven. Seven of them move: the sun, the moon, and the Five Planets. Hence they are called the Seven Regulators; all are moving luminaries.” He also said: “The sun is the chief embodiment of yang essence; the moon is the chief embodiment of yin essence; the Five Planets are the chief embodiments of the Five Phases. The sun travels along the ecliptic; the moon and the Five Planets all pass to either side of it.”
Thus, when a sage arises, he brings the Seven Regulators into alignment to establish a calendrical epoch, takes measurements with the gnomon and clepsydra indicator to observe seasonal qi, elucidates the nine paths to calculate the moon’s motion, and correlates slow and fast motions to calculate the planets’ movements. He examines the obliquity and alignment of the ecliptic and distinguishes the rising and falling configurations of the heavens, so that conjunctions and eclipses are understood in detail. Ah! For one who understands this, would rectifying government not be as clear as looking at one’s own palm? Now, as for the former kings’ providing the people with the proper seasons…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
齊七政也非曰文也以時作息保和也辨
氛祲先幾也審象器定制也裁成範圍贊
化也推衍德運明統也是以人神式序天
地官也故日月合璧五星聯珠數之値不
得已也非所以爲祥然王者逢吉丁辰亦
可慶焉日月之會是謂合朔會之値不得
已也非所以爲沴然聖人扶陽抑陰必謹
候焉春秋傳曰先王之正時也履端于始
舉正于中歸餘于終又曰龍見而戒事火
===
見而致用水昏正而栽日至而畢凡此皆
以欽若其道者也愚故曰明於天道明於
王政者也非大聖孰能與於此若乃十二
月令牽文附義不可經訓儒者多所譏彈
蓋政令有俟時而行有不俟時而行也而
月令惑於時正之拘則夏后周公之典逸
矣渾儀璣衡異器同用不可闕一儒者類
能言之鄭康成謂璣衡以視行度馬融謂
渾儀可旋轉曰璣其橫簫曰衡是矣而孔
punctuated: 齊七政也，非曰文也。以時作息，保和也；辨氛祲，先幾也；審象器，定制也；裁成範圍，贊化也；推衍德運，明統也。是以人神式序，天地官也。故日月合璧，五星聯珠，數之値不得已也，非所以爲祥；然王者逢吉丁辰，亦可慶焉。日月之會，是謂合朔，會之値不得已也，非所以爲沴；然聖人扶陽抑陰，必謹候焉。《春秋傳》曰：「先王之正時也，履端于始，舉正于中，歸餘于終。」又曰：「龍見而戒事，火見而致用，水昏正而栽，日至而畢。」凡此皆以欽若其道者也。愚故曰，明於天道，明於王政者也。非大聖，孰能與於此？若乃十二月令，牽文附義，不可經訓，儒者多所譏彈。蓋政令有俟時而行，有不俟時而行也。而月令惑於時正之拘，則夏后周公之典逸矣。渾儀璣衡，異器同用，不可闕一，儒者類能言之。鄭康成謂璣衡以視行度，馬融謂渾儀可旋轉曰璣，其橫簫曰衡，是矣。而孔
translation_en:
…to bring the Seven Regulators into order was no mere outward embellishment. Regulating work and rest according to the seasons preserves harmony; distinguishing ominous vapors anticipates incipient events; examining celestial configurations and instruments establishes standards; shaping and regulating things assists cosmic transformation; and tracing the succession of the dynastic powers clarifies legitimate succession. Thus humans and spirits take their proper places, and Heaven and Earth discharge their offices. Hence, when the sun and moon unite like paired jade discs and the five planets form a string of pearls, these are inevitable conjunctions in their calculated cycles, not grounds in themselves for declaring an auspicious omen. Nevertheless, when a king encounters good fortune at a propitious time, there is still cause for celebration. The meeting of the sun and moon is called conjunction at the new moon. Such conjunctions are inevitable, not grounds in themselves for declaring a baleful portent. Nevertheless, because the sage supports yang and restrains yin, he must observe them carefully.

The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “In regulating the calendar, the former kings established its starting point at the beginning, determined its correctness in the middle, and assigned the remainder at the end.” It also says: “When the Dragon appears, prepare for the work; when the Fire Star appears, bring out the implements; when the Water constellation culminates at dusk, begin construction; and finish at the solstice.” All these practices reverently accord with the Way of Heaven. Thus I humbly say that understanding the Way of Heaven means understanding kingly government. Who but a great sage could attain this?

As for the Ordinances for the Twelve Months, they strain the wording and attach meanings to it, and cannot serve as authoritative instruction; Confucian scholars have frequently criticized them. Government orders sometimes await the appropriate season before being implemented, and sometimes do not. Yet the Monthly Ordinances are misled by rigid restrictions concerning seasonal and calendrical correctness [?], so that the canonical institutions of the sovereigns of Xia and the Duke of Zhou are lost.

The armillary sphere and the jade mechanism and sighting tube are different instruments serving the same purpose, neither of which can be dispensed with. Confucian scholars can generally explain this. Zheng Kangcheng says that the mechanism and sighting tube are used to observe the degrees of celestial movement. Ma Rong says that the rotating part of the armillary sphere is called the mechanism, and its transverse tube is called the sighting tube. This is correct. But Kong…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授鄭 批〔救民之術貴於豫此策能道之末復寫出問外之意可以覘識見之遠矣〕
佳士佳士
昔者聖人刪詩也至豳風詳周事焉曰我
稼既同曰始播百穀其作春秋也紀魯事
焉曰大無麥禾曰告糴于齊夫我稼志農
事也明王業所由起大無志倉廩之竭也
則所以譏莊侯豫備之道下焉耳故知荒
歉因乎數救備在乎人救言臨時也當以
===
𥻆備言先事也貴於豫遠於此其於荒政
也庶幾乎執事以備荒發策詢諸士子且
欲準酌今古補敝援溺此其爲慮遠哉雖
草茅未諳世務至于西江土俗民隱則何
敢默默焉請竭其愚以對旱乾水溢何代無
之或曰此適然之數爾也天且不能違况
於人乎彼堯若湯者豈其道不神聖哉然
九年之水七年之旱載諸典訓固可考也
若是而安得不謂之天或曰堯憂水咨於
punctuated:
考試官教授鄭批〔救民之術貴於豫，此策能道之，末復寫出問外之意，可以覘識見之遠矣〕：佳士！佳士！

昔者聖人刪詩也，至豳風，詳周事焉，曰「我稼既同」，曰「始播百穀」。其作春秋也，紀魯事焉，曰「大無麥禾」，曰「告糴于齊」。夫「我稼」，志農事也，明王業所由起；「大無」，志倉廩之竭也，則所以譏莊侯豫備之道下焉耳。故知荒歉因乎數，救備在乎人。救言臨時也，當以𥻆；備言先事也，貴於豫。遠於此，其於荒政也庶幾乎？執事以備荒發策，詢諸士子，且欲準酌今古，補敝援溺，此其爲慮遠哉！雖草茅未諳世務，至于西江土俗民隱，則何敢默默焉？請竭其愚以對。

translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Professor: 〔The art of saving the people depends above all on preparedness. This policy essay articulates this well and, at its close, develops a point beyond the question itself, revealing the breadth of the candidate’s understanding and judgment.〕 An outstanding scholar! An outstanding scholar!

When the Sage edited the Book of Odes, he treated the affairs of Zhou in detail in the Airs of Bin, saying, “Our crops have all been gathered,” and “They began to sow the hundred grains.” When he composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, he recorded the affairs of Lu, saying, “There was a great failure of wheat and other grain,” and “They requested permission to purchase grain in Qi.” “Our crops” records agricultural affairs, making clear the origins of the royal enterprise; “a great failure” records the exhaustion of the granaries, thereby censuring Lord Zhuang for his inadequate preparations. Thus we know that famine and poor harvests arise from fate, but relief and preparedness depend on human effort. Relief concerns action when disaster strikes and should employ 𥻆 [?]; preparedness concerns action beforehand and depends above all on anticipation. Taking this further [?], might one approach sound famine administration? You, sir, have issued a policy question on preparing against famine to consult the examination candidates. You also wish to weigh past and present practices, remedy failings, and rescue those in distress. How far-reaching your concern is! Though I am a humble man unfamiliar with worldly affairs, how could I remain silent about the local customs and the people’s hidden sufferings in Xijiang? Allow me to offer what little understanding I possess in reply.

Drought and overflowing waters: what age has been without them? Some say: “These are merely the workings of chance and fate. Even Heaven cannot counter them, much less human beings. Was the Way of men such as Yao and Tang not divinely sagacious? Yet the nine years of flooding and seven years of drought are recorded in the canonical teachings and can certainly be verified. Given this, how can we avoid attributing them to Heaven?” Others say: “Yao, concerned about the floods, consulted …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
岳牧湯憂旱禱於桑林聖人盡人以合天
治乃於變民乃允殖水旱無能病焉若是
而安得不謂之人嗚呼虢豐而危魯饑不
害茲非天人之大故哉是知諉之數則莫
若求端於天求之天則莫若盡其在我考
之王制三年耕餘一年之積九年耕餘三
年之積國有歛荒民無菜色此何所患焉
周禮大司徒以荒政十二聚萬民法甚詳
也又有遺人掌邦之委積以待惠施下至
===
鄉里縣都亦皆有積廩人掌九穀之數以
詔糓用與夫移民就食節巡郊野而以王
命惠施之蓋遺人之職以待其未荒廩人
之職以計其將荒荒政十二以賑其既荒
成周之法此非其大備者歟王代既殊古
法胥晦人各其見爲計紛然固亦得人之
情循物之理倣古之意大都可稱焉平糴
之法李悝建之魏常平之法耿壽昌創之
漢社倉之制長孫平行之隋義倉之法戴
punctuated: 岳牧，湯憂旱，禱於桑林。聖人盡人以合天，治乃於變，民乃允殖，水旱無能病焉。若是，而安得不謂之人？嗚呼！虢豐而危，魯饑不害，茲非天人之大故哉？是知諉之數，則莫若求端於天；求之天，則莫若盡其在我。考之《王制》，三年耕，餘一年之積；九年耕，餘三年之積。國有歛荒，民無菜色，此何所患焉？《周禮》大司徒以荒政十二聚萬民，法甚詳也。又有遺人掌邦之委積，以待惠施，下至鄉里縣都，亦皆有積。廩人掌九穀之數，以詔糓用，與夫移民就食，節巡郊野，而以王命惠施之。蓋遺人之職，以待其未荒；廩人之職，以計其將荒；荒政十二，以賑其既荒。成周之法，此非其大備者歟？王代既殊，古法胥晦，人各其見，爲計紛然。固亦得人之情，循物之理，倣古之意，大都可稱焉。平糴之法，李悝建之魏；常平之法，耿壽昌創之漢；社倉之制，長孫平行之隋；義倉之法，戴
translation_en:
…the regional chiefs and governors; Tang, troubled by drought, prayed at Sanglin. The sages fulfilled their human responsibilities in order to accord with Heaven. Government was thereby transformed, and the people indeed prospered; floods and droughts could do them no harm. If so, how can this not be attributed to human action? Alas! Guo enjoyed abundance yet was imperiled; Lu suffered famine yet came to no harm. Is this not a fundamental matter concerning Heaven and humanity? Thus we know that, rather than putting the blame on fate, it is better to seek the cause in Heaven; yet in seeking it in Heaven, nothing is better than fully discharging the responsibilities that lie with ourselves.

Examining the “Royal Regulations” chapter of the Book of Rites, we find that three years of cultivation should leave one year’s reserve, and nine years of cultivation should leave three years’ reserve. If the state has provisions against famine [?] and the people show no signs of hunger in their faces, what is there to fear? In the Rites of Zhou, the Minister of Education brings the myriad people together through twelve measures for famine relief; the regulations are exceedingly detailed. There is also the Officer of Reserves, who manages the state’s accumulated provisions in readiness for charitable distribution. Down to the townships, villages, districts, and domains, all likewise have reserves. The Granary Officer keeps account of the quantities of the nine grains to advise on their use, and also moves people to places where food is available, periodically inspects the countryside, and distributes relief by royal command. The Officer of Reserves thus makes preparations before famine occurs; the Granary Officer plans for famine as it approaches; and the twelve famine measures provide relief once famine has struck. Was this not a most comprehensive feature of the institutions of Zhou?

As ruling dynasties changed, the ancient institutions all fell into obscurity. Each person held his own views, and schemes proliferated. Yet insofar as these grasped human circumstances, followed the principles of things, and emulated the intentions of antiquity, most were worthy of praise. Li Kui established the system of equitable grain purchases in Wei; Geng Shouchang founded the ever-normal granary system under the Han; Zhangsun Ping implemented the community granary system under the Sui; and the charitable granary system, Dai …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
胄行之唐巳試之效鑿鑿乎足徵也巳合
而較諸則常平平糴責在官社倉義倉責
在民舉其在官者行之猶反掌也唐太宗
遣使分詣郡縣有鬻子女者官爲之贖斯
煦煦小仁也其視代宗從劉晏之請年稍
不登得以便宜從事簡易近民可不爲千
萬世荒政章程乎宋眞宗命侍御史秉傳
發賑乃稽遲日月也其視仁宗命官收養
其不能自存者料理其暴露於野者且賑
===
法詳備法良意美豈直目前補塞虛應故
事巳耶當時諸臣後先懋績或行諸郡也
或議諸朝也若青州富弼也越州趙抃也
司馬光請察守宰也朱熹請建社倉也鬻
爵賞以勸賑也嚴糴禁以平價也約而言
之周官所論著也漢魏所舉行也唐宋所
創建也損益得宜參伍盡變本於人情合
於土俗何可闕一也大抵天下無不敝之
法惟在有救敝之人人事盡於下則未定
punctuated: 胄行之唐，巳試之效，鑿鑿乎足徵也巳。合而較諸，則常平、平糴責在官，社倉、義倉責在民。舉其在官者行之，猶反掌也。唐太宗遣使分詣郡縣，有鬻子女者，官爲之贖，斯煦煦小仁也。其視代宗從劉晏之請，年稍不登，得以便宜從事，簡易近民，可不爲千萬世荒政章程乎？宋眞宗命侍御史秉傳發賑，乃稽遲日月也。其視仁宗命官收養其不能自存者，料理其暴露於野者，且賑法詳備，法良意美，豈直目前補塞、虛應故事巳耶？當時諸臣後先懋績，或行諸郡也，或議諸朝也。若青州富弼也，越州趙抃也，司馬光請察守宰也，朱熹請建社倉也，鬻爵賞以勸賑也，嚴糴禁以平價也。約而言之，《周官》所論著也，漢魏所舉行也，唐宋所創建也，損益得宜，參伍盡變，本於人情，合於土俗，何可闕一也？大抵天下無不敝之法，惟在有救敝之人。人事盡於下，則未定
translation_en:
…Dai Zhou implemented it under the Tang. The results of these tested measures are amply and clearly attested. Considered together, responsibility for the ever-normal granaries and equitable grain purchases lay with officials, while responsibility for community granaries and charitable granaries lay with the people. To put the measures entrusted to officials into practice would be as easy as turning over one’s hand. Emperor Taizong of Tang dispatched envoys to the prefectures and counties, and officials redeemed the children of those who had sold them. This was merely a small act of tenderhearted benevolence. Compare it with Emperor Daizong’s acceptance of Liu Yan’s proposal that, whenever the harvest fell even slightly short, officials should be permitted to act as circumstances required. Simple to administer and responsive to the people, could this not serve as a standard for famine relief for countless generations? Emperor Zhenzong of Song ordered palace censors to travel with official warrants [?] and distribute relief, yet days and months were lost in delay. Compare this with Emperor Renzong’s orders that officials take in and support those unable to sustain themselves and attend to those left exposed in the countryside. Moreover, his relief regulations were detailed and comprehensive, the measures sound and their intent admirable. Were these merely makeshifts for immediate needs, empty compliance with established routine?

The ministers of those times achieved outstanding results in succession, some implementing measures in the prefectures, others proposing them at court. Such were Fu Bi in Qingzhou and Zhao Bian in Yuezhou; Sima Guang, who requested scrutiny of prefects and county magistrates; and Zhu Xi, who requested the establishment of community granaries. There were also measures to sell ranks and grant rewards to encourage contributions to relief, and to enforce prohibitions on grain purchases strictly so as to stabilize prices. In brief, these were measures expounded in the Offices of Zhou, put into practice under the Han and Wei, and established under the Tang and Song. With suitable additions and reductions, comparison and adjustment to meet every change, rooted in human circumstances and adapted to local customs—how could any one of them be dispensed with?

Generally speaking, no system in the world is immune to deterioration; everything depends on having people capable of remedying its defects. When human efforts have been exhausted here below, then the as-yet-unsettled…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
之天顏有不可挽回者哉江西聯十有三
大郡而爲藩襟以三江滙以彭蠡峙以匡
廬翼以章貢帶以湘洛環以閩廣接以吳
會非不垠然大也生齒繁息比屋接廬行
商居賈農耕女織專業事事敦禮尚儉宜
家給人足訟平盜息也乃今一遇歲荒朝
不及夕十室九空餓殍盈途枵腹待哺望
官司之賑而舉火者十之七八也蠲租發
粟至勞
===
宵旰之軫念三二年間發銀散粟改折減運
僅得蘇息此何究竟歟今歲雖稍登然先
事之備誠有如執事所云云也蓋歲荒民
自爲計者三一曰爲盜二曰轉徙三曰待
其自斃夫民豈不知盜賊之不可爲也小
民無恒心何所不至民情懷土而重遷旣
不能徙又不能聽其斃如之何不去而爲
盜以少延須臾之死也其苟知禮義者則
轉而就食以待稔歲然後歸其不能盜又
punctuated:
之天顏，有不可挽回者哉？江西聯十有三大郡而爲藩，襟以三江，滙以彭蠡，峙以匡廬，翼以章貢，帶以湘洛，環以閩廣，接以吳會，非不垠然大也。生齒繁息，比屋接廬，行商居賈，農耕女織，專業事事，敦禮尚儉，宜家給人足，訟平盜息也。乃今一遇歲荒，朝不及夕，十室九空，餓殍盈途，枵腹待哺，望官司之賑而舉火者十之七八也。蠲租發粟，至勞宵旰之軫念，三二年間，發銀散粟，改折減運，僅得蘇息，此何究竟歟？今歲雖稍登，然先事之備，誠有如執事所云云也。
蓋歲荒，民自爲計者三：一曰爲盜，二曰轉徙，三曰待其自斃。夫民豈不知盜賊之不可爲也？小民無恒心，何所不至？民情懷土而重遷，旣不能徙，又不能聽其斃，如之何不去而爲盜，以少延須臾之死也？其苟知禮義者，則轉而就食，以待稔歲，然後歸。其不能盜又
translation_en:
…could Heaven’s countenance [?] be beyond turning back? Jiangxi unites thirteen great prefectures into a province. The Three Rivers form its lapel; Pengli gathers its waters; Kuanglu rises above it; Zhang and Gong flank it; Xiang and Luo [?] gird it; Min and Guang surround it; and it adjoins Wu and Hui. Its territory is certainly vast. Its population multiplies, and houses stand side by side. Traveling merchants and settled traders, farming men and weaving women each pursue their occupations and attend to their work, honoring ritual propriety and valuing frugality. Households ought to be well supplied and individuals to have enough, with lawsuits settled and banditry at an end. Yet now, whenever a famine year comes, people cannot make it from morning to evening. Nine households in ten stand empty, and the roads are filled with those who have starved to death. Seven or eight people in ten wait with empty bellies for food, depending on relief from the authorities before they can light their cooking fires. Remitting taxes and distributing grain have even troubled the compassionate concern of the emperor, who works before dawn and late into the evening. Over the past two or three years, silver and grain have been distributed, payments in kind commuted, and grain shipments reduced; only then has some recovery been possible. Where will this ultimately lead? Although this year’s harvest has been somewhat better, preparations in advance are indeed just as you, honored examiner, have described.
In a famine year, the people have three courses open to them: first, to become bandits; second, to migrate; and third, to await their own deaths. Surely they know that they must not become bandits? Yet when ordinary people lack steadfast hearts, what will they not resort to? People cherish their native soil and are reluctant to move. If they cannot migrate, and we cannot simply let them die, how could they fail to turn to banditry, if only to postpone imminent death for a moment? Those who have some understanding of ritual propriety and righteousness move elsewhere in search of food, waiting for a year of plentiful harvest before returning home. Those who cannot become bandits and also…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
不能徙則伏床待其自盡耳執事忍聞之
哉夫周官唐宋之法今欲行之必須數年
愚謂且講目前之計然後及數年之計先
試以賑濟者籌之夫官司發銀與穀本爲
貧民也今則吏胥里書緣以爲奸縣官不
察任其開報詭名小民數十里而趨者百
里而趨者貸糧而候計銀穀未得入手已
償貸無餘矣故貧者未必賑賑者未必貧
而溝壑之塡終不可救矣然此亦在乎守
===
令加之意耳又况民之貧多由官吏貪墨
也小民終歲勤動累錙積銖以規微利儲
之數年曾不以滿其一饜重以額外無名
之派往來供應之辦以一斂十以十斂百
少遲則悍隷叫號豗突雞犬不得寧焉民
何堪也此等而肆於民上猶豢虎豹於郊
原而縱之牧羊豕也有得全其命者乎此
猶爲根本之論誠得一廉潔者父母之勝
於發數萬之粟多矣蓋寬一分則民受一
punctuated:
不能徙，則伏床待其自盡耳。執事忍聞之哉？夫周官、唐宋之法，今欲行之，必須數年。愚謂且講目前之計，然後及數年之計。先試以賑濟者籌之。夫官司發銀與穀，本爲貧民也。今則吏胥里書緣以爲奸，縣官不察，任其開報詭名。小民數十里而趨者，百里而趨者，貸糧而候，計銀穀未得入手，已償貸無餘矣。故貧者未必賑，賑者未必貧，而溝壑之塡終不可救矣。然此亦在乎守令加之意耳。
又况民之貧，多由官吏貪墨也。小民終歲勤動，累錙積銖，以規微利，儲之數年，曾不以滿其一饜。重以額外無名之派、往來供應之辦，以一斂十，以十斂百。少遲，則悍隷叫號豗突，雞犬不得寧焉。民何堪也？此等而肆於民上，猶豢虎豹於郊原，而縱之牧羊豕也。有得全其命者乎？此猶爲根本之論。誠得一廉潔者父母之，勝於發數萬之粟多矣。蓋寬一分，則民受一
translation_en:
…and cannot migrate, they can only lie on their beds and await death. Can you, sir, bear to hear this? If the institutions of the Offices of Zhou and of the Tang and Song dynasties were to be implemented now, they would certainly require several years. In my humble view, we should first discuss measures for the immediate situation, then turn to plans requiring several years. Let us first consider relief. When the authorities distribute silver and grain, these are intended for the poor. Now, however, government clerks and village scribes exploit this opportunity for fraud. The county magistrates fail to investigate and allow them to submit fictitious names. Common people hurry from several tens of li away, or even a hundred li, borrowing grain while they wait. By the reckoning, before the silver and grain have even reached their hands, repayment of their loans will already have consumed it all. Thus the poor do not necessarily receive relief, and those receiving relief are not necessarily poor; in the end, people still cannot be saved from dying in the ditches. Yet this, too, depends upon prefects and county magistrates giving the matter their attention.
Moreover, the people's poverty often results from the corruption of officials and clerks. The common people toil throughout the year, accumulating tiny amounts in pursuit of a meager profit. Even several years of savings cannot provide them with a single full meal. On top of this come unauthorized levies beyond the prescribed quotas and the obligation to provide supplies for those traveling on official business. For every one due, ten are collected; for every ten, a hundred. At the slightest delay, fierce runners shout and storm about, leaving even the chickens and dogs no peace. How can the people endure this? Allowing such men to run rampant over the people is like raising tigers and leopards in the countryside and then releasing them to tend sheep and pigs. Could any escape with their lives? This, indeed, concerns the root of the problem. Truly, obtaining one honest and incorruptible official to act as father and mother to the people would be far better than distributing tens of thousands of measures of grain. For every measure by which their burdens are eased, the people receive one…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
分之賜朝行而夕及豈勞餘力哉若平糴
常平義倉社倉行之固爲利益然亦止救
目前故曰目前之計也蘇軾所謂萬世之
計亦不過以三十年之通有十年之餘耳
若夫重農桑以厚其生招流移以復其業
裁冗費以節其流禁游民以力其本抑豪
右以均其利去奢侈以崇其儉假以歲月
縱不能計十年之餘而其於三年之餘獨
不可計乎大抵法固有宜古而不宜於今
者惟在善爲法者審酌其時勢通之於權
變毋膠柱鼓瑟爾也蓋荒歉固適然之數
所不能逃然天道遠人事邇何可諉之莫
之爲遂輟然止也愚謂救之臨時以權備
之先事以豫夫亦若是已矣中庸曰致中
和天地位焉萬物育焉此心說也心生道
也故道位天地育萬物不尸其功而適然
之數不與存焉
punctuated: 分之賜，朝行而夕及，豈勞餘力哉？若平糴、常平、義倉、社倉，行之固爲利益，然亦止救目前，故曰目前之計也。蘇軾所謂萬世之計，亦不過以三十年之通有十年之餘耳。若夫重農桑以厚其生，招流移以復其業，裁冗費以節其流，禁游民以力其本，抑豪右以均其利，去奢侈以崇其儉，假以歲月，縱不能計十年之餘，而其於三年之餘獨不可計乎？大抵法固有宜古而不宜於今者，惟在善爲法者審酌其時勢，通之於權變，毋膠柱鼓瑟爾也。蓋荒歉固適然之數所不能逃，然天道遠，人事邇，何可諉之莫之爲，遂輟然止也？愚謂救之臨時以權，備之先事以豫，夫亦若是已矣。《中庸》曰：「致中和，天地位焉，萬物育焉。」此心說也。心生道也，故道位天地，育萬物，不尸其功，而適然之數不與存焉。
translation_en:
…a corresponding measure of benefit. Put into effect in the morning, it reaches them by evening: what additional effort would this require? As for equitable grain purchasing, the ever-normal granaries, charitable granaries, and community granaries, their operation certainly brings benefits, but they provide relief only for immediate needs; hence I call them plans for the present. Even what Su Shi called a plan for ten thousand generations amounts to no more than ensuring that, reckoning over thirty years, there is a surplus sufficient for ten years. But if we give priority to farming and sericulture to enrich the people's livelihood, summon back displaced people to restore their occupations, cut unnecessary expenditure to restrain the outflow of resources, curb idleness to strengthen agriculture as the foundation, restrain powerful families to distribute benefits evenly, and eliminate extravagance to promote frugality, then, given time, even if we cannot expect a surplus sufficient for ten years, could we not expect one sufficient for three?

In general, some methods suited to antiquity are indeed unsuited to the present. Everything depends on those skilled in devising methods carefully weighing the circumstances of their time and adapting them through expedient adjustments, rather than playing a zither with its bridges glued in place. Famine and poor harvests are indeed contingencies that cannot be escaped. Yet the Way of Heaven is distant, while human affairs are near at hand. How can we attribute everything to these contingencies, do nothing, and simply abandon our efforts? In my humble view, we should provide relief through expedient measures when the crisis arrives and make preparations beforehand through foresight. That is all there is to it.

The Doctrine of the Mean says: “Bring equilibrium and harmony to their utmost, and Heaven and Earth will take their proper places, and the myriad things will be nurtured.” This is a teaching about the heart-mind. The heart-mind gives rise to the Way; thus the Way places Heaven and Earth in their proper positions and nurtures the myriad things without claiming credit for its achievements, and contingent fate has no part therein.

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
歲丙午秋八月江西鄉試錄成
諸所規畫以共成休美在〔道夫〕
亦旣有言矣〔恩〕也無良當申諸
末簡敢再告之曰兹賓興
盛典實惟
聖天子登選俊良圖惟治理視昔益
===
加隆焉御史〔謨〕日懼無以祗承
休德朝夕矢于百執事曰無相負也
而百執事亦日惟御史言更相
飭戒自鎖院迄于有成凡二十
二日罔朝夕罔內外罔不悉謀
殫議至于論定而百執事之心
鮮弗盡矣凡以期得眞才爲
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

歲丙午秋八月，江西鄉試錄成。諸所規畫以共成休美，在〔道夫〕亦旣有言矣。〔恩〕也無良，當申諸末簡，敢再告之曰：兹賓興盛典，實惟聖天子登選俊良，圖惟治理，視昔益加隆焉。御史〔謨〕日懼無以祗承休德，朝夕矢于百執事曰：「無相負也。」而百執事亦日惟御史言，更相飭戒。自鎖院迄于有成，凡二十二日，罔朝夕，罔內外，罔不悉謀殫議，至于論定，而百執事之心鮮弗盡矣。凡以期得眞才爲
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth month, in autumn of the bingwu year [1546], the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination was completed. Daofu has already spoken of the various arrangements through which we jointly brought this worthy undertaking to completion. Unworthy though I, En, am, I ought to elaborate upon these matters in the closing pages, and venture to address you once more as follows: this grand ceremony of recommending worthy men is indeed the means by which the sagely Son of Heaven advances and selects outstanding men of ability and virtue, intent upon good government. Its importance has been further heightened in comparison with former times.

Censor Mo feared daily that he would be unable reverently to uphold this excellent virtue. Morning and evening he solemnly charged all those responsible: “Let us not fail one another.” Those responsible likewise kept the Censor’s words in mind each day, admonishing and cautioning one another. From the sealing of the examination compound until the work was completed, twenty-two days elapsed. Morning and evening, inside and outside alike, everyone gave full thought to the task and deliberated exhaustively until decisions were settled; scarcely any of those responsible failed to give their utmost. All this was in the hope of obtaining men of true talent for …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
國用也然而眞僞易淆也華實易
眩也庸有不得若人者乎〔恩〕兹
乎懼矣今有越人走四方入山
而得希世之珍乃飾以金函被
以文繡愛倍恒品及歸齋戒卜
日而啓之果玉也天下無不愛
且貴矣其不然至獲燕石而號
===
諸人曰玉在是人其謂何諸士
歌鹿鳴而來也有司得一佳士
如獲奇珍而或有不盡然者視
文考德難乎哉士出而果良于
行則稱乎其文斯天下將稱之
曰斯錄也而有若人也庸不爲
是科重耶其弗良于行則不稱
punctuated: 國用也。然而眞僞易淆也，華實易眩也，庸有不得若人者乎？〔恩〕兹乎懼矣。今有越人走四方，入山而得希世之珍，乃飾以金函，被以文繡，愛倍恒品。及歸，齋戒卜日而啓之，果玉也，天下無不愛且貴矣。其不然，至獲燕石而號諸人曰：「玉在是！」人其謂何？諸士歌《鹿鳴》而來也，有司得一佳士，如獲奇珍，而或有不盡然者。視文考德，難乎哉！士出而果良于行，則稱乎其文，斯天下將稱之曰：「斯錄也，而有若人也！」庸不爲是科重耶？其弗良于行，則不稱
translation_en:
…for service to the state. Yet the genuine and the false are easily confused, and outward brilliance and inner substance easily mistaken for one another. Might we sometimes fail to obtain men of such worth? This is what I, En, now fear.

Suppose a man of Yue travels throughout the land, enters the mountains, and obtains a treasure rarely seen in the world. He adorns it with a golden case, covers it with patterned silk, and cherishes it far more than ordinary objects. Upon returning home, he fasts, purifies himself, and selects an auspicious day to open it. If it truly is jade, everyone under Heaven will cherish and prize it. But if it is otherwise—if he has merely obtained a stone from Yan and proclaims to others, “Here is jade!”—what will people say?

The candidates come to the singing of “The Deer Call.” When the responsible officials obtain one excellent scholar, it is like finding a rare treasure; yet some may not entirely live up to this estimation. How difficult it is to examine writing and assess virtue! If, upon going forth, a scholar proves good in conduct, he lives up to his writing. Then all under Heaven will praise him, saying, “This examination record includes such a man!” Would this not lend distinction to this examination? If his conduct is not good, however, he does not live up to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
乎其文斯天下將指之曰斯錄
也而亦有若人也庸不爲是科
累耶是故太上不辱身而榮名
次之得失榮辱之機亦可以自
考矣在昔陸贄柄文得一韓愈
卒之愈也果克自振在愈不爲
負贄在贄不爲負天下天下至
今稱之不衰乃今諸士所遇之
時又非唐比矣
===
皇上懋德建中
憲經定制煥乎人文以臻勳華之
治凡在物覩皆以爲
大聖人在上則夫率德而化是豈無
真才如臯夔諸人應運而出者
punctuated:
乎其文，斯天下將指之曰：「斯錄也，而亦有若人也，庸不爲是科累耶？」是故太上不辱身，而榮名次之。得失榮辱之機，亦可以自考矣。在昔陸贄柄文，得一韓愈，卒之愈也果克自振。在愈不爲負贄，在贄不爲負天下，天下至今稱之不衰。乃今諸士所遇之時，又非唐比矣。
皇上懋德建中，憲經定制，煥乎人文，以臻勳華之治。凡在物覩，皆以爲大聖人在上，則夫率德而化，是豈無真才如臯夔諸人應運而出者
translation_en:
…with his writing, then all under Heaven will point him out and say: “This examination record also contains such a man! Does he not bring discredit upon this examination?” Thus, the highest achievement is not to disgrace oneself; bringing glory to one’s name comes next. The critical juncture between success and failure, honor and disgrace, is something the candidates can also examine for themselves. In former times, when Lu Zhi directed the literary examinations, he selected a Han Yu. In the end, Han Yu indeed succeeded in distinguishing himself. Han Yu did not fail Lu Zhi, and Lu Zhi did not fail all under Heaven. To this day, the world’s praise of them has not diminished. Yet the age that you gentlemen now encounter is beyond comparison with the Tang.
His Majesty cultivates virtue and establishes the mean, takes the Classics as his standard and fixes institutions, making human culture resplendent so as to attain the governance of Yao and Shun. All who behold him consider that a great sage occupies the throne. Thus, as people follow virtue and are transformed, how could there fail to be men of true ability, like Gao and Kui, who emerge in response to the needs of the age…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
乎此固其會也若夫贊之得令
雖謂唐之得士可也而要之非
其至也是故鳴盛者文也迨會
者時也際時者遇也諸士生逢
盛世有其時矣以文見錄有其遇
矣士窮居隱約其蚤夜爲心恐
恐焉恒以不遇爲歉自今不爲
===
不遇矣庸無所表見樹立以罄
其平生耶夫有其材而弗遇有
司之責也遇矣而不盡其材諸
士之恥也諸士其勗之哉
直隸鳳陽府宿州儒學學正張
恩謹序
punctuated:
乎？此固其會也。若夫贊之得令，雖謂唐之得士可也，而要之非其至也。是故鳴盛者文也，迨會者時也，際時者遇也。諸士生逢盛世，有其時矣；以文見錄，有其遇矣。士窮居隱約，其蚤夜爲心恐恐焉，恒以不遇爲歉，自今不爲不遇矣，庸無所表見樹立，以罄其平生耶？夫有其材而弗遇，有司之責也；遇矣而不盡其材，諸士之恥也。諸士其勗之哉！
直隸鳳陽府宿州儒學學正張恩謹序。
translation_en:
…? This, indeed, is their opportunity. As for praising this occasion for securing worthy men [?], one might indeed compare it to the Tang dynasty’s recruitment of scholars; yet, ultimately, this does not express its highest significance. Thus, writing gives voice to an age’s flourishing; the times bring the opportunity [?]; and encountering those times constitutes a fortunate meeting. You scholars, born into a flourishing age, have the right times; selected for your writing, you have received your opportunity. When scholars live obscurely in straitened circumstances, their thoughts morning and night are full of anxiety, and they constantly regret having no opportunity. From now on, you can no longer be said to lack opportunity. How, then, could you fail to distinguish yourselves and establish achievements, giving full expression to your lifelong aspirations? If men possess talent but receive no opportunity, the responsibility lies with the officials concerned. If they receive an opportunity but fail to make full use of their talents, the disgrace belongs to the scholars themselves. You scholars, strive diligently!
Preface respectfully composed by Zhang En, Instructor in the Confucian School of Suzhou Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered territory.

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
嘉靖丙午秋八月時當鄉試江
西有司舉如
制巡按監察御史陶〔謨〕實惟監臨
乃矢心率衆爰稽典式用戒弗
虔先是巡撫右副都御史虞〔守〕
〔愚〕端軌植則夙造多士至是乃
===
協謀檄所司博選儒臣徵書四
馳于是考試官〔道夫〕暨學正張
〔愚〕同考試官教諭袁〔道〕招〔于莘〕
張〔溥〕詹〔世龍〕楊〔灝〕鄒〔文元〕韋〔紹〕
高〔士楠〕李〔成春〕聶〔勛〕咸以期至
提調則左布政使喻〔智〕左參議
李〔時達〕監試則副使李〔徵〕僉事
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序

嘉靖丙午秋八月，時當鄉試，江西有司舉如制。巡按監察御史陶〔謨〕實惟監臨，乃矢心率衆，爰稽典式，用戒弗虔。先是，巡撫右副都御史虞〔守〕〔愚〕端軌植則，夙造多士。至是，乃協謀檄所司，博選儒臣，徵書四馳。于是，考試官〔道夫〕暨學正張〔愚〕，同考試官教諭袁〔道〕、招〔于莘〕、張〔溥〕、詹〔世龍〕、楊〔灝〕、鄒〔文元〕、韋〔紹〕、高〔士楠〕、李〔成春〕、聶〔勛〕，咸以期至。提調則左布政使喻〔智〕、左參議李〔時達〕，監試則副使李〔徵〕、僉事
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the bingwu year of Jiajing [1546], when the Provincial Examination was due, the responsible authorities in Jiangxi conducted the proceedings according to the prescribed regulations. The Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Tao Mo, served as Supervising Official. Pledging himself wholeheartedly to the task, he led the assembled officials, consulted the established statutes and procedures, and warned against any lack of diligence and respect.

Previously, the Grand Coordinator, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Yu Shouyu, had rectified standards and established rules, working well in advance to cultivate the many scholars. Now they jointly deliberated and dispatched orders to the responsible offices, broadly selecting learned officials; summonses sped out in every direction. Accordingly, the Examiners, Daofu [surname absent?] and Instructor Zhang Yu, and the Associate Examiners, Instructors Yuan Dao, Zhao Yuxin, Zhang Pu, Zhan Shilong, Yang Hao, Zou Wenyuan, Wei Shao, Gao Shinan, Li Chengchun, and Nie Xun, all arrived by the appointed time. The Proctors were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Yu Zhi and Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Li Shida. Examination supervision was entrusted to Surveillance Vice Commissioner Li Zheng and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
黃〔文炳〕綜理防範既嚴且飭御
史又申告之曰江右大藩也文
衡重典也人臣以人事
君在兹役也惟公惟愼庶罔罪愆乃
合提學僉事蔡〔克廉〕所取士三
千九百有奇鎖院三試之〔道夫〕
于是得縱觀焉見其文愽而辯
===
達而暢雖其抑揚變化上下古
今要之折衷墳典明物達政不
詭於正義洋洋乎深邃而有遐
思譬之豫章山川匡廬彭蠡懸
奇逞異倏忽萬變不可攬結然
而淳龐之氣貞大之體似有未
易以淺近測者吁其眞
punctuated: 黃〔文炳〕綜理防範，既嚴且飭。御史又申告之曰：「江右大藩也，文衡重典也。人臣以人事君，在兹役也。惟公惟愼，庶罔罪愆。」乃合提學僉事蔡〔克廉〕所取士三千九百有奇，鎖院三試之。〔道夫〕于是得縱觀焉，見其文愽而辯，達而暢。雖其抑揚變化，上下古今，要之折衷墳典，明物達政，不詭於正義。洋洋乎深邃而有遐思！譬之豫章山川，匡廬彭蠡，懸奇逞異，倏忽萬變，不可攬結。然而淳龐之氣，貞大之體，似有未易以淺近測者。吁，其眞
translation_en: …Huang Wenbing, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, oversaw the precautions, which were both strict and orderly. The censor further admonished them: “Jiangyou is a great province, and the assessment of literary talent is a weighty institution. It is in this undertaking that a minister serves his ruler by finding worthy men. Be impartial and circumspect, so that you may be free of fault.” They then assembled the more than 3,900 scholars selected by Cai Kelian, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner for Education, closed the examination compound, and examined them in three sessions. Daofu thus had the opportunity to survey their work fully. He found their writing broad in learning and discerning in argument, lucid and fluent. Though its cadences and transformations ranged across antiquity and the present, in essence it took the ancient canons as its standard, clarified things, and showed an understanding of government, without departing from correct principles. How abundant, profound, and far-reaching in thought! It resembled the mountains and waters of Yuzhang—Kuanglu and Pengli—displaying marvels and unfolding wonders, changing ten thousand times in an instant, impossible to grasp and hold. Yet its rich, substantial spirit and upright, grand form seemed to possess something that could not readily be fathomed by a shallow understanding. Ah, is this truly …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
盛世之文乎拔其尤者九十五人
第其氏名并錄其文以
獻〔道夫〕作而言曰昔者聖人作易
取天下之象而神明之于渙則
曰風行水上至于賁之彖則曰
觀乎人文以化成天下是豈易
言哉成周以上無容論也漢魏
===
以還風斯下矣我
國家重熈累洽崇古敦典而庠序
絃歌之化漸被海宇一時能言
之士爭起濯磨而以文鳴世者
不少也蓋其初也因質以成文
及其既也用文以掩質而神化
轉移之機誠若有待者恭惟
punctuated:
盛世之文乎？拔其尤者九十五人，第其氏名，并錄其文以獻。
〔道夫〕作而言曰：「昔者聖人作易，取天下之象而神明之。于渙則曰：『風行水上。』至于賁之彖則曰：『觀乎人文，以化成天下。』是豈易言哉？成周以上，無容論也。漢魏以還，風斯下矣。我國家重熈累洽，崇古敦典，而庠序絃歌之化漸被海宇。一時能言之士爭起濯磨，而以文鳴世者不少也。蓋其初也，因質以成文；及其既也，用文以掩質，而神化轉移之機，誠若有待者。恭惟
translation_en:
…the writing of a flourishing age? Ninety-five of the most outstanding candidates were selected, their names placed in rank order, and their writings also recorded for presentation to the throne.
[Daofu 道夫] rose and said: “In ancient times, when the sages composed the Book of Changes, they took the images of all under Heaven and brought out their spiritual illumination. For the hexagram Dispersion, it says, ‘Wind moves over water.’ In the Commentary on the Judgment for the hexagram Adornment, it says, ‘Observe human culture, and thereby transform and perfect all under Heaven.’ Could these words have been spoken lightly? There is no need to discuss the flourishing Zhou or earlier times. Since the Han and Wei, however, literary standards have declined. Our dynasty has enjoyed successive reigns of prosperity and enduring harmony, venerating antiquity and honoring the canonical norms. The transforming influence of the schools, with their strings and songs, has gradually spread throughout the realm. Men skilled in expression have risen in eager rivalry to cleanse and polish themselves, and not a few have won renown in the world through their writing. At first, they built literary refinement upon substance; later, they used refinement to conceal substance. The crucial opportunity for a wondrous transformation and redirection thus seems truly to await something. Reverently considering…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
皇上聖神
天縱
建立人極而
德意所向惓惓於貞文敷教崇雅黜
浮是宜諸士之文一變而之於
正猗歟盛哉是故錄其文示式
也錄其名示廣遠也爾多士其
===
將自謀也無自多於文無自侈
於名夫文與行並擴之而經綸
天地是之謂天下之至文名與
實稱垂之而昭遡信後是之謂
天下之令名若徒以藝為文而
名亦惟外之求則亦難乎其為
鑑矣江右素稱多才甲於海內
punctuated: 皇上聖神天縱，建立人極，而德意所向，惓惓於貞文敷教、崇雅黜浮，是宜諸士之文一變而之於正。猗歟盛哉！是故錄其文，示式也；錄其名，示廣遠也。爾多士其將自謀也，無自多於文，無自侈於名。夫文與行並，擴之而經綸天地，是之謂天下之至文；名與實稱，垂之而昭遡信後，是之謂天下之令名。若徒以藝為文，而名亦惟外之求，則亦難乎其為鑑矣。江右素稱多才，甲於海內
translation_en: …His Majesty, endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom, establishes the supreme standard for humankind. His virtuous intentions are earnestly directed toward making writing upright and spreading moral instruction, honoring elegance and rejecting superficiality. It is therefore fitting that the writings of the scholars should undergo a transformation and turn toward correctness. Ah, how splendid! Thus we record their writings to provide models, and record their names to make them known far and wide. You scholars should take thought for yourselves: do not pride yourselves on your writing or vaunt your names. When writing keeps pace with conduct, and its scope is extended to ordering Heaven and Earth, this is called the finest writing under Heaven. When reputation accords with substance and is handed down to illuminate the past [?] and command the trust of later generations, this is called an illustrious name under Heaven. But if one treats mere technical skill as writing and seeks reputation only from external sources, it will be difficult indeed for these records to serve as a mirror. Jiangyou has long been renowned for its abundance of talent, foremost within the realm…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
名臣碩輔文章勳業彬彬然後
先相望景行在茲取則不遠非
獨得於山川之助已也〔道夫〕是
以知必有卓異之材純正之士
相繼起而名世果若人歟則取
人者得仰副
聖天子求賢之盛心固非私於其人
===
取於人者將對揚
文明之盛治抑非私於其身交〔相慶〕
而其道光也豈惟今日薦書之
榮雖豫章山川亦與榮矣是舉
也巡撫右僉都御史傅〔鳳翱〕雖
新被
簡命昔嘗觀風茲土士咸思奮提
punctuated:
名臣碩輔，文章勳業，彬彬然後先相望。景行在茲，取則不遠，非獨得於山川之助已也。〔道夫〕是以知必有卓異之材、純正之士，相繼起而名世。果若人歟，則取人者得仰副聖天子求賢之盛心，固非私於其人；取於人者將對揚文明之盛治，抑非私於其身。交〔相慶〕而其道光也，豈惟今日薦書之榮？雖豫章山川亦與榮矣。
是舉也，巡撫右僉都御史傅〔鳳翱〕雖新被簡命，昔嘗觀風茲土，士咸思奮。提
translation_en:
… Eminent ministers and distinguished chief councilors, accomplished in letters and meritorious service, have followed one another in splendid succession. Exemplary conduct is here before us; models to follow are not far away. These achievements owe more than merely the assistance of the mountains and rivers. I, 〔Daofu〕, therefore know that men of exceptional ability and scholars of integrity and rectitude will arise in succession and win renown in their age. If they indeed prove to be such men, those who select them will be able to fulfill the sagely Son of Heaven’s ardent desire to obtain worthy men: this is certainly no private favor to the individuals selected. Those selected will, in turn, acknowledge and extol his flourishing, enlightened rule: this, too, is no matter of private advantage to themselves. They will 〔congratulate one another〕, and their Way will shine forth. Would the honor extend only to having their names on today’s recommendation roll? Even the mountains and rivers of Yuzhang will share in that glory.
For this examination, the Governor and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, Fu 〔Feng’ao〕, although newly appointed by imperial selection, had previously inspected local conditions in this region, and all the scholars aspired to exert themselves. The …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
督南贛軍務右副都御史顧〔遂〕
克綏疆場戢武右文與有風化
之助焉右布政使韓〔楷〕左叅政
李〔錞〕右叅政吴〔從義〕庢叅議張
〔永明〕右叅議方〔任〕按察使楊〔本〕
〔仁〕副使楊〔沔〕范〔欽〕孫〔雲〕僉事陳
〔如綸〕王〔重賢〕吴〔源〕都指揮僉事
===
方〔恩〕陳〔燦〕效勞於外實翼賛同
心刑部郎中翁〔大立〕工部員外
郎周〔薇〕司務費〔懋樂〕戶部主事
林〔愛民〕蔣〔孝〕中書舍人王〔學〕行
人李〔萬實〕適以使事至樂觀盛
舉右叅政盧〔紳〕僉事施〔千祥〕署

translation_en:
… Gu Sui, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief supervising military affairs in Nan-Gan, succeeded in pacifying the frontier, restraining military force and honoring civil learning, thereby also contributing to moral transformation.

Han Kai, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Li Chun, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; Wu Congyi, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; Zhang Yongming, Administration Assistant Commissioner with an unclear designation [?]; Fang Ren, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner; Yang Benren, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; Yang Mian, Fan Qin, and Sun Yun, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Chen Rulun, Wang Chongxian, and Wu Yuan, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; and Fang En and Chen Can, Assistant Regional Military Commissioners, rendered service outside the examination compound and gave their support with a common purpose.

Weng Dali, Director in the Ministry of Justice; Zhou Wei, Vice Director in the Ministry of Works; Fei Maole, Office Manager; Lin Aimin and Jiang Xiao, Secretaries in the Ministry of Revenue; Wang Xue, Central Drafting Office Secretary; and Li Wanshi, Messenger, happened to arrive on official missions and were pleased to witness this grand occasion.

Lu Shen, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; Shi Qianxiang, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner; and Liu Xiang, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, respectfully encountering …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
萬壽聖節豫期入
賀若左布政使何〔鰲〕左叅政戴〔鰲〕
則以代遷行署都指揮僉事孫
〔蘭〕則以督運行皆先事與謀聿
相厥成者也例得備書云
直隸淮安府儒學教授鄭〔道夫〕
謹序
punctuated:
萬壽聖節，豫期入賀。若左布政使何〔鰲〕、左叅政戴〔鰲〕，則以代遷行；署都指揮僉事孫〔蘭〕，則以督運行。皆先事與謀，聿相厥成者也，例得備書云。
直隸淮安府儒學教授鄭〔道夫〕謹序。
translation_en:
…the sacred festival of the Emperor’s birthday, they went ahead of time to offer congratulations at court. As for He Ao, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Dai Ao, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner, they departed on account of replacement and transfer [?]; Sun Lan, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, departed to supervise transport. All had participated in planning beforehand and helped bring the undertaking to completion. Following established practice, their names are therefore recorded in full.
Preface respectfully composed by Zheng Daofu, Prefectural School Instructor of Huai’an Prefecture in the directly administered territory.

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄

嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試

監臨官：巡按江西監察御史陶　謨〔大顯，浙江秀水縣人，壬辰進士〕。

提調官：江西等處承宣布政使司左布政使喻　智〔子貞，直隸當塗縣人，甲戌進士〕。江西等處承宣布政使司左參議李時達〔伯可，四川南部縣人，乙未進士〕。

監試官：江西等處提刑按察司副使李　徵〔誠之，湖廣桃源縣人，壬辰進士〕。江西等處提刑按察司僉事黃文炳〔以約，福建莆田縣人，乙未進士〕。

translation_en:
Jiangxi Provincial Examination, the twenty-fifth year of Jiajing (1546)

Supervising Official
Tao Mo, Investigating Censor assigned to patrol Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Daxian and was a native of Xiushui County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the renchen year.

Proctors
Yu Zhi, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Zizhen and was a native of Dangtu County in the directly administered territory (Zhili). He was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.
Li Shida, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Boke and was a native of Nanbu County, Sichuan. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Examination Monitoring Officials
Li Zheng, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Chengzhi and was a native of Taoyuan County, Huguang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.
Huang Wenbing, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Yiyue and was a native of Putian County, Fujian. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Examiners
Zheng Daofu, Professor of the Confucian School of Huai’an Prefecture in Zhili, had the courtesy name Lizhi and was a native of Putian County, Fujian. He was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the wuzi year.
Zhang En, Instructor of the Confucian School of Suzhou Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Zitui and was a native of Xiangfu County, Henan. He was a tribute scholar of the dingyou year.

Associate Examiners
Yuan Dao, Instructor of the Confucian School of Jingling County, Mianyang Subprefecture, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Wenbo and was a native of Dahe County, Yunnan. He was a tribute scholar of the guimao year.
Zhao Yushen, Instructor of the Confucian School of Longyang County, Changde Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Qigeng and was a native of Panyu County, Guangdong. He was a tribute scholar of the jiawu year.
