title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰參乎吾道一以貫之曾子曰唯子出
門人問曰何謂也曾子曰夫子之道忠
恕而已矣
優優大哉禮儀三百威儀三千
君子所性仁義禮智根於心其生色也睟
然見於面盎於背施於四體四體不言
而喻
===
易
文言曰元者善之長也亨者嘉之會也利
者義之和也貞者事之幹也君子體仁
足以長人嘉會足以合禮利物足以和
義貞固足以幹事君子行此四德者故
曰乾元亨利貞
允升大吉上合志也
通其變遂成天地之文極其數遂定天下
之象
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「參乎！吾道一以貫之。」曾子曰：「唯。」子出，門人問曰：「何謂也？」曾子曰：「夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。」

優優大哉！禮儀三百，威儀三千。

君子所性，仁義禮智根於心。其生色也，睟然見於面，盎於背，施於四體；四體不言而喻。

易

文言曰：「元者，善之長也；亨者，嘉之會也；利者，義之和也；貞者，事之幹也。君子體仁，足以長人；嘉會，足以合禮；利物，足以和義；貞固，足以幹事。君子行此四德者，故曰：『乾，元亨利貞。』」

允升，大吉，上合志也。

通其變，遂成天地之文；極其數，遂定天下之象。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said, “Shen! My Way is threaded through by a single principle.” Zengzi replied, “Yes.” When the Master had left, the disciples asked, “What did he mean?” Zengzi said, “Our Master’s Way consists simply of doing one’s utmost for others and treating them as one would wish to be treated.”

How ample and great! Three hundred rules of ritual and three thousand rules of deportment.

What the gentleman possesses by nature—benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom—is rooted in his heart. Its expression appears in the pure radiance of his face, fills his back, and extends to his four limbs. His limbs convey it without words.

Book of Changes

The Commentary on the Words says: “The primal is foremost among forms of goodness; the flourishing is the convergence of what is excellent; the beneficial is the harmony of righteousness; the steadfast is the mainstay of affairs. By embodying benevolence, the gentleman is able to lead others; by bringing together what is excellent, he is able to accord with ritual propriety; by benefiting things, he is able to harmonize righteousness; by remaining steadfast and firm, he is able to manage affairs. The gentleman practices these four virtues; therefore it is said: ‘Qian: primal, flourishing, beneficial, and steadfast.’”

“Ascending with confidence: great good fortune”—because one’s purpose accords with that of those above.

By comprehending their transformations, one brings to completion the patterns of Heaven and Earth; by fully exploring their numbers, one determines the images of all under Heaven.

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
君子修此三者故全也
書
敷奏以言明試以功車服以庸
惟説式克欽承旁招俊乂列于庶位
貌曰恭言曰從視曰明聽曰聰思曰睿恭
作肅從作乂明作哲聰作謀睿作聖
乃用三有宅克即宅曰三有俊克即俊嚴
惟丕式克用三宅三俊其在商邑用協
于厥邑其在四方用丕式見德
===
詩
春日載陽有鳴倉庚女執懿筐遵彼微行
爰求柔桑春日遲遲采蘩祁祁
赤芾金舄會同有繹
既醉以酒既飽以德君子萬年介爾景福
既醉以酒爾殽既將君子萬年介爾昭
明
商邑翼翼四方之極赫赫厥聲濯濯厥靈
壽考且寧以保我後生
punctuated:
君子修此三者，故全也。

書
敷奏以言，明試以功，車服以庸。
惟説式克欽承，旁招俊乂，列于庶位。
貌曰恭，言曰從，視曰明，聽曰聰，思曰睿。恭作肅，從作乂，明作哲，聰作謀，睿作聖。
乃用三有宅，克即宅；曰三有俊，克即俊。嚴惟丕式，克用三宅三俊。其在商邑，用協于厥邑；其在四方，用丕式見德。

詩
春日載陽，有鳴倉庚。女執懿筐，遵彼微行，爰求柔桑。春日遲遲，采蘩祁祁。
赤芾金舄，會同有繹。
既醉以酒，既飽以德。君子萬年，介爾景福。既醉以酒，爾殽既將。君子萬年，介爾昭明。
商邑翼翼，四方之極。赫赫厥聲，濯濯厥靈。壽考且寧，以保我後生。
translation_en:
The gentleman cultivates these three things and thus achieves completeness.

Book of Documents

Have them present their statements in words, clearly test them through their accomplishments, and bestow carriages and robes according to their service.

Yue reverently carried out these instructions, seeking worthy and capable men far and wide and placing them in the various offices.

In demeanor, reverence; in speech, compliance; in sight, clarity; in hearing, acuteness; in thought, penetration. Reverence produces solemnity; compliance produces good order; clarity produces wisdom; acuteness produces sound deliberation; penetration produces sageliness.

Then employ those qualified for the three kinds of office, who can fulfill the duties of those offices; seek those possessing the three kinds of excellence, who can live up to that excellence. Reverently follow this great model, employing those qualified for the three kinds of office and those possessing the three kinds of excellence. In the city of Shang, thereby bring harmony to that city; throughout the four quarters, thereby broadly display virtue as a model.

Book of Odes

The spring days grow warm; the orioles sing. The girls carry fine baskets and follow the narrow paths, seeking tender mulberry leaves. The spring days lengthen; crowds gather white southernwood.

In red knee-aprons and gold-adorned shoes, they gather in an unbroken succession of assemblies.

Already drunk with wine, already sated with your kindness: may our lord live ten thousand years, and may great blessings be bestowed upon you! Already drunk with wine, with your dishes set forth: may our lord live ten thousand years, and may radiant glory be bestowed upon you!

The city of Shang is stately and well ordered, the pole toward which the four quarters turn. Resplendent is its renown; manifest is its spiritual power. May there be long life and peace, to safeguard our descendants.

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
春秋
秋七月庚午宋公齊侯衛侯盟于𡚁屋〔隱〕
〔公八年夏齊侯衛侯胥命于蒲桓公三〕
〔年〕公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子光
莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭
會于蕭魚〔襄公十有一年〕
齊人救邢〔閔公元年〕
冬十月不雨〔僖公二年〕春王正月不雨夏
四月不雨六月雨〔俱僖公三年〕
===
甲午晦晉侯及楚子鄭伯戰于鄢陵楚子
鄭師敗績公會尹子晉侯齊國佐邾人
伐鄭〔俱成公十有六年〕夏公會尹子單
子晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯曹伯邾人伐鄭
冬公會單子晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊人
邾人伐鄭〔俱成公十有七年〕夏公會齊
侯于夾谷公至自夾谷齊人來歸鄆讙
龜陰田〔俱定公十年〕叔孫州仇帥師墮
郈季孫斯仲孫何忌帥師墮費〔俱定公〕
punctuated:
春秋

秋七月庚午，宋公、齊侯、衛侯盟于𡚁屋〔隱〕〔公八年。夏，齊侯、衛侯胥命于蒲。桓公三〕〔年〕。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚〔襄公十有一年〕。

齊人救邢〔閔公元年〕。

冬十月，不雨〔僖公二年〕。春王正月，不雨；夏四月，不雨；六月，雨〔俱僖公三年〕。

甲午晦，晉侯及楚子、鄭伯戰于鄢陵，楚子、鄭師敗績。公會尹子、晉侯、齊國佐、邾人伐鄭〔俱成公十有六年〕。夏，公會尹子、單子、晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、邾人伐鄭。冬，公會單子、晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊人、邾人伐鄭〔俱成公十有七年〕。夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田〔俱定公十年〕。叔孫州仇帥師墮郈。季孫斯、仲孫何忌帥師墮費〔俱定公〕
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

In autumn, in the seventh month, on the gengwu day, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Qi, and the Marquis of Wei made a covenant at Biwu [?]. 〔Eighth year of Duke Yin. In summer, the Marquis of Qi and the Marquis of Wei exchanged pledges at Pu. Third year of Duke Huan.〕 The Duke of Lu joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi 杞, and the Viscount of Xiaozhu in attacking Zheng. They assembled at Xiaoyu. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xiang.〕

The men of Qi came to the aid of Xing. 〔First year of Duke Min.〕

In winter, in the tenth month, there was no rain. 〔Second year of Duke Xi.〕 In spring, in the first month by the royal calendar, there was no rain; in summer, in the fourth month, there was no rain; in the sixth month, it rained. 〔All in the third year of Duke Xi.〕

On the jiawu day, the last day of the month, the Marquis of Jin fought the Viscount of Chu and the Earl of Zheng at Yanling. The Viscount of Chu and the army of Zheng were routed. The Duke of Lu joined the Viscount of Yin, the Marquis of Jin, Guo Zuo of Qi, and the men of Zhu in attacking Zheng. 〔Both in the sixteenth year of Duke Cheng.〕 In summer, the Duke of Lu joined the Viscount of Yin, the Viscount of Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, and the men of Zhu in attacking Zheng. In winter, the Duke of Lu joined the Viscount of Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, and the men of Qi and Zhu in attacking Zheng. 〔Both in the seventeenth year of Duke Cheng.〕 In summer, the Duke of Lu met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu. The men of Qi came to restore the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. 〔All in the tenth year of Duke Ding.〕 Shusun Zhouchou led troops to demolish the fortifications of Hou. Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led troops to demolish the fortifications of Fei. 〔Both in Duke Ding’s …〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
十有二年
禮記
大樂正論造士之秀者以告于王而升諸
司馬曰進士
詩言其志也歌咏其聲也舞動其容也三
者本於心然後樂器從之
福者備也備者百順之名也無所不順者
之謂備言内盡於己而外順於道也忠
臣以事其君孝子以事其親其本一也
上則順於鬼神外則順於君長内則以
===
孝於親如此之謂備
廉而不劌義也
第貳塲
論
大而化之之謂聖
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢詔諸儒講五經異同於石渠閣詔〔甘露三年〕
punctuated:
十有二年。

禮記
大樂正論造士之秀者，以告于王，而升諸司馬，曰進士。
詩言其志也，歌咏其聲也，舞動其容也。三者本於心，然後樂器從之。
福者，備也。備者，百順之名也。無所不順者之謂備，言内盡於己而外順於道也。忠臣以事其君，孝子以事其親，其本一也。上則順於鬼神，外則順於君長，内則以孝於親，如此之謂備。
廉而不劌，義也。

第貳塲
論
大而化之之謂聖。

詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢詔諸儒講五經異同於石渠閣詔〔甘露三年〕
translation_en:
…the twelfth year.

Book of Rites
The Director of Music assesses the outstanding men among those who have completed their studies, reports them to the king, and advances them to the Minister of War. They are called “advanced scholars” (jinshi).
Poetry expresses their aspirations; singing gives voice to their sounds; dance sets their bodily forms in motion. These three originate in the heart; only then do musical instruments accompany them.
Blessing means completeness. Completeness is the term for being in accord in every respect. To be in accord in all things is called completeness: this means fully realizing oneself inwardly and conforming to the Way outwardly. The loyal minister serving his ruler and the filial son serving his parents share the same foundation. Above, one accords with ghosts and spirits; outwardly, one accords with rulers and superiors; within the family, one is filial toward one’s parents. This is what is called completeness.
Having sharp edges without cutting others: this is righteousness.

Second Session
Discourse
“To be great and to transform others is called sageliness.”

Imperial Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials〔One question from among these categories [?].〕
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor commanding the Confucian scholars to discuss agreements and differences in the Five Classics at the Shiqu Pavilion.〔Third year of Ganlu.〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
擬唐以楊綰爲國子祭酒詔〔大曆五年〕
擬
頒賜醫方選要羣臣謝表
判語〔五條〕
官員赴任過限
擅食田園瓜果
私越冒渡關津
軍民約會詞訟
修理橋梁道路
===
第叁場
策五道
問自古帝王以緝熙之學而成雍熙之治
皆以敬爲建極之要唐虞三代不可尚
已至漢唐宋心法弗傳治僅小康無足
言也我
太祖高皇帝肇造區宇建其有極心法之傳聿
追往聖嘗
命儒臣書洪範揭之座右朝夕觀覽且自爲
punctuated:
擬唐以楊綰爲國子祭酒詔〔大曆五年〕。
擬頒賜醫方選要羣臣謝表。
判語〔五條〕：官員赴任過限；擅食田園瓜果；私越冒渡關津；軍民約會詞訟；修理橋梁道路。
第叁場
策五道
問：自古帝王以緝熙之學而成雍熙之治，皆以敬爲建極之要。唐虞三代不可尚已，至漢唐宋，心法弗傳，治僅小康，無足言也。我太祖高皇帝肇造區宇，建其有極，心法之傳聿追往聖。嘗命儒臣書洪範，揭之座右，朝夕觀覽，且自爲

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
之註其上明聖道下福萬民而垂千萬
世之訓者炳若日星此誠天下臣民所
宜對揚而莊誦之者其詳可得聞歟
列聖相承授守一道敷訓錫福以綏斯民治教
之盛如一日也可得而敬陳歟今我
皇上聰明
天縱懋隆
聖學萬幾之暇
親製敬一之箴五箴之註
===
聖謨洋洋真有以發前聖之蘊而與
太祖高皇帝自註洪範者同一揆矣其所以立
皇極叙彝倫保萬民叙四時成百穀者實與九
疇之義相為表裏可仰窺其萬一歟諸
生服膺
聖訓者有年矣願悉心鋪張以覲祗承之學
問士學宜師孔孟先儒格言也孔子教人
以明誠博約即虞廷精一之旨而知言
養氣之學自孟子之後其傳泯焉宋儒
punctuated:
之註，其上明聖道，下福萬民，而垂千萬世之訓者，炳若日星。此誠天下臣民所宜對揚而莊誦之者，其詳可得聞歟？列聖相承，授守一道，敷訓錫福，以綏斯民，治教之盛如一日也，可得而敬陳歟？今我皇上聰明天縱，懋隆聖學，萬幾之暇，親製敬一之箴、五箴之註。聖謨洋洋，真有以發前聖之蘊，而與太祖高皇帝自註洪範者同一揆矣。其所以立皇極、叙彝倫、保萬民、叙四時、成百穀者，實與九疇之義相為表裏，可仰窺其萬一歟？諸生服膺聖訓者有年矣，願悉心鋪張，以覲祗承之學。
問：士學宜師孔孟，先儒格言也。孔子教人以明誠博約，即虞廷精一之旨，而知言養氣之學，自孟子之後，其傳泯焉。宋儒
translation_en:
…a commentary on it. Its teachings, which illuminate the Way of the sages above, bring blessings to the myriad people below, and endure for countless generations, shine as brightly as the sun and stars. These are indeed teachings that all subjects of the realm ought reverently to acclaim and solemnly recite. May their details be heard? The successive sage emperors transmitted and upheld the same Way, disseminating instruction and bestowing blessings to bring peace to the people; the flourishing of their government and teaching remained constant throughout. Can you respectfully set this forth? Our present emperor, endowed by Heaven with intelligence, assiduously advances his sagely learning. Amid the myriad affairs of government, he personally composed the Admonition on Reverent Oneness and commentaries on the Five Admonitions. His abundant sagely counsels truly disclose the profound meanings of earlier sages and accord with the same principles as Emperor Taizu Gao’s own commentary on the Great Plan. The means by which they establish the imperial norm, set the constant human relationships in order, protect the myriad people, order the four seasons, and bring the many grains to maturity are, in truth, complementary to the meaning of the Nine Categories. Can you reverently discern even a fraction of this? You students have cherished the imperial instructions for years. We ask that you devote your whole minds to expounding them fully, thereby displaying the learning through which you reverently receive them.
Question: That scholars should take Confucius and Mencius as their teachers is a maxim of earlier Confucians. Confucius taught people through understanding and sincerity, breadth of learning and restraint through ritual: this is precisely the purport of refinement and oneness taught at Shun’s court. Yet after Mencius, the transmission of the learning concerned with understanding words and nourishing vital energy died out. The Song Confucian scholars…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
周子始崛起而默契之及程張繼作相
與闡明雖往聖絶學賴之不墜然論說
漸廣後學罔所折衷至於朱子始集諸
儒之大成其同時諸賢若呂祖謙張栻
蔡元定輩皆相輔翼上下以考究遺經
獨九淵陸氏兄弟各持其說此其見果
何歟說者謂子靜主尊德性朱子所論
道問學之功爲多今觀其鵝湖邂逅往
復辨難無慮數千百言而朱子何卒兼
===
其所長歟厥後九淵有論朱子以爲切
中學者深痼之病又以陸氏學者多持
守而欲棄短集長則陸氏之學其可病
乎而始譏其不免流弊何歟昔子夏親
受業於聖門一再傳而爲子方莊周陸
氏流弊豈或然也今之學者私淑孔孟
宜無異論設若有之其尊德性之功擬
諸象山若是班歟朱子可作將得以同
異論歟是竊有疑者敢以質於諸士子
punctuated: 周子始崛起而默契之，及程張繼作，相與闡明。雖往聖絶學賴之不墜，然論說漸廣，後學罔所折衷。至於朱子，始集諸儒之大成。其同時諸賢，若呂祖謙、張栻、蔡元定輩，皆相輔翼，上下以考究遺經。獨九淵陸氏兄弟各持其說，此其見果何歟？說者謂子靜主尊德性，朱子所論道問學之功爲多。今觀其鵝湖邂逅，往復辨難，無慮數千百言，而朱子何卒兼其所長歟？厥後九淵有論，朱子以爲切中學者深痼之病，又以陸氏學者多持守，而欲棄短集長，則陸氏之學其可病乎？而始譏其不免流弊，何歟？昔子夏親受業於聖門，一再傳而爲子方、莊周，陸氏流弊豈或然也？今之學者私淑孔孟，宜無異論。設若有之，其尊德性之功擬諸象山，若是班歟？朱子可作，將得以同異論歟？是竊有疑者，敢以質於諸士子。
translation_en:
…Master Zhou first rose to prominence and attained a tacit understanding of it. When the Cheng masters and Zhang subsequently emerged, they joined in elucidating it. Although their efforts preserved the lost learning of the ancient sages from extinction, their discussions gradually proliferated, leaving later students without a standard by which to adjudicate among them. Only with Master Zhu were the teachings of the various scholars brought together into a grand synthesis. His worthy contemporaries, such as Lü Zuqian, Zhang Shi, and Cai Yuanding, all supported one another, ranging widely in their examination of the surviving Classics. Only Lu Jiuyuan and his brothers each maintained their own explanations. What, in fact, were their views?

Some say that Zijing emphasized “honoring the moral nature,” whereas Master Zhu devoted more discussion to the work of “pursuing inquiry and study.” Now, when we examine their encounter at Ehu, their exchanges and disputations amounted to hundreds upon thousands of words. Why, then, did Master Zhu ultimately also incorporate the strengths of the other’s approach? Later, Jiuyuan advanced an argument that Master Zhu considered to strike directly at a deeply entrenched failing among students. He also considered students of the Lu school generally steadfast in their convictions and wished to discard their shortcomings and gather their strengths. Can Lu’s learning, then, be faulted? And why had he initially criticized it as unable to avoid harmful consequences in its subsequent development?

In former times, Zixia received instruction personally at the sage’s own school, yet after one or two transmissions his teaching became that of Zifang and Zhuang Zhou. Might the subsequent degeneration of Lu’s teaching perhaps be of this kind? Students today learn from Confucius and Mencius through their transmitted teachings and ought to have no divergent doctrines. Suppose, however, that some do: when their efforts to honor the moral nature are compared with those of Xiangshan, do they belong to the same rank [?]? If Master Zhu could rise again, could they then be judged in terms of agreement or disagreement with him? These are matters about which I privately harbor doubts, and I venture to submit them to you candidates.

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
問選舉考課之法尚矣周的前古其法大
備自今觀之以德詔爵以功詔祿以能
詔事以久奠食有司馬以掌選法而又
以六計弊羣吏之治詔廢置於歲終計
誅賞於三歲其載之周禮者可按籍考
也漢初行調選辟除之法後設吏部總
三曹之事選法畧備矣然以課爲考者
若甘泉明堂之受計其得失何如也唐
之選法分爲文武而置掌功過善惡之
===
考大率以四善二十七最爲例不知果
能稽功過之實否乎至宋選法兼總左
右而興國元祐紹興之考大率以四善
三等爲則不知果能核名實之真否乎
我
國家以科目取士以資格論官制盡善矣三
年一考六年再考九年通考法旣詳矣
其於成周之制同歟否歟抑或有可言
者歟豈因時損益固自有道歟試究言
punctuated: 問：選舉考課之法尚矣。周的前古，其法大備。自今觀之，以德詔爵，以功詔祿，以能詔事，以久奠食。有司馬以掌選法，而又以六計弊羣吏之治，詔廢置於歲終，計誅賞於三歲，其載之《周禮》者，可按籍考也。漢初行調選辟除之法，後設吏部總三曹之事，選法畧備矣。然以課爲考者，若甘泉明堂之受計，其得失何如也？唐之選法分爲文武，而置掌功過善惡之考，大率以四善二十七最爲例，不知果能稽功過之實否乎？至宋，選法兼總左右，而興國、元祐、紹興之考，大率以四善三等爲則，不知果能核名實之真否乎？我國家以科目取士，以資格論官，制盡善矣。三年一考，六年再考，九年通考，法旣詳矣。其於成周之制同歟否歟？抑或有可言者歟？豈因時損益固自有道歟？試究言
translation_en:
Question: Methods for selecting officials and evaluating their performance have existed since antiquity. The Zhou drew upon earlier antiquity [?], and its methods were comprehensively developed. Viewed from the present, rank was prescribed according to virtue, emoluments according to merit, duties according to ability, and maintenance according to length of service. There was a Minister of War to administer the selection rules; moreover, the six criteria were used to judge the administration of the assembled officials. Dismissals and appointments were prescribed at the year’s end, and punishments and rewards were assessed every three years. These provisions, recorded in the Rites of Zhou, can be examined by consulting that text. Early in the Han, methods of transfer and selection, recruitment, and appointment were practiced. Later, the Ministry of Personnel was established to oversee the affairs of the three bureaus, and the selection system became fairly comprehensive. Yet what were the strengths and weaknesses of evaluating officials through performance assessments, as in the reception of administrative accounts at Ganquan and the Hall of Light?

The Tang selection system distinguished civil from military officials and provided for assessments of merits and faults, good and bad conduct, generally taking the four virtues and twenty-seven standards of excellence as its norms. Could it truly ascertain actual merits and faults? Under the Song, the selection system encompassed both the left and right divisions, while the assessments of the Xingguo, Yuanyou, and Shaoxing eras generally took the four virtues and three grades as their standards. Could these truly verify whether reputation corresponded to actual performance?

Our dynasty recruits men through the examinations and determines official appointments according to qualifications and seniority: its institutions are thoroughly sound. There is an initial evaluation after three years, a second after six years, and a comprehensive evaluation after nine years: the rules are already detailed. Are they the same as the institutions of the Zhou, or not? Or is there something further to be said? Might there indeed be a proper way to modify institutions in accordance with the times? Examine this thoroughly and explain …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
之
問儒者明天之道纘政之紀洞索幽奧不
遺小物者也矧在天成象垂章效法有
弗求其故者乎夫星有經緯鉅細中外
可名圖籍具在姑置毋論試以大者言
之列宿之於四序隨指可辨也而書何
取諸中星太史之著天官四宮咸列也
而篇何首諸北極且書舉四仲聖謨既
彰月令載月所舉或戾魁杓七星居陰
===
布陽稱名取義厥文咸殊何歟考諸孔
氏鄭氏之禮疏春秋斗樞石氏星經之
訓釋圖可歷數也而劉焯與諸儒之論
歲差數又何異張衡以七政為緯義亦
何居呂氏十二章紀敬何如玉衡渾儀
法象何似然乎否歟諸士必聞其說願
有以質之也夫曆象日月星辰敬授人
時堯以正統也在璇璣玉衡以齊七政
舜以御天也帝王握樞者圖撫馭宇內
punctuated:
之。
問：儒者明天之道，纘政之紀，洞索幽奧，不遺小物者也。矧在天成象，垂章效法，有弗求其故者乎？夫星有經緯、鉅細、中外，可名，圖籍具在，姑置毋論。試以大者言之：列宿之於四序，隨指可辨也，而《書》何取諸中星？太史之著《天官》，四宮咸列也，而篇何首諸北極？且《書》舉四仲，聖謨既彰；《月令》載月，所舉或戾。魁杓七星，居陰布陽，稱名取義，厥文咸殊，何歟？考諸孔氏、鄭氏之禮疏，《春秋斗樞》、《石氏星經》之訓釋圖，可歷數也。而劉焯與諸儒之論歲差，數又何異？張衡以七政為緯，義亦何居？呂氏十二章紀敬何如？玉衡渾儀，法象何似？然乎否歟？諸士必聞其說，願有以質之也。夫曆象日月星辰，敬授人時，堯以正統也；在璇璣玉衡，以齊七政，舜以御天也。帝王握樞者圖，撫馭宇內
translation_en:
…this.
Question: Confucian scholars elucidate the Way of Heaven, carry forward the guiding principles of government, and probe deeply into hidden mysteries, overlooking nothing, however small. How much more, then, should they investigate the causes of the configurations formed in Heaven, which display patterns and offer models to follow?
The stars comprise fixed stars and wandering planets, large and small, inner and outer; they can be named, and charts and records of them are all available. Let us set these aside for now and discuss the major matters. The stellar lodges in relation to the four seasons can readily be pointed out and distinguished; why, then, does the Book of Documents select the stars culminating at dusk? In the Grand Astrologer’s Treatise on the Celestial Offices, all four celestial palaces are enumerated; why does the chapter begin with the north celestial pole? Furthermore, the Book of Documents sets forth the middle month of each of the four seasons, clearly revealing the sage’s designs. Yet the Monthly Ordinances records each month, and the stars it names sometimes conflict with these. The seven stars forming the bowl and handle of the Dipper occupy yin and disseminate yang; why do the texts differ in their names and the meanings assigned to them?
Consult the ritual commentaries of Kong and Zheng, and the explanations and diagrams in the Spring and Autumn: Pivot of the Dipper and Master Shi’s Star Canon: these matters can be enumerated one by one. Yet why do the numerical values for precession discussed by Liu Zhuo and the other scholars differ? What is the meaning of Zhang Heng’s treating the Seven Regulators as the wandering celestial bodies? What of Master Lü’s twelve chapters and their recording of reverence [?]? What do the jade sighting tube and armillary sphere take as their models? Are these accounts correct or not? You scholars must have heard these explanations; we hope you can offer something by which to assess them.
By calculating and observing the sun, moon, stars, and constellations, and reverently communicating the seasons to the people, Yao rectified the calendrical order. By examining the rotating mechanism and jade sighting tube to bring the Seven Regulators into harmony, Shun governed in accordance with Heaven. Emperors and kings grasp the pivot and make their plans [?], governing all within the realm…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
政莫尚焉其詳推所以於篇以觀博雅
之學
問歲有荒歉固適然之數而因時區畫以
爲之圖者人事不可緩也是故九年之
水七年之旱在堯湯所不免而民不告
饑者蓄積備也考周禮荒政十二而又
有遺人廩人司救之所掌其後若平糴
常平義倉之法或移粟以通用或移民
以就食或爲粥以救饑殍或興工作以
===
聚失業之民皆於荒政有補今亦可酌
行歟唐時遣使賑饑鬻子女者出金帛
以遺之而劉晏掌財賦不待困敝饑殍
然後賑宋命侍御史兼傳賑貸至慶曆
間其政尤詳時若富弼司馬光趙抃各
有賑饑之法與或建社倉或立賞格以
示勸或用八字榜文以示禁其法果可
行歟蘇氏論備荒有萬世之計非堯湯
所已行歟夫江右諸郡素稱富饒近年
punctuated:
政莫尚焉。其詳推所以於篇，以觀博雅之學。

問：歲有荒歉，固適然之數，而因時區畫以爲之圖者，人事不可緩也。是故九年之水、七年之旱，在堯湯所不免，而民不告饑者，蓄積備也。考《周禮》，荒政十二，而又有遺人、廩人、司救之所掌。其後若平糴、常平、義倉之法，或移粟以通用，或移民以就食，或爲粥以救饑殍，或興工作以聚失業之民，皆於荒政有補，今亦可酌行歟？唐時遣使賑饑，鬻子女者，出金帛以遺之；而劉晏掌財賦，不待困敝饑殍然後賑。宋命侍御史兼傳賑貸，至慶曆間，其政尤詳。時若富弼、司馬光、趙抃，各有賑饑之法與？或建社倉，或立賞格以示勸，或用八字榜文以示禁，其法果可行歟？蘇氏論備荒，有萬世之計，非堯湯所已行歟？夫江右諸郡，素稱富饒，近年
translation_en:
…no matter of governance ranks above this. Explain its underlying reasons fully in your essay, so that we may assess the breadth and refinement of your learning.

Question: Years of dearth and failed harvests are certainly contingencies of fate; yet devising measures suited to the circumstances is a human responsibility that cannot be delayed. Thus even Yao and Tang could not escape nine years of flooding and seven years of drought. That their people did not complain of hunger was due to adequate accumulated reserves. Examining the Rites of Zhou, we find twelve measures for famine administration, together with the responsibilities of the Provisioners (yiren), Granary Directors (linren), and Directors of Relief (sijiu). Later there were such institutions as equitable grain purchasing, ever-normal granaries, and charitable granaries. Some transported grain to make supplies available where needed; some moved people to places where they could obtain food; some prepared gruel to save those dying of hunger; and some initiated public works to gather and employ people who had lost their livelihoods. All these contributed to famine administration. Could they also be adopted today with appropriate discretion?

Under the Tang, envoys were dispatched to relieve famine, and money and silk were distributed to people who were selling their sons and daughters. When Liu Yan administered state revenues, he provided relief before people were reduced to destitution and death from starvation. The Song ordered a Palace Censor concurrently to convey relief and loans [?]; by the Qingli reign period, these administrative measures were especially detailed. Did men of that time such as Fu Bi, Sima Guang, and Zhao Bian each have their own methods of famine relief? Some established community granaries; some instituted schedules of rewards to encourage assistance; and some used proclamations of eight characters to announce prohibitions. Could these methods actually be put into practice? Master Su, in discussing preparations against famine, proposed a plan for all ages. Was this not what Yao and Tang had already practiced? Now, the prefectures of Jiangyou have long been renowned for their wealth and abundance, but in recent years…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
以來饑饉相仍蠲租發賑至厪
宵旰憂勞至渥也今雖歲一稍登然而備荒之
政亦不可不豫講者願一陳之以備採
擇
punctuated: 以來，饑饉相仍，蠲租發賑，至厪宵旰憂勞，至渥也。今雖歲一稍登，然而備荒之政亦不可不豫講者，願一陳之，以備採擇。
translation_en: … famine has followed famine. Tax remissions and the distribution of relief have even occasioned His Majesty’s anxious labors, from before dawn until late in the day; his solicitude has been most generous. Although the harvest has now somewhat improved [?], measures for preparing against famine must nevertheless be discussed in advance. Please set these forth for consideration and adoption.

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人九十五名

第二名張敏德　萬安縣學增廣生　易
第三名金　達　浮梁縣學生　書
第四名劉　憲　安福縣學增廣生　春秋
第五名李　衮　南昌縣學附學生　禮記
第六名黎　澄　樂平縣學生　詩

第十名羅　良　萬安縣學增廣生　禮記

First Session
Four Books

The Master said: “Shen! My Way is threaded together by one principle.” Master Zeng said: “Yes.” When the Master went out, the disciples asked: “What did he mean?” Master Zeng said: “Our Master’s Way is simply conscientiousness and reciprocity.”

Yi Hongqi

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔This passage speaks in terms of practice; this composition grasps it.〕

The great worthy deeply apprehended the transmission of the sage’s Way and thereby revealed its underlying meaning. For the entirety of the sage’s Way consists in nothing beyond its unity through one principle. The great worthy deeply apprehended it and revealed its underlying meaning: he indeed knew how to learn from the sage.

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
□之由當者同歸而殊途大公以立順應之原
而物理之散殊者百慮而一致成性爲道義之
門一實萬分也大本妙達道之用萬原於一也
吾之道知是而已曾子一聞斯言而卽應之曰
唯蓋當可之施適觸其將得之機而神契之妙
自不假於言語之贅矣于時門人聞言雖同而
悟道則異故於夫子旣出而有何謂之問焉蓋
心法之傳固非淺學所能識而獨得之蘊有難
直指而明言故曾子借學者之事而曉之曰夫
===
子之道非有他也卽學者之盡其心而忠焉推
其心而恕焉耳矣果雖勉强以推行若不出乎
下學之功要其體用之合一亦可通乎上達之
妙知忠之達乎恕也推之於物而各足則一實
萬分以昭吾心之大用者卽此而在矣知恕之
本乎忠也反之於己而有餘則萬原於一以立
吾心之全體者又豈有他哉故謂夫子之道不
外於忠恕可也謂由忠恕以求夫子之道亦可
也噫若曾子者可謂善發聖人之蘊者矣非其
punctuated: □之由當者，同歸而殊途；大公以立順應之原，而物理之散殊者，百慮而一致。成性爲道義之門，一實萬分也；大本妙達道之用，萬原於一也。吾之道，知是而已。」曾子一聞斯言，而卽應之曰：「唯。」蓋當可之施，適觸其將得之機，而神契之妙，自不假於言語之贅矣。于時門人聞言雖同，而悟道則異，故於夫子旣出，而有何謂之問焉。蓋心法之傳，固非淺學所能識，而獨得之蘊，有難直指而明言，故曾子借學者之事而曉之曰：「夫子之道，非有他也，卽學者之盡其心而忠焉，推其心而恕焉耳矣。果雖勉强以推行，若不出乎下學之功，要其體用之合一，亦可通乎上達之妙。知忠之達乎恕也，推之於物而各足，則一實萬分，以昭吾心之大用者，卽此而在矣。知恕之本乎忠也，反之於己而有餘，則萬原於一，以立吾心之全體者，又豈有他哉？故謂夫子之道不外於忠恕，可也；謂由忠恕以求夫子之道，亦可也。」噫！若曾子者，可謂善發聖人之蘊者矣。非其
translation_en:
…those that attain fittingness through □ [?] reach the same destination by different paths. Perfect impartiality establishes the source of responding appropriately, so that the diverse principles of things converge upon one through a hundred deliberations. Fully realized nature becomes the gateway of the Way and righteousness: one reality differentiates into myriad manifestations. The great foundation wondrously brings into operation the universally practiced Way: the myriad have their source in the one. To know this is all there is to my Way.” Upon hearing these words, Zengzi immediately answered, “Yes.” The instruction, fittingly bestowed, touched precisely the moment when he was about to attain understanding. The marvel of this intuitive accord required no superfluous words.

Although the disciples then heard the same words, their understanding of the Way differed. Thus, after the Master had left, they asked what he meant. The transmission of the teaching of the mind is indeed beyond the comprehension of those of shallow learning; moreover, the profound meaning that Zengzi alone had grasped was difficult to point out directly and explain plainly. He therefore drew upon the practices of learners to enlighten them, saying: “The Master’s Way is nothing other than learners exhausting the capacities of their own minds in conscientiousness and extending their minds to others in reciprocity. Though putting these into practice may indeed require effort, and may seem confined to the work of learning at the ordinary level, their unity of substance and function can nevertheless lead to the subtle understanding attained on high. Recognize that conscientiousness extends into reciprocity: extend it to things so that each receives its due, and here lies the one reality differentiated into myriad manifestations, revealing the great functioning of my mind. Recognize that reciprocity is rooted in conscientiousness: turn back to oneself and find more than enough, and what else could establish the complete substance of my mind, with the myriad having their source in the one? Thus it is permissible to say that the Master’s Way does not go beyond conscientiousness and reciprocity; it is also permissible to say that one seeks the Master’s Way through conscientiousness and reciprocity.”

Ah! Someone such as Zengzi may be called adept at bringing forth the sage’s profound meaning. Had he not…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
學之眞有得焉烏足以語此抑斯道也卽夫子
博約之訓而無隱於二三子者也但學者習矣
不察雖賜之穎悟猶不免於多識之疑以參之
魯亦必待積久而後得惟不違如愚者其殆庶
幾乎蓋上焉者得意而忘言其次因言以得意
是知賜之達不若參之魯參之魯不若回之愚
優優大哉禮儀三百威儀三千
金達
同考試官教諭李　批〔道體事無不在作者藹〕
〔於優優發揮殊失本旨子能卽禮會道而文足以發之其善〕
===
〔作中庸義者錄之〕
考試官學正張　批〔說理精切非有得於道〕
〔者不能作此也〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔詞語充足而思致縝密〕
〔文字之優者是用錄出〕
中庸贊聖道之大必舉禮之全者以見之也夫
道者禮之原也舉禮之全而道無不在焉則其
大也可見矣中庸二十七章發明人道也意以
punctuated:
學之眞有得焉，烏足以語此？抑斯道也，卽夫子博約之訓，而無隱於二三子者也。但學者習矣不察，雖賜之穎悟，猶不免於多識之疑；以參之魯，亦必待積久而後得。惟不違如愚者，其殆庶幾乎！蓋上焉者得意而忘言，其次因言以得意。是知賜之達不若參之魯，參之魯不若回之愚。

優優大哉！禮儀三百，威儀三千。
金達

translation_en:
…without true attainment in his learning, how could he have spoken of this? Moreover, this Way is precisely what the Master taught concerning breadth of learning and restraint through ritual; he concealed none of it from his disciples. Yet learners grow accustomed to it without examining it. Even Ci, with his keen understanding, could not escape uncertainty over whether the Master’s learning consisted in knowing many things. Shen, with his dullness, likewise had to accumulate learning over a long period before attaining understanding. Only the one who never contradicted the Master and seemed foolish came close! The highest grasp the meaning and forget the words; those next in rank attain the meaning through the words. Thus we know that Ci’s intelligence did not equal Shen’s dullness, and Shen’s dullness did not equal Hui’s foolishness.

“How abundant and great! Three hundred ceremonial observances and three thousand rules of deportment.”
Jin Da

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The substance of the Way is present in every affair. Writers [?] elaborate upon ‘abundant,’ greatly missing the original purport. You can apprehend the Way through ritual itself, and your writing adequately brings it forth. This is someone skilled at composing an exposition of the Doctrine of the Mean; I select it.”

Examiner Zhang, School Director, comments: “The explanation of principle is precise and penetrating. No one without an understanding of the Way could have written this.”

Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: “The language is ample, and the thought meticulous. This is an excellent piece of writing, and for that reason it is selected.”

In praising the greatness of the sages’ Way, the Doctrine of the Mean necessarily presents ritual in its entirety to make that greatness manifest. The Way is the source of ritual. When ritual is presented in its entirety, the Way is present everywhere within it, and its greatness can thus be seen. Chapter twenty-seven of the Doctrine of the Mean elucidates the human Way. Its meaning is that…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖人之道之大豈惟發育峻極而已哉然亦入
於至小而無間也使小有弗入則亦大之未至
矣蓋其易簡之能貫徹於事爲而隨在各足中
正之則分布於酬酢而體物不遺極天下之至
繁有以盡該括之神裕於此而達於彼也舉天
下之至賾有以極充周之妙此有餘而彼無不
足也不亦優優其大矣乎自今觀之敦典於會
通之觀而盡倫之教行焉夫是之謂禮儀於稽
其類不有三百者乎本天常以爲則而陳之藝
===
極以辨天下之輿因人情以爲制而章之軌物
以合天下之敬是雖宏綱要領區以別矣而大
經大法所以範圍而不過者道爲之綱維也道
固無體之禮矣果於禮儀而有遺乎顯設於人
文之賁而盡飾之教行焉夫是之謂威儀其數
可陳不有三千者乎登降有度而恭遜之施順
適於動容之間隆殺異宜而品節之詳雍容於
嘉會之合是雖繁文縟節散以殊矣而中規中
矩所以曲成而不遺者道爲之推行也道固無
punctuated: 聖人之道之大，豈惟發育峻極而已哉？然亦入於至小而無間也。使小有弗入，則亦大之未至矣。蓋其易簡之能，貫徹於事爲，而隨在各足；中正之則，分布於酬酢，而體物不遺。極天下之至繁，有以盡該括之神，裕於此而達於彼也；舉天下之至賾，有以極充周之妙，此有餘而彼無不足也。不亦優優其大矣乎？自今觀之，敦典於會通之觀，而盡倫之教行焉。夫是之謂禮儀，於稽其類，不有三百者乎？本天常以爲則，而陳之藝極，以辨天下之輿；因人情以爲制，而章之軌物，以合天下之敬。是雖宏綱要領，區以別矣，而大經大法，所以範圍而不過者，道爲之綱維也。道固無體之禮矣，果於禮儀而有遺乎？顯設於人文之賁，而盡飾之教行焉。夫是之謂威儀，其數可陳，不有三千者乎？登降有度，而恭遜之施，順適於動容之間；隆殺異宜，而品節之詳，雍容於嘉會之合。是雖繁文縟節，散以殊矣，而中規中矩，所以曲成而不遺者，道爲之推行也。道固無
translation_en:
…Could the greatness of the sage’s Way consist merely in nourishing and developing all things and reaching the loftiest heights? It also enters into the very smallest things without leaving any gap. If there were anything small that it failed to enter, its greatness would still fall short of perfection. Its capacity for ease and simplicity permeates human affairs and actions and is fully sufficient wherever it is found; its standards of centrality and correctness extend throughout reciprocal dealings, embodying all things without omission. Even amid the utmost complexity of the world, it fully manifests its wondrous power of comprehensive inclusion, abundant here and reaching there. Encompassing the deepest intricacies of the world, it brings its marvelous all-pervasiveness to perfection: here there is more than enough, and there nothing is lacking. Is its greatness not ample indeed?

Viewed from our present standpoint, it gives substance to the constant norms through a comprehensive understanding of their interconnections, and thus instruction that fulfills all human relationships takes effect. These are what we call the ceremonial rites. When their categories are examined, are there not three hundred? Taking Heaven’s constant principles as their standard, they set these forth as normative limits to distinguish the multitudes of the world [?]; grounding their regulations in human feelings, they make these manifest in rules of conduct so as to unite the reverence of all under Heaven. Although these broad outlines and essential principles are divided into distinct categories, it is the Way that holds them together as its guiding framework, enabling these great norms and laws to encompass all things without overstepping their bounds. The Way is indeed ritual without bodily form. Could it really leave anything out of the ceremonial rites?

It is visibly displayed in the embellishments of human culture, and thus instruction that brings refinement to its fullest expression takes effect. These are what we call the rules of dignified deportment. Their number can be enumerated: are there not three thousand? Ascending and descending have their prescribed measures, and expressions of respect and deference accord fittingly with each movement and bearing. Greater and lesser degrees of ceremony each have their appropriate application, and the detailed gradations of observance unfold with composed grace in auspicious gatherings. Although these elaborate forms and intricate observances are dispersed into distinct particulars, it is the Way that puts them into operation, enabling them to accord with compass and square and to bring each particular to fulfillment without omission. The Way is indeed without …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
形之禮矣果於威儀而有問乎是知禮本乎道
道寓於禮其入乎小者乃所以爲大也體道君
子其功豈可忽哉是故尊德性而存吾心焉所
以極乎其大也道問學而致吾知焉所以盡乎
其細也二者交致其功而聖道之大可馴至矣
或者不察以問學爲可緩是不免擇之不精於
德性也亦蔽矣不然則孔子之問禮問官何哉
吁學者可以自悟矣
君子所性仁義禮智根於心其生色也睟
然見於面盎於背施於四體四體不言
而喻
===
劉憲
同考試官教諭招　批〔根本於心由於氣稟無累此作深得孟子之意而詞意燁然子非根心生色者耶起〕
敬起敬
考試官學正張　批〔融會傳註成文必積盛者宜錄〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔曲盡所性之藴〕
punctuated:
形之禮矣，果於威儀而有問乎？是知禮本乎道，道寓於禮，其入乎小者，乃所以爲大也。體道君子，其功豈可忽哉？是故尊德性而存吾心焉，所以極乎其大也；道問學而致吾知焉，所以盡乎其細也。二者交致其功，而聖道之大可馴至矣。或者不察，以問學爲可緩，是不免擇之不精，於德性也亦蔽矣。不然，則孔子之問禮問官何哉？吁！學者可以自悟矣。
君子所性，仁義禮智根於心，其生色也睟然見於面，盎於背，施於四體，四體不言而喻。
劉憲
同考試官教諭招，批〔根本於心，由於氣稟無累。此作深得孟子之意，而詞意燁然。子非根心生色者耶？起〕
敬起敬
考試官學正張，批〔融會傳註成文，必積盛者，宜錄。〕
考試官教授鄭，批〔曲盡所性之藴。〕
translation_en:
…ritual without form; can there really be any gap [?] between it and ceremonial deportment? Thus we know that ritual is rooted in the Way, and the Way resides in ritual. Its penetration into small matters is precisely how it achieves greatness. How could the gentleman who embodies the Way neglect this work? Therefore, honoring our moral nature and preserving our heart is how we reach the utmost of its greatness; pursuing inquiry and learning and extending our knowledge is how we fully comprehend its subtleties. When these two bring their efforts to bear together, the greatness of the sages’ Way can gradually be attained. Some fail to perceive this and suppose that inquiry and learning may be postponed. They inevitably lack discrimination in their choices and are also obscured in their understanding of moral nature. Otherwise, why did Confucius inquire about ritual and official institutions? Ah! Students can come to understand this for themselves.
What the gentleman possesses as his nature—benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom—is rooted in his heart. The luster it produces appears with pure clarity in his face, fills his back, and extends to his four limbs. Without speaking, his four limbs make it understood.
Liu Xian.
Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: “Being rooted in the heart comes from freedom from the encumbrances of one’s endowment of vital energy. This composition deeply grasps Mencius’s meaning, and its language and ideas shine brilliantly. Are you not yourself one whose virtue is rooted in the heart and produces this luster? [The annotation ends with the stray character 起, ‘rise’ or ‘begin’; its connection to the following text is unclear.]
[The text here reads 敬起敬, ‘reverence—rise—reverence’; its meaning is unclear.]
Examiner Zhang, Instructor (xuezheng), comments: “He integrates the commentarial tradition into a coherent composition. He must be someone with abundant accumulated learning; this deserves selection.”
Examiner Zheng, Instructor (jiaoshou), comments: “It fully explores every subtlety of what the gentleman possesses as his nature.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
大賢著君子所性之蘊而有積中發外之妙焉
蓋性立天下之有也君子性既積於中矣則其
發外之妙豈容已耶孟子之意以爲君子所性
夫既欲樂不與存而窮達無加損矣顧不有所
蘊之可言乎蓋其得於天者有以全於我足於
已者無所待於外仁義禮智根於心也我固有
之也存存者其成性也而純粹之精不誘於攻
取之欲性性者其存神也而清明之稟不梏於
有我之私是其性命於德德勝其氣德之積也
===
亦盛矣由是而生於色也誠則必形和順妙於
英華之發德則能潤光輝溢於篤實之餘以言
乎面非有期於睟也神之所融而聚爲有象自
爾清和潤澤一兌之悅而示人可親矣以言乎
背非有期於盎也精之所凝而適得吾體自爾
豐厚盈溢一艮之止而示人可重矣以言乎四
體不必議之後動也從心所欲不踰乎矩不必
言而後信也動容周旋自中乎禮蓋有手之舞
足之蹈而莫知其然者矣夫孰非其根於心者
punctuated: 大賢著君子所性之蘊，而有積中發外之妙焉。蓋性立天下之有也，君子性既積於中矣，則其發外之妙豈容已耶？孟子之意以爲：君子所性，夫既欲樂不與存，而窮達無加損矣，顧不有所蘊之可言乎？蓋其得於天者有以全於我，足於已者無所待於外。仁義禮智根於心也，我固有之也。存存者其成性也，而純粹之精不誘於攻取之欲；性性者其存神也，而清明之稟不梏於有我之私。是其性命於德，德勝其氣，德之積也亦盛矣。由是而生於色也，誠則必形，和順妙於英華之發；德則能潤，光輝溢於篤實之餘。以言乎面，非有期於睟也，神之所融而聚爲有象，自爾清和潤澤，一兌之悅，而示人可親矣。以言乎背，非有期於盎也，精之所凝而適得吾體，自爾豐厚盈溢，一艮之止，而示人可重矣。以言乎四體，不必議之後動也，從心所欲不踰乎矩；不必言而後信也，動容周旋自中乎禮。蓋有手之舞、足之蹈而莫知其然者矣。夫孰非其根於心者
translation_en:
The great worthy reveals the depth of what constitutes the gentleman’s nature, together with the wondrous way in which what accumulates within manifests itself outwardly. For nature establishes all that exists under Heaven [?]. Once the gentleman’s nature has accumulated within, how could its wondrous outward manifestation be restrained? Mencius’s meaning is this: what constitutes the gentleman’s nature is independent of his desires and pleasures, and neither adversity nor success adds to or diminishes it. Yet surely its inner depth can be discussed? What he receives from Heaven is preserved whole within himself; what is sufficient in himself depends on nothing external. Benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom are rooted in his heart: he inherently possesses them. Continually preserving them brings his nature to completion, so that its pure essence is not enticed by desires for conquest and acquisition. Giving full expression to his nature preserves his spiritual efficacy, so that his clear and luminous endowment is not fettered by selfish attachment to the self. Thus his nature takes its mandate from virtue, and virtue prevails over his vital force; the accumulation of virtue is indeed abundant.

From this it comes to manifest itself in his countenance. Sincerity necessarily takes visible form: harmony and accord find wondrous expression in blossoming beauty. Virtue imparts lustre: radiance overflows from the fullness of solid integrity. As for his face, he does not deliberately seek a clear and lustrous appearance. His spiritual efficacy suffuses it and gathers into visible form, making it naturally clear, harmonious, and radiant—the joy of the Dui trigram, showing others that he is approachable. As for his back, he does not deliberately seek fullness. His concentrated essence finds fitting embodiment in his person, making it naturally ample and overflowing—the stillness of the Gen trigram, showing others that he commands respect. As for his four limbs, he need not deliberate before moving: he follows his heart’s desires without overstepping the bounds. He need not speak before being trusted: his bearing and every movement naturally accord with ritual propriety. Indeed, his hands dance and his feet stamp without his knowing how it comes about. Which of these is not something rooted in his heart …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
爲之耶是則所性之蘊豫於內而利於外道本
至足吾自足焉而已使其達也以之兼善天下
窮也以之獨善其身隨其所遇夫亦安之而已
又何加損之有是何也吾性本無大行窮居也
是故無加損也舜禹有天下而不與孔子用則
行舍則藏凡以是也彼以性爲外而庸心於得
喪者固不勝其私而戚矣孟子存心養性勿助
勿忘雖加齊之卿相而不動心去齊而未嘗不
豫可以占其蘊矣
===
易
文言曰元者善之長也亨者嘉之會也利
者義之和也貞者事之幹也君子體仁
足以長人嘉會足以合禮利物足以和
義貞固足以幹事君子行此四德者故
曰乾元亨利貞
張敏德
同考試官教諭聶　批
〔人之四德法天之健斯能合德于天善發揚者其惟子乎〕
punctuated:
爲之耶？是則所性之蘊，豫於內而利於外，道本至足，吾自足焉而已。使其達也，以之兼善天下；窮也，以之獨善其身。隨其所遇，夫亦安之而已，又何加損之有？是何也？吾性本無大行窮居也，是故無加損也。舜禹有天下而不與，孔子用則行，舍則藏，凡以是也。彼以性爲外而庸心於得喪者，固不勝其私而戚矣。孟子存心養性，勿助勿忘，雖加齊之卿相而不動心，去齊而未嘗不豫，可以占其蘊矣。

易

文言曰：「元者，善之長也；亨者，嘉之會也；利者，義之和也；貞者，事之幹也。君子體仁，足以長人；嘉會，足以合禮；利物，足以和義；貞固，足以幹事。君子行此四德者，故曰：『乾，元亨利貞。』」

張敏德

同考試官教諭聶　批〔人之四德，法天之健，斯能合德于天。善發揚者，其惟子乎！〕
translation_en:
…bring this about? Thus the riches of one's inherent nature bring contentment within and benefit without. The Way is supremely sufficient in itself; I simply find my own sufficiency in it. Should one attain prominence, one uses it to bring goodness to all under Heaven; in obscurity, one uses it to perfect oneself alone. Whatever circumstances one encounters, one simply rests content in them. What increase or diminution could there be? Why is this? Our nature originally makes no distinction between exercising great influence and dwelling in obscurity; hence it suffers neither increase nor diminution. Shun and Yu possessed all under Heaven yet remained unattached to it; Confucius acted when employed and withdrew when set aside. All this followed from the same principle. Those who regard their nature as something external and occupy their minds with gain and loss cannot overcome their selfishness and are therefore distressed. Mencius preserved his mind and nourished his nature, neither forcing its growth nor neglecting it. Even the prospect of appointment as a high minister or chief councilor of Qi did not move his mind; nor did he cease to be content when he left Qi. From this we may discern his inner resources.

Book of Changes

The Commentary on the Words of the Text says: “Origination is the chief of goodness; flourishing is the convergence of excellence; benefit is the harmony of righteousness; steadfastness is the foundation of affairs. The gentleman embodies benevolence and is thereby able to lead others; he brings excellence together and is thereby able to accord with ritual propriety; he benefits things and is thereby able to harmonize with righteousness; he is steadfast and firm and is thereby able to manage affairs. The gentleman practices these four virtues. Hence it is said: ‘Qian: origination, flourishing, benefit, and steadfastness.’”

Zhang Minde

Comment by Associate Examiner Nie, Instructor: 〔Only when the four human virtues take Heaven's vigor as their model can human virtue accord with Heaven. Surely you are one who excels at elucidating this!〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭高　批〔善說乾象之義佳士佳士〕
同考試官教諭袁　批〔題意簡潔此作得之〕
考試官學正張　批〔詞采自是渾成〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔精練〕
觀文言申乾象之意而天人合一之妙見矣蓋
君子之有四德猶夫天也而所以行之者健也
乾亦健而已矣天人合一之妙不可見哉文言
申乾象傳之意所以盡其藴也蓋謂乾之道具
===
於易其原出於天神而明之存乎其人是故在
天有元亨利貞在人為仁義禮智繼之者善成
之者性也仁則心之德愛之理而統天下之善
者在是禮則敬之合德之聚而嘉天下之會者
在是義其動而正用而和公天下之利者乎智
其守之貴行之利一天下之動者乎是則天之
未始不為人而能體之者君子也君子以仁為
體無弗愛也大心體物而宜君宜王矣嘉其所
會無弗敬也周旋中禮而有經有緯矣使物各
punctuated:
同考試官教諭高批〔善說乾象之義，佳士！佳士！〕
同考試官教諭袁批〔題意簡潔，此作得之。〕
考試官學正張批〔詞采自是渾成。〕
考試官教授鄭批〔精練。〕
觀文言申乾象之意，而天人合一之妙見矣。蓋君子之有四德，猶夫天也，而所以行之者健也。乾亦健而已矣，天人合一之妙不可見哉？文言申乾象傳之意，所以盡其藴也。蓋謂乾之道具於易，其原出於天，神而明之，存乎其人。是故在天有元亨利貞，在人為仁義禮智，繼之者善，成之者性也。仁則心之德、愛之理，而統天下之善者在是；禮則敬之合、德之聚，而嘉天下之會者在是；義，其動而正、用而和、公天下之利者乎？智，其守之貴、行之利、一天下之動者乎？是則天之未始不為人，而能體之者君子也。君子以仁為體，無弗愛也，大心體物，而宜君宜王矣；嘉其所會，無弗敬也，周旋中禮，而有經有緯矣；使物各
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: 〔“An excellent explanation of the meaning of the Image of Qian. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!”〕
Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: 〔“The meaning of the topic is concise and clear; this composition captures it.”〕
Examiner Zhang, School Director, comments: 〔“The literary expression is naturally an integrated whole.”〕
Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: 〔“Refined and concise.”〕
When we examine how the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) elaborates the meaning of the Image of Qian, the subtle wonder of the unity of Heaven and humanity becomes apparent. The gentleman possesses four virtues, just as Heaven does, and what enables him to put them into practice is vigor. Qian, too, is simply vigor. Can we not see here the subtle wonder of the unity of Heaven and humanity? The Wenyan elaborates the meaning of the Commentary on the Image of Qian in order to bring out all that it contains. The Way of Qian is fully embodied in the Book of Changes, and its source lies in Heaven; making its spiritual efficacy manifest and comprehensible depends upon the person. Thus, in Heaven there are origination, flourishing, benefit, and firmness; in humanity these are benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom. What continues this is goodness; what brings it to completion is human nature. Benevolence is the virtue of the heart and the principle of love: herein lies that which encompasses all goodness under Heaven. Ritual propriety is the convergence of reverence and the gathering of virtue: herein lies that which makes the gatherings of all under Heaven admirable. Is righteousness not that which is correct in action, harmonious in application, and impartial in distributing benefits throughout the world? Is wisdom not that which is precious to preserve, beneficial to practice, and unifies all activity under Heaven? Thus Heaven has never been separate from humanity, and it is the gentleman who can embody it. The gentleman takes benevolence as his substance and loves everything without exception. Enlarging his heart to embody all things, he is fit to be a ruler and a king. Making admirable that which he brings together, he treats everything with reverence. His every movement accords with ritual propriety, giving his conduct both warp and weft. He causes all things each to …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
得其利則雖嚴而泰衆動得時措之宜矣知正
而固守之則能擇而守凡事有豫立之基矣是
則人之未始不爲天而其所以行之者至健也
蓋欲之勝者或得以間理氣之餒者不能以配
道君子則直養無害而天德之剛能勝夫人欲
之私故德性常用而四端之善不虧於付畀之
初兼體而不累存神其至矣非天下之至健其
孰能與於此故曰乾元亨利貞以元亨利貞而
必屬之乾者此也蓋天運而不已故物生而不
===
窮非乾則天道亦幾乎息矣是則天人合一之
妙而文王象乾之餘蘊也非文言其孰能發之
抑乾道也天道也人道也皆本於健固也而健
豈易言哉天良能本吾良能顧爲有我所喪爾
有我則私私則二二則息息則與乾道天道不
相似矣君子乾乾自強所以成之於天者亦惟
去其有我之私耳故曰自勝者強
允升大吉上合志也
張正位
punctuated:
得其利，則雖嚴而泰，衆動得時措之宜矣。知正而固守之，則能擇而守，凡事有豫立之基矣。是則人之未始不爲天，而其所以行之者，至健也。蓋欲之勝者，或得以間理；氣之餒者，不能以配道。君子則直養無害，而天德之剛能勝夫人欲之私，故德性常用，而四端之善不虧於付畀之初。兼體而不累，存神其至矣。非天下之至健，其孰能與於此？故曰：「乾，元亨利貞。」以元亨利貞而必屬之乾者，此也。蓋天運而不已，故物生而不窮。非乾，則天道亦幾乎息矣。是則天人合一之妙，而文王象乾之餘蘊也。非《文言》，其孰能發之？抑乾道也，天道也，人道也，皆本於健固也，而健豈易言哉！天良能，本吾良能，顧爲有我所喪爾。有我則私，私則二，二則息，息則與乾道、天道不相似矣。君子乾乾自強，所以成之於天者，亦惟去其有我之私耳。故曰：「自勝者強。」

允升，大吉，上合志也。
張正位
translation_en:
…each obtain its proper benefit, then, though strict, he brings ease, and all activities are undertaken as the circumstances require. Knowing what is correct and holding firmly to it, he can choose and maintain it, giving every undertaking a foundation established in advance. Thus human beings have never been separate from Heaven, and what enables them to put this into practice is utmost vigor. When desires prevail, they may intrude upon principle; when vital energy falters, it cannot match the Way. The gentleman, however, nourishes it with uprightness and does it no injury, so that the firmness of Heaven’s virtue can overcome the selfishness of human desires. Thus his virtuous nature remains constantly active, and the goodness of the four beginnings is undiminished from the moment of its original endowment. Embracing all things without being burdened by them, he preserves the spirit to the utmost. Who but one possessed of the greatest vigor under Heaven could attain this? Hence the statement: “Qian: origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy.” This is why origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy must be attributed to Qian. Heaven moves without ceasing, and thus the generation of things is inexhaustible. Without Qian, even the Way of Heaven would come close to stopping. This is the subtle wonder of the unity of Heaven and humanity, and the further meaning implicit in King Wen’s representation of Qian. Without the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan), who could bring it to light? Moreover, the Way of Qian, the Way of Heaven, and the human Way are all rooted in vigor and firmness. Yet how could vigor be easy to speak of! Heaven’s innate capacity is fundamentally my own innate capacity; it is only lost through attachment to a self. Attachment to a self produces selfishness; selfishness produces division; division produces cessation. With cessation, one no longer resembles the Way of Qian or the Way of Heaven. The gentleman tirelessly exerts himself and strengthens himself; the means by which he fulfills himself in relation to Heaven consist simply in removing the selfishness of attachment to a self. Hence the saying: “He who overcomes himself is strong.”

“Sincerely ascending: great good fortune.” This is because his purpose accords with that of the one above.
Zhang Zhengwei.

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭聶　批　〔君子脩于家而未獲允升之吉志未孚也安有志既孚而不獲允升之吉者乎子可謂能言其義者矣錄之〕
同考試官教諭袁　批　〔講上下交孚處讀之令人灑然〕
同考試官教諭高　批　〔善發明君子獲吉之旨〕
考試官學正張　批　〔題義是矣〕
考試官教授鄭　批　〔簡明可誦〕
象傳原爻獲升之善而著其同德之孚也蓋君
===
子之於天下未嘗孤而立也初六志同於上而
德孚焉則其進而獲善也必矣夫子小象之意
以為欲升者君子之同心而能升者君子所難
必乃惟初六之辭曰允升大吉則是攸往之利
得於交孚之間而兼善之施溥於協恭之下以
見大人則勿用憂恤而明良胥慶於一時以之
南征則尚往志行而名實得加於上下若是者
而豈徒哉亦以志之上合耳蓋門庭不出由上
無應與之人而拔茅彙征以陽皆在外之志初
punctuated:
同考試官教諭聶　批　〔君子脩于家而未獲允升之吉，志未孚也。安有志既孚而不獲允升之吉者乎？子可謂能言其義者矣，錄之。〕
同考試官教諭袁　批　〔講上下交孚處，讀之令人灑然。〕
同考試官教諭高　批　〔善發明君子獲吉之旨。〕
考試官學正張　批　〔題義是矣。〕
考試官教授鄭　批　〔簡明可誦。〕
象傳原爻獲升之善，而著其同德之孚也。蓋君子之於天下，未嘗孤而立也。初六志同於上而德孚焉，則其進而獲善也必矣。夫子小象之意，以為欲升者君子之同心，而能升者君子所難必。乃惟初六之辭曰：「允升，大吉。」則是攸往之利得於交孚之間，而兼善之施溥於協恭之下。以見大人，則勿用憂恤，而明良胥慶於一時；以之南征，則尚往志行，而名實得加於上下。若是者，而豈徒哉？亦以志之上合耳。蓋門庭不出，由上無應與之人；而拔茅彙征，以陽皆在外之志。初
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Nie, Instructor, comments: 〔When a gentleman cultivates himself at home but has not yet obtained the good fortune of “ascending with confidence,” it is because his aspirations have not yet won trust. How could his aspirations have won trust without his obtaining this good fortune? You may indeed be said to have expressed its meaning well. Include this answer.〕
Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: 〔The discussion of mutual trust between those above and below is refreshing to read.〕
Associate Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: 〔It elucidates well the meaning of the gentleman’s obtaining good fortune.〕
Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning of the topic is correctly understood.〕
Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: 〔Concise, clear, and worthy of recitation.〕
The Commentary on the Images traces the source of the good attained through ascent in this line and makes manifest the mutual trust arising from shared virtue. For a gentleman never stands alone in the world. When the initial six shares the aspirations of those above and wins their trust through virtue, its advancement and attainment of good are assured. The Master’s meaning in the Lesser Image Commentary is that the desire to ascend is common to gentlemen, but their ability to ascend is something they cannot readily count upon. Yet the text of the initial six specifically says: “Ascending with confidence: great good fortune.” Thus the benefit of having somewhere to go is obtained through mutual trust, and the beneficent work of bringing goodness to others spreads widely through harmonious, reverent cooperation. In seeing the great man, there is no need for anxiety, and an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers rejoice together at the same time. In going south, advancement is esteemed and aspirations are realized, while both reputation and actual achievement may accrue to those above and below. Could such results come about without cause? They arise because one’s aspirations accord with those above.

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
六以陰居下爲巽之主當升之時巽於二陽利
用禴者二也上下交孚者也初則賴其孚而因
以上達焉進退得以關其忠升虛邑者三也進
往無疑者也初則隨其進而與之同升焉任職
得以行其術相須之殷也而相契之深利見以
從王之事者乃與類行不戒以孚也奚用憂恤
乎同道相益也而同心相與南征以熙帝之載
者朋至斯孚不謀而協也志有不行乎如是而
其升也固在所必然其獲吉也亦非爲倖致矣
===
否則道之不同不相爲謀抱格天之業者或阻
於機會之難逢而欲升得乎抑論聖主必待賢
臣而弘功業俊士亦俟明主以顯其德上下交
而成泰固其所也而其得進有由也是故貴合
志也虞廷命官必由疇咨僉謀而九官濟濟乃
成風動之休故易於良馬之逐金車之梶每致
意焉則允升合志安得不爲君子之慶
書
敷奏以言明試以功車服以庸
punctuated:
六以陰居下，爲巽之主。當升之時，巽於二陽。利用禴者，二也，上下交孚者也；初則賴其孚，而因以上達焉，進退得以關其忠。升虛邑者，三也，進往無疑者也；初則隨其進，而與之同升焉，任職得以行其術。相須之殷也，而相契之深，利見以從王之事者，乃與類行，不戒以孚也，奚用憂恤乎？同道相益也，而同心相與，南征以熙帝之載者，朋至斯孚，不謀而協也，志有不行乎？如是而其升也，固在所必然；其獲吉也，亦非爲倖致矣。否則，道之不同，不相爲謀，抱格天之業者，或阻於機會之難逢，而欲升得乎？抑論聖主必待賢臣而弘功業，俊士亦俟明主以顯其德。上下交而成泰，固其所也，而其得進有由也，是故貴合志也。虞廷命官，必由疇咨僉謀，而九官濟濟，乃成風動之休。故《易》於良馬之逐、金車之梶，每致意焉。則允升合志，安得不爲君子之慶？
書
敷奏以言，明試以功，車服以庸。
translation_en:
…the six in the first place, being yin and occupying the lowest position, is the ruling line of the trigram Xun, Submission. At the time of Ascending, it submits to the two yang lines. It is the second line for which “it is beneficial to offer the yue sacrifice”: those above and below trust one another. The first line relies upon that trust and thereby reaches upward; in advancing and withdrawing, it can give expression to its loyalty [?]. It is the third line that “ascends into an empty city,” advancing without doubt. The first line follows its advance and ascends together with it; in holding office, it can put its methods into practice. So earnest is their mutual dependence, and so profound their accord, that those who find it beneficial to see the great man and undertake the king’s service proceed with their kind and inspire trust without admonition. What need have they for anxiety? Sharing the same Way, they benefit one another; sharing the same purpose, they support one another. Those who journey south to advance the emperor’s work find that trust follows upon their companions’ arrival, and accord arises without deliberation. How could their purpose fail to be carried out? Thus their ascent is assured, and the good fortune they obtain is no mere stroke of luck.
Otherwise, those whose Ways differ do not take counsel together. Even someone whose achievements could reach Heaven might be thwarted by the difficulty of finding a suitable opportunity. Could he then ascend merely by wishing to do so? Moreover, a sage ruler must await worthy ministers to enlarge his achievements, while outstanding scholars likewise await an enlightened ruler to make their virtue manifest. Communication between those above and below naturally brings about Peace, or Tai; yet their advancement has its causes. This is why unity of purpose is prized. At the court of Yu, appointments to office necessarily proceeded through consultation and collective deliberation. Only when the holders of the nine offices stood together in dignity was the splendid result achieved of transforming the people as wind moves them. Thus the Book of Changes repeatedly draws attention to fine horses pursuing one another and the fitting of a metal carriage [?]. How, then, could “ascending through trust” and unity of purpose fail to be a cause for celebration among gentlemen?
Book of Documents
“Let them present their statements in words; clearly test them by their accomplishments; award them carriages and robes according to their service.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭李　批
〔詞氣典雅通篇無一長語而廣延考課之意形容殆盡場中如此作者絕少隻七〕
也
考試官學正張　批
〔瑩粹可誦〕
考試官教授鄭　批
〔自是度越〕
聖世於來朝之臣而許其課賞之法也夫敷言
試功而厚其報法莫有許焉者矣聖世欲率作
以興事得不於是而加之意哉史臣之意蓋謂
===
帝王有以制上下之經則必有以嚴統御之法
稽之虞舜不可尚已彼以陳志者尚乎言有
不達吾懼上下之勢隔而稽政者之無其術也
敷言之典其可已耶則必大虛受於聽納之間
使各陳其爲治之說其何以出之身也其何以
致之民也必欲羣而進之而無有不獲自盡者
矣以核實者尚乎功功有弗試吾懼矯僞之弊
滋而靜言者之飾其辭也試功之典其可已耶
則必綜核之以盡其實上下之以程其能察之
punctuated:
同考試官教諭李　批〔詞氣典雅，通篇無一長語，而廣延考課之意形容殆盡。場中如此作者絕少，隻七〕也。

考試官學正張　批〔瑩粹可誦〕

考試官教授鄭　批〔自是度越〕

聖世於來朝之臣而許其課賞之法也。夫敷言試功而厚其報，法莫有許焉者矣。聖世欲率作以興事，得不於是而加之意哉？史臣之意蓋謂：帝王有以制上下之經，則必有以嚴統御之法。稽之虞舜，不可尚已。彼以陳志者尚乎言，有不達，吾懼上下之勢隔，而稽政者之無其術也。敷言之典，其可已耶？則必大虛受於聽納之間，使各陳其爲治之說。其何以出之身也？其何以致之民也？必欲羣而進之，而無有不獲自盡者矣。以核實者尚乎功，功有弗試，吾懼矯僞之弊滋，而靜言者之飾其辭也。試功之典，其可已耶？則必綜核之以盡其實，上下之以程其能，察之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔“The diction and tone are classically elegant. Throughout the piece there is not one superfluous phrase, yet it describes almost exhaustively the intent behind broadly receiving men and assessing their performance. Very few candidates in this examination write like this. ‘Only seven’ [?].”〕 An isolated concluding particle follows: “…indeed.”

Examiner Zhang, School Director, comments: 〔“Luminous and refined, worthy of recitation.”〕

Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: 〔“It certainly surpasses the rest.”〕

In a sage age, a method of assessment and reward was sanctioned for ministers who came to court. To hear their statements fully, test their accomplishments, and reward them generously—no method could equal this [?]. If a sage age sought to lead men to action and set undertakings in motion, could it fail to give this attention? The court historian’s meaning was presumably this: when emperors and kings establish the enduring principles governing superiors and subordinates, they must also possess means to make their methods of governance strict. Examining the example of Shun of Yu, we find that he could not be surpassed.

For setting forth one’s intentions, what matters is speech. If those intentions are not communicated, I fear that the positions of superiors and subordinates will keep them apart, and those who scrutinize government will have no means to do so. Could the practice of hearing statements fully be abandoned? One must therefore listen with the utmost openness, allowing each man to present his proposals for governing. How will he put them into practice in his own person? How will he extend them to the people? The aim must be to bring them all forward, so that none is denied the opportunity to express himself fully.

For verifying substance, what matters is accomplishment. If accomplishments are not tested, I fear that the abuses of deceit and falsehood will proliferate, and those whose words are unaccompanied by action will embellish their statements. Could the practice of testing accomplishments be abandoned? One must therefore examine them comprehensively to ascertain the full truth, rank them higher or lower to gauge their abilities, and scrutinize them…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
國以觀政也察之民以觀俗也莫不等而辨之
而無有相爲混淆者矣以激勸者尚乎賞賞以
功懋者大君之所以勵世也有弗然焉吾又懼
激勸之無機而天下日就于惰矣報功之典如
之何而可已耶則必嘉其明作之績而隆其錫
予之恩賜之輅車昭其德之在輿也賜之玄衮
昭其德之在躬也康侯之忠自有以彰於旌異
之際而無功者則亦有以告飭之矣夫是則維
持之制盡臧否之辨明而侯度之所以日謹治
===
道之所以日隆有由然哉抑治世尚行而必敷
言者至公也敬事後食而必試功者至明也不
賞而勸而必以庸者至仁也一事行而三善具
焉唐虞之治其斯以爲至乎是故責實則益隆
虛則損不易之道也成周而下若綜核名實而
吏稱其職稱致治如漢宣者謂非有得於此者
歟
貌曰恭言曰從視曰明聽曰聰思曰睿恭
作肅從作乂明作哲聽作謀睿作聖
punctuated:
國以觀政也，察之民以觀俗也，莫不等而辨之，而無有相爲混淆者矣。以激勸者尚乎賞，賞以功懋者，大君之所以勵世也。有弗然焉，吾又懼激勸之無機，而天下日就于惰矣。報功之典，如之何而可已耶？則必嘉其明作之績，而隆其錫予之恩。賜之輅車，昭其德之在輿也；賜之玄衮，昭其德之在躬也。康侯之忠，自有以彰於旌異之際，而無功者則亦有以告飭之矣。夫是則維持之制盡，臧否之辨明，而侯度之所以日謹、治道之所以日隆，有由然哉！抑治世尚行而必敷言者，至公也；敬事後食而必試功者，至明也；不賞而勸而必以庸者，至仁也。一事行而三善具焉，唐虞之治，其斯以爲至乎！是故責實則益，隆虛則損，不易之道也。成周而下，若綜核名實而吏稱其職，稱致治如漢宣者，謂非有得於此者歟？

貌曰恭，言曰從，視曰明，聽曰聰，思曰睿。恭作肅，從作乂，明作哲，聽作謀，睿作聖。
translation_en:
…in the states to observe their government, and examine them among the people to observe their customs. All must be graded and distinguished, with none confused with another. To encourage and exhort, rewards are prized. Rewarding those whose achievements are outstanding is how the great ruler spurs the world onward. If this is not done, I fear that encouragement will lack an effective means and that all under Heaven will daily lapse into indolence. How, then, could the institution of rewarding achievement be abandoned? The ruler must commend their accomplishments in enlightened action and bestow generous favors upon them. He grants them state carriages, displaying their virtue in the vehicles they ride; he grants them dark ceremonial robes, displaying their virtue upon their persons. The loyalty of the lord who brings peace is thereby made manifest through special honors, while those without achievements also receive an admonition.

Thus, the institutions that sustain order are fully provided, and the distinction between the worthy and unworthy is clear. There is consequently good reason why the standards governing the feudal lords become daily more exacting and the way of government daily more exalted! Moreover, although an orderly age prizes action, it nevertheless requires statements to be fully presented: this is perfect impartiality. Although men attend reverently to their duties and put remuneration afterward, their achievements must nevertheless be tested: this is perfect discernment. Although men exert themselves without rewards, they must nevertheless be rewarded for their service: this is perfect benevolence. One undertaking is carried out, and all three virtues are present. Was it not through this that the government of Tang and Yu attained perfection? Thus, demanding substantive results brings benefit, while exalting empty appearances brings harm: this is an unchanging principle. From the Zhou dynasty onward, men such as Emperor Xuan of Han comprehensively scrutinized titles and actual performance, so that officials were equal to their posts, and won acclaim for achieving good government. Could one say that they had gained no understanding of this principle?

“Demeanor is to be reverent; speech, compliant; sight, clear; hearing, keen; thought, penetrating. Reverence produces gravity; compliance produces order; clarity produces wisdom; hearing produces planning [?]; penetrating thought produces sageliness.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭李　批〔德與用敷衍精切其善〕
何淥
發箕子之蘊者可錄以式
考試官學正張　批〔說理文字非苟作者〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔精確〕
君子於五事之曉必著其德而及其用焉夫五
事之德之用合内外而一之者也君子演而言
之而誠身之道不可以觀乎箕子之告武王意
若曰君子建皇極以作則取諸吾身而自足妙
===
體用以成身本之以敬而有餘自夫人之具五
事也而豈徒哉有物必有則而則所以善乎其
物者也貌取諸恭吾心之莊敬恭之謂也容貌
非此不重矣貌曰恭焉言取諸從吾心之理順
從之謂也辭氣非此不達矣言□從焉目以司
視也貞觀不眩有以善天下之色是之謂視遠
之明耳以司聽也至虛能應有以善天下之聲
是之謂聽德之聰以至思之所蘊則極深研幾
足以通天下之故足以類萬物之情而恭從明
punctuated:
同考試官教諭李　批〔德與用敷衍精切，其善〕
何淥
發箕子之蘊者，可錄以式。
考試官學正張　批〔說理文字，非苟作者。〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔精確。〕
君子於五事之曉，必著其德而及其用焉。夫五事之德之用，合内外而一之者也。君子演而言之，而誠身之道不可以觀乎？箕子之告武王，意若曰：君子建皇極以作則，取諸吾身而自足；妙體用以成身，本之以敬而有餘。自夫人之具五事也，而豈徒哉？有物必有則，而則所以善乎其物者也。貌取諸恭，吾心之莊敬，恭之謂也。容貌非此不重矣，貌曰恭焉。言取諸從，吾心之理順，從之謂也。辭氣非此不達矣，言□從焉。目以司視也，貞觀不眩，有以善天下之色，是之謂視遠之明。耳以司聽也，至虛能應，有以善天下之聲，是之謂聽德之聰。以至思之所蘊，則極深研幾，足以通天下之故，足以類萬物之情，而恭從明
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The exposition of virtue and function is precise and incisive. It ably brings out Jizi’s underlying meaning and merits inclusion as a model.” [The transcription interrupts this comment with the author’s name.]

He Lu.

Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This writing expounds principle; it is no careless composition.”

Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: “Precise and sound.”

In elucidating the Five Activities, the gentleman must bring their virtues to light and address their functions. The virtues and functions of the Five Activities unite the inner and outer as one. When the gentleman elaborates upon them, can we not discern the way of making oneself sincere? In addressing King Wu, Jizi meant something like this: The gentleman establishes the August Ultimate as a standard, finding within himself all that is sufficient. By mastering the subtle interplay of substance and function, he perfects himself; by grounding this in reverence, he has more than enough.

Surely people’s possession of the Five Activities is not without purpose! Wherever there is a thing, there must be a norm, and the norm is what makes that thing good. Demeanor draws upon respect: the solemn reverence of my heart is what is meant by respect. Without it, one’s appearance cannot be dignified; thus, of demeanor it is said, “respectful.” Speech draws upon accordance: the orderly conformity to principle in my heart is what is meant by accordance. Without it, one’s words and tone cannot convey their meaning; thus, speech [an illegible character] “accordant.”

The eyes govern sight. To look steadfastly without being dazzled, thereby properly discerning the visible forms of the world, is what is meant by the clarity of far-reaching sight. The ears govern hearing. To be utterly receptive and able to respond, thereby properly discerning the sounds of the world, is what is meant by the acuity that hears virtue. As for what thought contains, it probes the deepest matters and investigates the subtlest beginnings, sufficiently to comprehend the workings of the world and to classify the dispositions of the myriad things; and respect, accordance, clarity…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
聰一以貫之矣夫有是事則有是德純乎其粹
者渾乎其各足固非有待於強勉而後得者也
所謂本然之德者如此然有德必有用而用所
以彰乎其德者也恭之形也則可畏可象自顯
而爲顯若之觀斯以作肅焉從之著也則有倫
有要自發而爲德音之秩斯以作乂焉出其明
焉知來藏往見天下之賾而不亂哲非明之作
耶運其聰焉圖成審會周天下之慮而不遺謀
非聰之作耶以至睿之所發則百慮渾融洞幽
===
明之故而契焉通晝夜之道而知焉而肅乂哲
謀合而一之矣夫有是德則有是用寂然不動
者感而遂通固非有事於脩飾而後成者也所
謂自然之用者如此夫德之與用非有二也敬
以立本而達之用焉則彝倫以叙而皇極有不
建者哉抑是道也達上下者也故五事脩休徵
應焉五事失咎徵應焉天人相與之際不可誣
已王者求端於天非敬曷以哉是故論堯之德
者必曰欽明而舜禹之相授受也亦惟致慎於
punctuated:
聰，一以貫之矣。夫有是事，則有是德。純乎其粹者，渾乎其各足，固非有待於強勉而後得者也。所謂本然之德者如此。然有德必有用，而用所以彰乎其德者也。恭之形也，則可畏可象，自顯而爲顯若之觀，斯以作肅焉。從之著也，則有倫有要，自發而爲德音之秩，斯以作乂焉。出其明焉，知來藏往，見天下之賾而不亂，哲非明之作耶？運其聰焉，圖成審會，周天下之慮而不遺，謀非聰之作耶？以至睿之所發，則百慮渾融，洞幽明之故而契焉，通晝夜之道而知焉，而肅乂哲謀，合而一之矣。夫有是德，則有是用。寂然不動者，感而遂通，固非有事於脩飾而後成者也。所謂自然之用者如此。
夫德之與用，非有二也。敬以立本而達之用焉，則彝倫以叙，而皇極有不建者哉？抑是道也，達上下者也。故五事脩，休徵應焉；五事失，咎徵應焉。天人相與之際，不可誣已。王者求端於天，非敬曷以哉？是故論堯之德者，必曰欽明，而舜禹之相授受也，亦惟致慎於
translation_en:
…and acuity of hearing are threaded together by a single principle. Wherever these activities exist, their corresponding virtues exist. Pure in their essential nature, they form an integrated whole, each complete in itself; they certainly do not await strenuous effort before being attained. Such are the virtues inherent in our original nature. Yet virtue necessarily has its function, and function makes virtue manifest. When reverence takes visible form, it inspires awe and provides a model; it reveals itself as a manifestly dignified appearance, thereby producing solemnity. When compliance becomes manifest, it possesses order and essential coherence; it issues forth as the orderly expression of virtuous speech, thereby producing good order. When clarity of vision is brought forth, one knows what is to come and retains what has passed, perceiving the intricacies of the world without confusion. Is discernment not the product of clarity of vision? When acuity of hearing is exercised, one plans for completion and examines how things converge, comprehensively considering the concerns of the world without omission. Is sound planning not the product of acuity of hearing? As for what penetrating understanding brings forth, the hundred deliberations blend into a unified whole: one penetrates and accords with the principles of the hidden and the manifest, comprehends and knows the Way of night and day. Solemnity, good order, discernment, and sound planning are thus united as one. Wherever these virtues exist, their corresponding functions exist. What is still and unmoving, when stimulated, forthwith responds and penetrates all things; it certainly does not require deliberate embellishment before reaching completion. Such is the spontaneous functioning of virtue.
Virtue and its functioning are not two separate things. If reverent attentiveness establishes the foundation and extends into practice, the enduring human relationships will be properly ordered. How, then, could the Sovereign's Ultimate Standard fail to be established? Moreover, this Way extends through both what is above and what is below. Thus, when the Five Activities are cultivated, favorable signs respond; when the Five Activities go awry, baleful signs respond. The interaction between Heaven and humanity cannot be gainsaid. If a king seeks the guiding principle in Heaven, by what means could he do so other than reverent attentiveness? Therefore, those who discuss Yao's virtue invariably speak of his reverence and illumination; and in the transmission from Shun to Yu, they likewise devoted their utmost care to…
