考試官教授鄭，批〔舂容不迫，可誦。〕
translation_en:
…the purport of refinement and single-mindedness: all speak of reverent attentiveness. When the gentleman examines the teachings of Tang and Yu, he finds therein the whole learning transmitted from mind to mind by the myriad sages.

Book of Odes

“Already drunk with wine,
Already sated with virtue.
May our lord live ten thousand years;
May great blessings attend you.
Already drunk with wine,
Your dishes have already been served.
May our lord live ten thousand years;
May radiant brightness attend you.”

Yi Hongqi

Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor, comments: “The topic itself is outstanding and brilliant [?]. Writers mostly repeat stale expressions, which is tiresome. Late in the process I found this piece: warm, pure, and elegant, it leaves the reader refreshed. It may be recommended. Fitting [?].”

Associate Examiner Zou, Instructor, comments: “The writing flows and the reasoning is coherent; it does not concentrate solely on diction. We select it as a model for the many candidates.”

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “Its diction and tone are balanced and peaceful. The atmosphere of great peace in ‘Already Drunk’ can be vividly imagined.”

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Calm, elegant, and unhurried, it brings the poet’s feelings of blessing and good wishes increasingly into view. This is how the meaning of the Court Hymns should be conveyed.”

Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: “Reading this makes the poet’s gentle, leisurely manner still more apparent.”

Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: “Ample and unhurried, it merits recitation.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
詩人既叙君恩之厚而願其久於獲福也夫景
大昭明而久焉福之全也詩人承君恩之厚而
以是祝之其亦忠愛之不能自已者歟此父兄
所以答行葦也若曰敦典厚親人君之盛德而
感恩圖報臣子之至情今吾君之燕也洗爵之
奠隆於黃耇之養則既醉以酒矣且几筵之設
廣其愛也射樂之舉洽其情也又飽我以德焉
我之寵承於君如此將何以爲祝哉蓋運撫盈
成吾君之福固大矣然不但已也其必於萬斯
===
年介爾以景福焉天休之至延之爲有秩之祜
者俾單厚而未艾元吉之旋引之爲有道之長
者極多益而無窮以百祿則是遒也以萬福則
來同也蓋有與天地相爲久大者矣大斗之酌
加於旅醻之後則既醉以酒矣且醓醢之薦其
品豐也燔炙之陳其物備也又將我以殽焉我
之蒙惠於君如此將何以爲願哉蓋治隆熙洽
吾君之福固顯矣然非自今也其必於萬斯年
介爾以昭明焉重明麗正而所以爲顯比之吉
punctuated: 詩人既叙君恩之厚，而願其久於獲福也。夫景大昭明而久焉，福之全也。詩人承君恩之厚，而以是祝之，其亦忠愛之不能自已者歟？此父兄所以答行葦也。若曰：敦典厚親，人君之盛德；而感恩圖報，臣子之至情。今吾君之燕也，洗爵之奠，隆於黃耇之養，則既醉以酒矣。且几筵之設，廣其愛也；射樂之舉，洽其情也；又飽我以德焉。我之寵承於君如此，將何以爲祝哉？蓋運撫盈成，吾君之福固大矣，然不但已也。其必於萬斯年，介爾以景福焉。天休之至，延之爲有秩之祜者，俾單厚而未艾；元吉之旋，引之爲有道之長者，極多益而無窮。以百祿，則是遒也；以萬福，則來同也。蓋有與天地相爲久大者矣。大斗之酌，加於旅醻之後，則既醉以酒矣。且醓醢之薦，其品豐也；燔炙之陳，其物備也；又將我以殽焉。我之蒙惠於君如此，將何以爲願哉？蓋治隆熙洽，吾君之福固顯矣，然非自今也。其必於萬斯年，介爾以昭明焉。重明麗正，而所以爲顯比之吉
translation_en:
The poet, having described the abundance of his lord’s favor, wishes that he may long continue to receive blessings. For blessings to be great, manifestly bright, and enduring is to possess them in their fullness. Having received his lord’s abundant favor, the poet offers him this benediction: is this not because his loyalty and love cannot be restrained? This is how the elder kinsmen respond to “Reeds along the Path” (Xing wei). It is as though they said: “To uphold the established norms and treat one’s kin generously is the sovereign’s splendid virtue; to feel gratitude for favor and seek to repay it is the deepest feeling of a subject.

“At our lord’s banquet today, the washed cups are set out, showing the honor accorded to the care of the yellow-haired elders; thus we are ‘already drunk with wine.’ Moreover, the provision of armrests and mats extends his love, while the archery and music bring his affection fully to bear. He also ‘sates us with virtue.’ Receiving such favor from our lord, what blessing shall we invoke for him? Presiding over an age of fullness and accomplishment, our lord’s blessings are assuredly great. Yet they must not stop here. Surely, ‘for ten thousand years,’ we must ‘aid you with great blessings.’ May the bounty Heaven bestows be prolonged into blessings bestowed in due measure, making them abundant and rich, never diminishing. May the return of supreme good fortune [?] be extended into enduring life in accord with the Way, increasing without limit. Thus the hundred forms of good fortune converge upon him, and the myriad blessings gather together. These blessings will indeed endure and expand with Heaven and Earth.

“The great ladle of wine is offered after the rounds of reciprocal toasts; thus we are ‘already drunk with wine.’ Moreover, the offerings of meat sauces are abundant in variety, and the roasted and broiled meats are fully arrayed. He also ‘sustains us with viands.’ Receiving such kindness from our lord, what wish shall we offer him? His rule has attained flourishing harmony, and our lord’s blessings are assuredly manifest. Yet this is not merely something beginning today. Surely, ‘for ten thousand years,’ we must ‘aid you with radiant brightness.’ With brightness doubled and grounded in rectitude, that which brings the good fortune of manifest union …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
者煥耿光於勿替緝熈純嘏而所以照長發之
祥者普臨照於無疆以土宇則昄章也以人文
則宣朗也殆有與日月同其貞明者矣夫福不
徒大也而且明焉不徒大且明也而又久焉蓋
必如是而後吾人報德之情其少伸乎噫詩人
忠愛之意至矣抑聞孔子之論九經以親親爲
重蓋萬邦協和必始於九族之睦而四方風動
亦自五典之愼徽者基之是其敦本崇化固自
有在矣王者之道至周大備而展親之典尤惓
===
惓焉乃今觀行葦之慈惠旣醉之祝頌誠意交
孚而雍穆氣象宛然可想昔人謂二詩見周家
之忠厚太平寔其然乎
商邑翼翼四方之極赫赫厥聲濯濯厥靈
壽考且寧以保我後生
黎澄
同考試官教諭章 批〔中興之盛模寫得出想當時詩人之意是如此〕
同考試官教諭鄒 批〔頌美功德大人能之而詞〕
punctuated:
者，煥耿光於勿替；緝熈純嘏，而所以照長發之祥者，普臨照於無疆。以土宇則昄章也，以人文則宣朗也，殆有與日月同其貞明者矣。夫福不徒大也，而且明焉；不徒大且明也，而又久焉。蓋必如是，而後吾人報德之情，其少伸乎！噫！詩人忠愛之意至矣。抑聞孔子之論九經，以親親爲重。蓋萬邦協和，必始於九族之睦；而四方風動，亦自五典之愼徽者基之。是其敦本崇化，固自有在矣。王者之道，至周大備，而展親之典尤惓惓焉。乃今觀《行葦》之慈惠、《旣醉》之祝頌，誠意交孚，而雍穆氣象宛然可想。昔人謂二詩見周家之忠厚太平，寔其然乎！

商邑翼翼，四方之極。赫赫厥聲，濯濯厥靈。壽考且寧，以保我後生。

黎澄

同考試官教諭章批〔中興之盛，模寫得出。想當時詩人之意，是如此。〕

同考試官教諭鄒批〔頌美功德，大人能之，而詞〕
translation_en:
…shine with an enduring radiance. Continuing and glorifying abundant blessings, that which illuminates the auspicious promise of lasting prosperity spreads its light without limit. In territorial extent, it is vast and manifest; in cultural refinement, it is bright and clear. It may indeed share the constant brightness of sun and moon. These blessings are not merely great, but also luminous; not merely great and luminous, but also enduring. Surely only then might our desire to repay our ruler’s virtue find some small fulfillment! Ah, the poet’s loyalty and affection have reached their utmost expression.

I have also heard that, in discussing the nine guiding principles, Confucius attached particular importance to affection for one’s kin. Harmony among the myriad states must begin with concord among the nine degrees of kinship; and the transforming influence that stirs the four quarters likewise rests upon the careful cultivation of the five human relationships. Thus, strengthening the foundations and promoting moral transformation assuredly have their proper basis. The Way of kings attained its fullest realization under the Zhou, who were especially solicitous about the rites for expressing affection toward kin. Now, contemplating the kindness of “The Reeds Along the Path” (Xing wei) and the blessings and praises of “Already Drunk” (Ji zui), we see sincerity mutually inspiring trust, and can vividly imagine their atmosphere of harmony and reverence. People of old said that these two poems reveal the Zhou dynasty’s loyalty, generosity, and peace. Is this not indeed so!

“The capital of Shang is majestic, the center toward which the four quarters turn. Illustrious is its renown; resplendent is its spiritual power. May there be longevity and peace, to protect our descendants.”

Li Cheng 黎澄

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The flourishing grandeur of the restoration is successfully depicted. I imagine this was precisely what the poet of that time intended.”

Associate Examiner Zou, Instructor, comments: “To extol achievements and virtue is something a person of great stature can accomplish, and the language…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
能達意場中如此作者絕少
同考試官教諭揚　批〔頌義貴洋洋作者類多浮〕
冗子獨迥異宜錄以式
同考試官教諭張　批〔詞理精粹而燁然之光不〕
可遏善說詩者
考試官學正張　批〔詞不費而理自足〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔欝茂高亭詞與衆自別〕
詩人頌賢王中興之盛而因以裕諸後焉夫國
勢振而聲威隆商王之中興亦盛矣則其垂裕
===
於後也宜哉此商人祀高宗之樂也其意若曰
功之懋者其勢必昌積之厚者其澤必遠我高
宗之中興也斯其至矣乎但見商邑之莅也刑
賞肅而紀法明有以飭王章於不紊敬畏崇而
雚綱一有以振百度於維貞宅中之地蓋翼然
其攸觀矣由是惟皇建極而中外式焉約天下
而定之趨大觀在上而遐邇則焉合天下而協
其軌四方之渙不翕然冀然極乎是以播之而
爲聲也風行而聲聞且遠□德之廣運蓋洋溢
punctuated:
能達意，場中如此作者絕少。
同考試官教諭揚，批〔頌義貴洋洋，作者類多浮〕冗，子獨迥異，宜錄以式。
同考試官教諭張，批〔詞理精粹，而燁然之光不〕可遏，善說詩者。
考試官學正張，批〔詞不費而理自足。〕
考試官教授鄭，批〔欝茂高亭，詞與衆自別。〕
詩人頌賢王中興之盛，而因以裕諸後焉。夫國勢振而聲威隆，商王之中興亦盛矣，則其垂裕於後也宜哉！此商人祀高宗之樂也。其意若曰：功之懋者，其勢必昌；積之厚者，其澤必遠。我高宗之中興也，斯其至矣乎！但見商邑之莅也，刑賞肅而紀法明，有以飭王章於不紊；敬畏崇而雚綱一，有以振百度於維貞。宅中之地，蓋翼然其攸觀矣。由是惟皇建極，而中外式焉，約天下而定之趨；大觀在上，而遐邇則焉，合天下而協其軌。四方之渙，不翕然冀然極乎？是以播之而爲聲也，風行而聲聞且遠，□德之廣運，蓋洋溢
translation_en:
…can convey the meaning. Writers like this are exceedingly rare in the examination hall.

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “In expounding the meaning of a hymn of praise, expansive fullness is prized. Most writers lapse into empty verbosity; you alone are markedly different. This should be recorded as a model.”

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The language and reasoning are refined and pure, and their radiant brilliance cannot be checked. Here is someone skilled in explaining the Odes.”

Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: “The language is economical, yet the reasoning is complete in itself.”

Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: “Luxuriant and lofty [?], its language stands apart from that of the others.”

The poet praises the flourishing restoration achieved by a worthy king and thereby speaks of the benefits passed down to later generations. When the strength of the state revived and its renown and authority grew exalted, the Shang king’s restoration was indeed splendid. How fitting, then, that he should bequeath blessings to posterity! This was the music used by the people of Shang in sacrificing to Gaozong. Its meaning is as though it said: Where achievement is great, power must flourish; where accumulated merit is abundant, its blessings must extend far. Surely our Gaozong’s restoration reached the utmost height!

Observe his governance of the capital of Shang: punishments and rewards were rigorously administered, and regulations and laws were clear, enabling him to put the royal statutes in order without confusion. Reverence and awe were exalted, and the governing framework was unified [?], enabling him to invigorate the numerous institutions and keep them upright. The seat at the center of the realm thus presented an imposing spectacle of reverent order. Accordingly, the sovereign established the supreme standard, and those within and beyond the capital took it as their model, drawing all under Heaven together and fixing the direction they should follow. A great example stood above, and those far and near patterned themselves upon it, uniting all under Heaven and bringing their courses into accord. Would not the scattered peoples of the four quarters unite and eagerly turn toward this supreme standard [?]?

Thus, when this influence spread and became renown, it traveled like the wind, and his fame reached far. The far-reaching operation of his □ virtue overflowed…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
乎中國而施及蠻貊矣何赫赫乎著之而爲靈
也德威而人心惟畏神功之丕振蓋自光天之
下以及于海隅矣何濯濯乎然此豈一時之盛
已哉天壽平格既膺夫難老之休福履孔綏且
介以和平之慶夫惟其壽也則道久化成而所
以垂裕後昆者自申錫於無疆凡其御都邑以
屬人心也萬世其永賴矣惟其壽而寧也則身
安德滋而所以佑啓後人者咸正大而無缺凡
其繼聲威以震天下也萬年如一日矣不有以
保我後生乎是則由其中興之盛也而業光於
前由其垂裕之遠也而澤及於後此高宗所以
爲賢而崇以百世不遷之廟不亦宜哉抑高宗
之功固大矣然豈無所自哉天命降鑒下民有
嚴敬天之心也不僭不濫不敢怠遑事天之政
也是故平荆楚以服諸侯莫非天命有在而中
興之本誠在是矣雖然聖敬日躋上帝是祗而
九圍之式昭受帝命成湯之所以造商也若高
宗者其亦率乃祖攸行而無忝者歟
punctuated: 乎中國而施及蠻貊矣，何赫赫乎！著之而爲靈也，德威而人心惟畏，神功之丕振，蓋自光天之下以及于海隅矣，何濯濯乎！然此豈一時之盛已哉？天壽平格，既膺夫難老之休；福履孔綏，且介以和平之慶。夫惟其壽也，則道久化成，而所以垂裕後昆者，自申錫於無疆。凡其御都邑以屬人心也，萬世其永賴矣。惟其壽而寧也，則身安德滋，而所以佑啓後人者，咸正大而無缺。凡其繼聲威以震天下也，萬年如一日矣。不有以保我後生乎？是則由其中興之盛也，而業光於前；由其垂裕之遠也，而澤及於後。此高宗所以爲賢，而崇以百世不遷之廟，不亦宜哉？抑高宗之功固大矣，然豈無所自哉？天命降鑒下民，有嚴敬天之心也；不僭不濫，不敢怠遑，事天之政也。是故平荆楚以服諸侯，莫非天命有在，而中興之本誠在是矣。雖然，聖敬日躋，上帝是祗，而九圍之式；昭受帝命，成湯之所以造商也。若高宗者，其亦率乃祖攸行而無忝者歟？
translation_en:
…throughout the central lands and extended to the Man and Mo peoples. How resplendent! Manifested as spiritual might, his virtue inspired awe, and the people’s hearts were filled with reverence. His divine achievements spread mightily, reaching everywhere beneath the shining heavens, even to the shores of the seas. How glorious! Yet could this have been prosperity for merely a single age? Heaven bestowed longevity, and peace was attained: he received the blessing of enduring life. His blessings brought profound tranquility, further augmented by the felicity of harmony and peace. Because he lived long, his Way endured and his transforming influence reached fulfillment; the abundance he bequeathed to his descendants was bestowed repeatedly without limit. Through his governance of the capital and other cities, he bound the people’s hearts to him, giving ten thousand generations something upon which they could forever rely. Because he enjoyed both longevity and tranquility, his person was at ease and his virtue increased; everything by which he protected and guided his successors was upright, great, and without deficiency. In perpetuating his renown and might so as to awe the world, ten thousand years would be as a single day. Did this not provide protection for our descendants?

Thus, through the splendor of his restoration, his achievements cast glory upon those before him; through the far-reaching abundance he bequeathed, his beneficence extended to those after him. This is why Gaozong was deemed worthy. Was it not fitting that he should be honored with an ancestral temple whose spirit tablet would remain unmoved for a hundred generations? Yet, great as Gaozong’s achievements certainly were, could they have been without a source? Heaven issued its mandate and looked down upon the people below: he possessed a heart that solemnly revered Heaven. Neither overstepping in rewards nor indiscriminate in punishments, daring neither to grow idle nor to indulge in leisure—such was his governance in serving Heaven. Thus, when he pacified Jing and Chu and brought the feudal lords into submission, all this manifested the presence of Heaven’s mandate. Here indeed lay the foundation of his restoration.

Yet it was through daily advancement in sagely reverence, honoring the Lord on High and becoming a model for the nine regions, that Cheng Tang illustriously received the Lord’s mandate and founded Shang. Was Gaozong not likewise one who followed the course of his ancestor without bringing him dishonor?

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
春秋
秋七月庚午宋公齊侯衛侯盟于瓦屋〔隱公八年〕
夏齊侯衛侯胥命于蒲〔桓公三年〕
公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子光
莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭
會于蕭魚〔襄公十有一年〕
同考試官教諭招　批　說聖人公天下之心如見
錄之　劉憲
===
考試官學正張　批　發明惡盟貴信義殆盡
考試官教授鄭　批　老成精當宜冠本房
春秋屢紀諸侯之邦交而深寓乎公天下之心
焉夫天下爲公無所事於盟矣聖人深致意於
諸侯之盟會豈得已哉昔者大道之行也諸侯
以信相與未有所謂盟也逮德下衰于是司盟
始設於秩官而爲諸侯之常事矣聖人思有以
維之也是故于瓦屋之參盟謹焉于齊衛之胥
命善焉于蕭魚之會美焉蓋前此皆特盟也三
punctuated:
《春秋》
秋七月庚午，宋公、齊侯、衛侯盟于瓦屋。〔隱公八年〕
夏，齊侯、衛侯胥命于蒲。〔桓公三年〕
公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚。〔襄公十有一年〕
同考試官教諭招批：「說聖人公天下之心如見，錄之。」劉憲。
考試官學正張批：「發明惡盟貴信義殆盡。」
考試官教授鄭批：「老成精當，宜冠本房。」
《春秋》屢紀諸侯之邦交，而深寓乎公天下之心焉。夫天下爲公，無所事於盟矣。聖人深致意於諸侯之盟會，豈得已哉？昔者大道之行也，諸侯以信相與，未有所謂盟也。逮德下衰，于是司盟始設於秩官，而爲諸侯之常事矣。聖人思有以維之也，是故于瓦屋之參盟謹焉，于齊衛之胥命善焉，于蕭魚之會美焉。蓋前此皆特盟也，三
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

“In autumn, in the seventh month, on the gengwu day, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Qi, and the Marquis of Wei covenanted at Wawu.” 〔Eighth year of Duke Yin〕

“In summer, the Marquis of Qi and the Marquis of Wei exchanged pledges at Pu.” 〔Third year of Duke Huan〕

“The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Xiaozhu in attacking Zheng. They assembled at Xiaoyu.” 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xiang〕

Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “The explanation makes the Sage’s intention to hold all under Heaven in common vividly apparent. Select this essay.” Liu Xian.

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “It elucidates almost exhaustively the meaning of disapproving of covenants and valuing trustworthiness.”

Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: “Mature, precise, and apt; it deserves first place in this examination room.”

The Spring and Autumn Annals repeatedly records diplomatic relations among the feudal lords, deeply embedding in these accounts the intention to hold all under Heaven in common. When all under Heaven is held in common, there is no need for covenants. Could the Sage have avoided giving such close attention to the lords’ covenants and assemblies? Formerly, when the Great Way prevailed, the lords dealt with one another in good faith; there was as yet no such thing as a covenant. When virtue subsequently declined, the office of Director of Covenants was first established among the ranked officials, and covenant-making became a regular practice among the lords. The Sage sought a means of holding them together. Thus he treated the three-party covenant at Wawu with caution, approved the exchange of pledges between Qi and Wei, and praised the assembly at Xiaoyu. For before this, all covenants had been bilateral; three…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
國爲盟自蒐屋始是烏可以不謹也約劑煩而
疑日以孳忠信泯而亂日以滋末流傾危之弊
固將無所不至矣噫有虞氏有未施之信焉夏
后氏有未施之敬焉其諸春秋謹參盟之意歟
古者不盟結言而退也齊衛相命寔爲近之是
烏可以不善也去載書而不尚乎俎詐畧牲歃
而從事於眞誠太上淳龐之風蓋庶幾其有望
矣噫以信易食聖人所以荅子貢焉以信易生
君子所以甚桓王焉其諸春秋善胥命之意歟
===
至若盟不足恃鄭不可信也悼公乃能推誠以
懷之是烏可以不美也觀其納質禁侵而兵車
之力不逞禮囚歸國而彼此之心不虞鄭自茲
不肯南向而朝者二十四年焉楚由是不敢北
向而窺者歷有三世焉至誠感人之驗不亦章
章明甚矣乎經故書蕭魚之會以美之也此義
行則大道可復民心可歸今之天下即古之天
下矣此聖人之本志也柰之何古道之不可復
也故參盟未已也有諸侯齊盟者矣齊盟未已
punctuated:
國爲盟，自蒐屋始，是烏可以不謹也？約劑煩而疑日以孳，忠信泯而亂日以滋，末流傾危之弊，固將無所不至矣。噫！有虞氏有未施之信焉，夏后氏有未施之敬焉，其諸《春秋》謹參盟之意歟？古者不盟，結言而退也。齊衛相命，寔爲近之，是烏可以不善也？去載書而不尚乎俎詐，畧牲歃而從事於眞誠，太上淳龐之風，蓋庶幾其有望矣。噫！以信易食，聖人所以荅子貢焉；以信易生，君子所以甚桓王焉。其諸《春秋》善胥命之意歟？
至若盟不足恃，鄭不可信也，悼公乃能推誠以懷之，是烏可以不美也？觀其納質禁侵，而兵車之力不逞；禮囚歸國，而彼此之心不虞。鄭自茲不肯南向而朝者二十四年焉，楚由是不敢北向而窺者歷有三世焉。至誠感人之驗，不亦章章明甚矣乎？經故書蕭魚之會以美之也。此義行，則大道可復，民心可歸，今之天下即古之天下矣。此聖人之本志也。柰之何古道之不可復也？故參盟未已也，有諸侯齊盟者矣；齊盟未已
translation_en:
…states entered into a covenant, beginning at Souwu [?]; how could this fail to warrant caution? Covenant documents multiplied, and suspicion grew daily; loyalty and trust disappeared, and disorder increased day by day. The resulting evils of instability and peril would inevitably go to every extreme. Alas! The ruler of Youyu possessed trustworthiness even before putting it into practice, and the rulers of Xia possessed reverence even before putting it into practice. Might this be the meaning behind the Spring and Autumn Annals’ caution concerning the three-state covenant? In antiquity, men made no covenants: they pledged their word and withdrew. The mutual pledges of Qi and Wei truly approached this practice; how could they fail to merit approval? By dispensing with written covenants and setting no store by deception at the sacrificial stand [?], by omitting sacrificial victims and the smearing of blood upon the lips, and by conducting affairs with genuine sincerity, they offered some hope of recovering the simple, generous ways of highest antiquity. Alas! Choosing trust over food was the Sage’s answer to Zigong; choosing trust over life was the basis for the gentleman’s severe censure of King Huan. Might this be the meaning behind the Spring and Autumn Annals’ approval of those mutual pledges?
As for the occasion when covenants could not be relied upon and Zheng could not be trusted, Duke Dao nevertheless extended his sincerity to win Zheng over. How could this fail to merit praise? Consider how he accepted hostages and prohibited incursions, restraining the force of his war chariots; he treated prisoners courteously and sent them home, so that neither side harbored suspicions of the other. Thereafter, for twenty-four years Zheng refused to turn south to pay court, and for three successive reigns Chu dared not turn north with designs upon its neighbors. Is this not exceptionally clear evidence of perfect sincerity’s power to move others? The Classic therefore recorded the meeting at Xiaoyu to praise it. If this principle were practiced, the Great Way could be restored and the people’s hearts won back: the world of today would become the world of antiquity. This was the Sage’s fundamental aspiration. Why, then, could the ancient way not be restored? Thus, before three-state covenants had ceased, there were already general covenants among the regional lords; before these general covenants had ceased…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
也又有霸者摟諸侯而主盟者矣其流至於口
血未乾而渝盟交質子而不信者矣然則聖人
之志何由而遂乎故其言曰大道之行也與三
代之英丘未之逮也而有志焉此歸與之嘆發
於在陳四代禮樂不得已而一授之回也然則
春秋之作獨非此意乎蓋至是而後見夫子之
心
甲午晦晋侯及楚子鄭伯戰于鄢陵楚子
鄭師敗績公會尹子晋侯齊國佐邾人
===
伐鄭〔俱成公十有六年夏公會尹子單〕
子晋侯齊侯宋公衛侯曹伯邾人伐鄭
冬公會單子晋侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊人
邾人伐鄭〔俱成公十有七年夏公會齊〕
侯于夾谷公至自夾谷齊人來歸鄆讙
龜陰田〔俱定公十年叔孫州仇帥師墮〕
郈季孫斯仲孫何忌帥師墮費〔俱定公〕
〔十有二年〕
李栻
punctuated:
也，又有霸者摟諸侯而主盟者矣。其流至於口血未乾而渝盟，交質子而不信者矣。然則聖人之志何由而遂乎？故其言曰：「大道之行也，與三代之英，丘未之逮也，而有志焉。」此歸與之嘆發於在陳，四代禮樂不得已而一授之回也。然則春秋之作，獨非此意乎？蓋至是而後見夫子之心。

甲午，晦，晋侯及楚子、鄭伯戰于鄢陵，楚子、鄭師敗績。公會尹子、晋侯、齊國佐、邾人伐鄭。〔俱成公十有六年。夏，公會尹子、單〕子、晋侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、邾人伐鄭。冬，公會單子、晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊人、邾人伐鄭。〔俱成公十有七年。夏，公會齊〕侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。〔俱定公十年。叔孫州仇帥師墮〕郈。季孫斯、仲孫何忌帥師墮費。〔俱定公〕〔十有二年〕

李栻
translation_en:
…there were then hegemons who drew the regional lords together and presided over their covenants. This practice degenerated until covenants were violated before the blood upon their lips had dried, and even the exchange of sons as hostages failed to secure trust. How, then, could the sage’s purpose be fulfilled? Thus he said: “The practice of the Great Way and the outstanding men of the Three Dynasties—I, Qiu, did not live to see them, but there are records of them.” Hence his lament, “Let me return!” arose while he was in Chen; having no alternative, he entrusted the rites and music of the four dynasties in their entirety to Yan Hui. Was the composition of the Spring and Autumn Annals not likewise informed by this intention? Only at this point do we perceive the Master’s heart.

On the jiawu day, the last day of the month, the Marquis of Jin fought against the Viscount of Chu and the Earl of Zheng at Yanling. The Viscount of Chu and the army of Zheng suffered a crushing defeat. The duke joined the Viscount of Yin, the Marquis of Jin, Guo Zuo of Qi, and men of Zhu in attacking Zheng. [Both entries are from the sixteenth year of Duke Cheng.]

In summer, the duke joined the Viscount of Yin, the Viscount of Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, and men of Zhu in attacking Zheng. In winter, the duke joined the Viscount of Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, and men of Qi and Zhu in attacking Zheng. [Both entries are from the seventeenth year of Duke Cheng.]

In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu. Men of Qi came to restore the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. [All entries are from the tenth year of Duke Ding.]

Shusun Zhouchou led an army to demolish the walls of Hou. Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led an army to demolish the walls of Fei. [Both entries are from the twelfth year of Duke Ding.]

Li Shi.

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭招　批〔分別霸功聖化處甚有　分曉不凡之士也〕
考試官學正張　批〔春秋義只如此〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔高古迥異他作〕
春秋紀晉魯之事見服人者不以幸而以理也
蓋天下莫大於理而幸勝者不足言矣觀於厲
公孔子之事不亦可見也哉在昔晉厲襲屢霸
之餘以逞其駕鄭之志鄢陵一戰楚君傷而師
敗焉宜霸業爲益振矣然未幾而楚氣愈熾晉
===
勢益微區區目前之勝曾無補於後日之失者
何哉君子曰此幸非持勝之謂也蓋方楚共強
而鄭成貳正敵國外患時也使厲公能釋鄭求
其內寧舒楚以爲外懼則鄭之歸也有日矣乃
令用郤至六間之謀儌呂錡一矢之捷所恃以
成其功者幸焉而已國以幸勝是故其心驕焉
其政怠焉師有□伐之勤而不能回南向之轅
朝有三郤之去而竟行于欒氏之諸力疲於奔
命釁起於不虞茲非自貽之戚歟春秋書之以
punctuated:
同考試官教諭招批〔分別霸功聖化處甚有分曉，不凡之士也。〕
考試官學正張批〔春秋義只如此。〕
考試官教授鄭批〔高古迥異他作。〕

春秋紀晉魯之事，見服人者不以幸而以理也。蓋天下莫大於理，而幸勝者不足言矣。觀於厲公孔子之事，不亦可見也哉？在昔晉厲襲屢霸之餘，以逞其駕鄭之志。鄢陵一戰，楚君傷而師敗焉，宜霸業爲益振矣。然未幾而楚氣愈熾，晉勢益微。區區目前之勝，曾無補於後日之失者，何哉？君子曰：「此幸，非持勝之謂也。」蓋方楚共強而鄭成貳，正敵國外患時也。使厲公能釋鄭，求其內寧，舒楚以爲外懼，則鄭之歸也有日矣。乃令用郤至六間之謀，儌呂錡一矢之捷，所恃以成其功者幸焉而已。國以幸勝，是故其心驕焉，其政怠焉。師有□伐之勤，而不能回南向之轅；朝有三郤之去，而竟行于欒氏之諸。力疲於奔命，釁起於不虞，茲非自貽之戚歟？春秋書之以
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zhao, a Confucian School Instructor, comments: 〔“His distinction between hegemonic achievement and the sage’s transforming influence is exceptionally clear. He is no ordinary scholar.”〕
Examiner Zhang, a Confucian School Instructor, comments: 〔“This is precisely how the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals should be expounded.”〕
Examiner Zheng, a Confucian School Professor, comments: 〔“Elevated and antique in style, markedly different from other compositions.”〕

The Spring and Autumn Annals records the affairs of Jin and Lu to show that one secures others’ submission through principle, not through luck. Nothing under Heaven is greater than principle; victories won by luck scarcely merit discussion. Is this not evident when we consider the affairs of Duke Li and Confucius?

Formerly, Duke Li of Jin inherited the legacy of repeated hegemonic ascendancy and sought to fulfill his ambition to dominate Zheng. In the battle of Yanling, the ruler of Chu was wounded and his army defeated. This should have strengthened Jin’s hegemony still further. Yet before long Chu’s spirit grew ever more ardent, while Jin’s power steadily declined. Why did this paltry immediate victory do nothing to offset the losses that followed? The gentleman says: “This was luck, not what is meant by sustaining victory.”

At that time Duke Gong of Chu was powerful, while Duke Cheng of Zheng was wavering in his allegiance: it was precisely a time of rival states and external threats. Had Duke Li been able to leave Zheng alone and seek peace within his own state, easing pressure on Chu so that it remained an external source of apprehension, the day would have come when Zheng submitted. Instead, he had Xi Zhi’s scheme exploiting six vulnerabilities put into effect [?] and sought the success afforded by Lü Qi’s single arrow. What he relied upon to achieve his success was merely luck. Because his state won through luck, his heart grew arrogant and his government lax.

His armies endured the toil of □ campaigns, yet could not turn back the shafts of the chariots heading south. At court, the three Xi were removed, yet matters ultimately proceeded to the Luan clan’s … [?]. His strength was exhausted by rushing to meet commands, and disaster arose unexpectedly. Was this not suffering he brought upon himself? The Spring and Autumn Annals records this to …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
爲乎勝名也至若魯定來稍弱之後以當強
齊之衝夾谷一會萊兵加而偪好爲侵魯勢斯
亦危矣然未幾而侵疆盡歸名器繼臨臨式
微之魯非復前日之比者何哉君子曰此以理
服人之徵也蓋方齊景橫而三家悖正外陵內
叛時也使孔子而威刼於裔夷謀沮於私黨則
魯之削也滋甚矣乃今明兩君合好之禮申百
雉都城之禁所恃以相其君者理焉而已爲國
以理是故言出而順事爲而成行乎諸侯則謝
===
過不暇而何敢逞其強行乎大夫則改步惟謹
而何敢仍其僭威重於三軍化成於俄頃茲非
自強之驗歟春秋書之以爲循理者勸也故觀
於晉事可見霸功之淺觀於魯事可見聖化之
大王霸之相遠固如是也范文子嘗曰惟聖人
能內外無患斯言蓋有見哉厲惟不用以及於
此也悼公起而三駕焉蕭魚之會其重光矣魯
定昏而桓子膚焉女樂之受孔子之行不脫冕
矣用之弗終爾也不然魯其東周乎豈止齊人
punctuated: 爲乎勝名也。至若魯定來稍弱之後，以當強齊之衝，夾谷一會，萊兵加而偪，好爲侵魯勢，斯亦危矣。然未幾而侵疆盡歸，名器繼臨，臨式微之魯，非復前日之比者，何哉？君子曰：「此以理服人之徵也。」蓋方齊景橫而三家悖，正外陵內叛時也。使孔子而威刼於裔夷，謀沮於私黨，則魯之削也滋甚矣。乃今明兩君合好之禮，申百雉都城之禁，所恃以相其君者，理焉而已。爲國以理，是故言出而順，事爲而成。行乎諸侯，則謝過不暇，而何敢逞其強？行乎大夫，則改步惟謹，而何敢仍其僭？威重於三軍，化成於俄頃，茲非自強之驗歟？春秋書之，以爲循理者勸也。故觀於晉事，可見霸功之淺；觀於魯事，可見聖化之大。王霸之相遠，固如是也。范文子嘗曰：「惟聖人能內外無患。」斯言蓋有見哉！厲惟不用，以及於此也。悼公起而三駕焉，蕭魚之會，其重光矣。魯定昏而桓子膚焉，女樂之受，孔子之行，不脫冕矣，用之弗終爾也。不然，魯其東周乎？豈止齊人
translation_en:
…to establish a reputation for victory [?]. As for Duke Ding of Lu, coming after a period of gradual decline [?], he faced the onslaught of powerful Qi. At the meeting at Jiagu, troops from Lai advanced threateningly, and friendly relations became a means of encroaching upon Lu [?]. The situation was indeed perilous. Yet before long all the seized territory was returned, and the insignia of rank followed. Declining Lu [?] was no longer what it had been. Why was this? The gentleman says: “This demonstrates how principle brings others to submit.”

At that time Duke Jing of Qi was overbearing, while the Three Families were insubordinate: there was aggression from outside and rebellion within. Had Confucius been intimidated by the outlying barbarians, and his plans thwarted by private factions, Lu would have suffered still greater losses. Instead, he clarified the rites by which the two rulers established friendly relations and reaffirmed the prohibition against walled cities exceeding one hundred zhi in extent. What he relied upon in assisting his ruler was principle alone. When a state is governed through principle, its words accord with what is right and its undertakings succeed. Applied among the feudal lords, it leaves them scarcely time enough to apologize for their offenses: how could they dare flaunt their strength? Applied among the grandees, it makes them take the utmost care to amend their conduct: how could they dare persist in their usurpations? His authority outweighed the three armies, and his transforming influence took effect in an instant. Was this not proof of strengthening oneself? The Spring and Autumn Annals records this to encourage those who follow principle.

Thus, by examining the affairs of Jin, one sees the shallowness of hegemonic achievements; by examining the affairs of Lu, one sees the greatness of sagely transformation. Such indeed is the distance between true kingship and hegemony. Fan Wenzi once said: “Only a sage can be free of troubles both within and without.” These words surely showed insight! Duke Li failed to employ this teaching, and so came to such a pass. Duke Dao arose and mounted three campaigns; at the meeting at Xiaoyu, Jin’s former glory shone anew.

Duke Ding of Lu was benighted, and Huanzi was shallow. The acceptance of the female musicians and Confucius’s departure followed without even time to remove the ceremonial cap [?]. It was simply that they failed to employ him to the end. Otherwise, might Lu not have become an Eastern Zhou? Would the result have been confined merely to the people of Qi…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
頑心三家華面已也是知王道有神用而無近
功
禮記
詩言其志也歌咏其聲也舞動其容也三
者本於心然後樂器從之
李褎
同考試官教諭詹　批〔樂以彰德說者多未〕
明此作精切得旨錄以示式
考試官學正張　批　得論樂旨
===
考試官教授鄭　批　簡當可誦
記者論樂必原夫德之發而及樂之成也夫德
蘊於心樂乃德之華也則樂由德之發而後成
也不其然乎樂記之旨如此且樂之作不能離
乎器而樂之本則有在於德也樂以彰德何如
蓋人生而靜性本寂然未有所謂詩也及性感
爲情必形諸言而詩以著凡以宣暢其湮鬱者
一天機之不可遏也詩未有成聲固泯然未有
所謂歌也及志動爲詩乃永言之而歌以彰凡
punctuated:
頑心、三家華面已也？是知王道有神用而無近功。

禮記

詩言其志也，歌咏其聲也，舞動其容也，三者本於心，然後樂器從之。

李褎

同考試官教諭詹批〔樂以彰德，說者多未〕明。此作精切得旨，錄以示式。

考試官學正張批：得論樂旨。

考試官教授鄭批：簡當可誦。

記者論樂，必原夫德之發而及樂之成也。夫德蘊於心，樂乃德之華也，則樂由德之發而後成也，不其然乎？樂記之旨如此。且樂之作不能離乎器，而樂之本則有在於德也。樂以彰德，何如？蓋人生而靜，性本寂然，未有所謂詩也。及性感爲情，必形諸言，而詩以著。凡以宣暢其湮鬱者，一天機之不可遏也。詩未有成聲，固泯然未有所謂歌也。及志動爲詩，乃永言之，而歌以彰。凡
translation_en:
…the stubborn hearts [of the people of Qi] and the outward transformation of the Three Families [?]? From this we know that the Kingly Way has wondrous efficacy, rather than merely immediate results.

Record of Rites

“Poetry expresses one’s intent; song gives prolonged utterance to one’s voice; dance sets one’s bearing in motion. These three originate in the heart; only afterward do musical instruments follow.”

Li Xiu 李褎

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhan, Instructor: 〔Music serves to manifest virtue; most interpreters have not〕 understood this. This composition is precise and incisive and grasps the essential meaning. It is recorded here as a model.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, School Instructor: It grasps the essential meaning of the discussion of music.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Professor: Concise and apt; worthy of recitation.

In discussing music, the author of the Record necessarily traces the manifestation of virtue before proceeding to the completion of music. Virtue is stored within the heart, and music is the flowering of virtue. Thus music takes shape only after virtue manifests itself. Is this not so? Such is the purport of the Record of Music. Moreover, the performance of music cannot dispense with instruments, yet its foundation lies in virtue. How does music manifest virtue?

Human beings are tranquil at birth; their nature is originally quiescent, and there is as yet nothing called poetry. When that nature is stirred and becomes feeling, it must take form in words, and poetry thereby emerges. Whatever gives free expression to what has been pent up is simply the irrepressible working of Heaven’s impulse. Before poetry has taken shape in sound, it remains indistinct, and there is as yet nothing called song. When intent is stirred and becomes poetry, its words are then prolonged, and song thereby manifests itself. Whatever…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
以舒揚其意趣者一天眞之不容已也由是樂
意油然施之四體手以舞之不知其所以舞足
以蹈之不知其所以蹈亦欣喜之情所由以敷
達矣夫德發於外雖有三者之殊推厥所原則
由一心而出蓋性具於心德本於性惟此心因
物而有感則此志遂形而爲詩而歌也舞也皆
從此作矣和順之英華性情之流衍也夫然後
越之金石絲竹以諧其聲則倡和清濁迭相爲
經有平中而無怨懘也所以流通精神而奮至
===
德之光者此矣音律抑何盛耶從以干戚羽旄
以治其飾則俯仰疾舒要其節奏有正齊而無
陵犯也所以動盪血脉而導至和之蘊者此矣
物采抑何華耶是則德本於心以成乎樂此樂
以彰德而爲德之華也樂其可以僞爲乎哉大
抵樂有本文非二物也惟情深文明本末具舉
而後可以言樂此舜之韶所以盡善盡美孔子
聞之忘味也然五帝殊時不相沿樂何哉蓋樂
以彰德亦以象功聖人與時偕行而已故惟聖
punctuated: 以舒揚其意趣者，一天眞之不容已也。由是樂意油然，施之四體，手以舞之，不知其所以舞；足以蹈之，不知其所以蹈，亦欣喜之情所由以敷達矣。夫德發於外，雖有三者之殊，推厥所原，則由一心而出。蓋性具於心，德本於性，惟此心因物而有感，則此志遂形而爲詩，而歌也、舞也，皆從此作矣。和順之英華，性情之流衍也。夫然後越之金石絲竹，以諧其聲，則倡和清濁，迭相爲經，有平中而無怨懘也。所以流通精神而奮至德之光者，此矣。音律抑何盛耶！從以干戚羽旄，以治其飾，則俯仰疾舒，要其節奏，有正齊而無陵犯也。所以動盪血脉而導至和之蘊者，此矣。物采抑何華耶！是則德本於心，以成乎樂；此樂以彰德，而爲德之華也。樂其可以僞爲乎哉？大抵樂有本文，非二物也。惟情深文明，本末具舉，而後可以言樂。此舜之韶所以盡善盡美，孔子聞之忘味也。然五帝殊時，不相沿樂，何哉？蓋樂以彰德，亦以象功，聖人與時偕行而已。故惟聖
translation_en:
…what gives free expression to its meaning and feeling is an unrestrainable natural spontaneity. Thus the impulse toward music wells up and extends to all four limbs: the hands dance without knowing why they dance, and the feet stamp without knowing why they stamp. Through these, too, feelings of delight find full expression. Although virtue manifests itself outwardly in these three different forms, traced to their source they all issue from a single heart. Human nature resides in the heart, and virtue is rooted in that nature. When this heart is moved by things, its intent takes form as poetry, and singing and dancing both arise from this. The flowering of harmony and accord is the flowing forth of human nature and feeling.

Only then is this conveyed through metal, stone, silk, and bamboo instruments to harmonize its sounds. Leading and responding voices, high and low tones, alternate in an ordered pattern, possessing balance and due measure, without resentment or discord. These are the means by which vital spirit circulates and the radiance of perfect virtue is stirred into manifestation. How magnificent are these musical tones! Shields and axes, feathers and yak-tail pennants follow, providing its embellishments. Bending and rising, quick and slow movements all conform to its rhythm, possessing correctness and uniformity without encroachment or disruption. These are the means by which the blood and vessels are stirred and the inward richness of perfect harmony is brought forth. How splendid are these material adornments!

Thus virtue is rooted in the heart and finds fulfillment in music; this music manifests virtue and constitutes its flowering. How could music be produced through pretense? In general, music has both a foundation and an outward pattern: these are not two separate things. Only when feeling is deep and outward expression is brilliant, with root and branches alike fully realized, can one speak of music. This is why Shun’s Shao music was perfectly good and perfectly beautiful, and why Confucius, on hearing it, forgot the taste of food. Yet the Five Emperors lived in different ages and did not perpetuate one another’s music. Why was this? Music manifests virtue, but it also represents achievements; the sage simply moves in step with the times. Thus only the sage…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
昔之能作也彼不聞性與天道者不足與論樂
矣
福者備也備者百順之名也無所不順者
之謂備言內盡於己而外順於道也忠
臣以事其君孝子以事其親其本一也
上則順於鬼神外則順於君長內則以
孝於親如此之謂備
同考試官教諭詹　批〔體信達順之旨發明〕
羅良
===
〔透徹而詞亦精當非有志忠孝者乎錄之〕
考試官學正張　批〔講忠孝之理甚切可錄〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔理精而明詞約而盡〕
記者推福之義在於備必著其所以備也夫盡
己而順道則德無不備矣賢者之祭其受福固
如此哉祭統之意若謂賢者盡祭之義固存乎
福而所謂福者何哉蓋福之爲言備之謂也備
豈強致哉亦曰百順而已矣然所謂百順者亦
惟以吾心之理妙時措之宜而施無不順焉斯
punctuated:
昔之能作也。彼不聞性與天道者，不足與論樂矣。

福者，備也。備者，百順之名也。無所不順者之謂備，言內盡於己而外順於道也。忠臣以事其君，孝子以事其親，其本一也。上則順於鬼神，外則順於君長，內則以孝於親，如此之謂備。

同考試官教諭詹　批〔體信達順之旨，發明〕
羅良
〔透徹，而詞亦精當，非有志忠孝者乎？錄之。〕
考試官學正張　批〔講忠孝之理甚切，可錄。〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔理精而明，詞約而盡。〕

記者推福之義在於備，必著其所以備也。夫盡己而順道，則德無不備矣。賢者之祭，其受福固如此哉！祭統之意，若謂賢者盡祭之義，固存乎福，而所謂福者何哉？蓋福之爲言，備之謂也。備豈強致哉？亦曰百順而已矣。然所謂百順者，亦惟以吾心之理，妙時措之宜，而施無不順焉，斯
translation_en:
…those of antiquity could create it. Those who have not heard the teachings concerning human nature and the Way of Heaven are unfit to discuss music.

“Blessing means completeness. Completeness is the name for accord in every respect. To be in accord with everything is called completeness: this means inwardly fulfilling oneself and outwardly according with the Way. A loyal minister serves his ruler, and a filial son serves his parents; their foundation is one. Above, one accords with ghosts and spirits; outside the household, one accords with rulers and superiors; within it, one acts filially toward one’s parents. This is what is called completeness.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhan, Instructor: “The meaning of embodying sincerity and attaining accord is elucidated thoroughly, and the wording is also precise and apt. Surely this is someone devoted to loyalty and filial piety? Accept it.”

Luo Liang.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, School Instructor: “The discussion of the principles of loyalty and filial piety is most pertinent. It merits acceptance.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Professor: “The reasoning is refined and clear; the wording concise yet comprehensive.”

The author of the Record traces the meaning of blessing to completeness and must therefore make clear how that completeness is achieved. By fulfilling oneself and according with the Way, one’s virtue becomes complete in every respect. Surely this is how the worthy receive blessings through their sacrifices! The purport of “The System of Sacrifices” seems to be that the worthy, in fully realizing the meaning of sacrifice, indeed have blessing in view. But what is meant by blessing? The word “blessing” means completeness. Can completeness be attained by force? It means simply being in accord in every respect. Yet this accord in every respect consists only in using the principles within one’s own mind to achieve a subtle mastery of what is appropriate to each occasion, so that every application accords with the Way; then…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
□謂之備矣何以言之蓋道見於事而行之在
我使己有弗盡則違於道而難以言順矣必反
身以存誠眞實之懿粹之以躬行湛一不虧無
一毫之僞妄也如是則虛中以體物推己之心
循之以泛應性眞流布無一事之矯拂也內盡
於己而外順於道如此可謂無不順矣又何以
見之彼忠以事君臣之職也孝以事親子之分
也有不本於自盡乎必鞠躬盡瘁勵匪懈之節
承懽養志厚罔極之恩則臣子之道盡矣殆見
===
行義烝乎精誠默契質諸鬼神合德而不疑矣
以事君言之志同道合而倚任之有賴恪恭所
事外焉孚於君而無所違也以事親言之服勤
盡孝而繼述之有託共爲子職內焉悅其親而
無所悖也夫然則體信而達順道修而德全信
乎純篤不欺而可以爲備矣備非所以爲福乎
抑此內盡外順卽忠恕之理也忠臣孝子求諸
我而已云身天地在我者一有歉焉其不忝所
生哉張子曰聚百順以事君親又曰無入而非
punctuated: □謂之備矣。何以言之？蓋道見於事，而行之在我。使己有弗盡，則違於道，而難以言順矣。必反身以存誠，眞實之懿，粹之以躬行，湛一不虧，無一毫之僞妄也。如是，則虛中以體物，推己之心，循之以泛應，性眞流布，無一事之矯拂也。內盡於己，而外順於道，如此可謂無不順矣。又何以見之？彼忠以事君，臣之職也；孝以事親，子之分也。有不本於自盡乎？必鞠躬盡瘁，勵匪懈之節；承懽養志，厚罔極之恩，則臣子之道盡矣。殆見行義烝乎，精誠默契，質諸鬼神，合德而不疑矣。以事君言之，志同道合，而倚任之有賴；恪恭所事，外焉孚於君，而無所違也。以事親言之，服勤盡孝，而繼述之有託；共爲子職，內焉悅其親，而無所悖也。夫然，則體信而達順，道修而德全，信乎純篤不欺，而可以爲備矣。備非所以爲福乎？抑此內盡外順，卽忠恕之理也。忠臣孝子，求諸我而已云。身天地在我者一有歉焉，其不忝所生哉？張子曰：「聚百順以事君親。」又曰：「無入而非
translation_en:
…[illegible] is called completeness. How can this be explained? The Way manifests itself in affairs, but putting it into practice rests with oneself. If one fails to exert oneself fully, one departs from the Way and can hardly be said to accord with it. One must turn inward to preserve sincerity, refining the excellence of truthfulness through personal practice, remaining profoundly undivided and unimpaired, without the slightest falsehood or deception. Thus one empties the heart to comprehend things, extends one’s own heart to others, and follows it in responding to all circumstances. The genuineness of one’s nature flows forth, with no action distorted or contrary to it. Fully exerting oneself within and according with the Way without: this may be called according in every respect.

How else can this be seen? Serving the ruler loyally is a minister’s duty; serving one’s parents filially is a child’s obligation. Do these not both rest upon fully exerting oneself? One must devote oneself utterly, strengthening one’s unwavering resolve; attend to one’s parents’ happiness and nurture their aspirations, deepening one’s response to their boundless kindness. Then the way of minister and child is fully realized. One may then see righteous conduct flourishing [?], with perfect sincerity bringing silent accord: tested before the spirits, one’s virtue accords with theirs beyond doubt.

Speaking of service to the ruler, one shares his aspirations and accords with his Way, so that his reliance and trust have a dependable foundation. Respectfully attending to one’s service, one outwardly wins the ruler’s trust and does nothing contrary to him. Speaking of service to one’s parents, one labors diligently and fulfills filial duty, so that the continuation of their undertakings has someone to whom it may be entrusted. Respectfully performing a child’s duties, one inwardly pleases one’s parents and does nothing contrary to them. In this manner, one embodies trustworthiness and achieves accord; the Way is cultivated and virtue made whole. Truly pure, steadfast, and without deception, one may be called complete. Is not completeness what constitutes blessing?

Moreover, this fully exerting oneself within and according without is precisely the principle of wholeheartedness and reciprocity. Loyal ministers and filial children seek it only within themselves. If there is any deficiency in what Heaven and Earth have endowed in one’s person [?], would one not disgrace those who gave one life? Master Zhang said: “Gather together every form of accord to serve your ruler and parents.” He also said: “There is no situation one enters in which one does not…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
自順君子樂得其道正此意也故易推孝饗亦
本於聚蓋能聚百順則孝饗可致聚之理微矣
唯賢者能之
第貳場
論
大而化之之謂聖
張敏德
同考試官教諭靳　批　學至于聖有未易以言
語形容者此作議論甚精詞復脫去藻繪是可以舉業文字
目之哉錄之以式多士
同考試官教諭高　批　化本德業言而通篇
詞意渾融不煩繩削佳作也
===
同考試官教諭袁　批　論義類多汗漫此篇
詞理精當蓋究心于希聖之學而有得者
考試官學正張　批　造語用意不苟
考試官教授鄭　批　說理之言自別
聖人者渾然無迹者也是故存之於心也則爲
內聖之德而其幾有所不容測發之於事也則
punctuated:
自順，君子樂得其道，正此意也。故易推孝饗，亦本於聚。蓋能聚百順，則孝饗可致，聚之理微矣，唯賢者能之。
第貳場
論

同考試官教諭靳批：學至于聖，有未易以言語形容者。此作議論甚精，詞復脫去藻繪，是可以舉業文字目之哉？錄之以式多士。

考試官學正張批：造語用意不苟。
考試官教授鄭批：說理之言自別。
聖人者，渾然無迹者也。是故存之於心也，則爲內聖之德，而其幾有所不容測；發之於事也，則
translation_en:
…in accord of oneself. The gentleman delights in attaining this Way: this is precisely the meaning. Thus, when the Book of Changes commends filial offerings, it likewise grounds them in Gathering. For if one can gather together the hundred forms of accord, filial offerings can be accomplished. The principle of gathering is subtle; only the worthy can put it into practice.
Second Session
Discourse
“To Be Great and Transform Others Is Called Sageliness”
Zhang Minde
Comment by Associate Examiner Jin, Instructor: When learning reaches sageliness, there is something not readily described in words. This composition’s argument is exceptionally refined, and its language is also free of ornamental embellishment. Can it be regarded merely as writing for examination preparation? It is recorded here as a model for the many scholars.
Comment by Associate Examiner Gao, Instructor: “Transformation” is fundamentally spoken of in terms of virtue and achievement. Throughout this piece, language and meaning blend seamlessly, requiring no further correction or pruning. An excellent composition.
Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: Discourses on principles tend mostly toward diffuseness. In this piece, the language and reasoning are precise and apt. Its author has evidently devoted himself to learning that aspires to sageliness and gained insight from it.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: The phrasing and conception are carefully considered.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Professor: Language that elucidates principle stands distinctly apart.
The sage is an integrated whole, leaving no traces. Thus, when this resides in his heart, it constitutes the virtue of inward sageliness, whose subtle workings cannot be fathomed; when it manifests in affairs, then …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
□□王之業而其功有所不容禦何則有其德
者非德之盛也有其業者非業之大也滯於其
迹固於其偏固不能達之於大而進於化是不
足以語聖也者非不以德先天下也而天下
不知有聖人之德非不以道治天下也而天下
不知有聖人之道是豈聖人之有所爲而爲也
哉要亦德深而幾不露業盛而功不顯渾內外
於無迹者耳此則純粹之精通神化之妙也聖
備之極也天下之人殆將涵泳鼓舞於聖人之
===
化而莫之知者矣豈惟人不知之雖聖人亦不
得而自知之也使存之於□者幾有所容測而
德不足以語盛發之於外□功有所容禦而業
不足以語大聖人爾得而指名之曰此吾之德
也此吾之業也天下之人亦得指而名之曰如
是而爲聖人之德也如是而爲聖人之業也則
其所謂德者未始不流於隘而其所謂業者殆
亦不免泥於迹耳奚足以言大奚足以言化奚
足以言聖也哉今夫天之生人也太極以凝其
punctuated: □□王之業，而其功有所不容禦。何則？有其德者，非德之盛也；有其業者，非業之大也。滯於其迹，固於其偏，固不能達之於大而進於化，是不足以語聖也者。非不以德先天下也，而天下不知有聖人之德；非不以道治天下也，而天下不知有聖人之道。是豈聖人之有所爲而爲也哉？要亦德深而幾不露，業盛而功不顯，渾內外於無迹者耳。此則純粹之精，通神化之妙也，聖備之極也。天下之人殆將涵泳鼓舞於聖人之化，而莫之知者矣。豈惟人不知之？雖聖人亦不得而自知之也。使存之於□者，幾有所容測，而德不足以語盛；發之於外□，功有所容禦，而業不足以語大。聖人爾得而指名之曰：「此吾之德也，此吾之業也。」天下之人亦得指而名之曰：「如是而爲聖人之德也，如是而爲聖人之業也。」則其所謂德者，未始不流於隘，而其所謂業者，殆亦不免泥於迹耳。奚足以言大？奚足以言化？奚足以言聖也哉？今夫天之生人也，太極以凝其
translation_en:
…the accomplishments of outward kingship [?], whose efficacy cannot be resisted. Why is this? Virtue that can be singled out as such is not virtue at its fullest; achievement that can be singled out as such is not achievement at its greatest. To remain caught in outward traces and fixed in partial views is assuredly to be unable to attain greatness and advance to transformation. This is insufficient to warrant speaking of sagehood. It is not that the sage does not lead all under Heaven through virtue, yet all under Heaven are unaware of the sage’s virtue. It is not that the sage does not govern all under Heaven through the Way, yet all under Heaven are unaware of the sage’s Way. Could this be a matter of the sage acting with a deliberate purpose in mind? It is simply that his virtue is profound while its incipient workings remain undisclosed; his achievements are abundant while their efficacy remains unseen. The inward and outward merge without leaving traces. This is the finest essence of purity, penetrating the marvels of spiritual transformation—the utmost perfection of sagehood. The people of the world are thus immersed in and inspired by the sage’s transforming influence without knowing it. Nor is it only other people who do not know it: even the sage himself cannot be conscious of it.

Suppose that what is preserved within [?] had incipient workings that could be fathomed, so that its virtue could not be called complete; and that what issued outward [?] had an efficacy that could be resisted, so that its achievements could not be called great. The sage could then [?] point to and name these, saying, “This is my virtue; these are my achievements.” The people of the world could likewise point to and name them, saying, “Such is the sage’s virtue; such are the sage’s achievements.” Then what was called virtue would invariably lapse into narrowness, and what were called achievements would probably also remain mired in outward traces. How could this warrant speaking of greatness? How could it warrant speaking of transformation? How could it warrant speaking of sagehood? Now, when Heaven gives birth to human beings, the Great Ultimate consolidates their …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
性其性同也二氣以〔䡄其□□其形同也則何有〕
於愚何有於賢何有於聖也而孟軻氏以大而
化之歸諸聖豈天之所以降才者爾殊而聖人
有絶德於天下也乎殊不知聖人之所以至於
化者非有以異於人也不爲知誘不爲物化氣
之昏明不足以蔽之遇之吉凶不足以戕之性
所同也而所以盡其性者聖人之所爲師也夫
人不得而同也形所同也而所以踐其形者聖
人之所爲塞也夫人不得而同也是故始之以
===
善焉善之實而信也信之積而美也美之發而
光輝也德輝之合而大也而要之以化焉此入
聖之漸也噫學而至於化幾之神也功之極也
德之純也道之至也聖人之能事畢矣是故以
觀乎聖人之內也而見其順性命也和道德也
具衆理也會萬善也通晝夜也窮物理也盡
人情也存之於內者莫非聖人之德也以觀乎
聖人之外也而見其備六禮也明七教也齊八
政也勸九歌也表裏人物也彌綸天地也出入
punctuated:
性，其性同也；二氣以〔䡄其□□，其形同也，則何有〕於愚，何有於賢，何有於聖也？而孟軻氏以大而化之歸諸聖，豈天之所以降才者爾殊，而聖人有絶德於天下也乎？殊不知聖人之所以至於化者，非有以異於人也。不爲知誘，不爲物化，氣之昏明不足以蔽之，遇之吉凶不足以戕之。性所同也，而所以盡其性者，聖人之所爲師也，夫人不得而同也；形所同也，而所以踐其形者，聖人之所爲塞也，夫人不得而同也。是故始之以善焉，善之實而信也，信之積而美也，美之發而光輝也，德輝之合而大也，而要之以化焉。此入聖之漸也。
噫！學而至於化，幾之神也，功之極也，德之純也，道之至也，聖人之能事畢矣。是故以觀乎聖人之內也，而見其順性命也，和道德也，具衆理也，會萬善也，通晝夜也，窮物理也，盡人情也，存之於內者莫非聖人之德也。以觀乎聖人之外也，而見其備六禮也，明七教也，齊八政也，勸九歌也，表裏人物也，彌綸天地也，出入
translation_en:
…nature: their nature is the same. The two vital forces thereby 〔[shape?] their □□; their bodily form is the same. What distinction, then, is there〕 between the foolish, the worthy, and the sage? Yet Meng Ke attributes greatness that brings about transformation to the sage. Could Heaven’s endowment of capacities differ so greatly that the sage possesses virtue unequalled throughout the world? This wholly fails to recognize that the sage attains transformation through nothing that sets him apart from other people. He is neither enticed by cleverness nor transformed by external things. Neither the obscurity nor the clarity of his vital force can cloud him; neither good nor ill fortune in his circumstances can injure him. Human nature is shared, but fully realizing that nature is what makes the sage a teacher [?]; not everyone can equal him in this. Bodily form is shared, but fulfilling that form is what the sage accomplishes [?]; not everyone can equal him in this. Thus one begins with goodness. When goodness is made real, there is trustworthiness; when trustworthiness accumulates, there is beauty; when beauty manifests itself, there is radiance; when virtue and radiance unite, there is greatness. Ultimately, all culminates in transformation. These are the successive stages of entering sagehood.
Ah! When learning reaches transformation, this is the spiritual efficacy of incipient workings, the utmost achievement of effort, the purity of virtue, and the culmination of the Way. All that the sage can accomplish is fulfilled. Thus, looking within the sage, one sees that he follows his nature and Heaven’s mandate, harmonizes the Way and virtue, embodies all principles, unites the myriad forms of goodness, comprehends day and night, fathoms the principles of things, and fully understands human feelings. Everything preserved within is the sage’s virtue. Looking at the sage’s outward conduct, one sees that he makes the six rites complete, elucidates the seven teachings, orders the eight affairs of government, encourages the nine songs, embraces the inner and outer aspects of people and things, encompasses and orders Heaven and Earth, and moves in and out of …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
造化也進退古今也發之於外者莫非聖人之
業也人見夫聖人之德脩於內也而遂以爲聖
人之德倚於內而可以內求者也而不知聖人
之內而無內而所以脩乎內者忘乎內者也人
見聖人之業發於外也而遂以爲聖人之業倚
於外而可以外求者也而不知聖人之外而無
外而所以發乎外者忘乎外者也天德之立者
因天命自然之理而全之耳是故所知者天德
之良知也所能者天德之良能也而天下之仰
===
其德者夫固囿於其德而莫之知者也夫是之
謂發微而不可見夫是之謂清通而不可象夫
是之謂其幾也有所不容測王道之敷者因天
下自然之勢而道之耳是故順萬事而吾無所
容其情也普萬物而吾無所容其心也而天下
之仰其業者夫固安於其業而莫之知者也夫
是之謂順帝則於不知夫是之謂忘帝力於何
有夫是之謂其功也有所不容禦盛德大業至
矣哉今夫天其靜也專其動也直而萬物由之
punctuated: 造化也，進退古今也，發之於外者，莫非聖人之業也。人見夫聖人之德脩於內也，而遂以爲聖人之德倚於內，而可以內求者也；而不知聖人之內而無內，而所以脩乎內者，忘乎內者也。人見聖人之業發於外也，而遂以爲聖人之業倚於外，而可以外求者也；而不知聖人之外而無外，而所以發乎外者，忘乎外者也。天德之立者，因天命自然之理而全之耳。是故所知者，天德之良知也；所能者，天德之良能也。而天下之仰其德者，夫固囿於其德而莫之知者也。夫是之謂發微而不可見，夫是之謂清通而不可象，夫是之謂其幾也有所不容測。王道之敷者，因天下自然之勢而道之耳。是故順萬事而吾無所容其情也，普萬物而吾無所容其心也。而天下之仰其業者，夫固安於其業而莫之知者也。夫是之謂順帝則於不知，夫是之謂忘帝力於何有，夫是之謂其功也有所不容禦。盛德大業，至矣哉！今夫天，其靜也專，其動也直，而萬物由之
translation_en:
…creation and transformation, bringing forward or setting aside the ways of past and present: whatever is expressed outwardly is the sage’s accomplishment. People see that the sage cultivates his virtue within and consequently suppose that his virtue resides within and can be sought there. They do not understand that the sage’s inwardness has no boundary of “within,” and that his inward cultivation proceeds through forgetting the inward. People see that the sage’s accomplishments are expressed outwardly and consequently suppose that his accomplishments reside without and can be sought there. They do not understand that the sage’s outwardness has no boundary of “without,” and that his outward expression proceeds through forgetting the outward.

Establishing Heaven’s virtue is simply a matter of following and fulfilling the spontaneous principle of Heaven’s mandate. Thus what he knows is the innate knowledge of Heaven’s virtue; what he can do is the innate capacity of Heaven’s virtue. Those throughout the world who look up to his virtue are indeed encompassed by that virtue without understanding it. This is what is meant by manifesting the subtle yet remaining invisible; this is what is meant by being pure and all-pervading yet admitting of no depiction; this is what is meant by having incipient workings that cannot be fathomed.

Extending the Kingly Way is simply a matter of following the spontaneous tendencies of all under Heaven and guiding them. Thus he accords with the myriad affairs without interposing his own feelings, and reaches all things without interposing his own mind. Those throughout the world who look up to his accomplishments are indeed at ease within those accomplishments without understanding them. This is what is meant by following the Lord’s rules without knowing it; this is what is meant by forgetting the emperor’s power, asking what it has to do with oneself; this is what is meant by having achievements that cannot be checked. How consummate are this flourishing virtue and these great accomplishments! Now Heaven, in its stillness, is concentrated; in its movement, it is direct; and through it the myriad things…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
以資始焉天之所以成化也今夫地其靜也翕
其動也闢而萬物由之以資生焉地之所以成
化也然其主宰之神推行之妙則圓莫得而測
其幾而其功亦有不容禦者矣學而至於能化
則所存者與天地同其體所發者與天地同其
用是知聖人者合德於天地而上下同流者也
是故巍巍乎成功煥乎文章四方從欲風動堯舜
以之帝也而安安允克垂華協帝而周悉者性
而化焉者也聖敬大烈彰信丕冒湯武以之王
===
也而制事制心敬勝義勝者反之而化焉者也
達而在上明光迓衡以成文武之德者周公也
融其思兼之迹而化焉者也窮而在下從心所
欲不踰矩聖之時者孔子也生知安行不思不
勉無事於化而自無不化者也若顏子之見道
於卓爾而未達一間是其大而幾於化焉者也
若伯夷之清也伊尹之任也柳下惠之和也皆
聖人也舉其所至而言之者也然清矣而非化
於清也任矣而非化於任也和矣而非化於和
punctuated:
以資始焉，天之所以成化也。今夫地，其靜也翕，其動也闢，而萬物由之以資生焉，地之所以成化也。然其主宰之神、推行之妙，則圓莫得而測其幾，而其功亦有不容禦者矣。學而至於能化，則所存者與天地同其體，所發者與天地同其用。是知聖人者，合德於天地而上下同流者也。
是故巍巍乎成功，煥乎文章，四方從欲風動，堯舜以之帝也。而安安允克，垂華協帝而周悉者，性而化焉者也。聖敬大烈，彰信丕冒，湯武以之王也。而制事制心，敬勝義勝者，反之而化焉者也。達而在上，明光迓衡，以成文武之德者，周公也，融其思兼之迹而化焉者也。窮而在下，從心所欲不踰矩，聖之時者，孔子也，生知安行，不思不勉，無事於化而自無不化者也。若顏子之見道於卓爾而未達一間，是其大而幾於化焉者也。若伯夷之清也，伊尹之任也，柳下惠之和也，皆聖人也，舉其所至而言之者也。然清矣，而非化於清也；任矣，而非化於任也；和矣，而非化於和
translation_en:
…and thereby draw upon it for their beginnings: this is how Heaven accomplishes transformation. Now Earth, in stillness, closes together; in movement, it opens out. All things draw upon it for their birth: this is how Earth accomplishes transformation. Yet the spiritual power that presides over them and the subtle efficacy that sets them in motion are such that none can fathom their incipient workings [?]; their accomplishments likewise admit of no obstruction. When learning reaches the capacity for transformation, what one preserves within shares the substance of Heaven and Earth, and what one manifests shares their functioning. Thus we know that the sage unites his virtue with Heaven and Earth and flows together with them above and below.
Hence their achievements were towering and their cultural forms radiant; the four quarters followed their wishes, stirred as by the wind. Through this, Yao and Shun ruled as emperors. Their effortless repose and assured capacity, their spreading of brilliance, accord with the emperor, and all-embracing thoroughness [?] were transformation proceeding from their innate nature. Sagely reverence and great achievements, manifest trustworthiness and far-reaching protection: through these, Tang and Wu ruled as kings. Their ordering of affairs and regulation of the mind, with reverence and righteousness prevailing, were transformation achieved by returning to that nature. Holding high position when his way prevailed, he gloriously welcomed peace and fulfilled the virtue of Kings Wen and Wu: this was the Duke of Zhou. He dissolved the traces of his thinking to encompass all three kings and thereby attained transformation. Remaining below when his way was blocked, he followed his heart’s desires without overstepping the bounds and was the sage who acted according to the time: this was Confucius. Born knowing and acting with ease, without deliberation or exertion, he had no need to work at transformation, yet spontaneously there was nothing in him that was not transformed. As for Master Yan, who saw the Way standing loftily before him yet remained one interval short of attaining it, his was greatness approaching transformation. As for the purity of Bo Yi, the responsibility assumed by Yi Yin, and the harmony of Liuxia Hui, they were all sages: these descriptions speak of the attainments they reached. Yet there was purity without transformation within purity; responsibility without transformation within responsibility; harmony without transformation within harmony…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
也非所謂大而能化也非所謂內外兩忘也非
所謂神化性命通一無二也夫所謂大而化之
者大而能化也化則自不見其大之之迹矣故
達巷黨人之稱夫子曰大哉孔子愽學而無所
成名夫子亦嘗贊堯之德曰大哉堯之爲君蕩
蕩乎民無能名焉蓋其無可見之迹是亦無可
名之實耳故曰大而化之之謂聖非孟子造道
之深其孰能與於此然孟子善言聖矣而卒未
至於聖者何也其言曰自生民以來未有盛於
===
孔子也又曰乃所願則學孔子也其希聖之心
非不至也而未化者蓋㬰入聖域之爲難也故
曰孔子無迹顏子微有迹孟子其迹著有迹則
未易以語化矣雖然君子之學以聖神功化爲
要歸固不當以近小者自限也然不能以一蹴
而至焉積累之漸自善信美大而至於化則其
功不可誣也若曰化可爲也而躐等而進焉則
亦不足以語聖修之功而罔亦何所得也哉故
曰化不可助長順焉可也孟子曰勿忘勿助其
punctuated: 也，非所謂大而能化也，非所謂內外兩忘也，非所謂神化性命通一無二也。夫所謂大而化之者，大而能化也，化則自不見其大之之迹矣。故達巷黨人之稱夫子曰：「大哉孔子！愽學而無所成名。」夫子亦嘗贊堯之德曰：「大哉堯之爲君！蕩蕩乎，民無能名焉。」蓋其無可見之迹，是亦無可名之實耳。故曰：「大而化之之謂聖。」非孟子造道之深，其孰能與於此？然孟子善言聖矣，而卒未至於聖者，何也？其言曰：「自生民以來，未有盛於孔子也。」又曰：「乃所願，則學孔子也。」其希聖之心非不至也，而未化者，蓋㬰入聖域之爲難也。故曰：「孔子無迹，顏子微有迹，孟子其迹著。」有迹，則未易以語化矣。雖然，君子之學以聖神功化爲要歸，固不當以近小者自限也。然不能以一蹴而至焉，積累之漸，自善信美大而至於化，則其功不可誣也。若曰化可爲也，而躐等而進焉，則亦不足以語聖修之功，而罔亦何所得也哉？故曰：「化不可助長，順焉可也。」孟子曰：「勿忘勿助。」其
translation_en:
…nor is this what is meant by being great and capable of transformation, by forgetting both the inward and the outward, or by spiritual transformation, nature, and destiny forming one undivided whole. What is meant by “being great and transforming oneself” is being great and capable of transformation. Once transformed, one naturally leaves no visible traces of the process of becoming great. Thus a man of Daxiang praised the Master, saying: “Great indeed is Kongzi! His learning is broad, yet he has achieved fame in no particular field.” The Master also once praised Yao’s virtue, saying: “Great indeed was Yao as ruler! So vast was he that the people could find no name for him.” Since there were no visible traces, there was likewise no definite reality that could be named. Hence the saying: “To be great and transform oneself is called sagehood.” Had Mengzi not attained such profundity in the Way, who could have reached this understanding?

Yet Mengzi spoke well of sagehood but ultimately did not attain it. Why was this? He said: “Since humankind first came into being, there has been no one more eminent than Kongzi.” He also said: “As for what I desire, it is to learn from Kongzi.” His aspiration to sagehood was certainly utmost; that he had not yet undergone transformation was presumably because entering the realm of sagehood is difficult [?]. Thus it is said: “Kongzi left no traces; Yanzi left slight traces; Mengzi’s traces were conspicuous.” Where traces remain, one cannot readily speak of transformation.

Nevertheless, the gentleman’s learning takes sagehood, spiritual attainment, achievement, and transforming influence as its ultimate aims. He certainly should not confine himself to what is immediate and petty. Yet he cannot arrive there in a single leap. Through gradual accumulation, progressing from goodness to sincerity, beauty, and greatness, and thence to transformation, his effort cannot be gainsaid. But if he says that transformation can be brought about and advances by skipping stages, this is insufficient to qualify as the work of cultivating sagehood. What could he gain through such delusion? Thus it is said: “Transformation cannot be forced to grow; one may simply follow its course.” Mengzi said: “Neither forget nor help it grow.” Might this be…
