title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
儒者能言之夫愚則何能言哉雖然經史
所陳學士大夫所稱蓋側聞之試以質焉
可乎自黃帝創受河圖始明休咎爰建星
官顓其文不經見已後王代興紹天闡繹
體元則大莫不崇植斯理神明其用若驪
翰寅丑之所尚黃星素祇之所徵其術異
由其揆一也當時篤古博物代有其人閎
者馳其辯約者微其詞達者折其衷咸有
論著莫可殫述是後掌故最秘士所與資
===
授而切劘之者不過遷史〔兩漢晉隋以來〕
志記所載與書詩禮經疏義之文外此則
編袠既鮮無所承傳靡得而籍焉愚反復
明問惟以堯典月令爲旨而占驗弗及意
在茲乎是故萬物之精上爲列星各宿錯
峙咸有攸屬在野象物在朝象官在人象
神末之能易已今觀堯典以中星定仲月
者蓋人君嚮明而治南面而視仰而觀之
中星定而以次諸星可睹也以順節宣以
punctuated: 儒者能言之。夫愚則何能言哉？雖然，經史所陳，學士大夫所稱，蓋側聞之，試以質焉，可乎？自黃帝創受河圖，始明休咎，爰建星官，顓其文不經見。已後王代興，紹天闡繹，體元則大，莫不崇植斯理，神明其用。若驪翰寅丑之所尚，黃星素祇之所徵，其術異由，其揆一也。當時篤古博物，代有其人，閎者馳其辯，約者微其詞，達者折其衷，咸有論著，莫可殫述。是後掌故最秘，士所與資授而切劘之者，不過遷史〔兩漢晉隋以來〕志記所載，與書、詩、禮經疏義之文。外此則編袠既鮮，無所承傳，靡得而籍焉。愚反復明問，惟以《堯典》《月令》爲旨，而占驗弗及，意在茲乎？是故萬物之精，上爲列星，各宿錯峙，咸有攸屬。在野象物，在朝象官，在人象神，末之能易已。今觀《堯典》，以中星定仲月者，蓋人君嚮明而治，南面而視，仰而觀之，中星定而以次諸星可睹也。以順節宣，以
translation_en: …that Confucian scholars should be able to discuss these matters. But how could an ignorant person such as myself speak of them? Nevertheless, I have incidentally heard something of what the classics and histories set forth and what scholars and officials recount. May I venture to submit it for your consideration? Beginning when the Yellow Emperor first received the River Chart, he came to understand auspicious and inauspicious signs and accordingly established the celestial officials—the constellations; the details are not found in the classics [?]. Thereafter, kings arose in succession, carrying forward and elucidating Heaven’s patterns, embodying the primal source and taking its greatness as their model. All exalted and established this principle and brought its workings to wondrous fruition. As for the preferences concerning black and white horses and the yin and chou months [?], and the portents of the yellow star and white earthly spirit [?], their methods followed different paths, but their underlying standard was one. In those times, every age had men devoted to antiquity and broadly knowledgeable. Those of expansive learning gave free rein to their arguments; the concise made their expressions subtle; those of penetrating understanding adjudicated among them. All produced writings, too numerous to recount exhaustively. Subsequently, these inherited records became most secret. What scholars could draw upon for instruction and mutual refinement amounted to no more than the accounts in Sima Qian’s history 〔the two Han dynasties, Jin, Sui, and thereafter〕 and the historical treatises and records, together with the commentaries and explanations on the Documents, Odes, and ritual classics. Beyond these, books were scarce, no tradition was transmitted, and there was nothing on which to draw. Having repeatedly considered your illuminating question, I find that it takes the Canon of Yao and the Monthly Ordinances as its purport without touching upon divination and its verification. Is this where your intention lies? Thus the essences of the myriad things become the arrayed stars above. The stellar lodges stand interspersed, each with its corresponding domain. In the countryside they represent things; at court they represent offices; in human beings they represent spiritual powers. None can alter this [?]. Now, considering how the Canon of Yao determines the middle month of each season by the culminating stars: the ruler turns toward the light to govern and faces south to look out. When he looks upward, once the culminating star is identified, the other stars can be observed in sequence. This serves to accord with the seasonal rhythms and their unfolding, and to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
布時令故中星爲要焉天官書以北極爲
稱首者葢天運至健三光迭曜而極星不
移總而論之樞紐建而周天之星俱拱也
以含元氣以察分至故北極爲大焉至於
堯典仲春舉星鳥而月令主弧仲夏舉星
火而月令主亢仲秋舉星虛而月令主牽
牛仲冬舉星昴而月令主東壁書之中星
常後月令中星常前鄭康成釋禮則曰月
令舉其初朔尚書舉其月中未踰其旨矣
===
孔頴達之疏禮則曰月令但舉其大畧葢
以不合於曆數何言之踈矣斯殆不知夫
歲差所由始哉春秋運斗樞所次七星一
天樞二璇三璣四權五衡六開陽七搖光
一至四爲魁五至七爲杓魁杓合故曰斗
焉居陰布陽故稱北焉石氏乃曰一主天
二主地三主火四主水五主土六主木七
主金也又曰一秦二楚三梁四吳五燕六
趙七齊也其占法殊焉天官書則曰杓携
punctuated:
布時令，故中星爲要焉。《天官書》以北極爲稱首者，葢天運至健，三光迭曜，而極星不移。總而論之，樞紐建而周天之星俱拱也。以含元氣，以察分至，故北極爲大焉。
至於《堯典》仲春舉星鳥，而《月令》主弧；仲夏舉星火，而《月令》主亢；仲秋舉星虛，而《月令》主牽牛；仲冬舉星昴，而《月令》主東壁。《書》之中星常後，《月令》中星常前。鄭康成釋《禮》，則曰：「《月令》舉其初朔，《尚書》舉其月中。」未踰其旨矣。孔頴達之疏《禮》，則曰：「《月令》但舉其大畧。」葢以不合於曆數，何言之踈矣！斯殆不知夫歲差所由始哉？
《春秋運斗樞》所次七星：一，天樞；二，璇；三，璣；四，權；五，衡；六，開陽；七，搖光。一至四爲魁，五至七爲杓。魁杓合，故曰斗焉；居陰布陽，故稱北焉。石氏乃曰：「一主天，二主地，三主火，四主水，五主土，六主木，七主金也。」又曰：「一秦，二楚，三梁，四吳，五燕，六趙，七齊也。」其占法殊焉。《天官書》則曰：「杓携
translation_en:
…to promulgate the seasonal ordinances; hence the stars culminating on the meridian are essential. The Treatise on Celestial Offices gives first place to the northern celestial pole because the movement of heaven is supremely vigorous and the three luminaries shine in succession, while the pole star remains unmoving. Taken as a whole, once the pivot is established, all the stars throughout heaven pay it homage. It encompasses the primordial vital force and enables observation of the equinoxes and solstices; hence the northern celestial pole is paramount.
The Canon of Yao names the Bird star for mid-spring, whereas the Monthly Ordinances specifies the Bow; for mid-summer it names Fire, whereas the Monthly Ordinances specifies the Neck; for mid-autumn it names Emptiness, whereas the Monthly Ordinances specifies the Ox Leader; for mid-winter it names the Pleiades, whereas the Monthly Ordinances specifies the Eastern Wall. The culminating stars in the Documents are consistently later, and those in the Monthly Ordinances consistently earlier. In explaining the Rites, Zheng Kangcheng says: “The Monthly Ordinances refers to the new moon at the beginning of the month, while the Book of Documents refers to the middle of the month.” This accords with their purport. In his subcommentary on the Rites, however, Kong Yingda says: “The Monthly Ordinances gives only a general approximation.” Presumably he says this because it does not agree with calendrical calculations. How careless his statement is! Could this be because he did not understand the origin of the precession of the equinoxes?
The Spring and Autumn: The Pivot That Turns the Dipper (Chunqiu Yundou shu) lists the seven stars in this order: first, Tianshu; second, Xuan; third, Ji; fourth, Quan; fifth, Heng; sixth, Kaiyang; and seventh, Yaoguang. The first through fourth form the bowl, and the fifth through seventh form the handle. Bowl and handle together give it the name “Dipper”; dwelling in yin and spreading yang gives it the designation “Northern.” Master Shi, however, says: “The first governs Heaven; the second, Earth; the third, fire; the fourth, water; the fifth, soil; the sixth, wood; and the seventh, metal.” He also says: “The first corresponds to Qin; the second, Chu; the third, Liang; the fourth, Wu; the fifth, Yan; the sixth, Zhao; and the seventh, Qi.” His method of prognostication is different. The Treatise on Celestial Offices, by contrast, says: “The handle draws along …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
龍角衡中南斗魁枕參首斗爲帝車運于
中央臨制四海分陰陽建四時均五行移
節度定諸紀皆係於斗也其取義與焉斯
殆有見於七政所由叙哉夫所謂歲差者
蓋後世史官攷諸中星與太初曆不協大
要日躔之次常失不及未敢有制也迨晉
虞喜始創差法宋何承天倍之隋劉焯折
衷之唐一行復推以大衍皆以所推之年
爲日退一度至校以堯典月令之差又不
===
符合或謂呂不常已用差法故不宗堯典
載考自堯甲子歷秦莊襄漢太初越宋紹
興甲子積年三千四百二十一其日差也
計度以四十三積分以七千八百八十八
然或百歲計或七八十歲計又莫一焉噫
差法是也其不能必一者非差之咎也昔
者聖人作曆考之以象曰日月星辰驗之
以氣曰陰陽寒暑積之以數曰抄忽毫釐
夫以至微之數而推至變之氣動息升降
punctuated:
龍角，衡中南斗，魁枕參首。斗爲帝車，運于中央，臨制四海，分陰陽，建四時，均五行，移節度，定諸紀，皆係於斗也。」其取義與焉，斯殆有見於七政所由叙哉！
夫所謂歲差者，蓋後世史官攷諸中星，與太初曆不協，大要日躔之次常失不及，未敢有制也。迨晉虞喜始創差法，宋何承天倍之，隋劉焯折衷之，唐一行復推以大衍，皆以所推之年爲日退一度。至校以《堯典》《月令》之差，又不符合。或謂呂不常已用差法，故不宗《堯典》。載考自堯甲子，歷秦莊襄、漢太初，越宋紹興甲子，積年三千四百二十一。其日差也，計度以四十三，積分以七千八百八十八。然或百歲計，或七八十歲計，又莫一焉。噫！差法是也，其不能必一者，非差之咎也。
昔者聖人作曆，考之以象，曰日月星辰；驗之以氣，曰陰陽寒暑；積之以數，曰抄忽毫釐。夫以至微之數而推至變之氣，動息升降
translation_en:
…the Dragon’s horns; the Dipper’s crossbar aligns with the Southern Dipper, and its bowl rests against the head of Shen. The Dipper is the Celestial Emperor’s carriage, revolving at the center and overseeing and governing all within the four seas. The division of yin and yang, the establishment of the four seasons, the balancing of the Five Phases, the shifting of seasonal measures, and the determination of the various calendrical cycles all depend upon the Dipper.” Such is the significance it assigns to the Dipper. Surely this shows some insight into how the Seven Luminaries are ordered!
As for what is called precession, later officials charged with astronomical records examined the stars culminating at the meridian and found that they did not accord with the Grand Inception Calendar (Taichu li). Broadly speaking, the sun’s position along its course consistently fell short, but they did not venture to establish a rule. Only with Yu Xi of the Jin was a method for precession first devised. He Chengtian of the Song doubled it; Liu Zhuo of the Sui adopted a middle course; and Yixing of the Tang recalculated it using the Great Expansion Calendar (Dayan li). Each treated the number of years he had calculated as the interval in which the sun regressed by one degree. Yet when checked against the discrepancy between the Canon of Yao and the Monthly Ordinances, these calculations again failed to agree. Some say that Lü Buchang [?] had already used a method for precession and therefore did not follow the Canon of Yao. Further examination shows that from the jiazi year of Yao, through King Zhuangxiang of Qin and the Taichu era of the Han, down to the jiazi year of the Shaoxing era of the Song, a total of 3,421 years elapsed. The accumulated solar displacement amounted to forty-three degrees, with 7,888 fractional units. Yet some reckoned the interval as a hundred years, and others as seventy or eighty years: here again there was no agreement. Alas! The method of accounting for precession is correct. That its values cannot invariably be uniform is no fault of precession itself.
When the sages of antiquity made calendars, they investigated celestial phenomena—the sun, moon, stars, and constellations; verified them through qi—yin and yang, cold and heat; and accumulated numerical quantities—down to the minute units chao, hu, hao, and li. Now, using the very smallest numerical quantities to calculate the endlessly changing qi, its motion and rest, ascent and descent…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
不誺也盈縮遲速不律也非變通以達其
滯神明以妙其用毫忽之爽躔次之謬幾
南北易位冬春互建矣故杜預曰治曆者
當順天以求合非爲合以驗天程朱亦論
陰陽盈縮不齊不能無差凡此皆獨觀其
原者也愚故曰明於經者明於天道者也
非大智孰能與於此七政者肇於虞書至
漢劉歆張衡雅善星理厥術尤精歆曰太
極運三辰五星于上元氣轉三統五行于
===
下三辰合於三統五行合於五星三辰五
星而相經緯也衡曰文曜麗乎天其動者
七爲日月五星故曰七政皆緯又曰日陽
精宗也月陰精宗也五星五行宗也日行
黃道月與五星皆出入黃道也是故聖人
有作齊七政以立元測圭箭以候氣明九
道以步月交遲速以推星攷黃道之斜正
辨天勢之升降而交蝕詳焉噫明乎此其
於王政也視諸掌乎夫先王之以授人時
punctuated: 不誺也，盈縮遲速不律也。非變通以達其滯，神明以妙其用，毫忽之爽、躔次之謬，幾南北易位，冬春互建矣。故杜預曰：「治曆者當順天以求合，非爲合以驗天。」程朱亦論陰陽盈縮不齊，不能無差。凡此皆獨觀其原者也。愚故曰：明於經者，明於天道者也。非大智，孰能與於此？七政者，肇於《虞書》。至漢劉歆、張衡，雅善星理，厥術尤精。歆曰：「太極運三辰五星于上，元氣轉三統五行于下。三辰合於三統，五行合於五星，三辰五星而相經緯也。」衡曰：「文曜麗乎天，其動者七，爲日月五星，故曰七政，皆緯。」又曰：「日，陽精宗也；月，陰精宗也；五星，五行宗也。日行黃道，月與五星皆出入黃道也。」是故聖人有作，齊七政以立元，測圭箭以候氣，明九道以步月，交遲速以推星，攷黃道之斜正，辨天勢之升降，而交蝕詳焉。噫！明乎此，其於王政也，視諸掌乎！夫先王之以授人時
translation_en:
…are unerring [?], while their increases and decreases, slowness and swiftness follow no uniform rule. Unless one adapts to change to resolve what is obstructed and exercises inspired understanding to make the methods work with subtle precision, the slightest numerical discrepancy or error in celestial positions could almost cause north and south to exchange places and winter and spring to exchange their appointed months. Thus Du Yu said: “Those who construct calendars should follow Heaven in seeking agreement; they should not contrive agreement and then use it to test Heaven.” Cheng and Zhu likewise discussed how the waxing and waning of yin and yang are uneven and cannot be free of discrepancies. All these thinkers possessed exceptional insight into the underlying source. Thus I humbly say: to understand the Classics is to understand the Way of Heaven. Who but someone of great wisdom could attain this?

The seven celestial regulators were first mentioned in the Documents of Yu. In the Han, Liu Xin and Zhang Heng were thoroughly versed in celestial principles, and their techniques were especially refined. Liu Xin said: “The Supreme Ultimate moves the three luminaries and the five planets above; primordial qi turns the Three Concordances and the Five Phases below. The three luminaries correspond to the Three Concordances, and the Five Phases correspond to the five planets. The three luminaries and the five planets thus interweave like warp and weft.” Zhang Heng said: “The patterned luminaries adorn Heaven. Seven of them move: the sun, the moon, and the five planets. Hence they are called the seven celestial regulators; all are weft bodies.” He also said: “The sun is the chief embodiment of the essence of yang; the moon is the chief embodiment of the essence of yin; the five planets are the chief embodiments of the Five Phases. The sun travels along the ecliptic, while the moon and the five planets all pass to either side of it.”

Thus, when sages undertake this work, they bring the seven celestial regulators into accord to establish a calendrical epoch; take measurements with the gnomon and the clepsydra’s indicator to observe seasonal qi; elucidate the nine paths to calculate the moon’s progress; correlate slow and swift motions to calculate planetary positions; examine the ecliptic’s inclination; and distinguish the rising and falling configuration of the heavens. Conjunctions and eclipses can thereby be determined in detail. Ah! For one who understands this, would royal government not be as plain as looking at one’s palm? As for the former kings’ means of imparting the seasons to the people…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
齊七政也非曰文也以時作息保和也辨
氛祲先幾也審象器定制也裁成範圍贊
化也推衍德運明統也是以人神式序天
地官也故日月合璧五星聯珠數之值不
得已也非所以為祥然王者逢吉丁辰亦
可慶焉日月之會是謂合朔會之值不得
已也非所以為沴然聖人扶陽抑陰必謹
候焉春秋傳曰先王之正時也履端于始
舉正于中歸餘于終又曰龍見而戒事火
===
見而致用水昏正而裁日至而畢凡此皆
以欽若其道者也愚故曰明於天道明於
王政者也非大聖孰能與於此若乃十二
月令牽文附義不可經訓儒者多所譏彈
蓋政令有俟時而行有不俟時而行也而
月令惑於時正之拘則夏后周公之典逸
矣渾儀璣衡異器同用不可闕一儒者類
能言之鄭康成謂璣衡以視行度馬融謂
渾儀可旋轉曰璣其橫簫曰衡是矣而孔
punctuated:
齊七政也，非曰文也。以時作息，保和也；辨氛祲，先幾也；審象器，定制也；裁成範圍，贊化也；推衍德運，明統也。是以人神式序，天地官也。故日月合璧，五星聯珠，數之值不得已也，非所以為祥；然王者逢吉丁辰，亦可慶焉。日月之會，是謂合朔，會之值不得已也，非所以為沴；然聖人扶陽抑陰，必謹候焉。《春秋傳》曰：「先王之正時也，履端于始，舉正于中，歸餘于終。」又曰：「龍見而戒事，火見而致用，水昏正而裁，日至而畢。」凡此皆以欽若其道者也。愚故曰：明於天道，明於王政者也。非大聖，孰能與於此？
若乃十二月令，牽文附義，不可經訓，儒者多所譏彈。蓋政令有俟時而行，有不俟時而行也。而月令惑於時正之拘，則夏后周公之典逸矣。渾儀璣衡，異器同用，不可闕一，儒者類能言之。鄭康成謂璣衡以視行度，馬融謂渾儀可旋轉曰璣，其橫簫曰衡，是矣。而孔
translation_en:
…to regulate the seven celestial governors was not merely a matter of outward form. Scheduling work and rest according to the seasons preserves harmony; distinguishing ominous vapors anticipates the first signs of change; examining celestial images and instruments establishes standards; shaping and ordering things assists the transformations of nature; and tracing the succession of the dynastic Powers clarifies legitimate succession. Thus humans and spirits are duly ordered, and Heaven and Earth fulfill their offices. Hence, when the sun and moon join like paired jade discs and the five planets align like strung pearls, this is an inevitable concurrence of celestial cycles, not in itself grounds for calling it auspicious. Nevertheless, when a king encounters good fortune and a favorable moment, it may indeed be celebrated. The meeting of the sun and moon is called conjunction at the new moon. Such a conjunction is likewise an inevitable concurrence, not in itself grounds for calling it baleful. Nevertheless, because the sage supports yang and restrains yin, he must observe it attentively. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “In correcting the calendar, the former kings established its starting point at the beginning, determined the proper sequence in the middle, and assigned the remainder at the end.” It also says: “When the Dragon appears, preparations for work are ordered; when Fire appears, implements are brought into use; when Water culminates at dusk, work is curtailed; when the sun reaches the solstice, it is completed.” All these are ways of reverently following the Way of Heaven. Thus I humbly say: understanding the Way of Heaven is understanding kingly government. Who but a great sage could attain this?
As for the ordinances for the twelve months, they strain the wording and impose meanings, and cannot serve as authoritative instruction; Confucian scholars have frequently criticized them. Some governmental commands must await their season before being implemented, while others need not. Yet the Monthly Ordinances are misled by rigid calendrical constraints, and consequently the authoritative institutions of the rulers of Xia and the Duke of Zhou are lost. The armillary instrument and the ji-heng apparatus are different instruments serving the same purpose, and neither can be dispensed with: Confucian scholars can generally explain this. Zheng Kangcheng says that the ji-heng is used to observe the degrees of celestial motion. Ma Rong says that the part of the armillary instrument that can rotate is called the ji, and its transverse tube is called the heng. These explanations are correct. But Kong…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
頡涬謬於蔡邕之旨則淳古靈憲之制微
矣此何以稱焉抑愚蓋聞之昔言天者不
求之數而求之理蓋理乘數數載理也因
理以著數者先天者也因數以明理者後
天者也昔邵堯夫欲授其數於二程二程
弗遑豈非其旨趣各有攸歸乎愚也經生
闇於大道惟守成議而以臆對至於銳思
攄意測景驗度萬不失一非所及也惟執
事擇之
===
李裘
同考試官教諭詹 批 〔觀子之學不惟淹貫故實而斯民艱苦之狀拯救得失之原宛然在目抑且區畫得宜末復以醖釀和氣歸之人事于其留心〕
經世者乎敬服敬服
考試官學正張 批 〔救荒之策不難於敷演而難於處置處置盡善歲雖荒民不告饑矣子負〕
長策信哉有用之學乎
第五問
punctuated:
頡涬謬於蔡邕之旨，則淳古靈憲之制微矣。此何以稱焉？抑愚蓋聞之：昔言天者，不求之數而求之理。蓋理乘數，數載理也。因理以著數者，先天者也；因數以明理者，後天者也。昔邵堯夫欲授其數於二程，二程弗遑，豈非其旨趣各有攸歸乎？愚也，經生，闇於大道，惟守成議而以臆對。至於銳思攄意，測景驗度，萬不失一，非所及也。惟執事擇之。

李裘

同考試官教諭詹批：〔觀子之學，不惟淹貫故實，而斯民艱苦之狀、拯救得失之原，宛然在目。抑且區畫得宜，末復以醖釀和氣歸之人事，于其留心〕經世者乎？敬服！敬服！

考試官學正張批：〔救荒之策，不難於敷演，而難於處置。處置盡善，歲雖荒，民不告饑矣。子負〕長策，信哉，有用之學乎！

第五問
translation_en:
…the confused misreading of Cai Yong’s purport [?] obscures the venerable ancient system of celestial order. How can this be considered adequate? Yet I have heard that those of old who discussed Heaven sought understanding through principle rather than numbers. Principle rides upon numbers, and numbers carry principle. To elucidate numbers through principle is the approach of Prior Heaven; to illuminate principle through numbers is the approach of Later Heaven. Formerly, Shao Yaofu wished to transmit his numerical learning to the two Cheng brothers, but they had no leisure for it. Was this not because their respective intellectual aims led them in different directions? I am merely a student of the Classics, ignorant of the Great Way, who adheres to received opinions and ventures a reply based on conjecture. As for applying keen thought and fully developing ideas, measuring gnomon shadows and verifying celestial degrees, without a single error in ten thousand instances—this lies beyond my ability. I ask only that you, the examiners, select what is worth accepting.

Li Qiu

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhan, Instructor: 〔In examining your learning, I find not only a thorough command of historical precedents: the hardships of the people and the reasons why efforts to relieve them succeed or fail stand vividly before my eyes. Moreover, your plans are appropriate. At the end, you again attribute the fostering of harmonious qi to human affairs. Surely you are someone who devotes his attention〕 to statecraft! My admiration! My admiration!

Comment by Examiner Zhang, School Instructor: 〔The difficulty in a policy for famine relief lies not in expounding it, but in putting measures into effect. If these measures are entirely sound, then even in a year of crop failure the people will not complain of hunger. You possess〕 an excellent policy. Truly, this is learning of practical use!

Fifth Question

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授鄭　批　救民之術貴於豫此
策能道之末復寫出問外之意可以覘識見之遠矣
佳士佳士
昔者聖人删詩也至豳風詳周事焉曰我
稼既同曰始播百穀其作春秋也紀魯事
焉曰大無麥禾曰告糴于齊夫我稼志農
事也明王業所由起大無志倉廩之竭也
則所以譏莊侯豫備之道下焉耳故知荒
歉因乎數救備在乎人救言臨時也當以
===
雚備言先事也貴於豫達於此其於荒政
也庶幾乎執事以備荒發策詢諸士子且
欲準酌今古補救援溺此其爲慮遠哉雖
草茅未諳世務至于西江土俗民隱則何
敢默焉請竭其愚以對旱乾水溢何代無
之或曰此適然之數爾也天且不能違况
於人乎彼堯若湯者豈其道不神聖哉然
九年之水七年之旱載諸典訓固可考也
若是而安得不謂之天或曰堯憂水咨於
punctuated:
考試官教授鄭批：救民之術貴於豫，此策能道之。末復寫出問外之意，可以覘識見之遠矣。佳士！佳士！

昔者聖人删詩也，至豳風，詳周事焉，曰「我稼既同」，曰「始播百穀」。其作春秋也，紀魯事焉，曰「大無麥禾」，曰「告糴于齊」。夫「我稼」，志農事也，明王業所由起；「大無」，志倉廩之竭也，則所以譏莊侯豫備之道下焉耳。故知荒歉因乎數，救備在乎人。救言臨時也，當以雚；備言先事也，貴於豫。達於此，其於荒政也庶幾乎！執事以備荒發策，詢諸士子，且欲準酌今古，補救援溺，此其爲慮遠哉！雖草茅未諳世務，至于西江土俗民隱，則何敢默焉？請竭其愚以對。

旱乾水溢，何代無之？或曰：「此適然之數爾也，天且不能違，况於人乎？彼堯若湯者，豈其道不神聖哉？然九年之水、七年之旱，載諸典訓，固可考也。若是，而安得不謂之天？」或曰：「堯憂水，咨於
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Professor: In the means of saving the people, advance preparation is paramount. This policy essay succeeds in explaining this. At its close, it further expresses ideas beyond the question, revealing the breadth of the writer’s discernment. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!

In former times, when the Sage edited the Book of Odes, he treated the affairs of Zhou in detail in the Airs of Bin, saying, “Our crops have all been gathered,” and “Begin sowing the hundred grains.” When he composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, he recorded the affairs of Lu, saying, “A great failure of wheat and other grain,” and “Grain purchases were requested from Qi.” “Our crops” records agricultural affairs, making clear the source from which the royal enterprise arose. “A great failure” records the exhaustion of the granaries, thereby censuring Lord Zhuang for the inadequacy of his preparations. Thus we know that famine and poor harvests arise from fate, while relief and preparation depend on human action. Relief refers to action when the crisis arrives and should be undertaken with [?]; preparation refers to action before events and places a premium on foresight. One who understands this comes close to understanding famine administration! You, sir, have issued a policy question on famine preparedness to consult the candidates, wishing moreover to weigh past and present practice, remedy deficiencies, and rescue those drowning in distress. How far-reaching is your concern! Although I am a man of humble station, unfamiliar with worldly affairs, how could I dare remain silent concerning the local customs and the people’s hidden sufferings in Jiangxi? Allow me to offer all that my limited understanding affords in reply.

Droughts and floods: what age has been without them? Some say: “These are merely the workings of fate as they happen to fall. Even Heaven cannot contravene them, much less human beings. Were the ways of Yao and Tang not supremely sagely? Yet the flood of nine years and the drought of seven years are recorded in the canonical writings and can certainly be verified. If so, how can we fail to attribute these things to Heaven?” Others say: “Yao, troubled by the flood, sought counsel from …

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
岳牧湯憂旱禱於桑林聖人盡人以合天
治乃於變民乃允殖水旱無能病焉若是
而安得不謂之人嗚呼號豊而危會饑不
害兹非天人之大故哉是知諉之數則莫
若求端於天求之天則莫若盡其在我考
之王制三年耕餘一年之積九年耕餘三
年之積國有歉荒民無菜色此何所患焉
周禮大司徒以荒政十二聚萬民法甚詳
也又有遺人掌邦之委積以待惠施下至
===
鄉里縣都亦皆有積廩人掌九穀之數以
詔殺用與夫移民就食節巡郊野而以王
命惠施之蓋遺人之職以待其未荒廩人
之職以計其將荒政十二以賑其既荒
成周之法此非其大備者歟王代既殊古
法胥晦人各其見爲計紛然固亦得人之
情循物之理倣古之意大都可稱焉平糴
之法李悝建之魏常平之法耿壽昌創之
漢社倉之制長孫平行之隋義倉之法載
punctuated:
岳牧，湯憂旱，禱於桑林。聖人盡人以合天，治乃於變，民乃允殖，水旱無能病焉。若是而安得不謂之人？嗚呼！號豊而危，會饑不害，兹非天人之大故哉？是知諉之數，則莫若求端於天；求之天，則莫若盡其在我。考之《王制》，三年耕，餘一年之積；九年耕，餘三年之積。國有歉荒，民無菜色，此何所患焉？
《周禮》大司徒以荒政十二聚萬民，法甚詳也。又有遺人掌邦之委積，以待惠施，下至鄉里縣都，亦皆有積。廩人掌九穀之數，以詔殺用，與夫移民就食，節巡郊野，而以王命惠施之。蓋遺人之職以待其未荒，廩人之職以計其將荒，政十二以賑其既荒。成周之法，此非其大備者歟？
王代既殊，古法胥晦，人各其見，爲計紛然。固亦得人之情，循物之理，倣古之意，大都可稱焉。平糴之法，李悝建之魏；常平之法，耿壽昌創之漢；社倉之制，長孫平行之隋；義倉之法，載
translation_en:
…the regional chiefs and governors; Tang, troubled by drought, prayed at the Mulberry Grove. The sages exhausted human efforts to accord with Heaven. Government was thereby transformed and the people truly prospered; floods and droughts could do them no harm. How, then, could one not attribute this to human action? Alas! There may be danger amid reputed abundance, yet no harm when famine strikes. Is this not a great principle governing Heaven and humanity? Thus we know that, rather than attribute calamity to fate, it is better to seek its source in Heaven; and rather than seek it in Heaven, it is better to do everything within our own power. Examining the “Royal Regulations,” we find that three years of cultivation should leave one year’s provisions in reserve, and nine years of cultivation should leave three years’ provisions. Though the state suffered crop failures and famine, the people would show no signs of hunger. What would there be to fear?
In the Rites of Zhou, the Minister of Education used twelve measures of famine relief to keep the people together; these regulations were exceedingly detailed. There was also a Provisioner who managed the state’s stores for charitable distribution. Even the townships, villages, and outlying administrative districts all maintained reserves. The Director of Granaries kept account of the nine grains in order to advise reductions in expenditure, together with moving people to places where food was available, conducting periodic inspections of the countryside [?], and distributing relief by royal command. Thus the Provisioner’s duties prepared for famine before it arose; the Director of Granaries’ duties made provision when famine was impending; and the twelve measures brought relief once famine had struck. Was this not a thoroughly comprehensive feature of the institutions of the Zhou dynasty?
As ruling dynasties changed, the ancient institutions all fell into obscurity. Each person advanced his own views, and proposals proliferated. Yet insofar as these grasped human circumstances, followed the principles of things, and emulated the intent of antiquity, they were generally worthy of praise. Li Kui established the system of balanced grain purchases in Wei; Geng Shouchang originated the ever-normal granary system under the Han; Zhangsun Ping implemented the community granary system under the Sui; and the charitable granary system, Zai [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
肯行之唐已試之效鑿鑿乎足徵也已合
而較諸則常平平糴責在官社倉義倉責
在民舉其在官者行之猶反掌也唐太宗
遣使分詣郡縣有鬻子女者官爲之贖斯
煦煦小仁也其視代宗從劉晏之請年稍
不登得以便宜從事簡易近民可不爲千
萬世荒政章程乎宋眞宗命侍御史秉傳
發賑乃稽遲日月也其視仁宗命官收養
其不能自存者料理其暴露於野者且賑
===
法詳備法良意美豈直目前補塞虛應故
事已耶當時諸臣後先懋績或行諸郡也
或議諸朝也若靑州富弼也越州趙抃也
司馬光請察守宰也朱熹請建社倉也鬻
爵賞以勸賑也嚴糴禁以平價也約而言
之周官所論著也漢魏所舉行也唐宋所
創建也損益得宜參伍盡變本於人情合
於土俗何可闕一也大抵天下無不𢿱之
法惟在有救𢿱之人人事盡於下則未定
punctuated: 肯行之唐，已試之效，鑿鑿乎足徵也已。合而較諸，則常平、平糴責在官，社倉、義倉責在民。舉其在官者行之，猶反掌也。唐太宗遣使分詣郡縣，有鬻子女者，官爲之贖，斯煦煦小仁也。其視代宗從劉晏之請，年稍不登，得以便宜從事，簡易近民，可不爲千萬世荒政章程乎？宋眞宗命侍御史秉傳發賑，乃稽遲日月也。其視仁宗命官收養其不能自存者，料理其暴露於野者，且賑法詳備，法良意美，豈直目前補塞、虛應故事已耶？當時諸臣後先懋績，或行諸郡也，或議諸朝也。若靑州富弼也，越州趙抃也，司馬光請察守宰也，朱熹請建社倉也，鬻爵賞以勸賑也，嚴糴禁以平價也。約而言之，《周官》所論著也，漢魏所舉行也，唐宋所創建也，損益得宜，參伍盡變，本於人情，合於土俗，何可闕一也？大抵天下無不𢿱之法，惟在有救𢿱之人。人事盡於下，則未定
translation_en: …Ken [?] implemented it under the Tang; its proven results furnish unmistakable evidence. Considered together, the ever-normal granaries and balanced grain purchases were the responsibility of officials, while community granaries and charitable granaries were the responsibility of the people. To implement those measures entrusted to officials would be as easy as turning one’s hand. Emperor Taizong of the Tang dispatched envoys separately to prefectures and counties, and wherever people had sold their children, the authorities redeemed them. This was merely a kindly but limited benevolence. Compare this with Emperor Daizong’s acceptance of Liu Yan’s proposal that, whenever the harvest fell even slightly short, action could be taken as circumstances required. Simple to administer and responsive to the people, could this not serve as a model for famine relief for countless generations? Emperor Zhenzong of the Song ordered Attendant Censors to travel by relay [?] and distribute relief, yet months and days were lost in delay. Compare this with Emperor Renzong’s orders that officials take in and support those unable to sustain themselves and attend to those lying exposed in the countryside. Moreover, his relief regulations were detailed and comprehensive, his methods sound and his intentions admirable. How could these have been merely makeshift remedies for the moment or empty compliance with precedent? The ministers of those times achieved outstanding results in succession, some implementing measures in the prefectures, others proposing them at court. Such were Fu Bi in Qingzhou and Zhao Bian in Yuezhou; Sima Guang’s request to scrutinize prefects and county magistrates; Zhu Xi’s request to establish community granaries; the sale of ranks and the granting of rewards to encourage relief contributions; and strict prohibitions on grain purchases to stabilize prices. In sum, what was set forth in the Offices of Zhou, what was implemented under the Han and Wei, and what was instituted under the Tang and Song must be adapted through appropriate additions and reductions, compared and combined to meet every changing circumstance, grounded in human needs and suited to local customs. How could any of these be omitted? Generally speaking, no system in the world is immune to breakdown; what matters is having people who can remedy that breakdown. When human efforts here below have been exhausted, then Heaven’s as-yet-unsettled…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
之天顧有不可挽回者哉江西聯十有三
大郡而爲藩襟以三江滙以彭蠡峙以匡
廬翼以章貢帶以湘洛環以閩廣接以吳
會非不垠然大也生齒繁息比屋接廬行
商居賈農耕女織專業事事敦禮尚儉宜
家給人足訟平盜息也乃今一遇歲荒朝
不及夕十室九空餓殍盈途枵腹待哺望
官司之賑而舉火者十之七八也蠲租發
粟至勞
===
宵旰之軫念三二年間發銀散粟改折減運
僅得蘇息此何究竟歟今歲雖稍登然先
事之備誠有如執事所云云也蓋歲荒民
自爲計者三一曰爲盜二曰轉徙三曰待
其自斃夫民豈不知盜賊之不可爲也小
民無恒心何所不至民情懷土而重遷旣
不能徙又不能聽其斃如之何不去而爲
盜以少延須叟之死也其苟知禮義者則
轉而就食以待稔歲然後歸其不能盜又
punctuated:
之天，顧有不可挽回者哉？江西聯十有三大郡而爲藩，襟以三江，滙以彭蠡，峙以匡廬，翼以章貢，帶以湘洛，環以閩廣，接以吳會，非不垠然大也。生齒繁息，比屋接廬，行商居賈，農耕女織，專業事事，敦禮尚儉，宜家給人足，訟平盜息也。乃今一遇歲荒，朝不及夕，十室九空，餓殍盈途，枵腹待哺，望官司之賑而舉火者，十之七八也。蠲租發粟，至勞宵旰之軫念。三二年間，發銀散粟，改折減運，僅得蘇息，此何究竟歟？今歲雖稍登，然先事之備，誠有如執事所云云也。
蓋歲荒，民自爲計者三：一曰爲盜，二曰轉徙，三曰待其自斃。夫民豈不知盜賊之不可爲也？小民無恒心，何所不至？民情懷土而重遷，旣不能徙，又不能聽其斃，如之何不去而爲盜，以少延須叟之死也？其苟知禮義者，則轉而就食，以待稔歲，然後歸。其不能盜又
translation_en:
…can Heaven, whose course is not yet fixed, really be beyond recovery? Jiangxi unites thirteen great prefectures to form a provincial domain. The Three Rivers form its lapel; Pengli gathers its waters; Kuanglu rises above it; Zhang and Gong flank it; Xiang and Luo gird it [?]; Min and Guang surround it; and it adjoins Wu and Kuaiji. It is indeed a vast expanse. Its population multiplies, with houses standing side by side; itinerant merchants and settled traders, farming men and weaving women each pursue their occupations and attend to their work. They uphold ritual propriety and esteem frugality. One would expect every household to have enough, every person to be adequately supplied, litigation to subside, and theft to cease. Yet now, whenever famine strikes, people cannot see their way from morning to evening. Nine households out of ten stand empty, and the roads are filled with those who have starved to death. Seven or eight people out of ten wait with empty bellies to be fed, depending on relief from the authorities before they can light their cooking fires. Remitting taxes and distributing grain have even occasioned the anxious concern of His Majesty, who attends to government from before dawn until late at night. Over the past two or three years, silver has been issued, grain distributed, payments in kind commuted, and grain transport obligations reduced; yet these measures have brought only a little respite. Where will this end? Although this year's harvest has been somewhat better, advance preparations are indeed needed, just as you have stated.
In a famine year, the people have three ways of fending for themselves: first, becoming bandits; second, migrating elsewhere; and third, awaiting death. Can the people really be unaware that they must not become bandits? Without a constant moral resolve, what might ordinary people not resort to? People cherish their native soil and are reluctant to move. If they cannot migrate, yet cannot simply resign themselves to death, how can they fail to turn to banditry, thereby delaying death for just a moment? Those who have some understanding of ritual propriety and righteousness move elsewhere in search of food, waiting for a good harvest before returning home. Those who cannot become bandits and also…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
不能徙則伏床待其自盡耳執事忍聞之
哉夫周官唐宋之法今欲行之必須數年
愚謂且講目前之計然後及數年之計先
試以賑濟者籌之夫官司發銀與穀本爲
貧民也今則吏胥里書緣以爲奸縣官不
察任其開報詭名小民數十里而趨者百
里而趨者貸糧而候計銀穀未得入手已
償貸無餘矣故貧者未必賑賑者未必貧
而溝壑之塡終不可救矣然此亦在乎守
===
令加之意耳又况民之貧多由官吏貪墨
也小民終歲勤動累錙積銖以規微利儲
之數年曾不以滿其一饕重以額外無名
之派往來供應之辦以一斂十以十斂百
少遲則悍隸叫號隳突雞犬不得寧焉民
何堪也此等而肆於民上猶豢虎豹於郊
原而縱之牧羊豕也有得全其命者乎此
猶爲根本之論誠得一廉潔者父母之勝
於發數萬之粟多矣蓋寬一分則民受一
punctuated:
不能徙，則伏床待其自盡耳。執事忍聞之哉？

夫周官、唐宋之法，今欲行之，必須數年。愚謂且講目前之計，然後及數年之計。先試以賑濟者籌之。夫官司發銀與穀，本爲貧民也。今則吏胥里書緣以爲奸，縣官不察，任其開報詭名。小民數十里而趨者，百里而趨者，貸糧而候，計銀穀未得入手，已償貸無餘矣。故貧者未必賑，賑者未必貧，而溝壑之塡，終不可救矣。然此亦在乎守令加之意耳。

又况民之貧，多由官吏貪墨也。小民終歲勤動，累錙積銖，以規微利，儲之數年，曾不以滿其一饕。重以額外無名之派，往來供應之辦，以一斂十，以十斂百。少遲，則悍隸叫號隳突，雞犬不得寧焉。民何堪也？此等而肆於民上，猶豢虎豹於郊原，而縱之牧羊豕也，有得全其命者乎？此猶爲根本之論。誠得一廉潔者父母之，勝於發數萬之粟多矣。蓋寬一分，則民受一
translation_en:
…cannot migrate, then they can only lie upon their beds and await their end. Can you, sir, bear to hear this?

As for the institutions of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) and of the Tang and Song dynasties, putting them into practice now would necessarily take several years. In my humble view, we should first discuss measures for the present, and then turn to measures requiring several years. Let us begin by considering relief. When the authorities distribute silver and grain, their original purpose is to aid the poor. Now, however, clerks and village scribes exploit this to commit fraud. County magistrates fail to investigate and allow them to submit fictitious names. Common people hurry from several tens of li away, or even a hundred li, borrowing grain to sustain themselves while they wait. Reckoning what they owe, before the silver and grain have even reached their hands, nothing will remain after repayment. Thus the poor do not necessarily receive relief, and those receiving relief are not necessarily poor; in the end, people still cannot be saved from dying in the ditches and ravines. Yet this, too, depends simply upon prefects and county magistrates giving the matter their attention.

Moreover, the people's poverty often results from the corruption of officials and clerks. Common people toil throughout the year, accumulating tiny amounts in pursuit of a meager profit. What they save over several years cannot satisfy even a single bout of these officials' rapacity. Added to this are arbitrary levies beyond the prescribed quotas and the obligation to provide supplies for those traveling on official business. For every one required, they collect ten; for every ten, they collect a hundred. At the slightest delay, brutal underlings shout and rampage, leaving even the chickens and dogs no peace. How can the people endure this? Allowing such men free rein over the people is like raising tigers and leopards in the countryside and letting them loose among grazing sheep and swine. Could any escape with their lives? This addresses the root of the matter. Truly, obtaining one honest and incorruptible official to act as a father and mother to the people would be far better than distributing tens of thousands of measures of grain. For with each measure of burdens lifted, the people receive one…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
分之賜朝行而夕及豈勞餘力哉若平糴
常平義倉社倉行之固為利益然亦止救
目前故曰目前之計也蘇軾所謂萬世之
計亦不過以三十年之通有十年之餘耳
若夫重農桑以厚其生招流移以復其業
裁冗費以節其流禁游民以力其本抑豪
右以均其利去奢侈以崇其儉假以歲月
縱不能計十年之餘而其於三年之餘獨
不可計乎大抵法固有宜古而不宜於今
===
者惟在善為法者審酌其時勢通之於蘿
變毋膠柱鼓瑟爾也蓋荒歉固適然之數
所不能逃然天道遠人事邇何可諉之莫
之為遂輟然止也愚謂救之臨時以蘿備
之先事以豫夫亦若是已矣中庸曰致中
和天地位焉萬物育焉此心說也心生道
也故道位天地育萬物不尸其功而適然
之數不與存焉
punctuated: 分之賜，朝行而夕及，豈勞餘力哉？若平糴、常平、義倉、社倉，行之固為利益，然亦止救目前，故曰目前之計也。蘇軾所謂萬世之計，亦不過以三十年之通，有十年之餘耳。若夫重農桑以厚其生，招流移以復其業，裁冗費以節其流，禁游民以力其本，抑豪右以均其利，去奢侈以崇其儉，假以歲月，縱不能計十年之餘，而其於三年之餘獨不可計乎？大抵法固有宜古而不宜於今者，惟在善為法者審酌其時勢，通之於蘿變，毋膠柱鼓瑟爾也。蓋荒歉固適然之數所不能逃，然天道遠，人事邇，何可諉之莫之為，遂輟然止也？愚謂救之臨時以蘿，備之先事以豫，夫亦若是已矣。《中庸》曰：「致中和，天地位焉，萬物育焉。」此心說也，心生道也。故道位天地，育萬物，不尸其功，而適然之數不與存焉。
translation_en:
…measure of benefit. Put it into effect in the morning, and its benefits reach the people by evening: how could this require any further exertion? As for equitable grain purchases, ever-normal granaries, charity granaries, and community granaries, implementing these certainly brings benefits; yet they only relieve immediate needs, and are therefore called measures for the present. What Su Shi called a plan for ten thousand generations amounts to no more than securing, over a span of thirty years, a surplus sufficient for ten years.

If agriculture and sericulture are promoted to enrich the people's livelihood; displaced people are brought back to resume their occupations; unnecessary expenditure is curtailed to limit the outflow of resources; idleness is prohibited to strengthen agriculture, the fundamental occupation; powerful local families are restrained to distribute benefits equitably; and extravagance is eliminated to encourage frugality—then, given time, even if a ten-year surplus cannot be expected, surely a three-year surplus can? In general, some methods suited antiquity but do not suit the present. It rests with those skilled in devising policies to weigh the circumstances of their time and adapt to changes [?], rather than glue down the tuning bridges and then try to play the zither.

Famine and poor harvests are indeed contingencies of fate that cannot be escaped. Yet Heaven's Way is distant, while human affairs are near at hand. How can one use fate as an excuse for doing nothing and simply stop all effort? In my humble view, one should provide relief when the crisis arrives, with … [?], and make preparations beforehand with foresight. That is all there is to it.

The Doctrine of the Mean says: “Bring equilibrium and harmony to their fullest realization, and Heaven and Earth will take their proper places, and the myriad things will flourish.” This is a teaching about the mind; the mind is the Way of generating life [?]. Thus the Way sets Heaven and Earth in their places and nurtures the myriad things without claiming credit for its achievement; contingencies of fate have no part in it.

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
歲丙午秋八月江西鄉試錄成
諸所規畫以共成休美在〔道夫〕
亦既有言矣〔恩〕也無良當申諸
末簡敢再告之曰茲實與
盛典實惟
聖天子登選俊良圖惟治理視昔益
===
加隆焉御史〔謨〕曰懼無以祗承
休德朝夕矢于百執事曰無相負也
而百執事亦日惟御史言更相
飭戒自鎖院迄于有成凡二十
二日罔朝夕罔內外罔不悉謀
殫議至于論定而百執事之心
鮮弗盡矣凡以期得眞才爲
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

歲丙午秋八月，江西鄉試錄成。諸所規畫，以共成休美，在〔道夫〕亦既有言矣。〔恩〕也無良，當申諸末簡，敢再告之曰：茲實與盛典，實惟聖天子登選俊良，圖惟治理，視昔益加隆焉。御史〔謨〕曰：「懼無以祗承休德。」朝夕矢于百執事曰：「無相負也。」而百執事亦日惟御史言，更相飭戒。自鎖院迄于有成，凡二十二日，罔朝夕，罔內外，罔不悉謀殫議，至于論定，而百執事之心鮮弗盡矣。凡以期得眞才爲
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth month, in autumn of the bingwu year [1546], the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination was completed. Daofu has already spoken of all the planning through which we jointly brought this fine undertaking to fruition. I, En, unworthy as I am, ought to elaborate upon this in these closing pages, and venture to state once more: this is indeed participation in a grand ceremony [?]. In truth, the sagely Son of Heaven promotes and selects outstanding and worthy men with good government in view, and accords this undertaking still greater importance than in the past. The Censor, Mo, said, “I fear that I lack the means reverently to uphold his gracious virtue.” Morning and evening he solemnly exhorted all those charged with duties: “Let us not fail one another.” All those charged with duties likewise kept the Censor’s words in mind daily, admonishing and cautioning one another. From the sealing of the examination compound until the work was completed, twenty-two days elapsed. Morning and evening, within and without, everyone fully contributed to the planning and exhausted the issues in discussion, until final decisions were reached; scarcely any of those charged with duties failed to give their utmost. All this was done in the hope of obtaining men of genuine talent for…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
國用也然而眞僞易淆也華實易
眩也庸有不得若人者乎〔恩〕兹
乎懼矣今有越人走四方入山
而得希世之珍乃飾以金函被
以文繡愛倍恒品及歸齋戒卜
日而啓之果玉也天下無不愛
且貴矣其不然至獲燕石而號
===
諸人曰玉在是人其謂何諸士
歌鹿鳴而來也有司得一佳士
如獲奇珍而或有不盡然者視
文考德難乎哉士出而果良于
行則稱乎其文斯天下將稱之
曰斯錄也而有若人也庸不爲
是科重耶其弗良于行則不稱
punctuated: 國用也。然而眞僞易淆也，華實易眩也，庸有不得若人者乎？〔恩〕兹乎懼矣。今有越人走四方，入山而得希世之珍，乃飾以金函，被以文繡，愛倍恒品。及歸，齋戒卜日而啓之，果玉也，天下無不愛且貴矣。其不然，至獲燕石而號諸人曰：「玉在是！」人其謂何？諸士歌《鹿鳴》而來也，有司得一佳士，如獲奇珍，而或有不盡然者。視文考德，難乎哉！士出而果良于行，則稱乎其文，斯天下將稱之曰：「斯錄也，而有若人也！」庸不爲是科重耶？其弗良于行，則不稱
translation_en:
…for service to the state. Yet the genuine and the false are easily confused, and outward brilliance and inner substance easily mistaken for one another. Might we fail to obtain men of this kind? This is what I, 〔En〕, fear.

Suppose a man of Yue travels throughout the land, enters the mountains, and obtains a treasure rarely seen in the world. He then adorns it with a gold casket, covers it with patterned embroidery, and cherishes it far above ordinary objects. Upon returning home, he fasts, observes ritual abstinence, and chooses an auspicious day to open it. If it truly is jade, everyone in the world will cherish and prize it. But if instead he has obtained a stone from Yan and cries out to others, “Here is jade!” what will people say?

The candidates come to the singing of “The Deer Call.” When the responsible officials obtain one excellent scholar, it is like acquiring a rare treasure; yet some may not entirely live up to this. How difficult it is to examine writing and assess virtue! If a scholar goes forth and proves good in his conduct, then he lives up to his writing, and the world will praise him, saying, “This examination record contains such a man!” Would this not bring distinction to this examination? If his conduct is not good, then he does not live up to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
乎其文斯天下將指之曰斯錄
也而亦有若人也庸不爲是科
累耶是故太上不辱身而榮名
次之得失榮辱之機亦可以自
考矣在昔陸贄柄文得一韓愈
卒之愈也果克自振在愈不爲
負贄在贄不爲負天下天下至
今稱之不衰乃今諸士所遇之
時又非唐比矣
===
皇上懋德建中
憲經定制煥乎人文以臻勳華之
治凡在物覩皆以爲
大聖人在上則夫率德而化是豈無
真才如臯夔諸人應運而出者
punctuated:
乎其文，斯天下將指之曰：「斯錄也，而亦有若人也，庸不爲是科累耶？」是故太上不辱身而榮名，次之。得失榮辱之機，亦可以自考矣。在昔陸贄柄文，得一韓愈，卒之愈也果克自振。在愈不爲負贄，在贄不爲負天下，天下至今稱之不衰。乃今諸士所遇之時，又非唐比矣。
皇上懋德建中，憲經定制，煥乎人文，以臻勳華之治。凡在物覩，皆以爲大聖人在上，則夫率德而化，是豈無真才如臯夔諸人應運而出者
translation_en:
…with their writing, then all under Heaven will point to them and say: “In this record there are also men like these! Would they not bring discredit upon this examination?” Thus, highest is to avoid dishonoring oneself; next is to bring glory to one’s name. The factors that determine success and failure, honor and disgrace, can also be examined within oneself. In former times, when Lu Zhi presided over the literary examinations, he obtained a man such as Han Yu. In the end, Han Yu indeed proved capable of distinguishing himself. Han Yu did not fail Lu Zhi, and Lu Zhi did not fail all under Heaven. To this day, the world’s praise of them has not diminished. Yet the age that you gentlemen now encounter cannot be compared even with the Tang.
His Majesty cultivates virtue and establishes the mean, takes the classics as his standard and institutes regulations, making human culture resplendent so as to attain the governance of Yao and Shun. All who behold him hold that a great sage occupies the throne. Thus, as men follow his virtue and are transformed, could there be no men of genuine talent, like Gao and Kui, who emerge in response to the age…

title: 嘉靖二十五年江西鄉試錄
text:
乎此國其會也若夫贊之得會
雖謂唐之得士可也而要之非
其至也是故鳴盛者文也迨會
者時也際時者遇也諸士生逢
盛世有其時矣以文見錄有其遇
矣其窮居隱約其夙夜爲心恐
恐焉恒以不遇爲歉自今不爲
===
不遇矣庸無所表見樹立以罄
其平生耶夫有其材而弗遇有
司之責也遇矣而不盡其材諸
士之恥也諸士其勗之哉
直隸鳳陽府宿州儒學學正張
恩
謹序
punctuated:
乎？此國其會也。若夫贊之得會，雖謂唐之得士可也，而要之非其至也。是故鳴盛者文也，迨會者時也，際時者遇也。諸士生逢盛世，有其時矣；以文見錄，有其遇矣。其窮居隱約，其夙夜爲心，恐恐焉恒以不遇爲歉，自今不爲不遇矣，庸無所表見樹立，以罄其平生耶？夫有其材而弗遇，有司之責也；遇矣而不盡其材，諸士之恥也。諸士其勗之哉！
直隸鳳陽府宿州儒學學正張恩謹序。
translation_en:
…? This is the occasion for the realm [?]. As for praising this fortunate conjunction [?], one may indeed say that it resembles the Tang dynasty’s acquisition of worthy men; yet, ultimately, that is not the highest praise. Thus, writing gives voice to flourishing rule; the age provides the occasion for such a conjunction; and encountering that age constitutes opportunity. You gentlemen, born into a flourishing age, have had your proper time; selected on the strength of your writing, you have had your opportunity. While living in obscurity and straitened circumstances, your thoughts day and night were anxious, always regretting that you had found no opportunity. From now on, you can no longer be counted among those without opportunity. Should you not distinguish yourselves and establish achievements, giving full expression to all that you have cultivated throughout your lives? When men possess talent but find no opportunity, the responsibility lies with the officials concerned. When opportunity has come, yet men fail to use their talents fully, the disgrace belongs to you gentlemen. Exert yourselves, gentlemen!
Preface respectfully composed by Zhang En, School Director of the Confucian School of Suzhou, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered territory.
